The Emperor personally and grandly propagated the transformation of the Dharma. After the presiding master had finished striking the wooden gavel, he asked:

"In this field for selecting Buddhas from amidst a mass of a hundred blessings, the assembly by the sea listens intently seeking the essentials of the Dharma. What is the guest among guests? The Master said: "A single bowl of food from a thousand households."
The student said, "Within this, there is good news: it manifests in every land and at every dust mote.
What is the host within the guest? The Master said, "Blue eyes behold few people. The student said, "When one person has cause for celebration, the myriad people depend upon it.

What is the guest within the host? The Master said, "The ancient cypress before the courtyard shades the humans and devas. The student said, "The heavens are high; the multitude of forms are upright."
The ocean is vast, and a hundred rivers flow toward it. What is the Lord of Lords? The Master said:

"He does not sit upright upon the dais. The student asked: "The roles of guest and host are clearly distinguished as you have instructed; what about that single phrase in the light of the sun? The Master struck him and said:

"Rewards go to those who have merit. A questioner asked: "The Benevolent Emperor loved the Way and convened a great assembly at Chongxuan. The Patriarch’s command must be carried out; [how shall we] establish..."
The Dharma Banner asked, "Today, how do you unfold the principles of the ancestral school? The Master said, "Come forward, and I will tell you.
He stepped forward and said, "Upon the summit of the Golden Wheel, the Song of Non-arising is sung; it resonates through the imperial capital, its melody renewed.
The Master said, "A single phrase that startles the people. He stepped forward and said, "If so, then within the Hall of Myriad Virtues, you are rain and dew; the five..."

"A pure breeze rises from atop the dragon pavilion. The Master said, "May we together vow thus. The student asked, "As for the single phrase of 'looking up to respond to the sagely brilliance,' how would you speak of it?
The Master said, "The ten-thousand-year rattan of Mount Huading at Tiantai;
its heart of gratitude and recompense is as iron and stone. A question was asked: "Now, within the Hall of Myriad Goodness, one prostrates before the precious names of the myriad Buddhas. However—"
[The monk] knew his name, but did not know in which land he resided. The Master said, "Upādyāya, are you drunk? [The monk] replied, "I am not like that.
The Master then struck him. The monk shouted; the Master struck him again. [The monk] replied, "There is no need to bring it up again. The Master struck him once more.
[The monk] asked, "What is the Bhagavān of the ten directions? The Master said, "He strikes you everywhere. [The monk] continued, "As for..."
"What is the single path to the gate of nirvana? The Master said, "Look beneath your feet. He asked further, "What is the field for selecting Buddhas?
The Master said, "The eye upon the staff is as clear as the sun. He asked further, "What is it like to return with one's mind empty, having passed the examination?
The Master then struck him. He asked further, "If that is so, then all the stars in heaven bow toward the North; among humans, there is [no other]..."
"Water does not flow toward the east. The Master struck him again. A monk asked, "Under the Fifth Patriarch there was a Great Master Shenxiu;

for what reason did he not receive the robe and bowl? The Master said, "Because his entire body is Buddha. The monk pressed further, "For what reason did Layman Lu, however, receive the robe and bowl?
The Master said, "Because he did not understand Zen or the Way. The monk pressed further, "If that is so..."
"One may say they are clever; such people are found everywhere. Those who are truly foolish are rare indeed in this world. The Master then struck him.
On that day, there were many virtuous and eminent monks. The Master again looked around to his left and right and said, "When the World-Honored One held up the flower, Kāśyapa smiled.
A million humans and devas followed in succession to attain Buddhahood."
The Imperial carriage arrived with solemn dignity. He was commanded to ascend the Precious Throne of Myriad Virtues and reveal the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye and the Wondrous Mind of Nirvāṇa.
All the accomplished Zen companions emerged to meet him. "Is there anything further? he asked. Then he said: "Nine years facing the wall—the calculation remains unfulfilled;
standing in the snow waist-deep—the toil was in vain. He then performed three prostrations and stood in his place, showing that he understood the proper etiquette.
Thus it is. Repenting of offenses and untying bonds, the whip’s shadow flies high; where nature is non-existent, nature is empty, and the wind through the pines clamors in the ears.
Fundamentally there is not a single thing, yet one pursues gold and carves jade. Two branches of tender cassia spread their fragrance in five leaves;

with one voice from different mouths, ten thousand mountains reflect the same moon. Even unto Laughing Rock (Xiaoyan), the Great Patriarch, who emerged in the divine capital to establish the principles of the Linji school.
The waves at the Dragon Gate are vast; it stands solitary and precarious. The matter is such a matter; the person must be such a person.
If you can obtain such a person, why worry about such a matter? But tell me, what is this "such a matter"? [The Master] raises his *kāṣāya* and says:
"Like heaven covering all, like earth supporting all. When the fine wind blows, exert your strength; all turn toward this very place."

[The Master] blows the signal horn. He ascends the hall. After the head monk has finished striking the gavel, he asks: "The immortal guest rides upon the clouds across the purple capital; joyfully meeting the Sage Ruler, he speaks of the profound mystery.
For fifty days in the golden palace, the imperial grace was heavy; now he is permitted to board a small boat to cross the snowy ravine. I wonder—"
"Is this secret still known by all? The Master said, "The heavens are high and the earth is deep. The student continued, "The thunderous voice has already resounded beyond the azure sky;
the four seas have all heard the foremost pivot. The Master said, "The radiance of the sun and the brilliance of the moon.
[The student] asked, "The present Emperor is a sagely and enlightened sovereign. He causes the Three Jewels to flourish and clarifies the lamp of Chan. He has specifically invited the Master—"
[The Emperor] ascended the precious throne and personally presided over the turning of the Wheel of Dharma. [The monk asked: "What is the turning of the Wheel of Dharma?
The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, am ashamed. [The monk] further asked, "The Great Way of original nature is beyond words;

I wonder how there can yet be words? The Master said, "The Sacred Grace is difficult to repay. [The monk] further asked, "A single bright pearl is in the midst of the sea, its light illuminating the void."
"Vainly making a lamp of wisdom. The Master stood up, planted his staff on the ground, and said, "I am mindful of your sincerity.
A monk asked, "The tongue has no 'Ten-Character Barrier,' and the feet have severed the 'Five-Colored Thread. I ask the Master: what is this 'Ten-Character Barrier' on the tip of the tongue?"
The Master said, "When such a person comes, give him tea to drink. The student asked, "What is the five-colored thread severed beneath his heels?
The Master said, "When such a person comes, have him sit on the ground. The student asked again.
"Breaking through the crossroads; sweeping away the five-colored threads. The Master struck him and said, "I shall give you and him each thirty blows. He then continued:
"On this auspicious morning of the first day of the month in which Śākyamuni Buddha was born, by imperial decree I ascend the precious throne once more to proclaim the Great Dharma.
Tongxiu, prepare some traces of the Buddha-dharma here to offer as a tribute."
When the great assembly had ascended to their seats, [the Master] observed that every member of the assembly was entirely composed of the Dharma.
From every single pore issued forth immeasurable mouths; from each mouth issued immeasurable sounds; and within each sound were proclaimed immeasurable subtle meanings.
It was thus for every person and thus for every phenomenon, filling the void and pervading the entire Dharma-realm, without so much as a hair’s breadth of anything else.
As for the point of deficiency: there is not even a hair’s breadth of vacancy. As for Tongxiu, what more could he do than carry water to sell at the riverhead?
It is like the River God meeting the Sea Lord; he is suddenly struck with self-disappearance. I humbly entreat the assembly to each cherish yourselves.
Descend from your seats.
In the spring of the Ji-hai year, an imperial edict invited him to the capital, where he was commanded to reside in the Western Garden.
Emperor Shizu asked, "Does the mind abide in the seven locations, or does it not abide in the seven locations? The Master replied, "When seeking the mind, it is utterly unobtainable."
The Emperor asked, "Does one who has awakened to the Way still experience joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure? The Master said, "What do you call joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure?"
The Emperor asked, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth arise from deluded thoughts. If deluded thoughts cease, do mountains, rivers, and the great earth still exist or not?
The Master replied, "It is like a person waking from sleep: as for the events within the dream, are they existent or non-existent?"
The Emperor asked, "How does one apply effort? The Master said, "Upright and non-active.
The Emperor asked, "What is the Great? The Master said, "Its light covers the four quarters; it reaches to the heights above and the depths below."
The Emperor asked, "How does one investigate the original face? The Master said, "Investigate it as the Sixth Patriarch instructed. The Emperor asked, "What did the Sixth Patriarch say?
The Master said, "The Patriarch said: 'When you are neither thinking of good nor thinking of evil—at that very moment, what is your original face?'"
The Emperor asked, "When one is thinking good or thinking evil, how is it? The Master said, "If you like good, simply like good; if you hate evil, simply hate evil.
At the very moment you are liking good and hating evil, investigate: what is it that likes good and hates evil? This is what is meant by "investigating at all times.
First, one must investigate within movement. If you gain power within movement, then [power will follow] in stillness.
The realization within was increasingly superior. As the ancients said, "Attaining through conditions" refers to such swift resonance.
When Emperor Shizu withdrew, he commanded his attendants to convey these words: "I regret that we met so late."
In the autumn of the Gengzi year,
the Emperor had an awakening while on horseback;
he issued successive edicts earnestly inviting him to the capital.
Emperor Shizu went to visit the Master’s chamber in the Western Garden. They looked at each other and laughed; they discussed the profound mysteries until the day was done.
Shizu saw a short novice monk and pointed him out, asking the Master about him. The Master said, "The tall one is the long Dharma-body; the short one is the short Dharma-body."
The Emperor was pleased and thanked him;
he then received the imperial decree to present a eulogy.
Incense burns eternally within the deep hall; with a mind of fasting, one sits and forgets. The Great Perfect Mirror Wisdom is pure; its wondrous response to things knows no fixed method.
Furthermore:

In the compassionate inner chambers, filial care was perfectly fulfilled; sitting in attendance, we joyfully discussed the profound mysteries. Within every atom of the dharma-realm are Buddhas, their light together illuminating the great trichiliocosm.
Amidst the rain-soaked night, I received [the teaching].
The Essential Scripture.
A monk asked Zhaozhou, "How can one avoid going astray? Zhaozhou said, "Recognize your own original mind and see your own original nature;
then you will not go astray."
The mind is identical to the realm of empty space; it manifests dharmas equal to empty space. When the realization of empty space is attained, there is neither "is" nor "non-is.
But tell me, how does one realize empty space?
The mind turns according to the myriad objects; where it turns, it is truly profound. If you recognize your nature while following the current, there will be neither joy nor sorrow.
Seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing are the current—tell me, how do you recognize your nature?
When not a single thought arises, the whole body is revealed; as soon as the six sense organs stir, they are obscured by clouds. Tell me, when the whole body is revealed, how is it?
The narrow footbridge is not Zhaozhou’s bridge; bright moon and clear wind can hardly be compared to it.
When offering incense for the passing of the World-Honored Founder (Shizu), the Master said:
"The reward body is like a dream or an illusion; the world is like flowers in the sky. Only the man of transcendent capacity comes and goes without hindrance.
He then presented the *ruyi* (wishing-granting) jewel, saying: "This is..."
His Majesty’s resources will never be exhausted. The assembly here present shall single-mindedly and diligently recite this ultimate and steadfast Great Dharani.

The ritual attendants shall chant the divine mantras of the Śūraṅgama, the Great Compassionate One, Bhaisajyaguru, and the Rebirth [Sutra], while circumambulating and reciting the names of the Great Being Avalokitesvara.
They shall then perform repentance, make vows, and dedicate the merit.

Ascending the hall on New Year’s Day. Questions and answers are not recorded. The Master said: "Chasing gold and carving jade; embroidering the mouth and refining the mind—there are naturally those who are masters of their own craft.
Turning the body and swinging the arms, baring the eyes and knitting the brows, let the clever Chan practitioners display their brilliance as they will.
Eye to eye, true gold is not traded for brass. To know before it is raised is already to belong to the second or third rank. Right here in the light of day..."
To take this up [as a recommendation] would be nothing short of falling into the seventh or eighth stage of delusion.

If no Buddhas had appeared in the world and no Patriarchs had come from the West, there would be no *śrāmaṇera* before one’s eyes and no old monk here. All verbal explanations are devoid of true meaning. (He hurls down his whisk.)

Treading upon the fields of one’s native land, everyone drums their bellies in joy at the peace and prosperity. [The Master] descends from his seat. On the occasion of the Dragon Boat Festival, he ascends the hall.

After the mallet has struck for the formal address, he cites the following: When Tianlong was serving as an attendant to Xuansha, they were traveling through the mountains together when they encountered a tiger.
Long said, "Monk, a tiger! Sha replied, "It is you, tiger. The Master calls to the assembly, saying: "In the sphere of action of a patch-robed monk, it is like..."
Fire melts ice; the myriad dharmas are fundamentally tranquil, yet only humans create their own clamor. The Great Master Huineng said, "It is not the wind or the banner that moves;
it is your mind, O virtuous one, that moves. One might think this speaks of the Chan of the mind-nature, but those who rely on words perish, and those who cling to phrases are deluded.
Venerable Sheduo said, "It is not the wind-bell that rings; it is my own heart that rings. How many people stand with their backs to the wall! Their minds are once again...
Who is it? Because all are equally quiescent. Does the great assembly understand? One thing is quiescent;
many things are quiescent. One body is quiescent; many bodies are quiescent. One world is quiescent; many worlds are quiescent. Thus was the late Master Tianyin;
thus was the late Master Longchi Huan’eng; and so it is with all the masters of the Linji school, from the highest to the lowest.
The Patriarchs were thus. Two or three in the Eastern Land, four or seven in the Western Heaven—thus it was. (He plants his staff and says: The staff is thus; this mountain monk is thus;
the great assembly is thus. (Looking left and right, he says: Eating *zǒng* dumplings in the hall is thus.
The assembly descended from their seats. On the occasion of the Great Master Huan’s birthday, a memorial service was held. The Master pointed to the portrait and said:

"Sitting there, mouth agape—this old fellow has grown accustomed to taking advantage of people, leaving them with no recourse. Those who can penetrate this point will be like dragons gaining the water."
Like a tiger relying on its mountain: when there is spirit, it adds further spirit; where there is no elegance, it is nonetheless elegant.
Nowadays, within the Great Ming Empire, those who claim to be descendants of the Master Father (Shiweng) number more than hundreds of thousands, even billions.
Yet, in the end, how many can truly attain the great capacity and manifest the great function to be worthy of being his true-bone descendants? As for me, this monk, at the beginning...

While reading the *Recorded Sayings of Longchi*, I saw the Master say: "How many unjust people there are in this world who insist on seeking out another person with whom to measure their strength and compare their excellence against our old Śākyamuni!
Do they know what kind of countenance our Tathāgata Śākyamuni possesses? At this point, I, Monk So-and-so, lose my life."
I had thought that the patriarch’s countenance was merely like this. Later, when I presented my realization to the former master, he subjected me to many harsh and piercing interrogations.
Only then did I realize that if one's insight is equal to the patriarch’s, it diminishes his merit by half; only when one's insight surpasses the patriarch’s is one truly fit to carry on the lineage.
From that point on, I was able to manage my own affairs from the very ground up. Although I was born of the same root as the patriarch, [I was no longer dependent on him].
"I shall not die on the same branch as my late master. My late master was skilled at using cryptic language when he said, "Do people still know what the face of our Śākyamuni Buddha is like?

He caused me, this small blind shaveling, to see my late master’s "sword that kills" at first, but not yet his "sword that gives life. Today, I, the Elder, shall without hesitation reveal it, so that—
"Those who see me and those who hear me should know that beneath my ancestral teacher’s gate there is both the 'knife that kills' and the 'sword that gives life.
Looking left and right, he said: 'If someone were to ask, "What is the true face of my venerable teacher? [I would] offer incense and say: "
Pay close attention.
Entering the hall for the ordination of monks on the Buddha’s Birthday, the Master said: "The new Elder of Baolin is only twenty-four this year;
the Yellow-Faced Old Gautama is my youngest son. From antiquity to the present day, how many have sat upon the curved wooden seat?"
Good friends, on the eighth day of the fourth month, you all have your share of playing with the foul-smelling arrows of that old fellow Gautama.
Have you ever dreamed of Gautama’s teacher? If you can distinguish black from white here, then it matters not whether you shave your head or not;
you will not have come in vain to Bao’en Temple. If you cannot distinguish black from white here—
"Even if Xin Bao'en were to personally clear the weeds for him with his own hands, he would still not escape the fact that, face-to-face, ten thousand miles of white clouds lie between them.
He let out a sudden shout and descended from the seat.

While traveling through the region of Qiū to transform beings, the Master ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he called to the assembly, saying: "Throughout the day you have lived and dwelt together with this mountain monk;
yet do you still recognize where this mountain monk stands? You constantly see this mountain monk moving his lips and stirring his tongue;
yet do you still understand where this mountain monk manifests his true reality? If you can recognize where this mountain monk stands..."
To dwell here in these deep mountains and remote valleys, lying beneath the moon and shrouded in clouds, is precisely to be dragging through mud and water at the crossroads;
and to be dragging through mud and water at the crossroads is precisely to lie beneath the moon and be shrouded in clouds in these deep mountains and remote valleys.
If you can recognize the true state of this mountain monk’s dwelling, then I shall instruct you with my own ears and face-to-face.

"Though separated by thousands and tens of thousands of *li*, those thousands and tens of thousands of *li* have never been without my instructing the great assembly with ear-to-ear whispers and face-to-face commands.
Do you understand? (He strikes the meditation pillar with his staff. On the crown of your head, a single orb is full; where is its pure radiance not present?"

Ascending the hall on New Year’s Day, after the assembly had finished their questions, the Master said: "You practitioners of Zen, listen to me. This matter is not ordinary; it must not be approached with haste.
To climb a mountain, one must reach the very summit; to enter the water, one must go to the deepest cavern.
The vastness of heaven and earth is truly difficult to know, and the abyss of the blue sea is not easily recognized. Let us set aside this 'not knowing' for a moment and penetrate to the ultimate."

To speak the one phrase that reaches the very bottom, how would you say it? "The grasses and trees are no longer their former colors; when the sun warms the Lan-tien fields, the jade gives off its luster.

Then, Master Zhouhua, leading the assembly of lay practitioners from Kunshan, requested him to ascend the hall. The Master looked to his left and right and said: "One who has destroyed their physical form..."
Change your attire and become a world-transcending practitioner. You must simply not begrudge your own life; cast aside hunger, cold, and all hardships beyond your concern.

Devote yourself exclusively to investigating the Great Matter and seek to repay the Buddha’s kindness. Therefore, an ancient worthy said to the assembly: "Now that you have left the household life..."
Like a prisoner released from jail, you have attained life after ten thousand deaths within the Buddha-Dharma; do not ever abandon it again.
This is because I fear that later students, encountering difficult circumstances, might fail to overcome them all at once; thus, I have spoken with such bitter and earnest admonition.
Little do they realize that austere suffering is the fundamental duty of a monk, not only now, but as it has always been since antiquity. In the past, there was Dayu Zhi...
The Master’s permanent provisions are meager; I imagine they are much like those at Bōen. Yet Old Master Zhi is so frugal that he is truly frugal to the very end;
even a few stalks of preserved vegetables will not let one eat well. Once, as he ascended the hall, he said:
When everyone gathers to eat a single stalk of radish, it is called "a single stalk of radish. To enter hell for this is like being shot by an arrow.
Although the provisions here at Bão'ēn are meager, this mountain monk’s long-standing vow has been to provide both food and Dharma so that the assembly may dwell in peace.
Lately, due to famine, there has been no way to settle the community; indeed, my food does not go down my throat, and I am restless whether sitting or lying down. Fortunately, there is a donor...
The Master’s resolve was directed outward; he gradually led the faithful lay donors into the mountains. "For now, do not emulate the insights of those ancients;
their capacity was so small and their mouths were so narrow. Let us all gather here together: when it is plain food, we eat plain food;
when it is a vegetarian meal, we eat a vegetarian meal. To call this 'eating a vegetarian meal,' we and the donors shall together accomplish it."
The Buddha-way. Question: What is the phrase that encompasses heaven and earth? The Master said: "The fragrance of plum blossoms fills the courtyard.
Question: What is the phrase that cuts off all streams? The Master said: "Recently, the kitchen smoke has nearly ceased. Question:
What is the phrase that follows the waves and drifts with the current? The Master said: "Prostrate yourself. He then cited Master Xuedou.
The Master said: "A guest comes from afar, gifting me a jade disc an inch across. Within it are four characters, each character unrecognized by anyone.
Baen also has a verse: "When the Abbot returned from Kunshan, he presented me with several pieces of stone. My entire body is entirely mouth;
who with eyes would not recognize them? He then descended from his seat.
While traveling and teaching, he passed through Qingxi. At Kaifeng Temple, the elder Mr. Cai of Mingdao requested him to ascend the hall.
The Master said: "We are originally true persons; let us speak true words. If you wish to clarify the true matter, you must prepare a true mind.
Anyone among those present who has prepared a true mind, come forth and join in this mutual exchange. A question was asked: "When Linji questioned Huangbo regarding the Buddha-dharma..."
The general meaning is as follows: Huangbo struck him immediately. [The monk] said, "I asked the Master about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma;
how did the Master respond? The Master said, "To procure rice that lasts for a lifetime. The Master then said, "The Buddhas and Patriarchs appear in the world for the sake of one great matter:
that every person awakens to their own wondrous mind and attains their own precious treasury. Empty space is insufficient to metaphorize its duration; the universe is insufficient..."
This serves as a metaphor for its vastness. Mount Tai cannot be considered the highest; the Blue Sea cannot be considered the deepest. It is inexhaustible when drawn from and endless when employed.

The Elder Layman Mingdao, having deeply received the entrustment of Vulture Peak, desires to lift the seal of delusion for sentient beings, so that they may awaken to their own wondrous mind and obtain their own precious treasury. For this purpose, he has specially reconstructed this ancient [monastery] of Kaifeng.
At the Chan Hall, the Daoist Yulín arrived. [The Master] specifically raised this theme for him. He suddenly called out to the assembly, saying, "I do not slight the great assembly;

every member of the assembly shall become a Buddha. He then descended from his seat. Layman Cài bowed and said, "Every time I stand before the deities and Buddhas, I make a vow to protect and uphold the right mindfulness of Caiduó and to prohibit the perverse thoughts of Caiduó. I only pray that when I am about to..."

"At the time of death, will all obstacles and the like be completely purified? Is this so? The Master said, "If this vow is truly sincere, one shall attain the Buddha-way. The disciple bowed again in gratitude.
On his birthday, the Master ascended the hall. After the assembly of monks had finished their questions and discourse, the Master said: "A thousand acres of white clouds, a few old rooms;
sleeping soundly upon a single mat, causing the earth, wood, tiles, and stones to turn the Great Dharma Wheel for the great assembly—this was the ancestral style of my late Preceptor.
Now, Tang Cunweng, together with various donors, has constructed this great Zen hall, where the ten directions gather."
Gathering at this opportune time and season, those who have invited this mountain monk to preach the Dharma are the current practice of New Baoen. Now tell me:
was it the ancestral style of the former Master in days of yore, or is it the current practice of New Baoen? Holding up his staff, he said:
"If you can understand this, Śākyamuni is not before you, and Maitreya is not behind you; you, the great assembly, and all the Buddhas [are one]."
We have equally realized the samādhi of one mark; the mountain monk’s lifespan is no different from that of the great assembly.

If you do not understand this, it would be as if the father were young while the son was old—a thing that the whole world would not believe. [The Master] threw down his staff and descended from the seat.

Ascending the hall after the work period (chup'o), a monk asked: "The year is drawing to a close and half the term has passed; regarding the matter at the feet of the person here, I pray the Master will act for us.
The Master said: "Thirty blows—of those, not even a single blow can be spared. The Master then said: "The Chan of Baolin Monastery is entirely within the reach of the patch-robed monks.
Carrying firewood and transporting earth, they shoulder their loads crosswise all day long. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "Mazu said, 'With one gulp, I swallow up the waters of the West River. This was spoken out of compassion, as a discourse for those who have fallen into the weeds.
The World-Honored One said, 'The empty space of the ten directions arises within your mind, like a single cloud appearing in the vast clarity of the great sky.
If you can understand it in this way, I would just seize you and beat you three thousand times in the morning and eight hundred times in the evening. There was [laughter].
The people of this world mistake the reflection for the head; they abandon the root and pursue the branches.

They take that which is bright and lucid to be the awakening of the Lord of the House, and regard every lifting of a foot, every movement of a step, and every stirring of the lips and tongue as the eternally abiding essence of the mind.

They identify the conditioned reflections of the six sense-objects as the characteristics of their own minds. This is like a person with diseased eyes seeing flowers in the sky or a second moon—hundreds and thousands [of such errors].
"To cast aside the vast, clear ocean and recognize only a single floating bubble—this is to be doubly lost within delusion; it is for this that the Buddha feels deep compassion.
The World-Honored One further said to Ānanda: "As you now listen to my Dharma, this is a discrimination arising because of sound.

Even if you were to leave behind all seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing, and inwardly maintain a state of profound stillness, you would still be discriminating within the sphere of mental objects (*dharmadhātu*)."

This is a matter of shadows. Nowadays, non-Buddhists find it so laughable as to be nearly murderous. They take it to be awakening to one's own mind when one has mastered the art of running away from questions and talking back;
they further claim that because the conscious spirit is empty, even the "host" cannot be found, regarding this as the final state beyond doubt.
Who would have known that thousands of years ago, all were subjected to the World-Honored One’s piercing rebukes and stern admonitions?
Since such instances occurred, should not all students regard what is unwholesome as they would avoid touching boiling water?

They must vigorously penetrate the illusory nature of body and mind, and realize the vast essence of the mind at this very moment, prior to the arising of even a single thought. Even the word "realization" cannot be grasped. Thus it is.
Only when you have realized the vast and great mind-essence of all Buddhas and patriarchs can you truly transcend birth and death; only then can you enter death and enter life.
Such is the nature of this matter; such must one be. If it is not so, then when birth and death arrive, [you will be lost].
Thus one may verify the true from the false. Again, he raised [the point]: An ancient worthy said, "A difference of a hair’s breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth.

The Master suddenly held up his *niwan* (wish-fulfilling jewel) and called to the assembly, saying, "Do you understand? After a long silence, he threw down the *niwan* and said, "The moon in the empty expanse over the azure pool for ten thousand ages—only after searching for it again and again will you begin to know it."

Addressing the assembly, he said: "I address the assembly. He raised the case: Chan Master Fayan pointed to a bench and said, "If you recognize this bench, you will have more than enough room around it.
Yunmen Wenyan said, "If you recognize this bench, heaven and earth are vastly different. Tianyi Huai said, "If you recognize this bench, [it is like] a jujube tree..."
"Made of Nanmu wood. Dahui Zonggao said, "If you recognize the bench, it is good for shaving one's head and washing one's feet.
The Master said, "These great elders each displayed their skillful hands. If we let them pass, they could all occupy the Lion Throne of the Flower King.
However, if we examine them closely, each of them deserves thirty strokes on the legs of a short bench."

While presiding over a session of recitation, the Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Lately, demons have grown strong while the Dharma has weakened. This is because there are no strict teachers above;

thus, those who are heterodox and deluded are allowed to set foot within our school. Most of them merely study the 'essence of the teachings' (zongzhi) or discuss the 'essence of the teachings,' yet they falsely imagine the essence and engage in nothing but reckless fabrication and excavation, arbitrary guessing and conjecture.
The ancestral lineages and fundamental principles remain with their true countenances fully manifest—how [can you fail to see this?]"
I have once seen this in a dream; thus it is said that "every word accords with the ultimate meaning, yet every step misses the fundamental source.
Such shameless fellows as these falsely claim themselves to be descendants of Linji. As soon as they open their mouths, they say, "When one shows compassion, there must be a method."
There is no way not to bestow compassion. In the Linji school, there are the fundamental and the essential; there is the provisional and the real; there is illumination and function;

there is host and guest. Yet, you ultimately treat the formal affairs of the monastery and the liturgical recitations of the two halls as mere ritualistic ceremonies to be perfunctorily performed, claiming that one must at least recite the Buddha’s name to be worthy of the lineage of the patriarchs.
Guest: Alas! I do not know how thick the skin of such people as these is. If you say that [this matter] is but an ordinary occurrence, it obstructs the ancestral Way;
in that case, one should simply disregard it. How can you say "with little regard" or "make a mere effort"?

If one merely conforms to worldly conventions and compromises with the story, how could this be the conduct of a true man who acts as the eyes for humanity and the heavens, and serves as a teacher to the Buddhas and Patriarchs? I now sincerely point out these masters who are short-sighted and flow with the vulgar:
do not boast of being disciples of the Patriarchs, and do not falsely claim to have realized the fundamental principle.
Do not seek elsewhere for what it means to be a human being. Since you wish to clarify the fundamental principle (*zongzhi*), do not let it slip past you right before your face.

Do not practice the art of "picking up one and letting go of another. To teach you how to know gratitude, here—in this very place where the two halls chant their lessons—there is the profound and the essential, the provisional and the real, the illuminating and the functional. At times, when I, the Elder [Name], utter a single sound of "Buddha," it is like a vajra.
The King’s Precious Sword: sometimes a single utterance of "Buddha" is like a lion crouching on the ground; sometimes a single utterance of "Buddha" is like a probing pole and its shadow-grass;
sometimes a single utterance of "Buddha" does not function as a single utterance of "Buddha. Therein is both killing and there is also bringing to life.
There is also the expansive, and there is the subduing; there is the host, and there is the guest. It is like a cool pond, yet like a great mass of fire:
to turn one's back on it is to undergo all manner of suffering and affliction, while to touch it is to have one's face scorched away.

It favors people, shifting from left to right; sometimes advancing, sometimes retreating; sometimes deviant, sometimes correct; sometimes right, sometimes wrong; and sometimes the practice and understanding are in accord, and sometimes they are not.
It corresponds [to the truth]. Whether one perceives the ground as being penetrated or not, there is no need for separate examinations or tests;

these two sessions of recitation alone provide a complete and detailed discernment. For all those who practice at Baoke Monastery, you must by no means treat the recitations, the work periods, and so forth as mere formalities performed out of habit.
You must know that there is nothing that is not the secret Dharma of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, and nothing that is not...
The *dhāraṇī* gate of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is nothing other than the essential heart-essence not transmitted by the Buddhas and Patriarchs;
it is nothing other than the shortcut for self-benefit and benefiting others according to the Buddhas and Patriarchs.

If you claim there is a separate fundamental principle, a separate Buddha-dharma, or some superior understanding, and further seek to use Zhaozhou’s saying about "chanting the Buddha's name to rinse one's mouth" as a pretext to evade diligence, you are acting recklessly.
As for those who speculate: first, they slander Zhaozhou for not requiring people to recite the Buddha’s name;
then, they organize "Buddha-Recitation Assemblies" based on the *Baoen Jing* (Sutra on Gratitude). This is truly pitiable.

If you were truly a person of substance, you would be able to exert your own skillful means and provide a different kind of provision for others. I, this old monk, already know you; I do not want you to be like me.
If you all think that the Way must be like this, I am not like this either.

As for my being thus, there is nothing lacking among the profound and the essential, the provisional and the real, illumination and function, or the host and guest, yielding and seizing. How will you understand this?
Would you dare to venture a speculative judgment? Anyone who is possessed by demons and whose toxic breath has deeply entered—let them go elsewhere at their leisure to study the Buddha.

Regarding the Dharma, the fundamental tenets of our school often give rise to conceptual proliferation and various forms of discriminatory selection. Only when one’s eyes are opened in the future will one realize for oneself that one has fallen into error.
Therefore, you who are my true companions in the study of the Way must firmly plant your feet and exert yourself in practice;

do not allow yourselves to be deluded by demons. As for those who are like "lions with worms" within their own kind, they shall certainly not be permitted to act with negligence or to disrupt the pure regulations.
On the night of the *karmavācanā* (formal ritual), the Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Those who violate the precepts fall into the various realms of suffering;

those who uphold them receive retribution among humans and devas. But tell me, where will one be reborn who neither violates nor upholds them? After a long silence, he said: "From this point on, there is no returning;
once one returns, it is attained. Who can contest the wind and moon of the old garden? Thereupon, he returned to his quarters.
Addressing the assembly, the Master raised this case: A monk asked Ciming, "How is it when one seeks stillness amidst bustle? Ciming said, "My head rests upon a hemp sack.
The Master said, "If I had been sitting in the ranks below, I would have taught Xian Nanyuan not to stop there.
Why did he not press on by saying, 'Master, do not merely propagate worldly conventions'? Tell me, how then would Xian Nanyuan have responded?"
Addressing the assembly, the Master said: "All of you must believe that you are originally Buddhas.
Each of you must recognize your original face and tread upon the natural radiance of your own ground. If you can recognize your original face, then the golden world shall have a body of white jade;
there will be groves of sandalwood surrounded by sandalwood. Otherwise, the groves of grasses and trees will wither away at every moment."
At the funeral, the assembly prostrated. [The Master] addressed the assembly, citing: Chan Master Foyan ascended the hall and said: "The world says that traveling the road is difficult;

but when the gold of one's true nature enters the fire, it is tested. As it is refined again and again, the essence of the gold becomes pure, and with a single blow, it is fashioned into a jade railing. The Master said:
When the ancient masters spoke thus, there must have been those who leaped for joy upon hearing it, and there must have been those who were struck with awe and trepidation upon hearing it.
Addressing the assembly, the Master raised this case: Chan Master Jingjue Ben was asked by a monk, "What is it like when like sounds respond to one another?
Jingjue said, "The magpie crows on the tree. The Master said, "It is a pity that this monk asked in vain; he did not know where the point lay. When he saw Old Man Jingjue say..."
The turtledove cries upon the tree. Why not raise your palm toward the distant sky and say, "When you strike it down from the branch, what then?
If Old Taning were to reply again, "A master Chan guest has a natural presence," why not press him further by saying, "I have come to offer tea and invite the Master"?
If Old Taning were to reply again, "Truly a master indeed," then one should simply prostrate and depart. Is this not a dialogue?
"Not acting in vain. Nevertheless, "the magpie cries upon the tree"—how do you, the great assembly, understand this?

At the Dead Gate on the Thousand-Fathom Cliff, he addressed the assembly, saying: "During these one hundred and twenty days, this old monk has walked three times every day through the bellies of all you officials of the two orders.
Do you know it? After the assembly had finished offering their responses, the Master spoke again:
"For these one hundred and twenty days, the old monk has practiced asceticism in every hall and quarters day after day.
Have you Zen practitioners gone through three rounds within your bellies? Do you know? When the assembly had finished their remarks, the Master spoke again: "For these one hundred and twenty days..."
"Every day this old monk walks three times through the bellies of the great assembly, both inside and out. Does the assembly know? (The assembly stood for a long time.
The Master looked to his left and right, then descended from his seat.
In the evening *xiaochan*, the Master held up his staff and said: "In this mountain of mine, there is not a single thing. The boulders are large where they are large and small where they are small.
The people inside and outside come out for labor two or three times every day. Suddenly, if there were a man to come forth—"
The Way. The Master’s earlier words do not correspond to his later words. Simply say to him: "This is not your realm. Looking left and right, he said:
"If you can understand this, I grant that you need not chew a single grain of rice, yet you eat from a great bowl;

you need not wear a single thread of silk, yet you are clothed all day long. If you cannot understand this, it is not a matter of merely following forms or sounds, for you would otherwise fall into the deep pit of liberation."
A Pitfall. Great Assembly, when you arrive here, you must be extremely careful. After a long pause, he planted his staff on the ground and said, "Enter. Evening Session.
The Master took up his staff and said, "In the beginning, when Layman Pang reached the top of the hundred-foot pole, he thought he had surpassed others.
Opening his mouth, he asked: 'What is that person who does not take companionship with the myriad dharmas? Fortunately..."

At that time, there were people from all quarters who, encountering those like the foxes, wolves, and jackals of today—like the blind leading the blind—would see someone sitting atop a hundred-foot pole and immediately say, "You are already dead. One must penetrate the kōans of the Patriarchs.
This is precisely finding life within death. It is to have people drill and chisel recklessly—penetrating one case today and another tomorrow.
If you act like this, will you not be laughed at all at once and leave a foul stench for ten thousand generations?
What "Pang-erh who covers heaven and earth" are you seeking? Nevertheless, it is also because the person is willing to enter the furnace of a master craftsman.

Only by seeking out a person of great capacity and insight to undergo refinement can one truly attain it. Look at Layman Pang meeting Shitou: he asked, "Who is the one who does not take the myriad dharmas as his companion?
Shitou suddenly covered his mouth with his hand. If there were someone here who could understand this, they would feel no small measure of shame;
yet, they would still not have reached the state of the Great Rest and Great Cessation. It was only when he went to Mazu Daoshi in Jiangxi that he finally did so.
He asked again as before, "Who is it that does not take the ten thousand dharmas as a companion?
Master Mazu stepped forward one pace and said, "Wait until you can suck up all the water of the West River in a single draught, and then I will tell you.
At this point, Layman Pang’s very life-root snapped with a finality and broke through with a sudden burst; he let go of his impoverished belly, and the ocean [opened wide].
He receives the hundred rivers; he traverses in seven directions and ranges in eight. He is thoroughly proficient in a thousand ways and reaches mastery in ten thousand paths.

He strides with lofty steps upon the Great Way. When he utters a single word, no one dares to listen to it directly with their ears. When he establishes a single practice, no one dares to look at it directly with their eyes.
The Master called to the assembly, saying: "Great Master Mazu took that one step—have you all seen it yet? Only if you have seen it..."
"You may meet the mountain monk’s staff. If you have not yet seen it, how could a patch-robed monk be inferior to a layperson? Is there such a one? Is there?
He suddenly held up the staff and said, "Cease for now; even if you were to drink dry the Western River, how would you swallow this mountain monk’s staff?
After a long silence, he struck the ground with the staff and said, "The sword leaves its precious sheath because of injustice."
The Medicine Master brought out a golden pitcher to save the sick; he cast aside his staff and left the hall.

On the fifteenth night, there was a small *sengcan* (informal discourse). He raised the following case: A monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Zhaozhou said:
"The cypress tree in the courtyard. The Master said, "Baoyuan does not do it this way. If someone asks, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
simply say to them: 'Tonight the single orb is full; where is its clear light not present?'"
Small Assembly (Xiaocan). The Master said: "I, this mountain monk, shall not point out the way; let everyone wander blindly at will.

If you can wander blindly with such vigor—disregarding danger, death, gain, or loss—and press forward with all your might until you suddenly strike a sheer cliff or jagged crag and smash your skull open, then perhaps, just perhaps, you may once know what it is to feel pain. Question: "All..."
"If one were to wander about blindly, I would not question it. But when one has bumped one's skull and broken it, what then?

The Master said, "It is both shameful and laughable. The student asked, "I do not ask about bumping and breaking the skull; why is it both shameful and laughable? The Master said, "This is not within your realm."

Small Assembly Lecture. The Master raised an example: A monk asked Zen Master Huanglong of Meizhou, “What is the secret chamber? Huanglong said, “It cannot be split open. The monk asked, “Who is the person within the secret chamber? Huanglong said, “Neither male nor female. The Master said: When the ancients spoke thus, I, this mountain monk, am not like that. What is the secret chamber? It is sevenfold penetrating and eightfold unobstructed. What is the secret chamber? [He repeats the question. It is sevenfold penetrating and eightfold unobstructed. What is the person within the secret chamber? It is neither male nor female. But what about me? I am neither male nor female. Why is that? Because I have never been born. Therefore, I am neither male nor female. If you can understand it this way, you will see that the ancients were indeed speaking of the Way. If you do not understand it this way, you will be like a mosquito trying to bite an iron ox. Go on, go on! Try to say something. If you can speak, I shall grant you the seal of the Buddhas and patriarchs; if you cannot speak, I shall strike you with my staff. Do you understand? If you do not understand, you must go to a place where there is no one to ask. If you go to a place where there is someone to ask, you will surely be struck by my staff. Why? Because the staff is the Buddha-Dharma, and the staff is the ancestral Way. If you can understand it this way, you will see that the staff is the Buddha-Dharma and the staff is the ancestral Way. Because the staff is the Buddha
The people in the room—some tall, some short. Tell me, are they the same as the ancients or different?
He lets out a shout and strikes the meditation pillar once with his staff.
On a mid-spring evening, the Master entered the hall for a formal discourse. He said, "The ancients said that Lingyun’s place of seeing was not upon the peach blossoms.
But tell me, what was his place of seeing? The assembly was silent. The Master said, "This is truly like taking a fine, rare fruit."
The shell is gone; the kernel is gone. He offers it to people’s mouths, yet they do not know how to eat it.

When Feng Xitang was presiding over the whisk, the Master said: "In the past, Zhaozhou said, 'In the south, by my hearth, there is a story of neither guest nor host that no one has brought up to this day.
*Agh!* Even if you were to say, 'I am sleeping with the door closed,' [it would still be insufficient]."

Even those of the highest capacity have not yet reached it. If one were to maintain this kind of understanding, whenever people of the present day hear of the "Path Above" or the "Final Firm Barrier," they invariably engage in endless deliberation and debate. They are like the man who speaks of medicine:
when the true medicine appears before him, he is utterly unable to recognize it. Yuanming said: "The level fields meet the distant wind; the fine seedlings also embrace the new. Dongpo...

He said: "It is not one who plows with a companion and leans on a staff from antiquity who could speak thus; it is not one who has been a farmer in my own time who would know the subtlety of these words.
I say the same regarding Zhaozhou: in a short while, I shall trouble West Hall Feng to bring this out before the assembly."

Evening *zhan*. Questions and answers are not recorded. The Master said: "This morning, Senior Seat Zen'en led the assembly to request the Dharma. I, this mountain monk, said: 'When the bell strikes, eat your meal.

I then called to the assembly: 'The Great Encompassment extends beyond the mundane; its subtlety penetrates the tip of a hair. The sails are set upon the clear Xiang River; Mount Heng opens its nine faces.
Even when monastics are in moments of haste or distress, they do not depart from the side of their robes and bowls. They are truly able to [manifest] with the dew..."
The pillar and I are both clad in the same single robe; have we not shared the same alms bowl with this mountain monk to cook and enjoy our meal?

Here, every blade of grass and every tree attests equally to perfect enlightenment. Why then do some harbor doubts within themselves and create distinctions, thereby wasting the wealth of the Dharma and extinguishing their merit?
Is it not always due to this mind-consciousness? Truly, these words are true! South of Mount Taihang and north of Mount Daizong.
Guests from distant heavens and foreign lands all join this mountain monk in morning incense and evening lamps, sharing in this profound stillness.
Why is it that someone so close, separated only by mountains and passes, finds the clarity of their realization to be so extreme that what they seek is delayed? Is this not truly lamentable?
In days of yore at Shaolin, the Second Patriarch followed the wind of the teaching; he stood in the cold courtyard amidst the snow until it reached his knees and waist. How...
The patriarchs regarded an equanimous mind as the very backbone; even the Founder (Bodhidharma) still rebuked those with frivolous or arrogant minds as being toilsome and useless.

Only by severing the arm to settle the mind did he transcend the crowd and attain the marrow. Looking back at these former masters, how could one be like a mere peddler? He struck once with his whisk and said: "Refined gold shines with brilliance through a hundred smeltings;
let the quicksilver of medicinal elixirs boast of its metallurgy."
Evening *chan* session. A question was asked: "I have been reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* and reached the section on the 'Investigation of the Mind in Seven Places.

I have come to a certain understanding there. The Master said, "Tsk! This is not your mind. How do you understand it? He replied, "I am without mind. The Master said, "That is like biting a wooden peg used for tethering a dog."
"Not a good dog. A student asked, "Time flies like an arrow and days pass like a shuttle. How can one transcend birth and death? The Master said, "Do not be so shameless.
The Master then said, "Do not say that 'no-mind' is the Way; even no-mind is still separated by a single barrier.
Another said, "What do you mean by 'a single barrier'? It is truly a thousandfold and ten-thousandfold barrier. "If it is thus, what ultimately..."
"How does one clarify the mind and see the nature? After a long silence, he said, "Yesterday, while at Baoen Temple, I addressed the assembly, saying:
'The heavens, earth, sun, and moon of antiquity are the same as the heavens, earth, sun, and moon of today. The heavens, earth, sun, and moon have no distinction between past and present.'"

The Way of Chan and the Buddha-dharma should likewise have no distinction between ancient and modern. Why is it that the realized ones (zhishi) of antiquity remain vividly present before our eyes even after a thousand or ten thousand generations?
Yet the realized ones of later times, though existing in the present age, often seem as if they were people from the depths of the underworld.
Those who studied in ancient times attained sudden enlightenment in a single moment, illuminating both past and present; those of today...

Those who study this path may have some points of realization today and some points of realization tomorrow; yet when the matter of birth and death arrives, they remain as disoriented and frantic as before.
This is because the Way has neither sameness nor difference; sameness and difference reside in the person. The resolve of those today is no different from that of the ancients;
their investigation is no different from that of the ancients; their rigorous austerity is no different from that of the ancients.
The ancients reached the point where there was no longer any application of mind, yet they were never unlike the ancients;
however, when the ancients reached that state of no-mind, they never retreated out of fear of the precipice. From the top of a hundred-foot pole, they were able to advance even further.
Thus it is said: "Letting go at the edge of the cliff, one spontaneously accepts the burden; after death, one revives again—this cannot deceive the Master. People today...
At the summit of a thousand peaks, not only does one fail to advance, but one instead turns back and says, "I was dead and have now attained life.

To take this "attainment of what cannot be attained" as the ultimate goal, and to take the raising of a fist or the pointing of a finger as having penetrated the Patriarch's barrier—this is a grave error.
All of this is like standing on a precipice with one's feet drawn back; it is various forms of self-deception. One is far, far removed from the ancients.
(He plants his staff upright and says: "A man of resolve knows for himself what is good and what is evil."
Evening *chán*. The Master said: "Those who understand the Way are many; those who practice the Way are few. The great and small patriarchs have split the discourse into two separate pieces.
One may understand it, yet be unable to practice it. Where does that which is understood go? How is it that you all act throughout the twelve periods of the day?
After a long silence, he said: "The sound of water circling the hermitage is ever-present; the momentum of a thousand peaks embraces the platform."
[The Master] was about to take his leave when he went for the early morning assembly. The Master said, "The ancients said: 'Do not be deceived by the tongues of the old monks of the world. I say:
'Do not be deceived by the conduct of the spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) of the world. A guest in the Gate of the Patriarchs must be truly authentic in their practice."
Death. Only when the mouth does not chew a single grain of rice and the body does not wear a single thread of silk may one then freely dress and eat.
Only when the eyes see not a single stroke—neither horizontal nor vertical—and the ears hear not a single word or phrase may one then at will write characters and read books.
Otherwise, if the Great Matter is not yet clarified, it is as if one has lost one’s parents; if the Great Matter is already clarified, it is as if...
Regarding the loss of one's father and mother: if your resolve regarding life and death is not urgent, be careful not to leave the household life.

Even if you do leave the household life, be careful not to come to the School of the Patriarchs (the Chan/Zen tradition). Why is this? Although you may not yet be facing the matter of life and death at present, if you do not lightly leave the household life and do not lightly come to the School of the Patriarchs, you will still know that there is the business of leaving the household life, and you will still know that there is the business of the School of the Patriarchs. There are some...
Having left the household life in haste, you have come to this Chan school to follow the crowd and join the ranks, setting your mind to practice "work" as if striking at a target.
After practicing for some time, when you fail to hit the mark, you then become idle day by day and negligent moment by moment.
Since you are thus yourself, you assume that others are likewise; thus you slander the Great Prajñāpāramitā and suffer its bitter retribution.
Immeasurable. Those of noble resolve must strive for absolute certainty. Late evening session.
The Master said: "Dwelling together here, whether you are long-established practitioners or beginners, each of you must step back until you reach the ground of ultimate sincerity and non-deception."
Evening Assembly. The Master said: "At Longyuan this winter, we shall establish three rules for the assembly. First: when drinking water, you must not let it wet your mouth.
Second: when eating rice, you must not bite into the grains. Third: when walking in meditation, you must not collide with the pillar."
New Year’s Day. Master Zhiyu accepted an invitation from a lay patron for a small discourse (*xiao can*). The Master said: "Does the assembly know?

Since you attained Buddhahood, immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas have already passed. With every step you raise and every step you take, the ground beneath you is firm and solid, adorned with supreme and wondrous jewel wheels composed of vajra.
There are jeweled ponds, crystal pavilions, extraordinary trees, rare birds, and musical instruments."
It is overflowing and replete; there is no cause for suffering. One’s lifespan is immeasurable, one’s radiance is immeasurable, and one’s spiritual kin are immeasurable.

If you do not yet understand this, do not pride yourself on long-standing cultivation, nor disparage those who have only recently begun their studies. A single thought that turns the light back upon itself is identical to the state of all the Sages.
If your faculties and intellect are dull, simply request that not a single thought arise. If you possess much knowledge and understanding, yet are also full of delusion, [then likewise apply this].
I now invite Jingnian to follow in succession. If you simply possess the heart of resolve, I shall certainly not deceive you. Even so, tell me:
when Sudhana entered the gate of the pavilion, why did he close it behind him once he had entered? Therefore it is said: "The Tathāgata does not appear in the world;
the Patriarchs did not come from the West. You have already attained Buddhahood for immeasurable asaṃkhyeya kalpas."
Evening *zazen* assembly. The Master said: "Last night, the attendant announced the evening assembly for the great assembly. I, this mountain monk, delivered these words:
'What a magnificent moon! How do you all understand it? A monk said: 'If one were to cut down the cassia tree in the moon, its pure light would surely increase even more.'"
The Master said, "Adding a point to an arrowhead. The assembly stood for a long time. The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, shall personally receive thirty blows.

Knowing that Guyuan Linghai was leading the lay practitioners of Haining in requesting the lifting of the retreat restrictions, and that the lay practitioner Fan of Shaoxing was seeking absolution from his transgressions, they jointly requested a small-scale sermon (*xiaochan*).
After the question-and-answer session was concluded, the Master brandished his whisk and said: "Every person is extraordinary; every individual is pure and bright."

It is like a bird flying through the sky yet remaining oblivious to the sky, or a fish swimming in water yet forgetting the water. Within that which is free from blemish, one creates blemishes for oneself;
in a place where there are no obstructing conditions, one creates obstructions for oneself. One binds empty flowers to the top of the tree of ignorance—what real fruit could there be?
One plucks the moon reflected in water upon the sea of torpor—this merely results in wearying the mind. Since you are already able to roam freely beyond all things, [why do you labor thus?]
One must suddenly reach the true source. If you know how to take refuge in the Gate of Emptiness, you will certainly awaken to the clarity of the enlightened nature.
When the enlightened nature is clear and the true source is reached, you will finally know that the defilements of sin are fundamentally empty, yet there is no sin that is not repented;
that the Way of Dharma is fundamentally transcendent, yet there is no dharma that is not perfected. Great Assembly, I do not slight you; you shall all become Buddhas. Descend from your seats.
Small Assembly Lecture. The Master said: "Yesterday during the evening assembly, I, this mountain monk, said: 'Washing clean the place where he once drew water;
hewing out the cliff where he sat facing the wall in years gone by. Have you all, members of the assembly, each attained realization?
If you can hear this and open your true eye, then whether in busyness or leisure, movement or stillness, in every word and every silence, there will be a point of emergence."
The path of the body: when one employs the twelve periods of the day rather than being employed by them, one can turn all things around rather than being turned by them.
To churn the great river into cream and curd, and to transform the vast earth into gold, while making offerings to the great assembly—this is not considered extraordinary.
If it were otherwise, then even the morning and evening meals of gruel and rice would be like biting the peak of Mount Sumeru with one’s lips and teeth.
In the interim, it requires far too much support. This seven-foot frame, draped in ice-ridged iron armor, is extremely inconvenient when one bends or stretches;
thus, he leans upon his staff.
At the commencement of the summer retreat, a patron invited the Master for a small discourse (*xiao-chan*). The Master said: "Perfectly round, brilliantly radiant; utterly naked, starkly clear.

Though possessing three heads and six arms, or a thousand hands and a thousand eyes, fundamentally there is not a single thing. Pure and true, suchness itself; without odor and without sound, yet the myriad phenomena unfold in纵横 (zōnghéng—transverse and vertical).
Closing the door to sit in meditation, one is nowhere hidden throughout the entire world. Casting one's body across the bustling marketplace, one stands alone."
Sublime, majestic, and profound. All activities are manifold yet not in motion; not a single thing is done, yet it is not stillness.

Those who oppose it expose themselves; those who seek it lose all the more. Of the thousands of sages and ten thousand saints, there is no gate through which to enter; of the thousands of Buddhas and ten thousand patriarchs, each must step back.
The Master strikes once with his whisk and says: "Who will investigate the Brahmin Śaṇḍilya’s 'Six Months of Heat'?"
Frost flowers form upon the pillows and mats.

[The Master] descends from his seat. Evening Sermon. The Master says: "The time since the Sage departed is remote; words are lofty, yet aspirations are low. If you wish to clarify the meaning beyond the categories, you must exhaust the sentiments within the realm.
Looking left and right, he says: "Everyone, look beneath your feet!"
Evening Assembly. The Master said: "The kalpa-fire blazes fiercely; the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed. I wonder, does this one thing get destroyed or not?
If it is destroyed, then you must follow it along. But if you follow it along, what excellence is there in Da sui’s answering the question in such a manner?"

Touzi went up to the mountain to pay his respects; the assembly remained silent. The Master said, "Those who studied in antiquity did so for themselves," and striking the incense table with his bamboo staff, he returned to his quarters.
Evening Assembly. The Master said: "The Patriarch appears at all times upon the water bucket;
as soon as he sees someone carrying water, he slips inside the bucket. The Patriarch appears at all times within the flames;
as soon as he sees someone lighting a fire, he slips into the flames. The Patriarch appears at all times upon the wooden fish; as soon as he sees..."
When someone strikes a wooden fish drum, the Patriarch runs inside the wooden fish.
Whenever the Patriarch appears upon the bells and drums, as soon as he sees someone strike them, he runs inside the bells and drums. After a long silence, he said:
"If someone comes forward and says, 'How can you, Reverend, degrade the noble to the lowly? I want you to speak exactly like that."
Small Sermon. The Master said: "There is no principle outside of phenomena; there are no phenomena outside of principle. Phenomena outside of principle are foolishness;
principles outside of phenomena are madness. Madness leads to being seized by demons; foolishness leads to being pitied by Buddhas."

It is better to be moved by the Buddha’s compassion than to be seized by Māra. As you all come to this ancestral temple, you must establish profound vows, maintain right knowledge and right view, and practice upon the correct path; only then may we hope to realize together the perfect enlightenment of Bodhi.
Evening *Zanchi*. The Master said: "In years past, Chan Master Dahui encountered a student of Zen who could not penetrate a *gong'an* and requested a skillful means.
Dahui said, 'You are a man from Fujian. I shall give you a parable:
it is as if I were to take a fine grade of lychee, remove the skin, remove the pit, and place it right at the edge of your mouth; yet you simply will not eat it.'"
"Understood. The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "In the beginning, Dahui established this analogy for the sake of one person;
that person, at that very moment, bit off his own tongue. Because the monks here were investigating the 'Climbing the Tree' koan, I have repeatedly provided them with assistance, saying:"
"Pressing tightly against the fence while leaving the path wide open—how is this? Among the assembly, none were seen to have their feet touching the ground. He then said:

Evening *zhan*. The Master looked to his left and right and said, "Tonight’s evening *zhan* does not permit questions.

I do not ask you about other aspects of the Buddha-dharma; I ask you only this single, most ordinary statement:

"Speak a startling phrase and see! [He] looked left and right, let out a thundering shout, and gave a small discourse (*xiao can*).

"The physical body. Yet you do not see my Dharma-body. Subhūti was sitting in meditative seclusion in a mountain cave, yet he saw my Dharma-body.

He then picked up his staff and said, "Is there anyone here who can act as the true representative for the World-Honored One? If there is, come forth! Each of you must emerge from a different level of realization. He then planted the staff firmly in the ground.

Small Assembly (Xiaocan). He raised the following case: Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "Where does one who knows go?

Morning session. The Master said: "There is one person who is diligent in all communal duties every day, yet does not perform a single task for himself.

There is another person who does not perform a single task for himself, yet is diligent in all communal duties every day. Tell me, which of these two is a true master? A monk stepped forward; the Master struck him and sent him away.
Another monk prostrated; the Master likewise shouted at him and sent him out. The Master then said: "An old man’s sentiment is similar: incense by day, lamp by night."
Evening Assembly. The Master said: "Like pure lapis lazuli, it is transparent both inside and out.
Those who see the Way—if their body, mind, and the world around them are indeed like pure lapis lazuli, transparent inside and out—only then are they people who have truly seen their original face."
Not so; you are merely deceiving yourself. When birth and death arrive, what will avail your regrets? Have you not heard it said: "My mind is like a lantern;
when the flame is lit, both inside and out are red"? Though this is not a mere imitation of a model, it is nonetheless a breath drawn through the nose.
Evening *chan* assembly. The Master said: "Autumn has come; it is good for sitting in meditation. You worthy monks, do not wander about aimlessly.

Each of you shall attain the ground of the sitting mat, so that in years to come you may open your mouths wide. But as for the phrase 'attaining the ground,' how would you say it? With the mouth born of one's parents, one ultimately does not speak for others."
Lantern Festival. Knowing that the donor, Lord Yu, had invited him for a small discourse (*xiaocan*), the Master said: "Like pure lapis lazuli, it is transparent both within and without;
its radiance surpasses the sun and moon, and its measure envelops the great void. One cannot find its beginning by searching for it, nor can one fathom its limit by avoiding it.
Mountains, rivers, and the great earth—when approached, they all melt away. Brightness and darkness, form and emptiness—if one relinquishes them, there is nothing left upon which to establish."
It stands firm; neither spirits nor ghosts can gaze upon it, and neither sages nor saints can know it. Washed, it is not renewed; fouled, it does not grow old.

It does not diminish when wriggling creatures move within it, nor does it increase when Buddhas and Patriarchs appear. To call it "subtle" is because it pervades heaven and earth; to call it "manifest" is because no traces of its form remain.

It is designated as the "Wisdom Pearl," for though it remains dark, it shines daily more brightly; it is named the "Fortunate Mountain," for though it is level and plain, it grows daily more venerable. Thus it is summoned.
The assembly said, "I saw the auspicious light-omen of the Buddha Dīpaṃkara; its original radiance was like this.
[A monk] privately examined a document. Evening *can*: The Master said, "The top three strokes are long; the bottom two strokes are short. Heaven rotates to the left."
The earth turns to the right; the sun and moon shine upon it; dragons and elephants gallop beneath it. It rises higher than the Unbounded Heaven and plunges deeper than the Fragrant Water Sea.
Whether wise or foolish, noble or base, whoever recognizes this single word—the Sage Confucius and Master Mencius join their palms in praise;
Śākyamuni is not before it, Maitreya is not behind it—it surges forth in transcendent speed.

Transcending the dust of the world—whether ancient or modern—who would dare to be his peer? My good brother, if even directly cutting to the root is still considered circuitous, what can be said of searching for branches and plucking leaves?
Small Assembly Lecture. After the questions and answers were finished, the Master said: "A single expanse of cool clarity, peaceful and beyond compare.
Whether coming and going or staying among the assembly, take each step without losing the way. The assembly stood for a long time. The Master let out a thunderous shout and descended from his seat.
Small Assembly (Xiaocan). The Master said: "There is a person of no affairs who is busy and bustling all day long;
there is a man of diligent practice who for many years has been slow and dull-witted. Between these two kinds of people, one is fit to be a teacher for others.

You, the great assembly, must observe yourselves well when you come and go. After a long silence, he said: "How could the true realm of tranquil light ever be distant? We are together within the Kingdom of Lapis Lazuli."
