The Master said, "It is constantly extending, yet it cannot be brought forth. He added, "Even to become a Buddha or a Patriarch, it cannot be brought forth."
"One cannot escape the cycle of the six realms. The monk asked, "I do not understand what it is that one cannot escape. The Master said, "By day one sees the sun;
by night one sees the stars. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The colors of Mount Sumeru are green and green again."

When the Master returned from traveling the mountains, the Head Seat asked, "Where have you been, Reverend? The Master said, "I have come back from traveling the mountains. The Head Seat asked, "To what places did you go?
The Master said, "First I followed the fragrant grasses away; then I returned, chasing the falling blossoms. The Head Seat said, "That is very much like the spirit of spring.
The Master said, "It is even better than autumn dew dripping upon lotuses."

There was a scholar who, while reading the *Sūtra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas*, asked: "I see the names of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, but I do not know in what lands they dwell, nor whether they still transform sentient beings.
The Master said: "After Cui Hao inscribed his poem on the Yellow Crane Tower, have you, scholar, ever composed a verse there as well?
He replied: "I have not yet. The Master said: "When you find the leisure, you should compose a fine piece."
A monk asked, "Does the person of original nature become a Buddha or not? The Master said, "Do you see the Emperor of the Great Tang ever planting fields or harvesting rice himself?
The monk said, "I do not know who it is that becomes a Buddha. The Master said, "It is you who become a Buddha.

The monk was speechless. The Master said, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "It is like a person who falls because of the ground and relies on the ground [to rise]."
[The Master] rose. [The monk asked:

"What is the path of the stages? [The monk] asked: "Please tell me, what is the upward path? The Master said: "A single needle; three feet of thread. [The monk] asked: "How should one comprehend this?
The Master said: "Sichuan cloth; Yangzhou silk."
The Master showed them a verse, saying: "One who stands motionless atop a hundred-foot pole, Though they have gained entry, it is not yet the truth.
One must advance further from the hundred-foot pole; The worlds of the ten directions are one’s entire body. A monk then asked, "As for that hundred-foot pole, how does one advance?
The Master said, "The mountains of Langzhou; the waters of Lishui. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The four seas."
Within the Imperial Transformation of the Five Lakes, Minister Zhu asked: "When an earthworm is cut into two segments, both ends move. I do not know in which head the Buddha-nature resides.

The Master said: "Do not engage in false conceptualization. Zhu said: "But what can be done about its movement? The Master said: "If you understand, it is simply that wind and fire have not yet dispersed."
Shushu made no reply. The Master called out, “Shushu! Shushu responded, “Yes. The Master said, “That was not your original name, Shushu.
Shushu said, “It cannot be that apart from this present response, there is another second master.
The Master said, “May I call you ‘Supreme Honored One’? Shushu said, “When one does not respond at all like this, are you not my master? The Master said, “No.”
It is not merely a matter of whether one is attentive or inattentive; since beginningless kalpas, this has been the very root of birth and death.
He shows this in verse: "The student of the Way does not recognize the Real, Simply because from of old they have identified with the conscious spirit.
The root of birth and death since beginningless kalpas— The deluded call it the 'Original Person.'"
A monk asked, "How can one transform mountains, rivers, and the land so that they return to oneself?

The Master said, "How can one transform oneself so that it becomes mountains, rivers, and the land? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Under the city walls of Hunan, the people are well-nourished."
The monk said, "Rice is cheap and firewood is plentiful; it is sufficient for the four neighbors. The Master showed him a verse, saying: "Who asks about the turning of mountains and rivers?
Mountains and rivers turn toward whom? Perfect penetration has no two sides; The nature of phenomena fundamentally has no place of return."
He addressed the assembly: "If the mind were something born, then dreams, illusions, and empty flowers would also have to be born.
If the body were something born, then the mountains, rivers, the great earth, and the myriad phenomena of the universe would also have to be born."
The questioner asked, “In the teachings, it is said that the illusory mind exists. Master, what do you say? The Master replied, “Virtuous One, what kind of statement is this?
He said, “If that is so, then does the illusory mind not exist? The Master replied, “Virtuous One, what kind of statement is this?

He said, “If that is so, then is the illusory mind neither existent nor non-existent? The Master replied, “Virtuous One, what kind of statement is this? He said, “As for me, my three types of supernormal knowledge are exhausted.”
“I do not yet understand the meaning of ‘illusion’ within the teachings. How does the Master clarify this?

The Master said, “Virtuous One, do you believe that all phenomena are inconceivable? He replied, “These are the sincere words of the Buddha; how could I dare not believe them? The Master said, “Virtuous One, you say you ‘believe.
Between the two kinds of belief, which one is it? He replied, “According to my understanding, between the two kinds of belief, it is...”
"Named 'Conditioned Faith' (yuanxin). The Master asked, "By means of what teaching can this conditioned faith be generated? He replied, "The *Avataṃsaka* states:
'Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, by means of unobstructed and unhindered wisdom, believe that all worldly realms are the realm of the Tathāgata.
Furthermore, the *Avataṃsaka* states: 'All Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, fully know that the nature of worldly dharmas and the nature of Buddha-dharmas are without difference.'"

They are distinct, yet definitively non-dual. Furthermore, the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* says: "The Buddha-dharma and worldly dharmas—if one perceives their reality, there is no difference between them at all.
The Master said: "What you have cited, Venerable One, is indeed well-founded within the gate of faith in the teachings.

Listen as I, this old monk, clarify for you the illusory meaning within the teachings. If a person perceives that illusion is fundamentally real, this is what is called [the realization of suchness]."
One who sees the Buddha perceives that all dharmas are perfectly interfused and devoid of arising or ceasing. This absence of ceasing and arising is the Buddha-body. The Master of Huayan asked:
"Is space definitively existent, or is it definitively non-existent? The Master said: "It may be called existent, and it may also be called non-existent.
When space is said to exist, it exists only as a provisional existence; when space is said to be non-existent, it is simply the absence of that provisional [designation]."

[The monk] said, "No. [The Master] asked, "Regarding what the Preceptor has said, what scriptural authority is there for it? The Master replied, "Virtuous One, have you not heard that the *Śūraṅgama-sūtra* says:

'The empty space of the ten directions arises within your own mind, like a single speck of cloud appearing in the vast clarity of the sky'? Is this not to say that when empty space arises, it merely gives rise to a provisional name? Furthermore, it says:

'If even one person among you awakens to the truth and returns to the source, the ten [directions...]"* *(Note: The provided text fragment ends abruptly with "十", which in this context likely refers to the phrase "the ten directions all become clear," indicating the universal manifestation of reality upon the realization of the fundamental source.)*
When space itself is entirely dissolved and vanishes, is this not the extinction of space? It is merely the extinction of a provisional name.
This is why the old monk says: existence is provisional existence; non-existence is provisional non-existence.
Question: "What is Mañjuśrī? The Master said: "Walls, fences, tiles, and pebbles are. Question: "What is Avalokiteśvara?
The Master said: "Sounds and speech are. Question: "What is Samantabhadra? The Master said: "The minds of sentient beings are.

Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "The physical bodies of sentient beings are. Question: "Since the essence of all Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges is identical, for what reason..."
There are various names for them. The Master said: "Returning to the source from the eye-faculty is named Mañjuśrī; returning to the source from the ear-faculty is named Avalokiteśvara;
returning to the source from the mind is named Samantabhadra. Mañjuśrī is the Buddha’s wondrous discerning wisdom (*pratyavekṣaṇājñāna*);
Avalokiteśvara is the Buddha’s unconditional great compassion; Samantabhadra is the Buddha’s unconditioned wondrous practice. These three sages are the Buddha’s wondrous functions."

The Buddha is the true essence of the three sages. In terms of function, there are as many provisional names as there are grains of sand in the Ganges; in terms of essence, they are collectively named as one Bhagavān.
Haoyue asked for instruction, saying, "Have the good spiritual friends of the world yet realized the nirvāṇa of the three virtues? The Master said, "Great..."
De asked about nirvana in the state of fruition and nirvana within the causal stage. [The Master] said, "I shall answer regarding nirvana in the state of fruition.

The Master said, "The good spiritual friends of the world have not yet realized it. He asked, "Why have they not yet realized it? The Master said, "Their merit has not yet equalled that of the various sages. He asked, "..."

[The questioner] asked: "If one's merit has not yet equaled that of the various sages, how can they be called a *kalyāṇamitra* (spiritual friend)? The Master said: "One who clearly perceives the Buddha-nature may also be called a *kalyāṇamitra*.
[The questioner] asked: "I do not yet understand: to what level of attainment must one's merit equal that of, so as to be named a realization of Great Nirvāṇa? The Master presented this verse:
The Great Prajñā illuminates; it is the liberation of the most profound Dharma. The Dharma-body is the essence of quiescence; the three are one, their principle perfect and eternal.

If you wish to know where their merit is equal, this is called the Constant Quiescent Light (Nitya-śānta-prabhā). [The student] asked: "The Nirvāṇa of the three virtues on the level of fruition has already been explained to me.
What, then, is Nirvāṇa within the causal stage? The Master said: "It is you, Venerable One."
First: The Master had long relied upon Nanquan. He composed a verse on his realization, saying: "Today I return home and enter the great gate;
Nanquan’s direct path pervades heaven and earth. Every dharma is clearly the patriarch; Turning my head, I am ashamed—what fine descendants! Nanquan replied:
"Today, do not discuss the matter of this realization. Nanquan does not say it pervades heaven and earth. Returning home is entirely..."
"The affairs of sons and grandsons: from of old, the grandfather has never gone out the door.
When Master Zhuyan of Ezhou ascended the hall, he held up a piece of bamboo and said, "Is there anyone who can drive a stake into empty space? At that time, there was...
The senior monk Lingxu stepped forth from the assembly and said, "Empty space is the stake. The Master struck him. Lingxu said, "Do not strike me in error.
The Master then descended from his seat.
Chan Master Zilong Lizon of Zihu Rock addressed the assembly:
"All dharmas are vast and open; what fetters them, what binds them? It is you yourselves who within this give rise to notions of difficulty and ease.
The source of the mind is a single unity, extending throughout the ten directions. Those of the highest capacity naturally understand this. From antiquity until now, it has never been otherwise."
Suppose an ordinary person or a sage were to appear before you; yet not a single word—whether good or evil—would reach your own domain.
Why is this? Because when there is goodness, goodness has no form; when there is evil, evil has no characteristic.

Since the self (*ātman*) does not exist, with what would you distinguish good from evil, or establish who is an ordinary person and who is a sage? Do you believe this? Will you take responsibility for it?
What place is there to evade? It is just like trying to flee from one’s shadow at midday; can you really escape it? If it is so now, it was so in the past;
when the present and the ancient coincide, can you still deny it? The Buddha-dharma is profound and subtle; those who realize it will naturally spur themselves on.
Do not concern yourself with petty conditions, for they obstruct the Great Matter. Have you not seen it said: "It would be better..."
Laws are established for a lifetime; who can suddenly forget their conditions? Do you, O benevolent one, wish to realize Zen? Each of you go back and look beneath your robes and bowls.
A monk asked, "What is the Great Perfect Mirror? The Master said, "Nothing can adhere to it. The monk pressed further, "Why is that?"
"No thing at all can adhere to you. The Master said: "You are all things; can anything, in turn, adhere to you? The Master [the monk] said:
"A worthy one is fundamentally complete and fundamentally fully equipped. Only when not even a speck of dharma obstructs the light of your eyes can it be so.
If there is even a speck of something that is not exhausted, it will not be until another lifetime or half an eon before it ceases to deceive your skin."

Nang! Within the dharmas of your own life-force, faculties, and objects, you have conjured various demons. Mountain spirits and ghostly apparitions have taken possession of you as you practice, and you consider a mere trifle to be sufficient.
You flatter yourself with this fragmentary skin, yet you instead inflict poison upon the Buddha-dharma. You deride the veneration of stupas and temples and destroy those who uphold the sutras;
thus you become a worm within the lion’s body, devouring the very flesh of that lion.
The Master said, "O benevolent one, do you not see that within this great void before your eyes, there is not even a hair’s breadth of deficiency?

If you can realize this message within it, you will be able to transcend the realms of both ordinary beings and sages, and you will fully comprehend the wisdom of both the mundane and the supramundane.
If one dharma is thus, so too are all dharmas. Benevolent one, do you find joy in this?"

Addressing the assembly: From the heavens above to the human realm, throughout the cycle of the six paths, even down to the most minute insects and sentient beings—none have ever been at variance with this single portion of True Suchness (*tathatā*). Do you believe this? Can you truly receive it?
Generally speaking, when traveling on pilgrimage, one must possess great roots of faith and act as a true man before success can be achieved. Where could such a thing be found?
It is difficult to believe. Those ancients saw only that "this very mind is Buddha" and "this very mind is Dharma," and they accepted it with faith.
They dwelt in thatched huts and stone chambers wherever they were, nurturing the holy embryo until the fruit of the Way was matured. Why do you not now emulate their practice?
O Benevolent One, this is exceedingly clear and free from any admixture; it is no different from managing one's livelihood and engaging in productive industry.
The various true marks do not contradict one another.

Zen Master Xianchan of Vulture Peak asked Master Mingshui, "What is the sudden attainment of the Dharma-body? The Master replied, "Once you have passed through the Dragon Gate, you are beyond the clouds."
Wang said, "Do not become a fish that strikes its forehead against the Yellow River.
Yangshan asked, "When all is silent and wordless, how can there be seeing and hearing? The Master said, "Before the seamless pagoda, rainwater abounds."
Master Daemao of Silla ascended the hall and said:

"If you wish to recognize the Teacher of all Buddhas, recognize him within the mind of ignorance. If you wish to recognize the eternally abiding, unfading nature, recognize it in the midst of the shifting and changing of the myriad things."
Master Zhilin of Hunan used to scold Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra, calling them both malevolent spirits. Holding a wooden sword, he claimed to be subduing demons.
As soon as he saw a monk coming to visit him for instruction, he would say, "The demon has come! The demon has come! and brandish his sword wildly before returning to his quarters. It was like this.
This was twelve years later. [The Master] then set down his sword and remained silent. A monk asked, "Why did you subdue the demons twelve years ago?
The Master said, "Thieves do not strike the homes of the poor. The monk asked, "Why did you not subdue the demons after twelve years?
The Master said, "Thieves do not strike the homes of the poor."

When Chan Master Linjì Yìxuán was hoeing the ground, he saw Huángbò approaching; he stood leaning on his hoe. Huángbò asked, "Is this fellow exhausted? The Master said, "..."
"Before the pickaxe has even been raised, what is there to be exhausted? Baizhang struck him. The Master caught the staff and gave it a shove, knocking Baizhang down.

While the Master was planting pine trees, Huangbo said, "What is the purpose of planting so many pines in the deep mountains?

The Master replied, "First, to provide a scenic setting for the mountain gate; second, to serve as a landmark for future generations. Having said this, he struck the ground three times with his mattock.
[The Master] struck [Huangbo] three times. Huangbo said, "Even so, you have already received thirty blows from me.
The Master struck him again three times and sighed. Huangbo said, "When my school reaches you, it will flourish greatly in the world."
The Master arrived at Cuifeng. Cuifeng asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "I have come from Huangbo.
Cuifeng said, "What words or phrases did Huangbo use to instruct people? The Master said, "Huangbo had no words or phrases. Cuifeng said, "Why is that?
The Master said, "Even if he had them, there would be no place to bring them up. Cuifeng said, "Just bring them up and see. The Master said, "A single arrow passes beyond the Western Heaven."
The Master gave a small-scale discourse, saying: "There are times when the person is taken away but the environment is not; there are times when the environment is taken away but the person is not;

there are times when both person and environment are taken away; and there are times when neither person nor environment is taken away. Kefu asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not the environment'?
The Master said, "The warm sun brings forth life, spreading a carpet of brocade; the infant’s hair hangs down, white as silk. Fú.
[Daowu] asked: "What is 'seizing the environment but not seizing the person'? The Master said: "The imperial decree has been issued and spread throughout the world;

the general is beyond the frontier, where smoke and dust have ceased. [Daowu] asked: "What is 'seizing both the person and the environment'? The Master said: "Communication is cut off between Bingzhou and Fenzhou."
He dwelt alone in a certain place. Fu asked, "What is it like for one who is 'neither taken nor left' by both man and environment? The Master said, "The King ascends the jeweled throne;
the village elder sings his song."
A monk asked, "What are the true Buddha, the true Dharma, and the true Way? We beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "The Buddha is the purity of the mind.
The Dharma is the luminosity of the mind. The Way is the pure light that is unimpeded everywhere.

[There was] an interruption. Since Master Bodhidharma came from the Western Land, he sought only a person who would not be deluded by others.
Later, upon meeting the Second Patriarch, [Bodhidharma] was resolved in a single word; only then did he realize that all his previous efforts had been in vain.

The Master frequently used the shout (*he*) in response to the occasion. The disciples under his guidance also learned to shout like their teacher.
The Master said, "You all imitate my shouting. Now I ask you: suppose one person comes out from the East Hall and another comes out from the West Hall—[the two of them...]"
The assembly shouted in unison. "Can you distinguish guest from host here? How would you go about making that distinction?
If you cannot distinguish them, do not imitate the old monk’s shout in the future."
The Master said: "I, this mountain monk, have not a single dharma to give to anyone; I do nothing but treat illnesses and untie bonds.
Rather than taking the words from my mouth, it would be better for you to rest and remain free from affairs."
The Master said: "You need only enter everywhere—into the mundane and the subtle, into defilement and purity, into the lands of all Buddhas, into Maitreya’s pavilion, and into the world of Vairocana.
In every place, you will manifest the formation, abiding, destruction, and emptiness of lands;
the appearance of Buddhas in the world, their turning of the Great Dharma Wheel, and their entry into nirvana without remainder. You shall not perceive any signs of coming or going."
Mao sought the life and death [of phenomena], but finding them utterly unobtainable, he entered the realm of non-arising dharmas (*anutpattika-dharmadhātu*).
He traveled through various lands and entered the Flower Treasury World (*Kusumatalagarbha-lokadhātu*), where he saw that all dharmas are entirely true and are all the true mark (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*).
The Master said: "If a single thought of love arises in your mind, you are drowned by water; if a single thought of anger arises, you are burned by fire;
if a single thought of doubt arises, you are obstructed by earth; if a single thought of joy arises, you are blown away by wind. If you can discern things in this way,"
Not turned by external objects, one employs objects everywhere: the east surges while the west subsides; the south surges while the north subsides;
the center surges while the periphery subsides; the periphery surges while the center subsides. Treading on water as if on land; treading on land as if on water. Why is this so?

It is because one has realized that the four great elements are like dreams and like illusions. O Dharma-stream! You who are now listening to the Dharma are not these four great elements; it is you who can employ them.
Regarding your four great elements (*mahābhūta*): if you can see them in this way, then you will attain freedom in going and staying.
From my own perspective as a mountain monk, there is no dharma to be rejected. If you loathe the ordinary and crave the holy, you will be bound by the realms of the holy and the ordinary.
There is a class of students who seek for Mañjuśrī to appear at Mount Wutai; they have already made a mistake. Mañjuśrī does not exist on Mount Wutai. If you wish to recognize him—
Mañjuśrī! That which you employ right before your eyes is from beginning to end no different; it is unimpeded everywhere. This is the living Mañjuśrī.
The non-discriminating light of your single thought-moment is, in every place, entirely Samantabhadra.
Your single thought-moment is able to be sovereign, attaining liberation wherever you are; this is the samādhi-dharma of Avalokiteśvara. These manifest as mutual lords and attendants.

When they manifest, they manifest all at once; when they are hidden, they are hidden all at once. One is three, and three is one. Only when you understand it in this way can you truly begin to contemplate the teachings.
When Chan Master Jia Shan Shanhui was first serving as the head cook at Mount Gui, Guishan asked him, "What vegetables are we eating today? The Master replied, "Two years under the same spring.
Guishan said, "Attend well to your duties. The Master said, "The dragon dwells in the phoenix’s nest."
A monk asked, "Regarding the ancestral intent and the doctrinal intent established by the predecessors, why does the Master, on the contrary, say they do not exist?

The Master said, "For three years I have not eaten a meal; yet before my eyes, there is no hungry person. The monk said, "Since there is no hungry person, why is it that I have not attained awakening?

The Master said, "Precisely because of 'awakening,' you, O Kalyāṇamitra, have become deluded. He then presented this verse: "Clearly, there is no dharma of awakening; there is nothing at all to be realized."
Awakening to the Dharma yet deluding people; stretching out both legs and sleeping. Without falsehood and without truth. Question:
When the ancients spread their hair to cover the mud, what was the purpose? The Master said: "The nine suns have been shot down, yet one film still remains.
One arrow falls to the ground, and the world is plunged into darkness."
A monk asked, "What is the realm of Jia Shan? The Master said, "A monkey carries its young back into the green peaks;

Ascending the hall, he said: "The golden crow and the jade hare vie with one another for brilliance. When the sun is sat upon, the world falls into darkness.

The sun and moon are not sufficient for illumination; heaven and earth are not sufficient for greatness. No axe is wielded in the void; the skillful craftsman leaves no trace.

Straw sandals: it is better not to wear them at all than to wear them;

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Since the time of the Patriarchs, people have misunderstood; this has been handed down to the present day such that the words and phrases of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are taken as models for teachers and disciples.

You must seek a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) across thousands of miles, and you must possess the correct eye to seek liberation from erroneous views.

You must definitively examine the birth and death before your eyes: is it truly existent, or is it truly non-existent? If there is someone who can definitively attain this, I grant you permission to emerge [from the depths].

Those of superior capacity realize the Way upon hearing a single word; those of middling and inferior capacities wander like waves upon waves. Why not decisively take hold of it within birth and death?

Where else could you harbor doubts about the Buddhas and Patriarchs to substitute for your own birth and death? A person of wisdom would laugh at you. If you do not understand, listen once more to this verse:
Toiling to uphold the laws of birth and death, You seek only from the side of the Buddha. [The eyes]... (Note: The final character "目" [mù] appears to be a fragment or an incomplete line.)
Previously, being deluded regarding the correct principle, one denied fire while seeking bubbles in it.

One day, Chan Master Toudi Datong was traveling when he encountered Venerable Zhaozhou at Tongcheng County; the Master also came out from the mountains, and they met on the road. Thereupon, [Venerable Zhaozhou] went forward to meet him.
He asked, "Are you not the Master of Mount Touzi? The Master said, "Give me some money for tea and salt.
The Governor first returned to his hut and sat down; the Master later returned carrying a bottle of oil.

The Governor said, "I have long admired the Master of Touzi, yet upon arriving, I see only an oil-seller. The Master said, "You recognize only the oil-seller; you do not yet know the Master of Touzi."
Zhaozhou asked, "What is Touzi? The Master picked up an oil jar and said, "Oil! Oil! During tea service, the Master personally passed a fried cake to Zhaozhou, but Zhaozhou paid no attention.
The Master then ordered an attendant to pass the fried cake; Zhaozhou then prostrated three times to the attendant.
Zhaozhou asked, "What is it like when one who has undergone the great death returns to life? The Master said, "Night travel is not permitted;
you must arrive by the light of day. Zhaozhou said, "I was already waiting for the white; he is now waiting for the black."
Xuefeng arrived. The Master pointed to a flat stone in front of the hermitage and said to Xuefeng, "All Buddhas of the three periods of time are entirely contained within this.
Xuefeng said, "One must know that there is something which is not contained within this. The Master said, "An unglazed wooden bucket!
Later, while the Master and Xuefeng were traveling to Longmian, there were two paths. Xuefeng asked, "Which one is the road to Longmian? The Master pointed with his staff.
Feng said, "Go east; go west. The Master said, "A lacquer bucket that is not yet dry. He asked, "What is it like when one succeeds with a single blow?
The Master said, "Not a man of impatient temperament. He asked, "What is it like when one does not rely on a single blow? The Master said, "A lacquer bucket that is not yet dry.
Feng asked, "Is there anyone here who can administer ginseng? The Master threw his hoe toward Feng’s face.
Feng said, "If that is so, then I shall dig right here. The Master said, "You are a clumsy fellow.
As Feng was taking his leave, the Master saw him out the door and called out, "Dharma-candidate! Feng turned his head and responded, "Yes? The Master said, "Be well on your way."
A monk asked Zhaozhou, "Does a newborn infant possess the six consciousnesses? Zhaozhou said, "It is like hitting a ball on a swift current.
Later, a monk asked the Master, "What is the meaning of 'hitting a ball on a swift current'? The Master said, "Thought after thought, there is no lingering."
A monk asked the Master, "What is the Ten-Body Tamer? The Master descended from his meditation seat and stood there. The monk asked again, "How far apart are the ordinary person and the sage?
The Master likewise descended from his meditation seat and stood there.
Question: "Water is uniformly water; why is the sea salty and rivers fresh? The Master said: "Stars in the sky; trees on the earth.
While the Master was in the capital attending a lay patron’s vegetarian feast, the patron brought out a tray of grass. The Master clenched both hands and placed them upon his head.
The patron then proceeded to serve the meal. Later, a monk asked: "What was the underlying meaning of the Master placing his hands on his head when he attended the feast in the capital?"
"How is it? The Master said, "Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
He asked, "Since you, Reverend, have resided on this mountain, what kind of realization (境界) do you possess? The Master said, "A woman with bifurcated feet has white hair."
A monk asked, "What is it like when not a single thought arises? The Master said, "What could you possibly do? The monk was speechless. The Master spoke again:
"Having burst through the Dragon Gate, clouds and rain merge; mountains, rivers, and the great earth leave no trace."
When Chan Master Zunling of Qingping Anle first visited Cuiwei, he asked, "What is the very meaning of the coming from the West? Cuiwei said, "Wait until there is no one here, and I will tell you.
After a long while, the Master said, "There is no one. Please, Reverend, speak. Cuiwei stepped down from his meditation seat.
The Master was led into the Bamboo Garden. The Master said again, "There is no one here; I pray the Abbot will speak.
Cuiwei pointed to the bamboo and said, "This stalk is so long; that stalk is so short. The Master acknowledged this with gratitude.
A monk asked, "What is the Mahāyāna? The Master said, "A well-rope. The monk asked, "What is the Hīnayāna? The Master said, "A string of coins.
The monk asked, "What is 'with outflows' (sāsrava)? The Master said, "A bamboo sieve. The monk asked, "What is 'without outflows' (anāsrava)? The Master said, "A wooden ladle."
Question: "What is the家风 (family style) of the Qingping lineage? The Master said: "A measure of flour makes three steamed cakes.

The Master visited Mount Gui and asked, "Recently I heard the story of National Teacher Huizhong of Nanyang regarding 'insentient beings preaching the Dharma,' yet I have not yet fathomed its subtlety.
Mount Gui said, "I have it here as well; it is simply that such a person is rarely encountered. The Master said:
“I do not yet understand. I beg the Master for instruction. Miaoyan held up his whisk and asked, “Do you understand?
The Master said, “I do not understand. I request the Venerable One to explain it. Miaoyan said, “The mouth born of one’s parents will never speak for you, my son.

However, thirty *li* from here in You County, Liling, there is a man of the Way named Yunyan. If you can part the weeds and gaze at the wind, he will surely be someone you can honor. The Master [departed].
He then took his leave of Guishan and went directly to Yunyan. He asked, "Who can hear the Dharma preached by the insentient?
Yunyan said, "The insentient can hear it. The Master asked, "Does the Master hear it as well? Yunyan said, "If I were to hear it, you would not be hearing my preaching of the Dharma.
The Master asked, "Why is it that I do not hear it? Yunyan held up his whisk and said, "Do you see this?"
“Do you hear it? the Master asked. The Master said, “I do not hear it. Yan said, “If you cannot even hear me preaching the Dharma, how much less can you hear the insentient preaching the Dharma?
The Master asked, “In which scriptures is the insentient preaching the Dharma contained? Yan said, “Have you not seen that the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* says:
‘The waterfowl and the trees all recite the Buddha’s name and the Dharma’? At this, the Master attained realization and composed a verse, saying:
"How truly marvelous! How truly marvelous! The insentient preaching the Dharma is inconceivable. If one listens with the ears, it will ultimately be difficult to understand;
only when hearing sound through the faculty of sight can one truly know. Yuan said, "Dharma Master Jia, in taking up this matter, you must be extremely careful and discerning."
The Master was still harboring doubts. Later, while crossing a stream, he beheld his reflection and attained great enlightenment regarding the former principle.
He composed a verse, saying: "By all means, do not seek it from others; To do so would distance you from me. I now go forth alone, And everywhere I encounter him.
He is precisely myself at this moment, Yet I am not him. One must understand it in this way Before one can realize Suchness."

Within this there is a path separated from dust; if one can simply avoid touching the taboos of the present age, it is superior to the talent of those who had their tongues cut off in a former dynasty.

In the "Simultaneous Middle" (jiānzhōng zhì): When two blades cross in combat, there is no need to avoid them; a skilled hand is like a lotus in the fire, possessing naturally a will that soars toward the heavens.
In the "Arrival in the Simultaneous Middle" (jiānzhōng dào): Not falling into existence or non-existence, who would dare to harmonize with it? Everyone desires to transcend the ordinary.

if you do not save it, its form and shadow will not be revealed."
A monk asked, "Master, you usually teach students to practice the 'bird-path. I do not yet understand what this bird-path is.
The Master said, "Not meeting a single person. The monk asked, "How does one walk it? The Master said, "You must simply proceed with no self-interest beneath your feet.
The monk asked, "If one is walking the bird-path, is that not one's original face? The Master said, "Disciple, why are you so upside-down? The monk asked, "..."

[The student] asked, "What is the original face? The Master said, "Do not tread the path of birds."
The Master said: "People of these times who study the Way merely recognize that which precedes the donkey and follows the horse, taking this to be themselves.
That the Buddha-dharma has sunk into oblivion is precisely because of this. They have not yet distinguished the host within the guest; how then can they discern the host within the host?"
A monk asked, "What is the master among masters? The Master said, "You, Reverend, should speak for yourself. The monk said, "If I were to speak, that would be the master among guests.
What then is the master among masters? The Master said, "To speak thus is easy; to maintain continuity is very difficult. He then presented this verse:
"Alas, I see the practitioners of the Way nowadays, Countless thousands and tens of thousands, all merely recognizing the gate."
[The Master] said, "It is just like entering the capital to pay court to the Sovereign; as soon as one reaches Tongguan Pass, one stops.
A monk asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come to roam the mountains. The Master said, "Have you reached the summit? He replied, "I have.

The Master said, "Is there anyone at the summit? He replied, "There is no one. The Master said, "If that is so, then you have not reached the summit. He replied, "If I had not reached it," [the Master would have been wrong].
Ding said, "How can you know there is no one? The Master said, "Why do you not stay for a while? Ding said, "I am not unwilling to stay;
it is that someone in India does not approve. The Master said, "I have always suspected this fellow."
A monk asked, "What is the father of the green mountains and white clouds? The Master said, "That which is not dense and dark.
The monk asked, "What is the child of the white clouds and green mountains? The Master said, "That which cannot distinguish east from west.

The monk asked, "What is it that the white clouds lean upon all day long? The Master said, "They cannot depart from it. The monk asked, "What is it that the green mountains do not know at all? The Master said, "..."
"One who does not look back is such a person.
Once, when the Master and Yunju were crossing water, the Master asked, "How deep is the water? Yunju replied, "It does not wet me. The Master said, "You coarse fellow!"
Jiue asked, "How deep is the water? The Master said, "It does not dry up.

The meaning does not reside in the words; the arriving impulse also responds. To move is to form a habitual trap; to falter is to fall into hesitation.
Both "avoidance" and "contact" are incorrect, like a great mass of fire. Merely manifesting patterns and colors belongs to defilement. At midnight, there is perfect clarity; the heavens—
Dawn does not manifest; it serves as a model for all things, employing means to uproot all suffering. Although it is not conditioned (*saṃskṛta*), it is not without expression.
It is like facing a precious mirror, where form and reflection behold one another. You are not that [mirror], yet that [mirror] is precisely you.
Like an infant of the world, complete with the five marks, neither going nor coming, neither arising nor abiding—serene and harmonious, with phrases both existent and non-existent. At last...

when the transformations are exhausted, they become five. It is like the taste of the *zhí-cǎo* plant, like a vajra-staff: the center is perfectly correct while the sides subtly assist it. Striking and singing are raised together; it penetrates both the source and the path.
It carries along and encompasses the way; if one acts with such precision, there will be good fortune. One must not offend or oppose it. It is spontaneously true and wondrous. Not... [text ends]

With stillness on the outside and agitation within, it is like tethering a foal or subduing a rat. Out of compassion for this, the former sages established the *dāna-pāramitā* (perfection of giving) for the sake of the Dharma;
they sought to align with the ancient tracks. Please observe the ancients: when the Buddha’s Way was about to be perfected, he gazed at the tree for ten kalpas. As...

Because there is the startling and the extraordinary, the wildcat and the ox, the wooden man sings and the stone woman dances. This is not reached by consciousness or intellect; how could it admit of thought or deliberation?
As a minister serves his sovereign and a son obeys his father—to not obey is not filiality, and to not serve is not to be a loyal assistant. Its hidden movement and subtle function are like...
"Fools are as dull as the state of Lu; they can only continue on, which is called being the 'Lord of Lords. The Master further said:
In the age of the Final Dharma, many people possess only dry wisdom (*śuṣka-prajñā*). If one wishes to verify what is true and what is false, there are three kinds of leakage:
first, the leakage of views, wherein the faculty does not leave its station and falls into a sea of poison; second, the leakage of emotion."

They stagnate in orientation and opposition; their perspectives are partial and withered. Third is the leakage of speech: they investigate the subtle while losing the source, and their capacity for discernment is obscured regarding the beginning and the end.
Turbid wisdom revolves within these three types; you should understand this.
The verse says: "The Way has no mind with which to unite the person; The person has no mind with which to unite the Way. If you wish to understand the meaning herein, One is old, and one is not old.
—Master Guangyong of Nanta, Yangshan.
The Master received the tonsure under Yangshan. He traveled north to pay his respects to Linji, then returned to serve Yangshan. Yangshan asked, "What have you come for?
The Master replied, "To pay my respects to the Master. Yangshan asked, "Have you seen the Master? The Master replied, "I have. Yangshan said:
"The Master, how are you like a donkey? The Master said, "When I see the Master, I do not find you to be like a Buddha either.

Mount said, "If you are not like a Buddha, what are you like? The Master said, "If there were something I was like, how would that differ from being like a donkey? Mount was greatly startled and said:
"Ordinary and sage are both forgotten; when emotion is exhausted, the essence is revealed. For twenty years I have tested people by this standard, yet none have reached a definitive realization.
You must take responsibility for him. Every time Shanshan pointed to him and said to others, "This man is a Buddha in his physical body."

When Chan Master Shuangfeng Gu of Fuzhou was about to take his leave of Shishuang, Shishuang took up his whisk and followed him out to the entrance of the gate. He called out, "Attendant Gu! The Master turned his head.
Shishuang said, "To conceive of it is already a deviation; to grasp at it is to go astray. Do not conceive of it, do not be it, and do not even act as if there were nothing."
"One who understands. If one does not know that there is [this], one cannot know it. Go well! Go well! The Master responded with two "Nohs.
Later, a monk asked, "When you took your leave of Shishuang at that time, what was the meaning of Shishuang speaking thus?
The Master said, "He simply taught me not to cling to right and wrong."
Zen Master Huien of Sanseion ascended the hall and said:
"Whenever I meet someone, I come forward; yet when I come forward, I do not do so for others. He then descended from his seat.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master replied, "Stinking meat attracts flies."
After Chan Master Zhixian of Guankui resided at Mount Mo, he ascended the hall and said: "At my grandfather Linji’s place, I received half a ladle;
at my grandmother Mount Mo’s place, I received half a ladle. Together they made one full ladle which I have consumed, and until this very day, I remain full and never hungry."
A monk asked, "I have long heard of Guankui; having arrived here, I see only the hemp-soaking pool. The Master said, "You see only the hemp-soaking pool;
you do not yet see Guankui. The monk asked, "What is Guankui? The Master said, "As swift as a splitting arrow."

A monk asked Chan Master Jiufeng Daogyan, “What kind of practice does one who acts within the Uninterrupted [Hell] perform? The Master said, “The practice of a beast. The monk asked, “And what practice does a beast perform?
The Master said, “The practice of the Uninterrupted. The monk said, “This is still someone on the road of long life. The Master said, “You—”

"You must know that there is a life which is not shared," he said. [The student] asked, "What kind of life is it that is not shared? The Master said, "The vital breath of the long-lived is not permanent.
The Master then said, "Brothers, do you recognize this life? If you wish to know life: flowing springs are life; profound stillness is the body.
The surging of a thousand waves is the realm of Mañjuśrī; the vast expanse of the clear sky is the couch of Samantabhadra."
Next, as for borrowing a single phrase, it is like pointing at the moon while speaking of the moon.

For instance, before the former worthies of all quarters had established so many names and designations to point things out, what standard or framework did you brothers use to deliberate? When you arrive here—
It does not depend on three inches; try to speak and see. It does not depend on the ears; try to listen and see. It does not depend on the eyes;
try to discern and see. Therefore it is said: "Before the sound, nothing can be cast out; after the phrase, no form is hidden.
The entire universe and great earth are all the very body of you, the person here and now. Where, then, can you place your eyes, ears, nose, and tongue? Do not merely [seek them]...
The faculty of mind (manas) is difficult to fathom; even until the end of the future, there will never be a moment of rest. Therefore, Dongshan said:
"To attempt to study the profound mystery with the mind and intellect is much like heading west while facing east. Be careful.
Chan Master Jingxin of Yongquan in Taizhou ascended the hall and said:
"In my forty-nine years here, I have still occasionally made mistakes. You people must not open your mouths too wide.
Those with intellectual understanding are many; those with both realization and practice are not one in ten thousand. Intellectual understanding is merely words."
In short, you must know the principle of penetration. If your consciousness is not fully exhausted, I dare say you will remain in saṃsāra.

Why is this so? It is because the outflows of consciousness have not been eliminated. You need only exhaust them in the present moment, and only then can you achieve realization; this is also called "attaining merit within the midst of establishment."
He turns his merit over to him; this is also called "merit within the midst. He personally goes toward him. This is why I say: "The person cannot be saved by another;
he himself does not save the person who approaches him. Even with such a metaphor, you still do not understand how to take it up.
You merely manage your own nature while your tongue flutters about in confusion. Have you not seen Dongshan say: "Continuity is also very difficult"?
When Chan Master Yuan’an of Luopu arrived at Jiashan, he did not prostrate;
instead, he stood facing him with his hands joined at his chest. Jiashan said, "A rooster nesting in a phoenix’s nest."
"You are not of my kind; get out! The Master said, "I have come from afar to seek your teaching; I request that you grant me an audience. Mount San said, "Before my eyes there is no disciple;
here there is no old monk. The Master then gave a shout. Mount San said, "Stop! Stop! Do not be so hasty and reckless.
The clouds and moon are the same, yet the streams and mountains differ. To cut off the tongues of all people under heaven is certainly possible, O Disciple..."
Lí asked, "How can one teach a tongueless person to speak? The Master hesitated for a moment, and Shàn struck him. From this, Lí took heart and submitted himself to his teaching.
One day, he asked Shàn, "How does one realize the place where neither Buddha nor demons reach? Shàn said, "A candle illuminates the image for a thousand li."
The old monk in the dark room was deluded. Again he asked, "When the morning sun has already risen and the night moon no longer appears, what then?
Sansheng said, "A dragon carries a pearl in its mouth; the swimming fish do not look back. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
As Sansheng was about to pass away, he uttered a final remark, saying, "The branch of Stonehead—look, it is about to perish! The Master said, "Not so. Sansheng asked, "Why? The Master said:
"His own home has its own green mountains. Shanshan said, "If it is truly so, then our school will not fall into decline.
He ascended the hall and said: "The final phrase reaches the secure barrier; it locks off the vital passageway, allowing neither ordinary people nor sages to pass."
Ordinarily, I tell people: "Let everyone under heaven rejoice as they please; I alone am unwilling.

If you wish to know what it means to be a superior man of the highest stream, he does not paste the words and teachings of the Buddhas and Patriarchs upon his forehead, like a tortoise bearing a map that portends its own death, or a phoenix entangled in a golden net, wondering when it might soar into the clouds and mists. One must directly clarify the essence beyond the literal meaning.
Do not seek the standard within words. Therefore, even a stone man whose mechanism resembles yours can sing the *bāgē*;
if you were like that stone man, you would surely respond to the *xuěqǔ*. As for the single path pointed out by the guide, the wise know it to be remote.
He asked the monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Jingnan. The Master said, "There is a person who goes in such a manner;
do you encounter him? The monk said, "I do not encounter him. The Master said, "Why do you not encounter him? The monk said, "If I were to encounter him, my head would shatter into pieces.
The Master said, "Your three-inch tongue is very well-guarded. Later, when Yunmen saw this monk in Jiangxi, he asked, "Did you have these words? The monk said, "Yes."
[The Master] said, "It is so. The Gatekeeper said, "Luopu retreats three thousand li.
Chan Master Yantou Quanhuo addressed the assembly:
"Simply clarify the fundamental principle; fundamentally, there is no substantial dharma. Have you not heard it said: 'Neither real nor unreal'? If you turn toward...
When attending to the Master, look directly; if you search within the faculty of thought, you will ultimately fail to grasp it.
It is also said: "This is the livelihood of those who transcend the ordinary; it merely reveals a tiny fragment before one's eyes, like a flash of lightning or a spark struck from stone.
It cuts off both extremes, being luminously free. If you say there is a dharma or a matter 'above,' you are truly sounding a hollow bowl. *Tuō*.
"Smearing you. Binding and confining you. The ancients called this the 'donkey-tethering stake. If one were to give actual Dharma to others, even the earth could not contain it.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "Now, regarding matters within the great fundamental principles and the essential source, one must recognize the 'phrase' (jù). If one does not recognize the phrase, it will be difficult to become a person [of realization]."
A discourse on the phrase. What is a phrase? When there is no thought of anything at all, it is called the "correct phrase.
It is also called "abiding on the summit," "attaining stability," "vivid clarity," "alertness," "precise certainty," and "the time before the Buddha was born."
It is also called "attaining the ground," and it is also called "at such a time. By means of "such a time," one equally shatters all right and wrong.
As soon as it is thus, it is no longer thus; it turns and rolls about. One does not see the ancient saying: "Sinking into obscurity is not good."
It must be turned before it can be attained; as soon as one touches it, it turns. This phrase is cut away, and that which is not a phrase is also cut away.

It turns spontaneously and effortlessly; it is naturally revealed nakedly before one’s eyes, full and snoring with contentment. One does not seek to understand it back, nor does one seek to bite into it.
The slightest stir of emotion has already fallen to the ground. If you have not yet attained this, then wandering about in such a state is called "practicing according to the words.
As soon as there is something [to grasp], it must be shattered. At such a time, not a single thing remains.
You should know that all the phrases you have studied from the past are cramped within your chest; what use are they? Have you not heard it said: "Observe the exclusion"?
A word of exclusion: do not let anything enter from without, and do not let anything go out from within. Cut off both ends, and naturally there will be a state of luminous clarity.
Not being in opposition to a single thing—this is the Samādhi of Non-contention. Brothers, if you wish to understand easily, simply seek it clearly at the very root.
It is said: "Without dependence, without desire—this is the Capable One (Śākyamuni). An ancient said: "Set it aside."
Poisonous medicine placed within milk—even down to the clarified butter (*sarpis*)—can likewise kill a person. This is not something you can acquire through study;
this is not something you can control by coming or going; it is not something contained within your physical form.

Do not mistake the gateways and doorways, for they will deceive you on the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month, leaving you in a state of frantic turmoil to no avail. Thus one truly knows the ancient style.
Excellent! Have you not heard it said: "Existence is non-existence; non-existence is existence"? When such a thing is brought forth, one immediately knows its depth or shallowness.
This is the ancient style. Among those people, there are some who simply vomit it out with blind conviction; what inscriptions or records do they have?
They know nothing but to call it "Chan" or "the Way," and they know nothing but to call it a "single phrase"—how soft and weak they are!
"Di! This is truly a solid iron mallet without a hole. Even if you were to collect ten thousand of them, what use would they be?
If you have true backbone and strength, you need not have many; as you travel on pilgrimage to various places, you must also bring your eyes with you so as not to be deceived by others."
If one does not see the Way and instead gives rise to understanding based on the Dharma, one still falls into the realm of Māra.
Now, when preaching the teachings, one must be able to bring each and every word forth from within one's own breast to serve as a model for others. Is there such a person today?

Do not spend your entire day in a state of restless clamor; there will be no end to it. If you wish to understand this easily, simply know that before sounds and forms, you are not deluded or disturbed by the myriad objects of experience.
Then, naturally, you are revealed in your nakedness; naturally, you are without affairs.
Sent into the midst of sounds and forms, you remain vast and open, just like a single mass of flame that burns at the slightest touch. What more could there be?
Matter. Not seeing the Way, it is not that dust does not intrude; it is simply that I am without mind. It is hot now. Take care.
Chan Master Xuefeng Yicun’s monk asked West Mountain Wanshan: “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Wanshan raised his whisk and showed it to him.
The monk was unwilling to comply. Later, he went to visit the Master. The Master asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Zhejiang. The Master said, "Where were you this summer?
He replied, "At West Mountain in Suzhou. The Master said, "How is the Abbot there? He replied, "When I arrived, he was in full health. The Master said, "Why did you not remain there at ease?
He replied, "I do not understand the Buddha-dharma. The Master said, "What is the matter? The monk related [the incident].
[The Master] spoke of the previous conversation. The Master said, "Why do you not accept him? [The monk] said, "Because he is an object.

The Master said, "Do you see the men and women in the households of Suzhou? [The monk] said, "I see them. The Master said, "Do you see the trees and forests along the road? [The monk] said, "I see them. The Master said, "..."
"Whenever you see men and women in a household, the great earth, forests, and ponds—all these are objects. Are you willing to accept them? The monk said, "I am willing.
The Master said, "As for picking up the whisk—how is it that you are not willing? The monk then prostrated and said, "This student has spoken thoughtlessly;
I beg the Master’s compassion. The Master said, "The entire universe is a single eye. Where do you turn?"
The Master was squatting in a corner. The monks made no response.
The Three Sages asked, "What does the golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net eat? The Master said, "Wait until it comes out of the net, and I will tell you.
The Sages said, "A teacher of fifteen hundred people, and yet you do not even recognize the 'head-word' (hua-tou). The Master said, "I am but an old monk."
The abbot’s duties were many and busy.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Mount Huai. The Master said, "What words or phrases did Mount Huai have for you?
The monk said, "I once asked him, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? and Mount Huai remained seated upon his chair. The Master said, "Do you approve of him?"
"No. The monk said, "I do not agree with him. The Master said, "Tianhuai Shan was an ancient Buddha; you should go quickly and repent. He asked another monk, "Where are you going?
The monk replied, "If you recognize it, you will know where I am going. The Master said, "You are one who understands the matter."
[The Master] said, "Why are you running about in such disorder? He replied, "Venerable Sir, please do not defame others. The Master said, "I am certainly not defaming you.

But tell me, how was it that the ancients blew on the cloth-hair? Come, speak for me and see. He replied, "Leftover soup and rancid rice have already been eaten by someone else. The Master then withdrew.
Xuansha asked the Master, "I am now putting my great function into operation; how do you, Reverend, respond?

The Master simultaneously threw out three wooden balls. Xuansha made a gesture as if striking a shield. The Master said, "Only because you have been personally present at Vulture Peak can you act in this way.
Xuansha said, "This, too, is one's own affair."
While on communal work, the Master encountered a macaque on the road. He said, "Every person possesses a mirror of antiquity;
this macaque also possesses a mirror of antiquity. Sansheng said, "For vast eons it has been nameless; how can it be manifested as a 'mirror of antiquity'?"
The Master said, "A flaw has arisen. Xuedou said, "What such desperate haste is this old fellow! He does not even recognize the head of the phrase.
The Master said, "This old monk’s duties as abbot are many."

A monk asked, "What is it like when the cold spring flows in the ancient ravine? The Master said, "Staring with wide eyes, one cannot see the bottom. The monk asked, "And what of those who drink from it?
The Master said, "It does not enter through the mouth. The monk reported this to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou said, "'It does not enter through the mouth'—then can it not enter through the nostrils?
The monk then asked Zhaozhou, "What is it like when the cold spring flows in the ancient ravine? Zhaozhou said, "Bitter. The monk asked, "And what of those who drink from it?"
"How is it? Zhaozhou replied, "Dead. When the Master heard this, he said, "Zhaozhou is an ancient Buddha," and prostrated himself from afar.
From that time on, he no longer answered questions.
One day, while the Master was burning a fire inside the Sangha Hall, he closed both the front and back doors and cried out, "Help! Put out the fire! Help!
Put out the fire! Xuansha took a piece of firewood and threw it through the lattice window; the Master immediately opened the door.
Ascending the hall, [Zhaozhou] said: "On South Mountain there is a tortoise-nosed snake; you all must look at it very carefully.
Changqing came forward and said, "Today in this hall, many will lose their lives. Yunmen then thrust his staff toward the Master and made a gesture of fear.
A monk reported this to Xuansha. Xuansha said, "It takes an elder brother like Ling to do that. Although...
"However, it is so. I, however, am not like that. The King asked, "How do you do it, Preceptor? The Master said, "What use is Mount Nanshan?
The King of Min asked, "If I wish to build a Buddha hall, what should I do?
The Master said, "Great King, why not build a Hall of the Empty King instead? The King said, "Please give me a model, Preceptor. The Master extended both hands.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The entire great earth is gathered up and made as small as a grain of millet. I toss it before you; yet you, you lacquer buckets, do not understand.
I beat the drum and invite everyone to look!"
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "This matter is like a single field of land; it is left entirely to all of you to plow and sow.
There is no one who does not receive the power of this grace. Xuansha asked, "And what, pray tell, is this field? The Master said, "Look!
Xuansha said, "It is indeed so, yet I do not see it that way. The Master asked, "How then do you see it? Xuansha said, "Just..."

"This belongs to ordinary people. He ascended the hall and, raising his whisk, said: "This one is for those of middle and lower capacity. A monk asked, "How about when a person of the highest rank among the high comes?
The Master raised his whisk. The monk said, "This one is for those of middle and lower capacity. The Master then struck him.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Venerable elders, I have already met you at Wangzhou Pavilion;
I have already met you at Wushan Ridge; I have already met you before the Sangha Hall."

A monk asked Master Caoshan Benji, "Is it not the case that a śramaṇa is a person who possesses great compassion? The Master said, "Yes. The monk said, "What should one do when the six thieves encounter him?
The Master said, "One must likewise possess great compassion. The monk asked, "How does one possess great compassion?"
[Baoche] said, "With one stroke of the sword, it is all exhausted. [The monk] asked, "After it is exhausted, what then? The Master said, "Only then does harmony prevail.
[The monk] asked, "Do the eyebrows and eyes recognize each other or not? The Master said, "They do not recognize each other. [The monk] asked, "Why do they not recognize each other?
The Master said, "Because they reside in the same place. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then they are not distinct from one another. The Master said, "As for the eyebrows..."
"It is not the eyes. The monk asked, "What are the eyes? The Master said, "Go straight ahead. The monk asked, "What are the eyebrows? The Master said, [as before].
Caoshan, however, remained doubtful. [The Master] asked, "Why, Preceptor, do you remain doubtful? The Master said, "If you did not doubt, you would have attained the definitive truth."
Yunmen asked, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa? The Master said, "Those who eat the crops belonging to the monastery.
[Yunmen] asked, "What is it like when one proceeds in this very way? The Master said, "Are you able to maintain it? [Yunmen] said, "I am able to maintain it. The Master said, "How do you maintain it?
[Yunmen] said, "What difficulty is there in wearing robes and eating food? The Master said, "Why do you not say, 'Wearing fur and carrying horns'?"
At the corner of the gate, he paid his respects.
The Master asked Elder De, "When the Bodhisattva was in meditative absorption and heard the fragrant elephant crossing the river, from which sutra did this emerge?

He replied, "It emerges from the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*. The Master said, "Did he hear it before the absorption, or did he hear it after the absorption? He replied, "It is the flow of the Master. The Master said, "It is the Way."
“Too much talk! You have only spoken half of it. The monk asked, “How about you, Master? The Master said, “Receive it at the bottom of the rapids.
The Master asked a monk, “What are you doing? The monk replied, “Sweeping the floor. The Master said, “Are you sweeping before the Buddha or behind the Buddha?
The monk replied, “I sweep both front and back at once. The Master said, “Bring me my sandals to pass over to Cao Shan.”
A monk asked, "What kind of companion can one have so as to always hear what has not yet been heard? The Master said, "Sharing the same single blanket. The monk said, "This is still merely 'hearing.
What is it to 'always hear what has not yet been heard'? The Master said, "Being no different from wood or stone.
The monk asked, "Which comes first? Which comes after? The Master said, "Have you not heard it said: 'Always hearing what has not yet been heard'?"
A monk asked, "When a single ox drinks water and five horses do not neigh, what then? The Master said, "Caoshan knows how to avoid the taste.
When the practitioner Zhiyi came to pay his respects, the Master asked, "Are you not the practitioner Zhiyi? The practitioner replied, "I dare not say so.
The Master asked, "What is the matter beneath the paper robe? The practitioner said, "Once the single fur robe is hung upon the body, all myriad dharmas are entirely as they are."
The Master said, "What is the function beneath the paper robe? The student stepped forward, responded with an assent, and then immediately stood there as if shedding his skin.
The Master said, "You only know how to go like that; why do you not know how to come like this?

The student suddenly opened his eyes and asked, "When the singular, numinous true nature does not rely upon the womb, what then? The Master said, "That is not yet wondrous. The student asked, "What is wondrous? The Master—
He said, "Not-borrowed borrowing: cherish it and you will immediately transform. The Master presented this verse: "The nature of awakening is perfectly luminous, a formless body;
Do not falsely judge its intimacy through intellectual views. When thoughts differ, the profound essence becomes obscured; When the mind deviates, it does not dwell as a neighbor to the Way.

Emotional attachments cause the myriad dharmas to sink into external objects; Discriminating consciousness, with its many ends, loses the original truth. Within such words, there is total [completeness]."
Xiaohui was clearly enlightened and realized that there was nothing from the time before.
The Master asked Senior Monk Qiang, "The Buddha’s true Dharma-body is like empty space; it manifests forms in response to things, like the moon reflected in water.
How do you explain this principle of 'responding'? He replied, "It is like a donkey looking down a well. The Master said, "If you speak thus..."
"Too extreme! You have only managed to express eighty percent of it. The student asked, "How about you, Master? The Master said, "It is like looking at a donkey from inside a well.
The Master then read the Dharmakāya verses composed by Du Shun and Fu Dashi, saying, "In my view, I do not wish to speak of it in such a way."
His disciples requested that he compose another [work]. Having composed the verse, he further provided a commentary upon it.
The words are as follows: He is fundamentally not I (not *ātman*); I am fundamentally not he (not *sa*). Without him, I would perish (I rely on you for my life);

Without me, he would be nothing else (there is no other). If he were like me, he would be a Buddha (yet, in truth, he is not a Buddha); If I were like him, I would be a donkey (neither can be established). [This] does not eat.
The salary of the Empty King (if you encounter imperial food, you must spit it out). Why borrow a wild goose to deliver a letter (do not communicate)?

I speak of singing with a horizontal body (singing for the sake of the message). Look at the feathers on its back (not like yours). It is just like chanting the "White Snow" (thinking it is the "White Snow").
Yet I fear it might be a "Ba Song" (this line has no commentary).
Chan Master Yunju Daoying went to visit Dongshan.
Dongshan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "I have come from Cuiwei. Dongshan asked, "What words or phrases did Cuiwei use to instruct his disciples?
The Master said, "Cuiwei makes offerings to the Arhats. I asked him, 'Why do you make offerings to the Arhats? The Arhat... [text continues]
“Will Han return? Weiming said, “What have you been eating every day? Shan said, “Is this truly what you said? The Master replied, “It is.
Shan said, “Then you have not come in vain to visit a master. Shan asked, “What is your name? The Master replied, “...”
Daoying. Shanshan said, "Speak further beyond this. The Master said, "Beyond this, it is no longer called Daoying.
Shanshan said, "This is exactly the same as the words you spoke in response to Daowu. He deeply agreed with this. One day, Shanshan asked the Master, "Where have you come from?
The Master said, "I have come from treading the mountains. Shanshan said, "Which mountain is fit to dwell upon? The Master said, "Which mountain is not?"
"Can you abide? Mount said, "If that is so, then the entire country has been occupied by you, Master.
The Master said, "Not so. Mount said, "If that is so, then you have found a way of entry. The Master said, "There is no way.
Mount said, "If there is no way, how did you manage to meet with me, old monk? The Master said, "If there were a way, I would already be separated from the Master by a mountain. Mount said, "..."
"This child will later go away such that thousands and tens of thousands cannot hold him back.
A monk asked, "From what do the mountains, rivers, and the great earth arise? The Master said, "They arise from deluded thoughts.
The monk said, "Can you produce a bar of gold for me from my thoughts? The Master then ceased speaking. The monk did not accept this.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "In the Buddha-dharma, what complicated matters are there? Practice it and that is it. Simply know that the mind is the Buddha; do not worry that the Buddha cannot understand your speech.
If you wish to attain such a state, you must first become such a person. From antiquity, the virtuous predecessors have been pure and simple, acting in accordance with reality;
they were fundamentally without artifice. Even if someone were to ask, 'What is the Way? they would sometimes answer, 'A tile or a brick.'"
"What is the use of wooden things? They are all heavy. Originally, his foundation is solid and possesses great strength;

he is an inconceivable person who can grasp soil and turn it into gold. If one lacks such a capacity, even if you speak with the elegance of clustered flowers and brocade patterns, people will find it utterly unacceptable and will not believe or accept it at all. Originally, one's own foundation is empty and void.
Power. When members of the Sangha speak or breathe forth words, there must be a source for them; do not treat them with casual indifference.
If even a single word deviates from the truth, it will lead one ten thousand miles away. Those who truly know this understand how to guard and cherish their speech;

they never act recklessly. Of every ten utterances, they cease nine times. Why is this so? It is because they constantly fear that their words may lack benefit, wishing instead to attain such [a state].
As for this matter, it requires such a person. Since one is already such a person, there is no need to worry about such matters; yet such matters are difficult to encounter.
The Master said: "Even if you were to master the affairs on the Buddha’s side, you would already have misapplied your mind. Have you not seen..."
The ancients spoke of "heavenly flowers falling" and "stones nodding their heads," yet even this did not concern one's own affairs.
Now, you propose to employ your finite body and mind within the infinite; what connection can there be? Have you not seen the ancients say:
"If the place of study is not profound, it is entirely mundane. If one cannot let go of the things of the inner chamber, they all become leaks. One must simply..."
Coming here and taking it away; going and coming—only when all such activities are brought to an end is one finally free from fault.
Thus the ancients said: "It is like two mirrors facing each other; their radiance reflects one another, and there is neither deficiency nor excess."
Is it not the case that even this is still called a matter on the periphery of reflections? When the sun rises and its light illuminates the world, the clarity is one half;

what do you call that other half? Nowadays, people have not yet recognized even the coarse and shallow matters at the gate and threshold of light and shadow, yet they presume them to be the affairs within the house—how could that possibly suffice?

Question: Why is it that those who descend from heaven are immediately poor? Answer: Because they do not value what they have obtained. Question again:
Why is it that those who spring forth from the earth are wealthy and noble? Answer: Because there is something within the midst of nothingness.
Chan Master Shushan Kuangren ascended the hall and said:
"Before the Xiantong era, this sick monk understood the matter of the Dharma-body; after the Xiantong era, I understood the matter that transcends the Dharma-body.
Yunmen stepped forward and asked, "What is the matter of the Dharma-body? The Master replied, "A withered stump."
[The student] asked: "What is the matter that lies beyond the Dharma-body? The Master said: "It is not a withered stump. [The student] asked:
"Do you permit me to speak of the underlying principle? The Master said: "I do. [The student] asked: "Is a withered stump not, after all, a manifestation of the Dharma-body? The Master said: "It is."
[The Master] said, “It is. [The monk] asked, “Is it not the case that a withered stump is precisely the manifestation of the Dharma-body’s transcendent reality?
The Master said, “It is. [The monk] asked, “Does the Dharma-body encompass all things or not? The Master said, “The Dharma-body is all-pervasive; how could it not encompass them?
The monk pointed to a water jar and asked, “Does this water jar encompass the Dharma-body? The Master said, “Disciple, do not look for it in the water jar.”
He was searching at the edge of the gate when he suddenly prostrated himself.
The Master habitually held a wooden snake. A monk asked, "What is that in your hand, Master? The Master raised it and said, "A daughter of the Cao family."
A monk asked Chan Master Dunru of Baima in Luojing, "What is the matter that lies beyond the Dharma-body? The Master said, "A frog at the bottom of the well swallows the moon."
Chan Master Juedun Zhengkong of Longya Mountain had a verse that said:
"Studying the Way is like drilling for fire: When smoke appears, you must not yet stop. Only when the golden star manifests Will you have finally reached home."
Question: "How should one exert effort throughout the twelve periods of the day? The Master said: "It is like a person without hands who wishes to throw a punch;
only then can it be done. Question: "What did the ancients realize that they were able to rest? The Master said: "It is like a thief entering an empty house."
Question: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "Wait until the stone tortoise learns to speak, and then I will tell you.
[The monk] said: "The stone tortoise speaks! The Master said: "What would you have me say to you?"
The Master, the Chan Monk Xiange of Jingzhao Prefecture, had no fixed dwelling.
Having received the seal of mind from Dongshan, he lived among the common people in Minchuan. Throughout both winter and summer, he wore only a single robe;
each day he would gather shrimp and clams along the riverbanks to fill his belly, and at dusk he would stay overnight at Mount Dongbai.

Among the paper money at the Temple of the Horse, the local residents called him "The Shrimp Monk. When Chan Master Jing of Huayan heard of this, he wished to determine whether the man was genuine or not.
He first hid himself within the paper money. At the dead of night, the master returned; Jing seized him, saying, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The master immediately replied, "The wine table and dishes before the deity. Jing let go of him and said, "Not so."
Xu Yu was born from the same root as myself.
Master Qianfeng of Yuezhou ascended the hall and said:
"The Dharma-body has three kinds of illnesses and two kinds of lights; you must penetrate each one thoroughly before you can truly return."

He sat firmly in his place. You must know that there is yet another "upper opening" beyond this. Yunmen came forward and asked, "Why does the person inside the hermitage not know what is outside the hermitage?
The Master laughed heartily. Yunmen said, "This is still where the student has doubts."
The Master said, "What kind of mental activity do you have? Dongshan said, "I also wish for the Master to understand me. The Master said, "You must be thus;
only then will you be able to sit securely. Dongshan responded, "Yes, yes."
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "If you raise one, you must not raise two; to let pass one point is to fall into the second.

Yunmen stepped forward from the assembly and said, "Yesterday someone came from Tiantai and went on to Jingshan. The Master said, "The head cook shall not be required to work in the communal labor tomorrow," and then he descended from his seat.
Question: "The Bhagavāns of the ten directions all share one path to the gate of nirvāṇa. I do not yet know where the beginning of that path lies.
The Master drew a line with his staff and said: "It is right here."

He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Tiantai. The Master said, "I hear it is said that the Stone Bridge has been broken into two pieces—is this true? The monk replied, "Yes."
"From where did the Master receive this news? The Teacher said, "I took you for a visitor from the peak of Mount Huading;
it turns out you are a man from the village of Pingtian."
Chan Master Huiqing of Bajiao Mountain ascended the hall.
Holding up his staff, he showed it to the assembly, saying: "If you have a staff, I give you a staff;
if you have no staff, I take your staff away. He leaned on the staff and descended from the seat. — Tian Tong Zheng.
Jue said: "If you have it, then everything has it; if you lack it, then everything lacks it.
Whether there is or is not is simply a matter of the person’s own bestowing or withholding. What does this have to do with the banana tree? At such a time as this, what is your staff?"
Chan Master Huìyǒng of Nanyuan ascended the hall and said:

"People everywhere possess only the eye for the simultaneous moment of the chick pecking and the hen hatching, but they do not possess the function of the simultaneous moment of the chick pecking and the hen hatching.

A monk then asked: "What is the function of the simultaneous moment of the chick pecking and the hen hatching? The Master said: "An adept does not wait for the pecking; it is the simultaneous moment of the pecking and the hatching."
"Lost. The monk said, "This is still not where I was asking. The Master asked, "How is it at the place where you were asking?
