The monk said, "Lost. The Master then struck him. That monk did not accept this. Later, while under the assembly of Yunmen, he heard two monks raise this same story.
A monk asked, "At that time, why did Nan-yuan break his staff? Suddenly, the monk attained enlightenment.
Later, Chan Master Shiyan of Ruiyan in Taizhou resided at Ruiyan in Danqiu;
he sat upon a flat rock all day long as if he were a fool, constantly calling out to himself, "The Host."
He replied, "Understood. Then he said, "Stay alert! Hereafter, do not let others deceive you. Later, a monk visited Xuansha.
Xuansha asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "Ruiguan. Xuansha said, "What words did he give to his disciples? The monk recounted the previous conversation.
Xuansha remarked, "It is all the same—playing with the vital spirit—but it is truly extraordinary."
Jingqing asked, "Heaven cannot cover him; earth cannot support him. Is this not so? The Master said, "If it were so, he would be covered and supported.
Jingqing said, "If it were not so, how many times would Ruiyan have suffered [for his errors]? The Master referred to himself by name, saying, "Shiyan."
Chan Master Xuefeng Yicun of Shifeng ascended the hall and said:
"To understand this matter, it is like an ancient mirror set upon its stand: when a barbarian comes, a barbarian appears; when a Han Chinese comes, a Han Chinese appears.
Master Xuansha Shibei Zongyi stepped forward from the assembly and asked, "What happens when a bright mirror itself comes? Xuefeng replied, "Both barbarians and Han Chinese [appear]."
Yin. The Master said, "The old monk’s heels have not yet touched the ground.
One day, Xuefeng pointed to a fire and said, "The Buddhas of the three periods turn the Great Dharma Wheel within this flame.
The Master said, "Lately, the royal decree has become somewhat strict. Xuefeng asked, "How so? The Master said, "No one is permitted to encroach upon or seize the marketplace."
While attending Xuefeng as they were walking in the mountains, Xuefeng pointed to the ground before him and said, "On this patch of earth, one could build a seamless stupa.
The Master asked, "How high would it be? Xuefeng looked up and down. The Master said, "The blessings and rewards of gods and humans are certainly not lacking for you, Master;
however, as for the prophecy at Vulture Peak, you have not even dreamed of it. Xuefeng asked, "And what about you?"
[Sheng] said, “Seven feet or eight feet.
The Master said, “A world is one foot wide; an ancient mirror is one foot wide. A world is ten feet wide; an ancient mirror is ten feet wide.
The Master pointed to the brazier and asked, “How wide is this brazier? Xuefeng said, “As wide as an ancient mirror. The Master [nodded].
He said: "The Old Monk has not yet even touched the ground.
Once, while walking alongside Xuefeng through a bamboo fence, the Master asked, "Is there Buddha-dharma within this bamboo fence? Xuefeng replied, "There is."
The Master asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma at the place where the bamboo fence is? Feng shook the fence once. The Master said, "I do not say it is so.
Feng asked, "How would you put it, my son? The Master said, "It passes right through the ends of the bamboo strips."
A monk asked, "What is the student's own self? The Master said, "What use is there for your own self?
Gushan came forward; the Master drew a circle and showed it to him. Gushan stepped out and said, "Everyone cannot get out of this.
The Master said, "I knew you would be making your living in the womb of a donkey or a horse. Gushan asked, "And what about you, Master?"
[The Master] said, "Everyone is unable to produce this. Shan said, "The Master is able to speak thus;
why am I unable to speak it? The Master said, "I am able; you are not."
While the Master was engaged in tea conversation with Military Commissioner Wei, the Commissioner said, "The speech of the people of Jambudvīpa is already somewhat difficult to discern;
how much more so is the Sanskrit of the Five Indias? Is there anyone who can distinguish it? The Master lifted up his tea bowl and said, "If you recognize this, you will have distinguished it."
While they were working together to chop firewood, they saw a tiger. Tiantong said, "Master, it is a tiger. The Master replied, "It is you who are the tiger.
After returning to the monastery, Tiantong asked, "When you saw the tiger just now, you said, 'It is you. I do not understand what you meant by this. The Master said:
In the Sahā world, there are four kinds of most heavy matters. If a person can penetrate them, they will be able to transcend the realms of the aggregates.
The Master asked Jingqing, "The scriptures say that not seeing a single dharma constitutes a great calamity. Tell me, what dharma do you not see?
Jingqing pointed to a pillar and said, "Is it not this dharma that you do not see? The Master said, "That is just clear water in Zhejiang."
"You may eat white rice from me, but you have not even dreamed of the Buddha-dharma.
A monk asked, "I have heard the Master say that the entire world of the ten directions is a single bright pearl.
How can a student understand this? The Master said, "The entire world of the ten directions is a single bright pearl. What is there to understand? The monk...
He then desisted. The next day, the Master again questioned that monk: "The entire world of the ten directions is a single bright pearl;
how do you understand this? The monk said, "The entire world of the ten directions is a single bright pearl; what need is there to understand it?
The Master said, "I know you are making your living inside a ghost cave."
The Master said: "If one discusses this matter, it is like a plot of land whose boundaries on all four sides have been demarcated and sold to others;
only the tree in the center still belongs to me."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddha-way is vast and open; it has no fixed path. It is the gate of liberation that has no gate, the intent of the Way-man that has no intent.

It does not abide within the three periods of time, and thus it cannot be subject to rising or sinking. To establish it is to deviate from the Truth; it does not belong to the realm of conditioned creation.

To move is to give rise to the root of birth and death; to be still is to be intoxicated in the land of dullness and stupor. When both movement and stillness are extinguished together, one falls into emptiness."
Gone. Both movement and stillness are gathered together; the vast and open Buddha-nature must, when facing objects and conditions, be like withered wood or cold ashes.

When applied according to the occasion, its appropriateness is never lost. The Way is fundamentally suchness; it is naturally so, true as it is, and not something to be attained through cultivation or realization.

It simply requires being free from distraction and not obscuring one's functioning; as long as one does not involve oneself in the mire of worldly dust, even a hair’s breadth of it cannot be fully described—otherwise, one becomes a follower of the Demon King.

Even if you attain a state like the moon’s reflection in an autumn pond or the sound of a bell in a still night, which remains unimpaired by striking and does not dissipate when touching the waves, this is still merely a matter on the shore of birth and death. This is the realm where the Path-walker dwells.
Like fire melting ice, it never returns to become ice again. Once an arrow has left the bowstring, it has no power to return.
Therefore, they refuse to dwell within the cage and do not turn their heads when called. When one reaches this point, every step ascends the profound;

it belongs neither to the heterodox nor the orthodox. Consciousness cannot perceive it, and wisdom cannot know it. The paths of speech are cut off, and the movements of the mind are extinguished. One attains direct liberation.
Kāśyapa remained silent in Rājagṛha; Vimalakīrti was speechless in Vaiśālī. If it is thus, what further matter could there be to doubt before one’s very eyes?
Having no place of rest, transcending the past, present, and future, and not being produced by adornment—it is primordially true and pure.
Even if a thousand sages were to appear, they could not place a single word upon it. Long time has stood; take care.

Addressing the assembly: Now, the true teaching of the ancient Buddhas constantly manifests in accordance with things. Its majestic application shines radiantly everywhere; its appearance and disappearance are equanimous, illuminating all heights and depths.
Therefore, for the superior śramaṇa, the eye of the Way must take precedence. Only by realizing the fundamental and clarifying the mind can one reach the ultimate.
The myriad phenomena in their dense array share a single source and are of one essence; they are vast and boundless—who could speak of existence?
Obstructions. Events from kalpas ago are all present before one's eyes. Because people of today are distanced by time and separated by years, they deviate from the constant essence.
With deluded minds, they recognize external objects and turn their backs on the True Source; clinging to existence or stagnating in emptiness, they completely form conceptual constructs.

An ancient worthy said: "If the mind retains the measure of the holy, one still falls into the dust of dharmas. If one’s own views are not yet forgotten, it results in further leakage. One must not say that this refers to observing the fasts...

Observing the precepts, sitting upright without lying down, dwelling the mind in contemplation of emptiness, and concentrating the spirit to enter meditative absorption—when you do these things, you shall depart [from this world].
What connection does this have [to liberation]? Even the non-Buddhist practitioners of the Western Heavens can enter the eighty-thousand-eon samādhi, yet they cannot avoid the cycle of saṃsāra.
This is because their vision of the Way is not clear and they have not severed the root-source of birth and death. Right now, where is there that is not you? Where is there that is not...?
It is clear. Where is it not manifest? Why do you not understand it in this way? If you lack this ground, how can you deal with the various leaks during your daily life?
It all becomes empty delusion. Which of these is the place where you have gained strength throughout your life?
Phenomenal mental dharmas cannot be relied upon; as days and years pass, they provide no benefit at all. Only...
This constitutes a deviation from truth and an abandonment of the fundamental, a state of wearying detachment from ordinary sentiments and a joyful inclination toward the holy path.
To form such views and understandings is to remain within the limitations of others; you have not cast off the five aggregates, nor do you see that "all conditioned phenomena are impermanent;

they are dharmas of arising and ceasing. You merely intend to move forward, but how can you hope to realize it? Only when you have penetrated through to the core will you know it. If you have not yet investigated it thoroughly, [you shall not attain it].
You should know that all of this is empty pretension—a teaching difficult for the world to believe. Only those with great capacity can clearly penetrate it.
If you do not achieve thorough realization in this life, it will remain so for ten thousand kalpas. As the ancient masters said: "One must settle this directly in this very life;
who can endure the remaining retribution through successive kalpas? Be careful.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "I now ask you all: what matter can you take up and bear? In what world do you establish your body and settle your life? Can you discern this?
If you cannot discern it, it is just like pressing on the eyes and seeing flowers—your perception of things is immediately mistaken.
Do you know? Right now, before your very eyes, there are mountains, rivers, the great earth, form and emptiness, light and darkness—all manner of things."
All phenomena are but the illusory appearances of a weary, deluded mind; they are called inverted views. Now, one who leaves the household life recognizes the mind and penetrates its source;
therefore, he is called a śramaṇa. Great man, why do you not examine yourself and observe what this matter truly is?
As for the ancestral vehicle from of old, it is the crown lineage of all Buddhas, transmitted solely through the gate of Kāśyapa.
He suddenly transcended. This one gate transcends the cause and effect of ordinary beings and sages; it transcends the wondrously adorned world-ocean of Vairocana.
Directly beneath you, throughout eternal kalpas, not a single thing has been taught to serve as an object for your eyes to see. Why do you not urgently investigate and realize this for yourself?
I have not yet said that I shall wait for three lifetimes or two lifetimes to accumulate pure karma over a long duration. O worthy one, what is this vehicle of the essential teaching (*zongcheng*)?
What business is it of yours? You cannot attain it by applying effort or adorning yourself; you cannot attain it through the knowledge of others' minds or past lives.
Do you understand? To recognize this is to be one who has achieved great liberation and great penetration.

Therefore, one transcends the ordinary and the holy, emerges from birth and leaves behind death, departs from cause and effect, surpasses Vairocana, and surpasses Śākyamuni, no longer being constrained by the causes and conditions of the ordinary or the holy.
"You have been deceived by the fruits [of your actions]. Nowhere is there anyone who can recognize you. Do you understand? Do not merely remain attached to the net of love within birth and death;
you will be bound and carried away by good and evil karma, leaving you with no freedom.

Even if you were to refine your body and mind until they were as empty as space, even if you reached the state of brilliant clarity and profound stillness, it would still not transcend the *vijñāna-skandha* (the aggregate of consciousness). The ancients called this..."
It is like a rapid torrent; because the current flows so swiftly, one does not perceive it and falsely deems it calm.

To practice in such a manner, one will never be able to transcend the bounds of saṃsāra, and as before, one will continue to be carried away by the cycle of birth and death. Therefore it is said: "All conditioned phenomena are impermanent.
Even the fruits and merits of the Three Vehicles are not ultimate if one lacks the Eye of the Path. How could they compare to the ordinary person of the present day, who requires no [such effort]?
With a single moment of effort, you will suddenly transcend. Do you understand how to save your mental energy? I shall now cause you to grasp it on the spot;
I will not require you to apply further effort or refine your practice. If you do not do so now, when will you ever? [Descend from the seat.]

Ascending the hall, he said: "All of you are like people sitting inside the great ocean; submerged up to your heads and drenched through, you still stretch out your hands and ask others for water to drink.
Now, a Bodhisattva who studies Prajñā must possess a great vessel and have great wisdom before they can succeed.
There are certain masters sitting on their rope-benches who claim to be 'Good Knowledge' (Kalyāṇamitra), yet when questioned, they merely sway their bodies and wave their hands."

He fixes his eyes, sticks out his tongue, and stares. Furthermore, there is another class who speaks of "bright clarity" and "vivid awareness," claiming that the intelligent nature of the spiritual platform (*lingtai*) is capable of seeing and hearing, acting as the sovereign within the field of the five aggregates.

To act as a "good spiritual friend" (*kalyāṇamitra*) in such a manner is to greatly deceive people. Do you know? I now ask you: if you recognize this bright clarity and vivid awareness as your true reality, why...
When you are drowsy, it does not become this "bright and lucid" state. If it were not present when you are drowsy, why would there be this brightness at other times?
Do you understand? This is called "mistaking a thief for one's own son";
it is the root of birth and death, the conditioning energy of deluded thought. Do you wish to know its origin? I shall tell you: this very "bright and lucid" state—only...
It is because of external objects—such as forms, sounds, smells, and other phenomena—that discrimination arises; thus you claim, "This is the luminous and numinous.

If these external objects did not exist, this luminous and numinous nature of yours would be like the hair of a tortoise or the horns of a rabbit. O worthy one, where does true reality actually reside?
If you now wish to find the sovereign master within the field of the five aggregates and the body, you must simply recognize your own [true nature].
The secret vajra-body—ancients have told you this: it is perfectly accomplished and all-pervasive, encompassing the entire dharma-realm. Indeed, the mountains, rivers, and great earth;

the lands of the ten directions; form and emptiness, light and darkness; and even your own body and mind—all these are without exception manifested by the majestic radiance of your perfect accomplishment.
It is precisely through this that the various classes of beings, including devas and humans, perform their karmic actions and undergo their experiences.
The retribution of birth—whether sentient or insentient—is none that does not rely upon your majestic radiance.
Even the Buddhas, from their attainment of the Way and the realization of the fruit, to their reception of beings and benefitting of life, all without exception rely upon your majestic radiance.

Consider this: within the adamantine body, are there ordinary people and Buddhas? Is there the activity of your mind? One cannot say there is not, for if one were to say so, one would immediately fall into error. Do you understand?
Since you possess such a wondrous and extraordinary capacity for manifesting yourself in the presence of reality, why do you not clarify and grasp it?
Why, instead, do you follow others to make your living within the ghost-realm of the field of the five aggregates? You are simply deceiving yourself in this very moment.
If you do not realize this, the causes and conditions of these afflictions and evil karma will not come to rest for one or two kalpas; they will simply continue to pursue you.
"May you live as long as the Vajra-peak.
Do you understand? [The Master] ascends the hall: 'The sun-disk in the great void is that by which all people are established. The great void is present;
how is it that everyone cannot see it before their eyes nor hear it with their ears? If you cannot realize these two points, you are simply dozing.'"
Sleeping man! If you can attain clear penetration, you will sit upon both the ordinary and the holy; you will sit upon the three realms.
Your dream-like body and mind will not contain even so much as the tip of a needle to serve as a condition or an object of opposition.

Even if all the Buddhas were to appear and manifest infinite supernatural powers and transformations, or were to set forth such a vast web of teachings, they would never manage to touch you by even a single hair’s breadth. This only serves to assist the beginner in their sincerity.

This is the gateway of faith. Do you understand? Nowadays, śramaṇas do not realize this matter; instead, they become people who merely dally with shadows, floating and sinking within the ocean of birth and death.
When will they find rest? If you wish for clear penetration, then right here and now, you shall attain clear penetration.
I do not instruct you to grasp even a single dharma as large as a mote of dust, nor do I instruct you to abandon even a single dharma.
"Is it like even a hair’s breadth? Do you understand yet?
The Master said, "It is because these people perceive danger and evil;
they see tigers, swords, and blades threatening their very lives, and thus give rise to boundless fear. What is this like? It is exactly like a worldly painter. He himself—
When one paints a depiction of the transformations of hell and completes the images of tigers, knives, and swords, upon looking at them closely, one naturally feels fear and dread.
You people here are just like this: you perceive all manner of things as existing, yet these are merely illusions produced by yourselves;
you feel fear and dread within yourselves, and it is not anyone else who has done you wrong. Do you now wish to awaken from this delusive illusion?
Simply recognize your own adamantine eye. If you recognize it, I have never taught you that there is even a speck of dust that can manifest.
Where else would there be tigers, wolves, knives, or swords to intimidate and terrify you?
Therefore, I told you: "The eye of the śramaṇa holds fast the world; it encompasses heaven and earth without leaking so much as a hair's breadth. Where else could there be [anything more]?
"One thing is for you to know and see. Do you know it? Why do you not urgently investigate and grasp it?
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "The World-Honored One said: 'I possess the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, which I entrust to Mahākāśyapa.'"
"It is like painting the moon. Caoxi [Huiming] held up his whisk; it was like pointing at the moon. At that time, Master Gushan stepped forward from the assembly and asked, "Where is the moon?
The Master replied, "This fellow is seeking the moon from me. Gushan did not approve; he returned to the assembly and said, "I am telling you that he is seeking the moon from me."
The Master propped his staff against the ground and asked Changsheng, "What is the monastic view? What is the worldly view? What is the male view?
What is the female view? How do you see them? Changsheng replied, "Does the Master also see my clear vision? The Master said, "Familiar faces fill the world."
The Master was eating fruit with Inspector Wei. Wei asked, "What is it that the common people use every day yet do not know?
The Master picked up a piece of fruit and said, "Eat. After Wei had finished eating the fruit, he asked again. The Master said, "This very thing is what they use every day yet do not know."
A monk asked, "I am a student who has newly entered the monastery; I beg the Master to point out a path for me to enter.
The Master said, "Do you hear the sound of the Yan River water? He replied, "I hear it. The Master said, "Enter from here."
Cen Master Baofu Congzhan was asked by Changqing, "When you see form, you see the mind; do you also see the boatman? The Master said, "I see him.
Changqing said, "Setting aside the boatman for a moment, what is the mind? The Master then pointed to the boatman.
The Master saw a monk and struck a pillar with his staff; he then struck the monk on the head. The monk made a sound of pain.
The Master said, "Why does that one not feel pain? The monk was speechless.
The Master, while standing with his attendant monks, asked one of them, "How can you be so careless? The monk said, "In what way am I careless?
The Master picked up a clod of earth, handed it to the monk, and said, "Throw this out in front of the gate.
After the monk had thrown it, he returned and asked, "In what way was I careless? The Master said, "I saw you bumping into things and striking against them."
[The Master] said, "Therefore I say your mind is coarse.
One night, Chan Master Lingzhao Zhenjue of Longhua pointed to a crescent moon and asked the Elder Pu, "Where has that piece gone? Pu—
[The Master] said, "Do not engage in false conceptualization. The Teacher said, "You have lost a piece.
Cuiyan instructed [his disciples] to study with Chan Master Yongming.
He ascended the hall and said: "For an entire summer, I have been talking here and there with you, my brothers. Look: are Cuiyan’s eyebrows still there? Yuan.
Wuqin said: "Many people misunderstand this. To say that under the bright sun and clear sky one speaks words that have no point of reference is to create trouble where there is none.
At the end of summer, he first spoke of his own failings and first conducted his own inspection, so as to avoid having others inspect him.

It is fortunate that there is no connection here. Such a view is called 'extinguishing the lineage of the Hu. Throughout the generations, the ancestral masters appeared in the world [precisely for this reason]."
If one does not bestow this teaching upon others, there is no benefit at all; for what purpose is it drawn?
Only when one sees through to this point can one understand that the ancients possessed the skillful means to "drive away the plowman’s ox" and "snatch the food from the hungry man.
Nowadays, when people are questioned, they merely chew on words and phrases, making their livelihood out of the eyebrows. Look instead at those who are true masters within the house.
"Spontaneously one knows the place where others tread. Xuedou’s verse says: "For a thousand ages there has been no match.
He simply asked, "Look! Are the eyebrows of Cuiyan still there? What is so extraordinary about this that it remains unmatched for a thousand ages?
You must know that when the ancients brought forth even a single word or half-sentence, it was not done in haste; they surely possessed the eye that can settle heaven and earth.

Only then can it be attained. Xuedou’s utterance of a single word or half-phrase is like the Vajra King’s precious sword, like a lion crouching on its haunches, like sparks struck from flint, and like a flash of lightning.
Were it not for those who possess the eye at the crown of their heads, how could they perceive where these ancients have landed?
This address to the assembly is such that it remains without peer for a thousand ages; it surpasses Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout.
"Ho! Tell me, where does the intent of Cuiyan and Xuedou lie? Look quickly with your eyes! Jingqing said:
When Chan Master Tufun Shunde was on a communal work assignment, Xuefeng raised the case of Baizhang Huaihai saying, 'When you see form, you see the mind. Do you say there is a fault in this?"
[The Master] said, "None. The Master asked, "For what reason did the ancients do this? Fēng said, "Even so, I wish to deliberate with you.
The Master said, "In that case, it would be better to say, 'Tóu has gone off to hoe the fields. The Master visited Xuefeng again. Xuefeng asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master said, "From beyond the mountain ridges. Xuefeng asked, "Where did you encounter Bodhidharma? The Master said, "I encountered him even further back."
"Where is it? Feng said, "I do not yet believe you are there. The Master said, "Master, please do not be so sticky.
Feng then desisted.
Later, the Master traveled extensively throughout various regions, further enriching his mastery of expedient wisdom (*upāya-jñāna*).
He went to visit the former Caoshan, who asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "I left Ming-shui yesterday. Caoshan asked, "When did you arrive at Ming-shui?
The Master said, "I arrived when you arrived, Reverend. Caoshan asked, "When do you say I arrived? The Master said, "I still remember it just now. Caoshan [laughed].
He said, "So it is; so it is.
Once, when the Master was questioned by a monk, [the monk] asked, "Is there still Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year? The Master said, "There is.

The monk asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year? The Master said, "The first day of the new year inaugurates the reign; all things are renewed. The monk said, "Thank you for your answer, Master."
The Master said, "Jingqing has lost ground today.
He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk said, "Shiqiao. The Master said, "What is your fundamental matter? The monk said, "I have recently come from Shiqiao.
The Master said, "How is it that I do not know you have recently come from Shiqiao? What is your fundamental matter? The monk said, [silently].
"Master, why do you not acknowledge my words? The Master struck him. The monk said, "My point remains. The Master said, "You simply take this blow;
it is I who wish for these words to circulate."
The Master asked a monk, "What is that sound outside the gate? The monk replied, "The sound of raindrops. The Master said, "Sentient beings are inverted;

deluded about themselves, they pursue external objects. The monk asked, "How about you, Master? The Master said, "I have not, in fact, been deluded about myself. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'not being deluded about oneself'?
The Master said, "To leave one's body may still be easy; to speak from the standpoint of the whole person is difficult."
One day, when the Venerable Fu of Taiyuan visited Xuefeng, the Master pointed at the sun and showed it to him. The Master shook his hand and walked out.
Xuefeng said, "Do you not agree with me? The Master replied, "When the Master shakes his head, I wag my tail. Where is there any disagreement? Xuefeng—
He said, "One must avoid [such talk] wherever one goes. One day, during the evening assembly, Feng was lying in the central courtyard.
The Master said, "Within the jurisdiction of the Five Prefectures, only this old monk is somewhat superior. Feng then rose and left. Feng asked the Master:
"Is it true," he asked, "that Linji spoke of three phrases? The Master said, "Yes. The monk asked, "What is the first phrase?
The Master raised his eyes and looked at him. Feng said, "This is still the second phrase. What is the first phrase? The Master folded his hands and withdrew.
From that time on, Feng held him in deep esteem.
One day, Xuansha went up to inquire after Xuefeng’s health. Xuefeng said, "There is a little mouse here; it is currently in the bathhouse.
Xuansha said, "I shall wait to examine it for you, Master. Having said this, he went to the bathhouse and encountered the Master pouring water.
The monk said, "I am looking at you, Senior. The Master said, "We have already met. The monk said, "In what kalpa did we ever meet?
The Master said, "Why are you so drowsy? The monk then entered the abbot’s quarters. Xuefeng said, "He has already been thoroughly tested."
Feng said, "How would you examine him? Sha recounted the previous story. Feng said, "You have been robbed.
Chan Master Jinpeng Congzhi picked up a pillow, showed it to the monks, and said, "Everyone calls this a pillow; Jinpeng says it is not."
The monk asked, "I do not know, Master; what do you call this? The Master picked up his pillow.
The monk said, "If that is so, then I shall act accordingly. The Master asked, "What do you call it? He replied, "A pillow. The Master said, "It has fallen into the hollow of Jinfeng."
A monk asked, "This body is without consciousness, like earth, wood, tiles, or stones. What do you mean by this? The Master descended from his meditation seat and twisted the monk’s ear.
The monk cried out in pain. The Master said, "Today, for the first time, I have caught hold of this ignorant fellow.
The monk bowed and went out. The Master called out, "Acarya! The monk turned his head. The Master said, "If you go into the hall, you must not mention this."
[The monk] asked, "For what reason? The Master said, "There are many who laugh at Jingu Peak’s grandmotherly heart.
He ascended the hall and said, "In affairs, there is the meeting of the box and its lid; in principle, there is the meeting of arrowheads. Is there anyone who can speak thus?

If there were someone who could speak thus, I would divide half my monastery and give it to him for his residence. At that time, a monk came forward and paid his respects. The Master said, "Mutually..."
"It is easy to see [the truth], but difficult to live with those who claim to be men of realization.
Having said this, he descended from his seat. As the monk was attending him, the Master said, "I shall cite a kōan; you must not misunderstand it in the slightest.

The monk said, "Please, Master, cite it. The Master held up his whisk. After a long silence, the Master said, "I know that you, Dharma brother, have misunderstood. The monk looked at him with his eyes.
Looking toward the east and west, the Master said: "Adding frost upon snow.

Zen Master Fonben Kū of Japan was thirteen years old when he visited Jia Shan. As soon as he entered the gate, he saw the Rector. The Rector said: "In this place, we do not admit those who come behind."
[The Master] arrived. The Teacher said, "I do not seek formal admission as a resident; I have come for a brief visit to pay my respects to the Abbot.

The Rector informed Jia-shan, who granted him an audience. As the Teacher was about to ascend the steps, Jia-shan asked, "Of the three jeweled stairways, by which one do you ascend? The Teacher replied:
"The Threefold Jewel Staircase is designed specifically for this present age. As for the single path leading upward, I request that you, Master, point it out directly.
Yunmen then bowed. The Master then ascended the stairs and prostrated. Yunmen asked, "With whom do you travel, Ācārya? The Master replied, "With Old Man Wood."
Mount said, "Why do you not come to visit this old monk? The Master said, "The Master has his own share of seeing him. Mount asked, "Where is he?
The Master replied, "He is in the hall. Mount then went down with the Master to the hall, whereupon the Master took up his staff.
He threw it before the mountain. The mountain said, "Did you not get it from Tiantai? The Master said, "It was not produced by the Five Peaks.
The mountain said, "Did you not get it from Mount Sumeru? The Master said, "I did not even encounter it in the Moon Palace.
The mountain said, "If that is so, then you got it from a person. The Master said, "Even one's own self is an enemy; what could be made of something got from another?"
Shan said, "A single bean has burst within cold ashes. He then called for the *karmadāna* (rector) and said, "Prepare this under the bright window;
tomorrow there will be a communal work assignment (*pǔqǐng*). The *karmadāna* ordered the Master to deliver tea. The Master said, "I have come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma, not to deliver tea.
The *karmadāna* replied, "I am carrying out the Abbot’s instructions. The Master said, "If it is the Abbot’s honorable command, then so be it," and he took [the tea].

The Master went to the work area and made a sound by shaking his tea bowl. Master Shanzhao turned around. The Master said, "Three or five bowls of strong tea; the intent lies at the edge of the mattock.
Shanzhao said, "The pitcher has the momentum to pour tea; how many bowls are in the basket? The Master said, "The pitcher has the momentum to pour tea;
there is not a single bowl in the basket," and then he served the tea. At that time, the assembly all raised their eyes. The Master said, "Great!"
The assembly of cranes looked on and requested a word from the Master. The Mountain said: "When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it;
carry it home in a bottomless basket. The Master said: "Holding a night-bright talisman in hand, how many know the dawn? The assembly all gazed up in admiration and sighed.
Chan Master Shushan Zheng of Fuzhou went to visit Touzi.
Touzi asked, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "Yanping. Touzi said, "Have you brought the sword with you?
He replied, "I have brought it. Touzi said, "Present it to the old monk for him to see. The Master then pointed to what was before him.
Dizang said, "The ground. Touzi then stopped. When evening came, he asked his attendant, "Is the newcomer still here? The attendant replied, "He left just now.
Touzi said, "For thirty years I have been riding a horse; today I have been thrown by a donkey."
When Master An of Yǐngqiáo Iron Ladle was warming himself by the fire with Minister Zhōng, Zhōng asked, "When the three realms are ablaze, how can one escape?
The Master used the incense spoon to poke at the fire. As Zhōng hesitated, the Master poked the fire again and said, "Minister! Minister! At that moment, Zhōng suddenly attained realization.
Excerpts. When Chan Master Huimin of Tong’an first visited Dongshan, he asked: "By what do all the sages take their life? Dongshan replied: "By non-interruption. The Master...
[Zhaozhou] asked, "Is there anything further above this? Dongshan said, "There is. The Master asked, "What is this matter that is further above?
Dongshan said, "It does not proceed from interruption. Upon these words, the Master attained realization.
A monk asked Master Baoyun Zang, "What is the place of profound depth? The Master said, "A short man crossing a deep stream. The monk asked, "What about when one is barefoot?
The Master said, "Why do you not take them off?"
Chan Master Mingzhao Deqian went to the place of Elder Tan. Tan said, "In studying the Way, one must go to where a whole person is;
one must also go to where half a person is. The Master then asked, "I do not ask about where a whole person is; what is meant by 'half a person'?"
Where is he? Tan remained silent, offering no reply. Later, he ordered a junior monk to question the Master. The Master said, "Do you wish to know where that 'half-person' is?
He is merely a fellow playing with lumps of clay."
Arriving at Yao’s Hermitage, the Master raised his staff and said, "How can you be so shaggy and unkempt?
The hermit said, "Do not mistake the zero point on the scale. The Master said, "Exactly!"
He went to visit Baoning. Meeting him on the road, he asked, "Brother, are you one of my fellow practitioners?
He then pointed to his own nose and said, "This thing is obstructing me; could you remove it for a moment? Baoning replied, "How long has it been since the Master first attained realization?
The Master said, "Alas! You have nearly caused me to wear out a pair of straw sandals. With that, he turned back and departed.

When the Master went to Guo Tai, Nanquan Shen led his assembly out to meet him. Upon reaching the entrance, the Master pointed to the two *Vajrapāṇis* and asked, "What are these two fellows doing here?
Nanquan clenched his fists and assumed the posture of a *Vajrapāṇi*. The Master said, "The Old Man with the Yellow Face in the hall is laughing at you."
While the Master was at Zhaoqing, he was asked to go to the residence of Imperial Preceptor Wang to fetch a wooden Buddha for a communal work assignment (*pǔqǐng*).

The Preceptor then asked the assembly, "What would you do if you suddenly encountered Danxia? The assembly was speechless. At that moment, the Master picked up the statue, held it above his head, and said, "It must also be entrusted to someone."
A monk asked Master Tantang of Rumon, "What is the ground of ultimate reality? The Master said, "Jambudvīpa in the south; Uttarakuru in the north. [The monk] said, "..."
"If it is so, then we are of one family. The Master said, "Mount Sumeru stands between us.
Chan Master Guichen of Luohan Monastery was asked by Xuansha, "The three realms are but mind; how do you understand this? The Master pointed to a chair and said, "Does the Master call this a chair?"
"What is this? [the monk] asked. "It is a chair," he replied. The Master said, "You do not understand that the three realms are mind-only.
"I call this a bamboo-and-wood object; what do you call it? the monk asked. "Guichen also calls it a bamboo-and-wood object," the Master replied.
[Zhaozhou] said, "Throughout the entire earth, one cannot find a single person who understands the Buddha-dharma. From that time on, the Master redoubled his efforts to inspire himself.
While the Master was attending upon Zhaozhou in the abbot’s quarters, they were conversing late into the night. The attendant closed the door, and Zhaozhou said, "The doors are all shut."
[The Master] said, "Understood. How will you get out? The Master asked, "What do you call a door?
He questioned a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the South. The Master asked, "What words did the teachers there use to instruct their disciples?
The monk replied, "They say that although gold dust is precious, it cannot enter the eye. The Master said, "I say that even Mount Sumeru..."
While you were in your own eyes, Baofu’s monk arrived. The Master asked him, "How is the Buddha-dharma there? He replied, "Sometimes he addresses the assembly, saying:
'I block your eyes so that you cannot see; I block your ears so that you cannot hear; I sit upon your [minds]...'"
[The Master] said, "I am teaching you that the mind cannot be discriminated. The Teacher asked, "I ask you: when your eyes are not blocked, what do you see?
When your ears are not blocked, what do you hear? When your mind is not occupied by thoughts, how can you discriminate?"
The Master saw a monk and raised his whisk, saying, “Do you understand? The monk replied, “I thank the Master for his compassion in showing this to me, a student.
The Master said, “When you see me raise my whisk, you immediately say it is ‘showing a student. Every day you see mountains and rivers; do they not show themselves to you?
Then another monk came, and the Master again raised his whisk. The monk offered praise and prostrated. The Master said, “When you see me raise [the whisk]...”
The whisk-bearer immediately prostrated and offered praise. [The Master] swept the floor and stood holding the broom. "Why do you not offer praise? he asked.
He ascended the hall and said: "All you venerable seniors, do not stoop to deliberate. When deliberation fails, one simply says, 'There is no need for selection.'"
“Discernment! Do you truly know where to apply the mouth? Where will you apply it? Try and say:
Is there one dharma that approaches you, or is there one dharma that distances itself from you? Does it attain you through sameness, or does it attain you through difference?
Since this is so, why do you instead make such a deliberate difficulty of it?”
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The profound mystery of the Zen school—is it merely this? Or is there something else extraordinary?

If there is something else extraordinary, bring it forth for me to see. If there is not, then leave. One must not take these two words and claim they encompass the entire vehicle of the patriarchs. What are these two words?
They are 'the vehicle of the patriarchs' (zongcheng) and 'the vehicle of the teachings' (jiaocheng). As soon as you utter the word 'patriarchal vehicle'..."
This is the vehicle of the school (zōngchéng). To speak of the vehicle of the teachings (jiàochéng) is to be the vehicle of the teachings.
O Chan masters, the fundamental vehicle of the Buddha-dharma has originally been established by names placed within your own mouths; to grasp at it and speak of it is precisely what it is.
Yet for a moment, you speak here of "level," "real," "perfect," and "constant. O Chan masters, what do you call "level and real"? What do you take hold of?
To act with pretension and constant self-importance while traveling among other houses is something that must be clearly distinguished; do not let yourselves be buried together in obscurity.

If you have gained some fragment of sound and form, or names and words, and store them in your hearts, claiming, "I understand; I am skilled at discernment," then tell me: what exactly is it that you understand?
What is there to choose? That which you can memorize is merely a name; that which you can discern is but sound and form.
If it were not for sound and form, as well as names, how could you possibly memorize or discern anything? The wind blowing through the pine trees is sound;
the croaking of frogs and the cawing of old crows are also sound. Why do you not listen and discern right there? If [it were not so]...
Within it there is a certain intent and appearance. Just as in the mouth of the Master, how much intent could there possibly be for you, Venerable One?
Do not err. Right now, sounds and forms are resounding clearly; do they reach you or not?
If they do reach you, then your spiritual nature—the adamantine secret—would surely undergo destruction. Why is this so? Because...
Sound pierces through your ears; form penetrates your eyes. Conditions immediately block you; illusions and delusions run you to death.
The essence of sound and form is such that they cannot be contained. If they did not reach you, from where would sound and form come? Do you understand?
Try to discern for yourself whether they reach you or do not reach you. A short while later, he further said: "This is perfect and eternal, level and..."
"True. Who is it that speaks thus? Such a person is not yet a man from a village of barbarians who understands how to speak in this way.

It was the ancient sages who bestowed a small portion [of their teaching] to assist and manifest [the truth]. People of today do not recognize good from evil; they immediately claim "perfection and reality," saying, "I have a distinct lineage and a mysterious, wondrous teaching.
Śākyamuni Buddha would have no tongue; he would rather say, "It is not as good as your small portion," and would simply leave it at that.
Mozhan said: "If one discusses the offenses of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, though they are grave, they are still relatively light; there is still a time when they may cease.
But this slander of the Prajñāpāramitā blinds the eyes of sentient beings, leading them to swallow iron pellets in the Avīci Hell—do not take this to be a trivial matter."
Therefore, as the ancients said: "The fault lies with the master who transforms others; it is not your concern. Take care!
Chan Master Huigqiu of Anguo was foremost among those who questioned and investigated within the quarters of Xuan Sha. He asked, "What is the primary moon? Xuan Sha replied:
"What would you do with this month of yours? At these words, the Master attained awakening. He then ascended the hall and said:
"The circumstances of the rice porridge and meals here are raised for the sake of my brothers; in the end, they are not constant.
If you wish to attain the essential, it is rather the mountains, rivers, and the great earth that reveal it to you. That Way is constant, and it can also lead to ultimate realization."
If you enter through the gate of Mañjuśrī, all inanimate things—earth, wood, tiles, and pebbles—will assist you in triggering your awakening.
If you enter through the gate of Avalokiteśvara, all sounds and voices—even those of frogs and earthworms—will assist you in triggering your awakening.
If you enter through the gate of Samantabhadra, you will arrive without moving a step. These three gates are shown to you as skillful means, like leading [a child] by the hand.
A single pair of chopsticks stirs the waters of the great ocean, so that the fish and dragons may know that water is their life. Do you understand?
If one lacks the eye of wisdom to examine this with discernment, then no matter how many hundreds of skillful means you employ, they will not lead to the ultimate realization.
The Master asked Attendant Liao, "As the former Master said, 'The entire ten directions of the world are the true human body.
Do you still see the monks' hall? Liao replied, "Master, do not let your eyes deceive you. The Master said, "The former Master has passed away, yet his flesh is still warm."
When Chan Master Xingchong of Zhaoqing first visited Baofu,
Baofu one day entered the Great Hall, beheld the Buddha image, and raising his hand, asked the Master:
"The Buddha was like this—what was his intention? The Master said, "The Abbot, too, is lying across his body. Fokuang said, "I shall take this one piece for myself.
The Master said, "The Abbot is not only lying across his body. Fokuang approved of this.
A monk asked Chan Master Daling Zhihong, "The physical body perishes; what is the indestructible Dharma-body? The Master said, "Mountain flowers bloom like brocade."
The mountain stream water is as green as indigo. Xuedou Xian’s Verse: Question: "I have never known. Answer: "I still do not understand.
The moon is cold and the wind is high; the ancient crags hold frosty cypresses. How laughable! When meeting a man who has attained the Way, one does not respond with speech or silence.
Holding a coral whip in hand, he shatters all the dragon pearls. If he did not shatter them, flaws and blemishes would increase. The state has its laws and regulations—three thousand [offenses].
One day, Chan Master Huizhong of Guiyang said to his disciples:
"The reason sentient beings cannot attain liberation is due to the burdens of their emotions. It is easy to awaken to the Way; it is difficult to bring clarity [to that awakening]."
"The Way is difficult. A questioner asked, "How can one attain clarity regarding the Way? The Master said, "Simply shed your emotional attachments and views;
the Way will become clear of itself. Now, 'clarity' (ming) means trust. It is like a snake-handler who trusts the power of his incantations and the power of his medicines;

he binds and plays with snakes, even holding them in the folds of his sleeves without difficulty. Those who do not know the power of the incantations and medicines are terrified and flee. Simply be attentive..."

When one sees one's own mind, emotional views are immediately shattered. That one now possesses a thousand doubts and ten thousand anxieties such that they cannot be employed is because one has not yet seen one's own mind.
—Master Xiang, the "White Cloud" Chan Master.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Do you all understand? Simply seek it at the ends of streets and marketplaces; seek it among butchers and executioners; seek it in the cauldrons and boiling waters of hell.
If you can understand in this way, you are fit to be a teacher for gods and humans. But as for the gate of the patch-robed monks..."
Heaven and earth are vastly different. Furthermore, there is another kind of person who simply strives to be a "good person" while remaining on their long meditation couch.
You tell me: between these two types of people, which one possesses the superior quality? No need for further words; take care.
The Master asked a monk, "Without destroying conventional designations, how do you speak of the ultimate reality? The monk pointed to a chair and said, "This is a chair.
The Master pushed the chair away with his hand and said, "Bring me my shoe bag. The monk was speechless. The Master said:
When Yunmen heard of this pretentious fellow, he said, "It must have been my elder brother Xiang who did it.
Master Ciming Deshan, while presiding over the assembly, said:
"I have three statements to show you all. One statement encompasses heaven and earth; one statement cuts off..."
To cut off the myriad streams: how do you discern a single phrase that follows the waves? If you can discern it, you have the capacity for study;
if you cannot discern it, you will simply roll along the streets of Chang'an.
Addressing the assembly: Master Juzhi had nothing but questions and answers, always simply raising a single finger. When it was cold, all under heaven and all over the earth were cold;
when it was hot, all under heaven and all over the earth were hot.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Investigate only the living word; do not investigate the dead word. If you can attain realization beneath the living word, you will remain forever free from obstruction.
'A single speck of dust is a Buddha-land; a single leaf is a Śākyamuni'—this is a dead word. Raising an eyebrow, blinking an eye, pointing a finger, or holding up a whisk—these are dead words.
'Mountains, rivers, and the great earth—there is nothing more to be confused about'—this is a dead word. At that time, a monk asked: "How about this?"
"This is a living word. The Master said, "The Persian looks up at the sky. [The monk] said, "In that case, it is not mistaken. The Master then struck him.
This was Chan Master Haoying of Baling Xin Kaiyuan Monastery.
After the Master settled there, he no longer composed writings on Dharma heirs; he simply presented three turning phrases to Yunmen: A monk asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "A person with clear eyes falls into a well. He asked, "What is the 'blowing-hair' sword?
The Master said, "Coral branches branch out, supporting the moon. He asked, "What is the lineage of Deva? The Master said, "Snow in a silver bowl."
Yunmen saw [this] and said: "In the future, on the anniversary of this old monk's death, it will suffice merely to cite these three turning words;
this is enough to repay his kindness. — Master Kuangming Jiao of Shuangquan.
A monk asked Master Dongshan Chu, "What is the Buddha? Chu replied, "Three pounds of flax.
Upon hearing this, the Master said, "To the south there is bamboo; to the north there is wood."
One day, Yunmen asked the Master, "How many sesame cakes did you eat today? The Master said, "Five. Yunmen said, "How many did the pillar eat?
The Master said, "Please come to the tea hall with me to drink some tea."
One day the Master visited Baizhao. Baizhao said, "I have a verse on the wooden fish. The Master said, "Please recite it for me.
Baizhao said, "I humbly observe that this is but a piece of rotten wood; Buddhas and sentient beings are no different. If one strikes it with a staff—"
"Only when the paths of the sage and the ordinary person are utterly severed," [the Master said]. The Master asked, "Does this verse have a conclusion, or does it not?
Baizhao replied, "It has no conclusion. The Master said, "Then Buddhas and sentient beings are not distinct. An attendant intervened, saying, "It does have a conclusion.
The Master said, "Only when the paths of the sage and the ordinary person are utterly severed. At that moment, the entire assembly of Baizhao turned pale with alarm.

When Chan Master Shouchu Zonghui of Dongshan first visited Yunmen, Yunmen asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The Master said, "Chadu. Yunmen asked, "Where were you during the summer retreat?
The Master said, "Baoci in Hunan. Yunmen asked, "When did you leave there? The Master said, "The twenty-fifth of the eighth month. Yunmen—

[The Master] said, "I have spared you three blows of the staff. The next day, the Master went up to pay his respects and asked, "Yesterday I received the Master’s grace of being spared three blows of the staff;
I do not know where my fault lay. The Gatekeeper said, "You rice-bag! You have gone off to Jiangxi and Hunan acting just like this!
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. He then said, "In the future, I shall go to places where there is no human habitation and will not keep [disciples]."

"A single grain of rice; not planting a single stalk of vegetable. To receive and attend to those coming and going from the ten directions, I exhaustively pull out their nails and extract their wedges for them.
I strip away the greasy cap and cast off the stinking hemp robe, teaching them to become carefree, unburdened monks.
Is this not joyful? The Gatekeeper said, "Your body is as small as a coconut, yet you open [the door] so wide!"
Dagou bowed. The Master then addressed the assembly:
"Speech within speech is called a dead word; speech within which there is no speech is called a living word. Zen practitioners, what is a living word?
To reach this point, it is truly difficult to find anyone capable of it. If you can remain unmoved by a single speck of dust..."
One must not dismiss a single state of mind; upon seeing a matter, one speaks directly. The Elder replied, "The feet cannot be placed down.

East, west, south, and north—how much is known? If you wish to depart from the mud and water, to revive the eyes of men, to uphold the style of the School, and to stir up the Great Matter, it is not that these are entirely absent;
alas, they are still lacking. This is simply because you have not reached the source and have fallen into the eighth stage.

Within the realm of Māra, one recognizes that there is that which cannot be named and cannot be objectified—a state where there is neither right nor wrong. In every instance and every thing, nothing is not fully present.
One realizes, "I have attained the field of peace and bliss; I seek nothing further. Whenever anyone comes to strike at me with questions or challenges, [I respond thus].
Even if you strike the meditation bench and brandish the whisk, do not spare further effort; immediately bestow, immediately arrange, immediately act, and immediately employ.

Yet, you plunge head over heels into a pit of foul water, playing with a tailless monkey. When the thirtieth day of the twelfth month arrives, the drum will have been shattered and the monkey will have fled;
with hands flailing and feet scrambling, you will achieve nothing at all. When it comes to regret, how can it be of any avail?
If one is such a monk, he would rather freeze to death or starve to death than ever put on another’s "falcon-smelling robe.
He also said: "To proclaim the lineage of the school and expound the Great Teaching, one must possess a sharp and clear Dharma-eye; only then can one discern the black from the white.
This is because truth and falsehood share a single source, like water and milk in the same vessel; when it comes to this, they are difficult to distinguish. This was Dongshan’s usual way of speaking.
With the eye of the mind, one observes the external forms of the body; observing them again and again, one then discerns the true from the false.
If one does not do so, how can they be called a good spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*)? Indeed, a good spiritual friend is one who drives the ox of the plowman and seizes the food of the hungry man.
Only then can one be called a true spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*). In this world today, who among you is a true spiritual friend?

You practitioners of Chan, how many such friends have you encountered through your practice? This is no ordinary matter; you must practice until you reach the bottom and look through until you see clearly.
That not even a thousand sages could provide proof for it reveals the true man of great capacity.

Have you not seen how the Old Śākyamuni, at the moment the morning star appeared, attained sudden and great enlightenment, becoming a Buddha simultaneously with all sentient beings of the great earth?
There is no before or after—how magnificent this is! Nevertheless, even so, if one encounters a monk with clear eyes, he too deserves to be struck across the back with a staff.
Question: "Vimalakīrti supported the four worlds upon his palm; I wonder where Vimalakīrti’s own body was located?
The Master said: "It was behind you, O Teacher. [The questioner] asked: "Why was it behind this student? The Master said: "Give me back the head of the phrase!"
Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "Three catties of hemp. Question:
"From antiquity until now, it has not been obtained from others. When the Sixth Patriarch was at Huangmei, what did he hear during the night?
The Master said: "Master Zhi’s staff. [The student] asked: "When it is used, how is that? The Master said: "Why use that ruler for anything?"

Question: "When one is walking, standing, sitting, or lying down throughout the twelve periods of the day, how does one maintain self-reflection and awareness? The Master said: "Watch the person eating their meal. [The student] said:
"But what can be done about the fact that the shadows of the trees do not lean? The Master said: "The words of a parent come from the mouth of a parent."
Question: "Gold and brass are present before you; I request that the Master distinguish between them. The Master said: "A two-legged toad swallows the moon. The Supervisor Taibao asked:
"When the faculty of the eye enters right concentration (*samāpatti*), all sensory objects arise as *samādhi*.
What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "In the tea bowl of Dongshan is Taibao; in the tea bowl of Taibao is Dongshan. Taibao has none."
The Recorded Sayings. A monk asked Chan Master Shoushan Shengnian, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "The daughter-in-law rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it. The monk said, "I do not understand the meaning of these words."
"In what phrase is this contained? The Master said, "The Three Mysteries cannot contain it; how could the Four Propositions possibly encompass it? [The student] asked, "What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "Heaven is long-lasting and earth is enduring; the sun and moon shine together."
A monk asked, "I am a student newly entered into this monastery; I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "How long has it been since you have been in my assembly, *ācārya*?
He replied, "It has already been through winter and summer. The Master said, "Do not misrepresent this to others.
He then added, "As for this matter, in truth, it does not even touch the corner of a single character 'one' (*yuan*). Thereupon, he descended from his seat.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Guanghui.

The Master said, "If you pierce the clouds but do not cross the water, or cross the water but do not pierce the clouds—leaving these two paths behind, speak quickly! The monk said, "Last night I stayed at Changqiao.

The Master said, "In that case, you deserve a blow from Shoushan’s staff. The monk said, "I haven’t even entered the hall yet. The Master said, "A double case. The monk said, "Exactly so. The Master said, "..."

"Yes, yes. [The Master] addressed the assembly: "Venerable Elders, you must not shout blindly or shout recklessly. Here, I have always told you: when one is the guest, one remains the guest from beginning to end;
when one is the host, one remains the host from beginning to end. There is no second guest, nor is there a second host. If there were two guests..."
The two masters are both blind men. Therefore, when I stand, you must sit; when I sit, you must stand. If I sit, I sit together with you;
if I stand, I stand together with you. Even so, at this point, you must be quick to open your eyes.
If your eyes blink or waver, then you are already a thousand or ten thousand miles away. Why is this?
This is like looking at a horseman through a window; as soon as you deliberate, there is no connection. All you venerable seniors, since you have set your minds upon this, you must be careful;
do not seek to deceive yourselves with empty pretenses, for it will lead you astray on another day or at another time.
If any of you have a matter, come forward; if you have none, take care.
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "If you recognize this staff, your journey as a pilgrim is complete.
He once composed a verse on the essential principles (*gāṅzōng*) which says: "Alas, you clumsy young man! Your cleverness no one recognizes.
Having broken through the Fenglin Barrier, You stand upon the water wearing boots. Alas, you clever young woman! You ply the shuttle but do not know how to weave. Look at him fighting cocks!"
People do not even recognize a water buffalo; its back faces the shady mountains while its head points toward the sun. As it travels south and north, what is its intention?
If someone asks me about the meaning of the Westward Journey, I say: To the east of the Eastern Sea lies New Ra (Silla).
The Master ascended the hall to take leave of the assembly. He spoke a verse: "O children, you have been wandering in vain for many Ganges Rivers.
Avalokiteśvara points to Maitreya; Mañjuśrī can do nothing about it. After a long pause, he said: "The world of white silver and the body of golden hue—sentient and insentient share one true reality.
When light and darkness are both extinguished, there is no longer anything to be illumined. At the hour after noon, the whole body is revealed. [At] noon...
Later, he passed away peacefully.
One day, Chan Master Hongjin of Qingxi asked Master Xiu, the Mountain Head: "Since you clearly know the principle that birth is non-birth, why [do you still experience it]?"
"Flowing through birth and death," said Xiu. Xiu asked, "A bamboo shoot must ultimately become a bamboo; can it still be used as a strip of bamboo (mèi) now?
The Master said, "You will realize this for yourself later. Xiu said, "This is all my understanding. What is the meaning of your words, Senior?
The Master pointed and said, "This is the Director's quarters; that is the Head Cook's quarters."
Xiu immediately prostrated himself in thanks.
Zen Master Longji asked him:
"When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed, I wonder: does this [reality] also perish? The Master said: "No."
[The Master] said, "It is destroyed. [A monk] asked, "Why is it not destroyed? The Master said, "Because it is identical to the great trichiliocosm.

Ascending the hall, he said: "Rolling up the curtain removes obstructions; closing the door creates impediments. As for these very obstructions and impediments, no one in ancient or modern times has understood them.
To understand them is to be hindered by them; not to understand them is to lack self-mastery."
A monk asked, "How is it when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished? The Master said, "It illuminates heaven and earth. The monk asked, "How is it after it has been polished?
The Master said, "It is pitch black."
The myriad dharmas are the radiance of the mind; all conditions are nothing but the awakening of one's nature. Fundamentally, there is no person who is deluded or enlightened;

it simply requires realization this very day. Master Guizong Zhimen ascended the hall and said: "In the blazing sun is 'self' and 'other'; in the clouds and mist is compassion; in the frost and snow is the patched robe; in the hailstones is..."
"Conceal yourself. Can you still conceal yourself? If you cannot conceal yourself, you will have your skull shattered by the hailstones.
Addressing the assembly: "It has rained well for several days. Tell me, from where does the rain come? If you say it descends from heaven, what is that 'heaven'?
If you say it emerges from the earth, what do you call 'earth'? If you still do not understand, therefore the ancients said..."
The Way is the ancient path before heaven and earth; people of this age cannot forcibly alter it. To give rise to intellectual understanding within it is like placing an awl upon one’s eye.
—Master Xiang of Lotus Peak.
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "If this matter is concerned, it is most urgent. You must clearly realize it and attain it.

If you can so realize it, then in the midst of time you will avoid being bound by constraints, and you will attain peace and ease wherever you are. Furthermore, you need not apply the mind to suppress [delusions];
you must naturally accord with the ancient tracks before you succeed. As soon as you reach the point of distinguishing the stages of study, you must immediately—"
To take this principle and proclaim it as the Buddha-dharma—when will you ever find rest in the ground of your own mind?
Elder, please understand this well.
On the day of his passing, he held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying, "When the ancients reached this point, why did they refuse to stay?
No one in the assembly could answer. The Master then said, "Because on their journey, they had not yet gained strength. He spoke again, asking, "Ultimately, how is it?

Holding the staff across his shoulder, he said, "Carrying the knotted staff slung over my shoulder, I look back at no one; I go straight into a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks. Having finished speaking, he passed away.
[He] passed away.
Chan Master Zhenshi of Lantian ascended the hall and said:
"A mountain is formed by relying on the first basket of earth; a long journey depends upon the first step. As for you, Senior Monk, just now..."
Coming from the side of the brazier, it returns to the same place as the first step. Are they the same? Or are they different? If you say they are the same, you do not understand non-transmigration.
If you say they are different, you also do not understand non-transmigration. Elder, how will you understand this? Do you understand yet? Here is not there;
there is not here. Now tell me: are these one place or two places? Is this transmigration or non-transmigration? Is this coming?
"Going is not coming and going. If one attains clarity regarding this, then past and present are as one; from beginning to end, it is naturally so. Moment by moment there is impermanence;
thought after thought there is eternal cessation. Therefore it is said: 'By observing the directions one knows that person is departing, yet the departing one does not know the directions.
Elder, you have just now come in such a manner; now, please depart in such a manner. Study!"

Chan Master Wen Yi of Qingliang Fayen, together with Shaoxiu and Fajin—these three masters—were about to cross the mountain ridges when they passed through Dizang Monastery. Hindered by snow, they rested for a short while.
As they sat by the brazier, Dizang asked, "Where are you going on this journey? The Master replied, "I am traveling on pilgrimage. Dizang asked, "What is this 'traveling'?"
Regarding the matter of the feet, the Master said, "I do not know. Zang said, "Not knowing is most intimate.
Again, while the three of them were discussing the *Zhao Lun*, they reached the passage concerning "Heaven and Earth sharing the same root as myself.

Zang asked, "Are the mountains, rivers, and great earth the same as, or different from, your own self, Venerable? The Master said, "Different. Zang held up two fingers. The Master said, "The same. Zang again held up two fingers.

He then rose and departed. As Xueji was taking his leave, Zangmen saw him off at the gate and asked, "Upādhyāya, you usually say that the three realms are mind-only and all phenomena are consciousness-only.
Now, look at this stone in the courtyard: tell me, does it reside within the mind?"
“Is it outside the mind? the Master asked. Dazang said, “It is inside the mind. Dazang said, “What kind of reason does a wandering monk have for placing a piece of stone upon his heart?
The Master was at a loss for a reply; he immediately unpacked his bundle and sat beneath the master’s seat to seek decisive instruction.
For nearly a month, he presented his insights and explained his understanding of the principles. Dazang told him, “The Buddha-dharma is not like this. The Master said:
The monk said, "I am at a loss for words; my reasoning has reached its limit. Mazu said, "If we speak of the Buddha-dharma, everything is already fully manifest.
At these words, the master attained great enlightenment. The monk Huichao asked, "What is the Buddha? The master said, "You are Huichao."
Once, pointing to a bamboo, the Master asked a monk, "Do you see it? The monk said, "I see it. The Master said, "Does the bamboo come into the eye, or does the eye go to the bamboo?
The monk said, "It is not like either of those. The Master laughed and said, "Why such a desperate hurry?"
The Master was suffering from an ailment in his leg. When a monk came to inquire after him, the Master said, "When non-humans arrive, I cannot move;
yet when humans arrive, I cannot move. Tell me, what kind of words can be uttered within the Buddha-dharma? The monk replied, "I am glad that the Master has recovered.
The Master did not approve. He then spoke another verse himself: "Today the Master seems diminished."
While digging a well, the spring source was choked by sand. The Master said, "The spring source is blocked because it is obstructed by sand;
what obstructs the eye of the Way when it does not penetrate? The monk had no reply. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "It is obstructed by the eye."

Ascending the hall, the Master said: "The entire world of the ten directions is brilliantly clear; there is not a single thread of hair to be found. If there were a single thread of hair, it would simply be a single thread of hair.

The Master continued: "For those who have left the household life, it is enough simply to accord with the times and seasons. When it is cold, it is cold; when it is hot, it is hot. If you wish to know..."
Regarding the meaning of Buddha-nature, one should contemplate the conditions of time and season; the skillful means employed from ancient times to the present have been numerous.

When Shitou first read Sengzhao’s *Zhaolun*, he came to the passage: "To take the myriad things as oneself—this can only be the Sage. He then remarked: "The Sage has no self, yet there is nothing that is not his self.

Thereupon he composed the *Cantong qi* (Merging of Difference and Unity), beginning with the words: "The mind of the Great Immortal of the land of Chu—the words of none surpass these. This is indeed unsurpassed.

In the interim, he spoke only of ordinary matters. He said, "If you wish to realize that all things are for your own sake, you must see that throughout the entire earth there is not a single dharma to be perceived. Then he further instructed them, saying, "Do not let your time be spent in vain.
This is why I tell you all: simply act according to the season and the occasion. If you miss the timing or lose the opportunity, you are wasting your time. Regarding this:
It is not that one forms a perception of form within what is not form; rather, it is to form a perception of form within what is not form, which is to shift the time and miss the opportunity.
Now tell me: if one were to form a perception of non-form within form, would that still be acceptable? If you understand it in such a way, it is simply irrelevant;
it is precisely like a madman running back and forth between two extremes—what use is there in that? It is best simply to pass the time by maintaining your proper measure.

Ascending the hall, he said to the assembly as they had been standing for a long time, "Each of you has studied many treatises, such as the *Returning to the Source Contemplation*, the *Ocean of Meaning in a Hundred Gates*, the *Avataṃsaka-śāstra*, and the *Nirvāṇa-sūtra*.
In which of these teachings is there such a moment? If there is, try to cite it. Is it that within such a scripture there are such words? Is this the time?"
How so? What connection is there? Therefore it is said: "Subtle words stagnate at the forefront of the mind, constantly becoming a field of discursive thought;
the ultimate reality dwells before one's eyes, yet it turns instead into a realm of names and forms. Furthermore, how can one turn it back?
And if it is turned back, how can one attain the correct state? Do you understand? Do not merely recite it like this.
"Zechenzi, what use is there in that?
Chan Master Wensui had once investigated the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, composing a word-by-word commentary and phrase-by-phrase explanation, claiming it deeply accorded with the intent of the scripture.
He went to visit the Master, who said, "Does the *Śūraṅgama* not contain the principle of the 'eight returns'? Wensui replied, "It does. The Master said, "Light..."
"What does it return to? Suí replied, "The brightness returns to the sun. The Master asked, "What does the sun return to? Suí was left bewildered.
The Master commanded him to burn the commentary he had written; only then did Suí rely upon the Master to request further instruction.

Chan Master Xuánzé asked Qīngfēng, “What is the student’s own self? Qīngfēng said, “The child of fire comes seeking fire. Later, Xuánzé visited the Master [Linjì]. The Master asked, “Where have you come from? Xuánzé said, “From Qīngfēng. The Master asked, “What words did Qīngfēng say? Xuánzé recounted the previous dialogue. The Master said, “How do you understand this, Senior Monk? Xuánzé said, “The child of fire belongs to the south. The Master said, “So it is; so it is. But tell me, what did he mean by saying, ‘The child of fire comes seeking fire’? Xuánzé said, “It means that one who already possesses the nature seeks the nature. The Master said, “If you had said, ‘He was seeking something other than the nature,’ I would have approved your understanding. Xuánzé said, “I am not yet clear about this matter. The Master said, “Since you have not yet understood, go back and ask him again. Xuánzé returned to Qīngfēng and asked, “What did you mean when you said, ‘The child of fire comes seeking fire’? Qīngfēng said, “I meant that one who already possesses the nature seeks the nature. Xuánzé returned to the Master and reported this. The Master said, “Did you hear what he said? Xuánzé said, “He said exactly what I told you. The Master said, “If you had said, ‘He was seeking something other than the nature,’ I would have approved your understanding. Xuánzé said, “I am still not clear about this matter. The Master said, “Since you have not yet understood, go back and ask him again. Xuánzé returned to the Master and reported this. The Master said, “Did you hear what he said? Xuánzé said, “He said exactly what I told you.
