Pointing to himself, he said, "Pang Gong. The Master said, "Even Miao-de and Śūnyatā-saṃbhava would be unable to praise this adequately.
The layman asked in return, "Who can know the phrase by which you have attained power? The Master put on his bamboo hat and walked away.
The layman said, "Be careful on your way," but the Master did not look back.
While Master Chuanshan was picking tea, Pangyun said, "The Dharma-realm admits no body; do you still see me, Master?

The Master replied, "If it were not for the Old Teacher, I would have answered your question. The Layman said, "To have a question and an answer is merely the ordinary. Thereupon, the Master continued picking tea.
The monk did not listen. The scholar said, "Do not take offense; I was merely asking casually. The master still paid him no heed.

The scholar shouted, "This impolite old fellow! Wait until I report you one by one to those with clear eyes! Thereupon, the master threw down his tea basket and returned directly to the abbot’s quarters.
One day, while the Master was sitting in the abbot’s quarters, a lay practitioner came to see him. The Master said, "I am only aware of sitting upright in this room;
I did not notice the monk arrive for an interview. At that moment, the Master lowered one foot. The practitioner immediately left, but after walking two or three paces, he turned back.
The Master then withdrew his foot. The practitioner said, "This may truly be called being free and at ease. The Master replied, "I am the master here. The practitioner said, "Master, you yourself..."
He knew there was a host, but he did not know there was a guest. The Master called to his attendant to prepare tea; the scholar performed a dance and departed.

The Monk of Hitting the Ground in Xinxing had received the ultimate meaning from Jiangxi, yet he always kept his name hidden. Whenever a student posed a question, he would only strike the ground with his staff.
He demonstrated this by striking the ground; thus, he was known at the time as Master "Striking the Ground" (Dadidi Heshang).

One day, a monk hid his staff away before posing a question to him, whereupon the Master merely opened his mouth. The monk asked his attendant, "If it is true that whenever someone asks the Master a question, he strikes the ground—what is the meaning of this?
The attendant immediately took a piece of firewood from within the hearth and threw it into the cauldron.
While Master Bishu of Jiangxi was lying down, Daowu approached and pulled the blanket over him. The Master asked, “What are you doing? Daowu said, “Covering.
The Master asked, “Is it for the one who is lying down? Or for the one who is sitting? Daowu said, “It is neither of these two. The Master said, “But what about the covering?”
"What? I said. "Do not speak in such confusion.
One day, as Dao Wu was returning from outside, the Master asked, "Where have you been? Dao Wu replied, "I have come from being in close attendance."
The Master said, "What is the use of using these two pieces of skin as a winnowing fan? Dowu said, "I borrow them.
The Master said, "If he has nothing to lend you, what then? Dowu said, "Precisely because he has something, I borrow it."

Master Fubei was visited by Ling Xingpo to pay her respects. The Master offered her a seat and tea. The lady then asked, "To whom do you entrust that phrase which cannot be spoken even with one's full strength?
The Master said, "Fubei has no superfluous words. The lady said, "Before reaching Fubei, it was not so."

The Master said, "If you have another point of excellence, feel free to bring it forth. The woman folded her hands and wept, saying, "Alas! To this already bitter sky, you add further grievance and suffering. The Master was speechless.

The woman said, "In your words, you do not know the biased from the correct; in your principle, you do not recognize the upright from the perverse. To act as a teacher for others is to invite calamity.
Later, a monk recounted this to Nanquan. Nanquan said, "How bitter! Fubei has been ruined by this old woman."

The old woman struck him once. Later, when Baowen heard of this, he laughed and said, "Master Nanquan still has some mechanism left. One day, the Chan practitioner Yi encountered the old woman walking along and asked, "What does it mean that Nanquan still has some mechanism left?
The woman then wept, saying, "How tragic! How painful! Yi was at a loss for words. The woman asked, "Do you understand? Yi stood there with his palms joined. The woman said: *Note:

This passage illustrates a classic encounter in the Chan (Zen) tradition, where the "mechanism" (*ji-guan*) refers to the subtle, responsive function of enlightened awareness. The old woman’s weeping signifies the depth of her realization, while Yi’s gesture of joining his palms indicates his initial failure to grasp the point.*
These dead Zen practitioners are as numerous as hemp and millet. One time, Linji brought this up to Zhaozhou.
Zhaozhou said, "If I had seen that stinking old woman, I would have questioned her until her mouth was gagged. Linji asked, "I wonder, Master, how would you have questioned her?
Zhaozhou then struck him. Linji said, "Why did you strike me instead? Zhaozhou said, "For a dead fellow like you, when will I ever stop beating you?"
At that time, she struck him several times with her staff. When the nun heard this, she said, "Zhaozhou deserves to receive a blow from my hand.

Later, a monk reported this to Zhaozhou, who wept and said, "How tragic! How painful! When the nun heard these words, she joined her palms and sighed, "Zhaozhou’s eye shines forth, piercing through the four worlds.
Zhaozhou then instructed the monk to ask her, "What is Zhaozhou’s eye? The nun then held up her staff.
[The Master] raised his fist. The monk turned back and reported this to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou composed a verse, saying: "When the occasion arises, he presents it face-to-face;
Face-to-face, the occasion is swift. I tell you, Laywoman Lingxingpo: What gain or loss is there in your wailing? Laywoman Lingxingpo replied with a verse:

"The Master has already understood the sound of my wailing; Now that it is understood, who else could know it? At that time in the kingdom of Magadha, How nearly I lost the opportunity before my eyes!"

When Master Longshan of Tanzhou and his senior teacher, Master Mi, were traveling together with Dongshan, they saw vegetable leaves floating down a mountain stream. Dongshan said, "This is a deep mountain where there are no people;
why are there vegetables flowing downstream? Is there perhaps a practitioner of the Way living here? Thereupon, they searched through the weeds and traveled along the stream for five or seven [li].
After traveling for some distance, he suddenly saw the Master with an emaciated body and unusual appearance. Setting down his luggage, he paid his respects.
The Master said, "There are no paths on this mountain; from where have you come, Venerable? Dong said, "Setting aside the matter of there being no path, from where did the Master enter?
The Master said, "I did not come from among the wandering clouds and waters. Dong said, "How long has the Master resided on this mountain? The Master said:
"It has not been included in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Dong said, "The Master was the first to dwell here; this mountain was the first to be inhabited. The Master said, "I do not know. Dong said:
"Why do you not know? the Master asked. Dong said, "From where did you come, Master? The Master replied, "I did not come from the realm of humans or devas.

Dong said, "What principle have you realized, Master, that you dwell on this mountain? The Master replied, "I saw two clay oxen fighting and entering the sea; until this very day, there has been no further news.
At these words, Dongshan finally assumed his full ceremonial dignity and prostrated himself. He then asked, "What is the guest within the host? The Master [replied].

[Dongshan] said, "Green mountains shroud white clouds. [Dongshan] asked, "What is the host within the guest? The Master said, "Never leaving the door for many years. [Dongshan] asked, "How far apart are guest and host?
The Master said, "Waves upon the waters of the long river. [Dongshan] asked, "When guest and host meet, what words are spoken? The Master said, "A clear breeze brushes the bright moon.
Dongshan took his leave. The Master then composed a verse, saying: Three... [the rest of the verse is omitted in the source text].
"I have lived in this thatched hut from long ago; A single path of divine light leaves all phenomena at rest. Do not bring right and wrong to judge me;
The worldly life’s forced interpretations have no concern with me. He said again: "A pond of lotus leaves provides countless garments; The ground covered in pine pollen offers more than enough food.
Just because the world came to know my dwelling place, I moved my thatched hut once more into the deep recesses. This was due to his burning of the hermitage.
No one knew where he had gone; thus, people also called him Master Yishan.
In the early Zhenyuan era of the Tang dynasty, the layman Pang Yun of Xiangzhou visited Shitou and asked: "Who is it that does not consort with the myriad dharmas?"
He covered his mouth with his hand, whereupon he attained a sudden realization. Later, he became friends with Danxia.
One day, Shitou asked him, "Since you first met this old monk, what has been your daily practice? The scholar said, "If you ask about my daily practice," [he remained silent].

Thereupon, he had no words with which to respond. He then presented this verse: "In daily affairs there is nothing different; Only I myself find harmony. At every turn there is neither grasping nor rejecting;
In every place there is no discord or conflict. Who assigns the titles 'Red' and 'Purple'? Mountains and hills are free from even a speck of dust.
Spiritual powers and wondrous functions— They consist in carrying water and hauling firewood. Deshan said, "Are you a monk or a layman? The scholar replied, "A monk."
He said, "I wish to follow what I aspire to," and thus he did not undergo tonsure or ordination. Later, he visited Mazu and asked, "Who is it that does not act as a companion to the myriad dharmas?
Mazu replied, "Wait until you can suck up all the waters of the West River with a single mouth, and then I will tell you.
At these words, the scholar suddenly realized the profound essence of the teaching.
The Layman saw Danxia. Danxia made a gesture of running away. The Layman said, "That was still a gesture of casting off the body.
What is the gesture of groaning? Danxia then sat down. The Layman drew a seven-character figure on the ground with his staff;

Danxia drew a single character beneath it. The Layman said, "Because of the seven, one sees the one; having seen the one, one forgets the seven. Danxia then rose and departed. The Layman said, "Sit for a while longer."
At that time, there was still a second phrase remaining. Xie said, "Can you utter a word here? The scholar then wept and departed.

After the scholar attained enlightenment, he loaded his entire household's tens of thousands of precious bags onto a boat and sank them in the Xiang River; thereafter, the whole family practiced the Way.
The girl was named Lingzhao. She constantly sold bamboo water-strainers and mats to provide for her daily needs. She had a verse that said: "Having sons, I do not marry them off;
having daughters, I do not give them away. As a family, we sit together in a circle, discussing the discourse on non-arising."
One day, Layman Shishuang was sitting alone in his hermitage when he suddenly exclaimed, “Difficult! Difficult! Ten piculs of sesame oil spread upon a tree!
Laywoman Pang followed his voice and said, “Easy! Easy! The meaning of the Patriarchs is at the tips of the hundred grasses. Lingzhao said, “It is neither difficult nor easy;
when hungry, one eats; when tired, one sleeps.”
The scholar sat in his place and asked Lingzhao, "An ancient said, 'Brilliant at the tips of the hundred grasses, brilliant is the meaning of the Patriarch.
What does this mean? Lingzhao said, "Old man, old man, making such talk. The scholar said, "What about you?"
Zhao said, "Vividly clear at the tips of the hundred grasses, vividly clear is the meaning of the Patriarch.
Yunmen smiled. Yunmen was selling bamboo for a fishing screen when he fell down the bridge. Lingzhao saw this and also went to fall down beside her father.
Yunmen asked, "What are you doing? Lingzhao said, "Seeing my father fall, I went to help him up. Yunmen said, "Fortunately, no one else saw it."

As the Master was about to enter nirvana, he said to Lingzhao, "Observe the sun and report to me when it reaches noon. Lingzhao quickly reported, "The sun has already reached its zenith, yet there is an eclipse.
As the Master went out the door to observe, Lingzhao immediately ascended her father’s seat, joined her palms, and passed away while seated.
The Master smiled and said, "My daughter is sharp and quick-witted. Thereupon, he extended his life for another seven days. The Provincial Governor, Lord Yu, [heard of this].
When Wang Yin asked after his health, the Master said to him, "I only wish that you would empty all that exists; be careful not to fill what does not exist.

Be fond of departing from the world, for all things therein are like shadows and echoes. Having spoken these words, he leaned his head upon the Duke’s knee and passed away. His final instruction was to cremate his body and cast the remains into the rivers and lakes.

After Chan Master Yaoshan Weiyan took up residence at Yaoshan, the assembly from all directions gathered there in great numbers. When Zun the Novice was bathing the Buddha, the Master said, "This one is for you to bathe."
"Did you get that one back after your bath? Dun said, "Bring that one here. The Master then desisted.
The head of the monastery announced, "The bell has been struck; please come to the hall, Reverend. The Master said, "You go with me and carry my alms bowl."
[The monk] said, "How long has it been since the Master arrived handless? The Master said, "You are merely wearing the *kāṣāya* robe in vain.
[The monk] said, "I am just like this; how about you, Master? The Master said, "I have no such followers as these."
The Master said to Yunyan, "Call the śrāmaṇera here for me. Yunyan asked, "What will you do with him when he comes?
The Master said, "I have a broken-legged cauldron that I want him to carry up and down.
Yunyan said, "In that case, I shall lend my hand to the Master. The Master then ceased speaking.
While the head gardener was planting vegetables, the Master said, "I do not forbid you from planting; just do not let the roots grow.
The gardener asked, "If you do not allow the roots to grow, what will the assembly eat? The Master replied, "Do you have a mouth? The gardener had no answer.
The Master held an evening *can* (informal discourse), saying: "I have a phrase; I will tell it to you when a hornless ox gives birth to a calf.
At that time, a monk stepped forward and said, "A hornless ox has given birth to a calf; it is only that you, Master, do not speak [the phrase].
The Master called to his attendant, "Bring a lamp! The monk then withdrew and joined the assembly.
The Master asked Layman Pang, "Can this matter still be contained within the One Vehicle? The Layman said, "I simply spend my days seeking a few pints or quarts;
I do not know if it can be contained. The Master said, "Tell the Layman he has not yet seen Shitou."
"Is that so? The scholar said, "To pick up one thing and let go of another is not yet the mark of a master. The Master said, "I am a senior monk; my duties as abbot are many.
The scholar said, "Take care," and he departed. The Master said, "To pick up one thing and let go of another—this is truly the mark of a master.
The scholar said, "What an excellent inquiry into the One Vehicle! Today it has been lost. The Master said, "Yes, yes."

A monk asked the Master, "I, a student, have a doubt; I ask the Master to resolve it. The Master said, "Wait until the time for the formal assembly, and I will resolve your doubt with you, lay brother.
That evening, when the assembly had gathered for the evening lecture, the Master said, "Where is the elder who requested to resolve his doubt today?
The monk stepped forward from the assembly and stood there. As the Master descended from his meditation seat, he seized him by the collar and said, "Great assembly, this monk has—"
Suspecting him, he gave him a shove and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
He asked a monk, "How old are you? The monk said, "Seventy-two. The Master said, "Are you indeed seventy-two years old?"
The monk said, "Yes. The Master struck him.

The monk asked, "My own matter is not yet clear; I beg the Master for instruction. The Master remained silent for a long while and said, "It would not be difficult for me to speak a single word for you right now.
It would still be somewhat better if you could see [the truth] immediately upon hearing it. But if you enter further..."
[The Master] reflected, "This would instead become my own transgression. It is better that we each simply keep our mouths shut to avoid implicating one another.

The Master then ordered the master of offerings to go out for alms. When the lay practitioner Gan Zhi asked him, "Where have you come from? he replied, "From Yaoshan. Gan asked, "What are you doing there?
He said, "Teaching and transforming. Gan asked, "Have you brought any medicine with you? He replied, "Lay practitioner, what illness do you have?"
Gan immediately set aside two ingots of silver, thinking that since there were people in the mountains, they surely would not accept this.
When the host returned and presented his report, the Master asked, "Why have you returned so quickly? The host recounted the previous conversation. The Master said, "Return it to him at once;
you have already been robbed by thieves. The host then sent it back. Gan said, "There was indeed someone here from the start; I shall add more gold to give as a gift."
The Master had not ascended the seat for a long time. One day, the head of the monastery said, "The assembly has long been longing for the Master’s instructions.
The Master said, "Strike the bell! As soon as the assembly had gathered, he descended from the seat and returned to his quarters.
The head of the monastery followed him and asked, "The Master promised to speak to the assembly; why did you not utter a single word? The Master replied, "The sutras say..."
Regarding the masters of the Sūtras and the masters of the Vinaya, how could they possibly compete with this old monk?
One day, Chan Master Danxia Tianran addressed the assembly, saying, "Tomorrow, you must clear away the weeds in front of the Buddha Hall. When the next day arrived, the great assembly and all the...
While the novice trainees each prepared spades and mattocks to clear away the weeds, the Master alone filled a basin with water and washed his head. He knelt before the stone and bowed;
when the Abbot saw this, he laughed and proceeded to shave his hair. He then preached the precepts to him, whereupon the Master covered his ears and walked out.
He went again to Jiangxi to visit Mazu. Without even paying his respects, he entered the monks’ hall and mounted the neck of the sacred statue.
As he sat there, the great assembly was struck with amazement and immediately informed Mazu. Mazu entered the hall in person and, looking at him, said, "My son is naturally so.
The Master then descended from the seat and prostrated himself, saying, "I thank the Master for bestowing a Dharma name. Consequently, he was named Tianran (Natural). Mazu then asked:
"From where have you come? The Master said, "From Shitou. The Patriarch said, "The path at Shitou is slippery; have you perhaps stumbled and fallen?
The Master replied, "If I had stumbled and fallen, I would not have come here. Thereupon, he took up his staff and traveled to observe the various quarters.

He passed by Huilin Temple when the weather was bitterly cold. Taking a wooden Buddha, he burned it for a fire to warm himself. The temple administrator scolded him, saying, "How can you burn my wooden Buddha?
The Master prodded the ashes with his staff and said, "I am burning it to retrieve the *śarīra* (relics). The administrator said, "A wooden Buddha—how could it have *śarīra*?
The Master replied, "Since there are no *śarīra*, take two more statues and burn them. Thereafter, the administrator’s eyebrows and beard fell out.
He fell down. The next day he went again to pay his respects. Upon seeing the National Teacher, he spread out his sitting mat. The National Teacher said, "Not needed.
Not needed. The Master stepped back. The National Teacher said, "So it is. So it is. The Master then stepped forward. The National Teacher said, "It is not."
"Yes. The Master circumambulated the National Teacher once and then departed. The National Teacher said, "The time since the Sage has passed; people are mostly indolent.
Thirty years from now, it will be difficult to find such a man."
He visited Layman Pang and saw his daughter, Lingzhao, washing vegetables. The Master asked, "Is the Layman at home?
The girl set down her vegetable basket and stood with her hands folded. The Master asked again, "Is the Layman at home? The girl took up the basket and walked away.
The Master then turned back. A short while later, the Layman returned. The girl recounted the previous conversation, and the Layman said, "Danxia was here."
"Ma! The woman said, "He has gone. The scholar said, "It is like smearing red earth on a cow's udder.
The Master asked Layman Pang, "What was it like yesterday compared to today?

The Layman said, "If you bring up yesterday’s matter according to the Dharma, make it into the Eye of the School. The Master said, "As for that Eye of the School, can it contain Layman Pang? The Layman said, "..."
“I am within your eyes,” the layman said. The Master replied, “My eyes are narrow; where can you find a place to dwell? The layman said, “How can these eyes be narrow?
How can this body be at rest? The Master stopped speaking. The layman said, “Say one more phrase, and this dialogue will be complete.”
The Master also did not respond. The gentleman said, "Among all these words, there is this one sentence that no one can utter.
While the Master and Layman Pang were walking along, they came upon a pool of water. The gentleman pointed at it with his finger and said, "Even so, you still cannot discern it.
The Master replied, "Truly, I cannot discern it. Thereupon, the gentleman scooped up water and splashed two handfuls onto the Master.
The Master said, "Not so! Not so! The Layman said, "It must be so! It must be so!
The Master then scooped up water and made the Layman take three handfuls. The Master said, "At this very moment, what can you do? The Layman said, "There are no external things.
The Master said, "Those who gain the advantage are few. The Layman said, "Who is it that falls into disadvantage?"

The Master asked a monk, "Where did you stay overnight? The monk replied, "I stayed at the foot of the mountain. The Master said, "Where did you eat your meal? The monk replied, "I ate at the foot of the mountain.
The Master said, "Does the person who gave you the food to eat possess eyes or not? The monk was speechless.
A monk asked Chan Master Dadian of Chaozhou, "What is it like when those within meet? The Master said, "They have already missed the point.
The monk asked, "What about those who are within? The Master said, "Do not make such a question."
One day, Han Yu visited the Master and asked, "How many years have you been practicing? The Master held up his rosary and said, "Do you understand?
Han Yu replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "One hundred and eight, day and night. Not comprehending this, Han Yu turned back. The next day he came again;
arriving at the gate, he saw the Head Seat (Śrāmaṇera) and recounted the previous conversation, asking, "What was the meaning of that? The Head Seat clicked his teeth three times.
When he met the Master, he repeated his previous question. The Master also struck his teeth three times. The official said, "So, it turns out the Buddha-dharma is not of two kinds.
The Master asked, "What is your reasoning? The official said, "Just now, when I questioned the Head Seat, he answered in exactly the same way.
The Master then summoned the Head Seat and asked, "Was it you who answered in this manner? The Seat replied, "Yes. The Master then struck him and expelled him from the monastery.
One day, Duke Wen said to the Master, "The affairs of my commandery and state are numerous. I beg the Master for a single word regarding the essential points of the Buddha-dharma.
The Master remained silent for a long time; the Duke was at a loss. At that time, Sanping was serving as attendant, so he struck the meditation bench three times.
The Master asked, "What is this? Sanping replied, "First move with concentration, then extract with wisdom. The Duke then said, "Master!"
The style of this lineage was lofty and austere. A disciple gained an entry point through an attendant.
A monk asked, "The waves of the sea of suffering are deep; what shall serve as a boat or raft? The Master said, "Use wood as a boat and raft.
The monk said, "If that is so, then one can cross over. The Master said, "The blind remain blind as before; the mute remain mute as before."
One day, while walking along the corridor with Yanghezi, the Master encountered a monk.

As they exchanged greetings, the Master struck him over the mouth with Yanghezi and asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Old Wild Fox Dadian has never failed anyone."
The Zen Master Changzi of Tanzhou asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the Kongseng Hermitage on Mount Jiuhua. The Master asked, "Who is the abbot of that hermitage?
The monk replied, "An eminent elder under Mazu. The Master asked, "What is his name? The monk replied, "I do not know his dharma-name. The Master said:
[The Master] said, "I do not know; you do not know. [The monk] asked, "Where are the eyes of the Venerable One?
The Master said, "If the Abbot himself had come here, he would have had to receive a blow of the staff today as well. [The monk] said, "Fortunately, I encountered the Master who let me off.
The Master said, "A hundred years from now, it will be difficult even to find a monk like this."
Li Xingpo arrived. The Master asked, "Do you remember the events when we were in Jangzhou? The nun said, "It would not be without the Master that I would know.
The Master said, "Much is empty and little is real. The nun said, "What is there to hide? The Master said, "Out of consideration for your being a woman, I let you off with your staff.
The nun said, "I certainly do not see any fault in the Venerable Elder. The Master said, "That is my own fault."
"In what place? The old woman said, "The Master has no fault; how could I possibly have a fault? The Master asked, "What is it like for one who has no fault?
The old woman then held up her fist and said, "In this way, everything becomes a perversion. The Master said, "Truly, there is nowhere to hide."
The Master saw the monk and seized him, saying, "Lion cub! You belong to the lineage of jackals! The monk made a gesture with his hand as if brushing back his eyebrows.
The Master said, "Even so, you still lack the roar. The monk seized the Master and said, "You are particularly fond of employing this particular maneuver.
The Master gave him a slap. The monk clapped his hands three times. The Master said, "If you see someone of like mind, you would willingly [act] with them."
"No. The monk said, "In the end, it does not depend on anyone else. The Master made a gesture of flicking his eyebrows. The monk said, "There is still a lack of a roar.
The Master said, "I suspect it does not depend on anyone else."

A monk asked Chan Master Shilou of Fenzhou, "I do not yet recognize my original nature; I beg the Master for a skillful means to point it out. The Master said, "Shilou has no ears. [The monk] said, "..."
The monk said, "I know my own fault. The Master said, "Does the old monk also have a fault? The monk asked, "Where does the Master’s fault lie?
The Master said, "The fault lies in your place of non-fault. The monk bowed, and the Master struck him.
When Chan Master Datong Ji was visited by Mihuo leading his assembly, as soon as they were about to meet, the Master pulled the meditation bench around and sat facing the wall.
Mihuo stood behind him for a short while, then returned to the guest quarters. The Master said, "It is indeed so; yet if it were not verified and broken through..."
Later, he encountered a man who disparaged and undermined him. This man ordered an attendant to request some rice. When the rice was brought, the man dragged the meditation seat over and sat upon it.
The Master then walked once around the meditation seat and returned to his quarters. The man then pulled the meditation seat down and led the assembly out.
He visited Master Pang. The Master said, "When I was in my mother's womb, there was a single phrase.
I shall present it to you, Master; do not attempt to analyze or rationalize it. The Teacher said, "That is still from a previous life. The Master said, "I told you not to analyze it.
The Teacher said, "This is a startling statement; how could one not be afraid? The Master said, "According to your understanding, it may be so."
The Master said, "To startle others is not to act according to principle; it merely results in acting according to principle. The Layman said, "Not only for one or two lifetimes.
The Master said, "As for monks who subsist on rice gruel, let them be as they are, subject to scrutiny. The Layman snapped his fingers three times.
When the Master saw Layman Pang approaching, he closed the door and said, "An old man of much knowledge—do not let him see you.
The Layman said, "Sitting alone and speaking to oneself—who is at fault? The Master then opened the door; as soon as he stepped out, he was seized by the Layman, who said:

The Master said, "I am very knowledgeable; you are very knowledgeable. The Master said, "Let us set aside your great knowledge for a moment. Between closing a door and opening a door, between rolling it up and spreading it out—how much difference is there?
The scholar said, "This single question alone would exhaust me to death. The Master remained silent. The scholar said, "Seeking cleverness, I have only achieved clumsiness."
One day, he asked Layman Pang: "This matter of speech is something few people throughout ancient and modern times have been able to avoid;
do you, Master Pang, yourself avoid it? Pang replied, "Yes. The Master brought up the previous conversation again. The Layman asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said: [He did not answer.]
"It is not only now; the ancients also had this saying: 'The scholar performs a dance and departs. The Master said, "A madman! A madman!
Passing by yourself, whom would you have to check?"
A scholar came to visit. Holding up a bamboo sieve, he called out, "Master Datong! Master Datong! The Master did not look back.
The scholar said, "The school of Stonehead has crumbled like tiles and melted away like ice. The Master replied, "If it were not for people like Master Pang, it would certainly have been so."
The Layman threw down the basket and said, "I would rather have it not be worth a single coin. The Master said, "Though the coin may not be worth a thing, how can you avoid owing it to me?
The Layman performed a dance and withdrew. The Master then picked up the basket and said, "Pang Gong! Pang Gong!"
The scholar said, "You want my sieve; I want your wooden ladle. The Master performed a dance and withdrew.
The scholar clapped his hands and laughed, saying, "Go back! Go back!"
When Master Huangbo Xiyun ascended the hall, as soon as the assembly had gathered, the Master took up his staff and struck everyone, dispersing them at once. He then called out to the assembly;
when they turned their heads, the Master said, "The moon is like a drawn bow; little rain, much wind. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the West? The Master then—
One day, as he ascended the hall and the assembly gathered like clouds, he said, "What do you all seek?
He then drove them away with his staff, yet the assembly would not disperse. The Master sat back down and said, "All of you are nothing but wine-drinkers."
You wretched fellows! To travel on pilgrimage in such a manner is to become a laughingstock to others. You simply go wherever you see eight hundred or a thousand people;
you must not seek out their clamor. Since you all claim to be traveling on pilgrimage, you must also apply some measure of spirit and effort.
"Do you still not know that there are no Chan masters in the land of the Great Tang? At that time, a monk asked, "The venerable elders of all quarters are gathering assemblies to teach and transform;
why do you say instead that there are no Chan masters? The Master said, "I do not say there is no Chan; I simply say there are no masters."
A monk asked Chan Master Changqing Da’an:
“When this aggregate has already ceased and that aggregate has not yet arisen, what is it like? The Master said:

“If this aggregate has not yet ceased, who is that ‘Virtuous One’? The monk said: “I do not understand. The Master said: “If you understand this aggregate, you will clearly understand that aggregate.”
Question: "When Huang Chao’s army arrives, where will you, Master, take refuge? The Master said: "In the mountains of the five aggregates.
Question: "What if they suddenly catch you? The Master said: "I shall trouble the General."

When Chan Master Guling Shen was traveling on pilgrimage, he encountered Baizhang and attained enlightenment. Upon returning, his original preceptor asked him, "While you were away from me, what accomplishments have you gained?
He replied, "I have no accomplishments whatsoever. Thereupon, the master sent him to perform manual labor. One day, while bathing his body, [the master] commanded—
The Master [Nanyue Huairang] removed the dust from his back. He then patted him on the back and said, "A fine Buddha hall you have here, yet the Buddha is not holy.
The Original Master (Shitou) turned his head and looked at him. The Master said, "Though the Buddha is not holy, he is nonetheless able to emit light.

On another day, while the Original Master was reading a sutra by a window, a bee flew against the paper of the window, seeking an exit. Seeing this, the Master said, "The world is so vast and wide; why must you seek an exit through this small hole?"

"If you are willing to come out, you have been drilling through old paper for donkey years! He then spoke a verse: "Unwilling to leave the Gate of Emptiness, Even throwing yourself out the window would be too foolish.
Drilling through old paper for a hundred years— When will you finally emerge? The Master set aside the scriptures and asked, "Whom have you encountered during your travels?
I have observed that your speech has been extraordinary from the beginning. The Master replied, "I have received the grace of the Venerable Ba..."

Baizhang Huashang pointed out a place of rest; now I wish to repay his compassionate virtue. Thereupon, the Master [Baizhang] informed the assembly to prepare a vegetarian feast and invited the teacher to preach the Dharma.
The teacher then ascended the seat and proclaimed the tradition of Baizhang’s school, saying: "The numinous light shines alone."

"Completely detached from the sense organs and their objects, the essence reveals the true permanence. It is not constrained by words and letters; the nature of mind is unstained, fundamentally perfected from the beginning.

Simply by leaving behind delusive conditions, one is the Buddha of Suchness. The Original Teacher was awakened by these words and said, "Who would have thought that in my old age I would hear of such ultimate matters?"
Zen Master Puan of Tiantai Pingtian visited Master Maoyuan.
As soon as Yuan rose to greet him, the Master stepped forward, seized him, and said: "To open your mouth is to lose it."
"If you close your mouth, you lose it immediately. Departing from these two paths, I beg the Master to provide another way. Yuan covered his nose with his hand.

The Master released his grip and said, "One step is easy; two steps are difficult. Yuan said, "Why such a desperate hurry? The Master said, "If it were not for the Master, one would not escape being scrutinized by those everywhere."
When Linji visited the Master, he arrived at a crossroads and first encountered an older sister-in-law tending oxen in a field.
Linji asked the sister-in-law, "In which direction does the path across the level fields lead? The sister-in-law gave the ox a blow with her staff and said, "This beast wanders everywhere;

even when it comes to this very road, it does not recognize it. Linji spoke again, saying, "I am asking you, in which direction does the path across the level fields lead? The sister-in-law replied: [She struck him.]
"This beast! Even at five years old, it still cannot be used. Ji said to himself, "If you wish to observe the master, first observe those he employs.
Thereupon, he felt as though he were pulling out nails and extracting wedges. When he saw the Master, the Master asked, "Have you seen my sister-in-law yet?
Ji replied, "I have already taken her in. The Master then asked, "Where did you recently depart from? Ji replied, "Jiangxi."
Huangbo said, "I knew well that you would come before a master. Ji said, "I have come specifically to pay my respects to the Master.
The Master said, "We have already met. Ji said, "According to the etiquette between guest and host, three prostrations ought to be performed.
The Master said, "Since it is the etiquette between guest and host, then perform your prostrations."
When the attendant Da of Chan Master Hui of Dongshan in Hongzhou arrived, the Master asked: "The adamantine samādhi is such in all things. Autumn has passed and winter is coming;
what do you say to this? The attendant said, "It does not hinder me, Master, that you ask. The Master said, "That may be so for now, but after you have left, what will you do?"
"How is it? [The Master asked]. The attendant said, "Who would dare to question me? The Master said, "Can you even return it?
The attendant said, "I still require another to inspect it. The Master said, "Aids to the Patriarchal Teacher do not forfeit their brilliance. The attendant prostrated.
One day, National Teacher Nianbuan of Baizhang Mountain said to the assembly, "You all go and clear the fields for me; I shall explain the Great Meaning to you.

When the assembly had finished clearing the fields, they returned and requested him to explain the Great Meaning. The Master then opened his two hands, leaving the assembly at a loss as to what to do.
When Chan Master Zhaozhou Zhenji Congshen arrived at Huangbo, Huangbo saw him coming and immediately closed the door to his quarters. The Master then took a torch and entered the Dharma Hall.
He cried out, "Save me from the fire! Save me from the fire! Baizhang opened the door, seized him, and said, "Speak! Speak! The Master replied, "Drawing the bow after the thief has fled."
One day, while lying prostrate in the snow, the Master cried out, "Save me! Save me! A monk immediately went and lay down beside him;
the Master then rose and departed.
While the Master was on the latrine, he saw Attendant Wenyuan passing by. He suddenly called out, “Wenyuan! Wenyuan responded, “Yes?
The Master said, “I cannot speak the Buddha-dharma to you while on the latrine.”
A monk asked, "When two dragons contend for the pearl, who is the one that obtains it? The Master said, "I, the old monk, simply keep watching.
A monk asked, "'The ultimate Way is not difficult; it only dislikes discrimination. Is this the conceptual trap of ordinary people?
The Master said, "Someone once asked me this, and I could not resolve it for five years."

The Master asked the head of the monastery, "Where have you come from? The head replied, "I have come to deliver a birth. The Master said, "Why did the crow fly away? The head replied, "It was afraid of me.
The Master said, "Having served as the administrative head for ten years, how can you speak such words? The head then asked in return:
"Why did the crow fly away? The Master said, "The temple steward had no intention to kill.
A monk traveling to Mount Wutai asked an old woman, "In which direction does the path to Mount Wutai lead? The woman said, "Go straight ahead.
The monk then departed. The woman said, "What a fine monk! And yet he goes off like that. Later, another monk related this incident to the Master.
The Master said, "Wait until I have gone to test her. The next day, the Master went there and asked, "In which direction does the road to Mount Tai lead?
The old woman replied, "Go straight ahead. The Master then continued on his way. The old woman said, "What a fine monk! And yet he goes away like that.
When the Master returned to the monastery, he said to the monks, "The old woman of Mount Tai has thoroughly exposed you all."
Question: "What is the mystery within mysteries? The Master said: "For how long have you been with this mystery? He replied: "I have been with it for a very long time.
The Master said: "If you, Reverend, had not met me, you would have nearly died of this mystery."
There was an old woman who sent someone with money to request that he recite the *Tripitaka*.

After the Master had accepted the offering, he stepped down from his meditation seat, circumambulated it once, and said, "Give this message to the old woman: the recitation of the *Tripitaka* is finished. When the messenger returned, he reported these words to the old woman.
The Magistrate said, "I have recently requested that you transmit the entire Tripiṭaka; why then do you only transmit half?
The Master asked, "When you, sir, burn raw food until it becomes cooked within your own residence, who is it that does so?
The Magistrate replied, "It is my servant. The Master said, "In fact, he is quite capable."
Hand asked,
"By what skillful means can one hear that which has not yet been heard? The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment that which has not yet been heard,
what have you ever heard?"
A newly arrived monk entered for an audience. The Master asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From the South. The Master said, "The Buddha-dharma is entirely in the South.

Why have you come here? He replied, "How could the Buddha-dharma have north or south? The Master said, "Even if you had come from Yunju or Xuefeng, you would still be nothing more than a man carrying a single shoulder-pole."
The Master asked an old woman, "Where are you going? She replied, "I am going to steal Zhaozhou’s bamboo shoots.
The Master said, "What will you do if you encounter Zhaozhou? The woman gave him a slap, and the Master desisted.
A senior monk asked the Master, "Where have you recently departed from? The Master said, "Huazhou. The senior monk said, "How many stages did it take to get here?
The Master said, "I arrived in a single leap. The senior monk said, "What a swift ghost! The Master said, "Ten thousand blessings, Great King!
The senior monk said, "Go to the hall for practice. The Master responded, "Yes, yes."
He further said to the assembly, "If you do not leave the monasteries for the rest of your lives and remain silent for five or ten years, no one will call you a mute man;
even the Buddha himself will have no recourse against you later on. If you do not believe me, take the old monk’s head away with you!"
Nanquan was passing by the bathhouse when he saw the bath attendant tending the fire. He asked, "What are you doing? The attendant replied, "I am heating the water for the bath.
Nanquan said, "Keep this in mind; I will call for the Water Ox to bathe later. The attendant gave his assent.
That evening, the attendant entered the Abbot’s quarters. Nanquan asked, "What are you doing? The attendant replied, "I have gone to bathe the Water Ox. Nanquan said, "Did you bring a rope with you?"
"Have you come? The bath attendant gave no reply. The Master came to inquire after Quan; Quan reported this to the Master.
The Master said, "I have something to say. Quan then asked, "Have you brought a rope with you? The Master stepped forward and suddenly pulled him by the nose.
Quan said, "It is indeed so, but it is too coarse."
The Master asked Nanquan, "Beyond the four propositions and transcending the hundred negations, please speak, Master. Nanquan then returned to his quarters.
The Master said, "This old monk usually talks incessantly, yet when questioned, he cannot utter a single word.
The attendant said, "It would not be right to say the Master has no words. The Master then gave him a slap. Nanquan then closed the door to his quarters.
Master Quan surrounded the gate with ashes and asked a monk, "If you can speak a word, I shall open the gate.
Many people offered responses, but none accorded with Quan’s intent. The Master cried out, "Heaven! Heaven! and Quan then opened the gate.
Question: “I have heard that you, Master, personally met Nanquan. Is this true? The Master said: “Zhengzhou produces large radishes. Question:
“What is the Buddha’s true Dharma-body? The Master said: “What more could you possibly find wanting?”
Question: "What is the host within the guest? The Master said: "This mountain monk does not ask after his wife. Question: "What is the guest within the host?
The Master said: "This old monk has no father-in-law."
The monk asked, "How is it that all dharmas are eternally abiding? The Master said, "I, this old monk, do not conceal the Patriarchs. The monk asked again.
The Master said, "Today I will not answer questions."
Question: Among the myriad things, which is the most solid? The Master said: "When scolding one another, I allow you to jab with your beaks; when spitting at one another, I allow you to splash water.
Question: What is it like when day and night do not cease? The Master said: "Among the monks, there are no such people as the commoners subject to the two taxes."
The Master ascended the hall and said: "Brothers, you are currently in the midst of the third grievance. Therefore it is said: 'Only change the place where you formerly practiced;
do not change the person who was there. Each of you has left the household life for your own sake. Until now you have had no concerns, yet you further ask about Chan and the Way.
Thirty or twenty people gather their heads together to question me, as if they were lacking some Chan or Way from me."
It seems so. You call me a "good spiritual friend" (kalyāṇamitra), but I am one who has likewise undergone the same interrogation. This old monk is not joking;
I fear I might bring reproach upon those ancients, which is why I speak of the east and the west.
Question: "What is the master of Zhaozhou? The Master scolded him, saying: "You bucket-binder! The student responded with an assent.
The Master said: "Bind your buckets properly."
Question: "What is the fundamental matter of the student? The Master said: "When the tree shakes, the birds scatter;

when the fish are startled, the water becomes turbid. Question: "What is the mystery within mysteries? The Master said: "Why speak of the mystery within mysteries? It is seven among seven, and eight among eight."
Question: "What is the mystery within mysteries? The Master said: "If this monk were still here, he would be seventy-four or seventy-five years old.
The Master ascended the hall and said: "Brothers, simply reform your past and cultivate the future. If you do not reform, there is a great deal that will catch you."
The nun asked, "Setting aside what was said above, I request the Master to provide instruction. The Master scolded her, saying, "The iron pitcher has been baked to pieces!
The nun brought the iron pitcher back, filled with water, and requested, "I pray the Master answer my question. The Master laughed at her.
Question: From the beginning until now, it has been said that "the mind itself is Buddha. Is it not permitted for practitioners to deliberate upon this very point?
The Master said: "Setting aside for a moment the idea that 'the mind itself is Buddha,' what exactly is there to deliberate about?"
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "To conceive a thought is already to err. A monk then asked, "What is it like when one does not conceive a thought?
The Master struck him twice and said, "Do you think I, this old monk, am betraying you, Dharma brother?"
Question: "Whenever there is a question and answer, does it fall within the faculty of the mind, or does it not fall within the faculty of the mind?
How would you, Master, respond? The Master said: "Ask. The student said: "I request that the Master speak. The Master said: "Do not engage in right and wrong here."
Question: "The person of the highest rank is turned around by a single stroke; but what about when a person of the lowest rank arrives?
The Master said: "Are you the highest rank, or the lowest rank? He said: "Please, Master, give me a reply. The Master said: "The talk has no host yet. He said: "I have come from seven thousand li;
do not act with a calculating mind. The Master said: "Based on this question of yours, is it that you have no calculating mind?"
This monk stayed for one night and then departed. [The student] asked:
"If True Suchness and ordinary or holy beings are all but dream-words, what then is the true word?
The Master said: "I will not say those two things anymore. The student said: "Setting aside those two for a moment, what is the true word? The Master said: "Oṃ buraṇ phaṭ."
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "When the mind arises, all manner of phenomena arise; when the mind ceases, all manner of phenomena cease.
What do you all say to this? A monk then asked: "What is it like at the time when there is neither arising nor ceasing?
The Master said: "I grant you this one question."
During a session of inquiry, the Master said: "The light is not yet bright; the darkness is about to dawn. Where are you? The monk said: "I am not at either of the two ends. The Master said:
"If that is so, then you are in the middle. The monk said: "If I were in the middle, I would be at one of the two ends. The Master said:
"How long has this monk been here with me, making such talk as this? He did not acknowledge him.
"One may emerge from within the three phrases; yet even if one does emerge, one remains within the three phrases. How do you manage this?
The monk said, "I can employ all three phrases. The Master said, "Why did you not speak like this earlier?"
Question: When the myriad objects arise together, are there any delusions that cannot be attained? The Master said: Yes. The student asked: What is it that cannot be attained as a delusion?
The Master said: Do you believe that the Buddha-dharma exists? The student said: I believe the Buddha-dharma exists.
The ancients said: "What is it that cannot be deluded? The Master asked, "Why do you not ask me, old monk?
The student replied, "I have already asked. The Master said, "You are deluded."

The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Those whom one succeeds in transforming and teaching are matters of this present life; those whom one fails to transform and teach are enemies from a third life.
If one does not transform them, there is the fear that all sentient beings will fall into ruin; yet even transformation is itself an act of enmity."
"Are you still teaching and transforming others? The monk said, "I am. The Master said, "Do all sentient beings see you?
The student said, "They do not. The Master said, "Why do they not see you? The student said, "Because I have no form. The Master said, "Do you see me, this old monk, right now?
The student said, "The Master is not a sentient being. The Master said, "Then recognize your own fault."
He immediately attained realization.
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Of these eight hundred men who have become Buddhas, it is difficult to find even one true Way-man.
A monk asked: "What is it like when white clouds do not fall? The Master said: "This old monk does not know how to ride an elephant. The student said: "Is there no [other way]?"
Guest and Host. The Master said, "I, the old monk, am the host; you, Dharma brother, are the guest. Where is the white cloud?
The Master addressed the assembly, saying, "As for the word 'Buddha,' I do not like to hear it. A question was asked: "Does the Master still act for the sake of others or not?"
The Master said, "To act for others. The student asked, "How does one act for others? The Master said, "Not knowing the profound principle, you labor in vain by contemplating stillness."
The student said, “Since it is ‘mysterious’ (xuán), what is the essential meaning (zhì)? The Master said, “I do not hold a text. The student said, “This is the mystery;
what is the essential meaning? The Master said, “My answer to you is the essential meaning.”
Question: Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not? The Master said: "No. The student said: "From the Buddhas above down to the ants below, all possess Buddha-nature.
Why does the dog have none? The Master said: "It is because it still possesses the nature of karmic consciousness."
Question: "What is a man of the Way? The Master said: "I say he is a man of the Buddha. Question:
"Whenever there are words and phrases, or the raising of hands and the moving of feet, it all falls within the net of the student. Apart from this, please let the Master speak.
The Master said: "The old monk has finished his meal and has not yet drunk tea."
The Grand Master Ma asked, "Does the Master still practice cultivation? The Master said, "If this old monk were to practice cultivation, it would be a disaster.
Ma said, "Since the Master does not practice cultivation, whom do you have practice? The Master said, "The Grand Master is the one who practices.
Ma said, "In what way am I practicing? The Master said, "If you were not practicing, how could you have fallen [into this state]?"
"Amidst the rank of a king of men, you have been fed until you are crimson and frozen upon the red earth; there is no time for release.

The Great Officer then shed tears, bowed in thanks, and asked: "Since you, Master, have only just arrived, you do not know at all how matters stand at the gate. The Master said: "What is your name, Senior?"
"Ma? The student said, "Huainan. The Master said, "Very good at not knowing.
A student asked, "I wish to study, yet I am slandering the Master. How can I avoid slandering you?
The Master said, "What is your name? The student said, "Daoyue. The Master said, "Go to a quiet place; you are nothing but a grain bin."
Question: "What is it like when one is not hung with even an inch of silk? The Master said: "What is there not to hang? The student said: "Not hung with even an inch of silk.
The Master said: "Excellent! Not hung with even an inch of silk!"
Question: "When the place of function does not manifest, how is it? The Master said: "Functioning is not non-existent; but who is it that manifests? Question:
"In the kalpa of emptiness, is there still anyone practicing cultivation or not? The Master said: "What do you call the 'kalpa of emptiness'? [The questioner] said: "..."
"There is not a single thing that is correct. The Master said, "This is what is truly called 'cultivating practice.
What do you call the 'empty kalpa'? Question: "What is leaving home? The Master said: "Not treading upon high fame; not seeking out defilement or destruction."
A certain scholar saw the staff the Master was holding and said, "The Buddha does not take away the vows of sentient beings—is this so?
The Master replied, "It is. The scholar said, "May I beg for the staff in your hand, Reverend? May I have it? The Master said:
"A gentleman does not take away what others cherish. The Xiucai said, "I am no gentleman.
The Master said, "Neither am I a Buddha."
The Master went outside and saw an old woman weeding a rice paddy. He asked, "What would you do if you suddenly encountered a fierce tiger?
The old woman said, "There is not a single dharma that can withstand the mind. The Master said, "Heh! The old woman said, "Heh! The Master said, "It is difficult to find such a one as this."
Question: "Who is the person above the Buddha? The Master said: "It is simply this person who is tending the oxen. Question:
"Does a newborn infant possess the six consciousnesses or not? The Master said: "Hitting a ball on a swift-flowing stream."
Question: “Is it that only the Buddha alone is a true spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra)? The Master said: “That is the speech of Māra. Question:
“What is the point of urgency? The Master said: “One question, one answer.”
Question: What is unlearned wisdom? The Master said: "I have never taught you, O *śrāmaṇera*.
Question: What is the one phrase of intimacy? The Master said: "Your words have fallen away."
Question: "What is the meaning of [the Master’s] coming from the West? The Master said: "Hairs grow on wooden teeth. Question:
"What is the six-foot golden body? The Master said: "Tucking the collar under the armpit. [The student] said: "I do not understand. The Master said:
"If you do not understand, ask someone else to tailor it for you."
The nun asked, "What is the meaning of the 'dense and secret'? The Master pinched her with his hand.
She said, "The Master still has this. The Master said, "It is you who have this."
Question: "What is one who dwells among the dust? The Master said: "Bring me money for tea and salt. Question:
"What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "Prostrate yourself. As the monk was about to offer his reply, the Master called out, "Śrāmaṇera Wenyuan!
When Wenyuan arrived, the Master rebuked him, saying: "Where have you been just now?"
Question: What is loyal speech? The Master said: "Your mother is ugly. Question:
What is loyal speech? The Master said: "Eat an iron staff."
Question: "What is the state beyond thought? The Master said: "Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Question:
"What is the state beyond deliberation? The Master said: "Speak swiftly! Speak swiftly!"
Question: “Who is this person who has come out? The Master said: “A Buddha or a Bodhisattva.
Question: “What is the holy? The Master said: “Not ordinary. Question: “What is the ordinary? The Master said: “Not holy. Question:
“When one is neither ordinary nor holy, what then? The Master said: “A fine Zen monk indeed!”
Question: "When two mirrors face each other, which one is the clearest? The Master said: "Dharma brother, your eyelids cover Mount Sumeru. Question:
"What is it like when it is so high and steep that it is difficult to ascend? The Master said: "I, the old monk, do not go to the summit of the high peak."
Question: What is the practice of a śramaṇa? The Master said: "Transcending practice. Question:
I beg the Master to point out the place of true rest. The Master said: "Pointing it out would mean no rest at all."
Question: "What is it like when a sharp sword emerges from its scabbard? The Master said: "Black. Question:
"What is the place where a śramaṇa gains power? The Master said: "Where would you not have gained power?"
Question: “When it is high, steep, and difficult to ascend, what then? The Master said: “I, this old monk, dwell atop the peak myself.

[The questioner] said: “What can be done about the road by the side of Caoxi? The Master said: “Caoxi is evil. [The questioner] said: “Why do people not arrive there now? The Master said: “Because they do not arrive.”
"This channel is high and steep.
He asked, "How is it at the place where the lives of the patriarchs and Buddhas are never severed? The Master said, "No one knows.
He asked, "When a poor man comes, what object will you give him? The Master said, "Nothing is lacking."
While the Master was sitting in meditation in his room, the administrative official informed him, saying, "The Great King has come to pay his respects.
After the King had finished his prostrations, those around him asked the Licheng (Lieshi), "The King has arrived; why did you not rise? The Master replied, "You do not understand."
In this old monk’s place, when those of inferior capacity come, I go out to the three gates to receive them; when those of middling capacity come, I descend from my meditation seat to receive them;
when those of superior capacity come, I receive them while remaining upon the meditation seat. One must not address a Great King as being of middling or inferior capacity.
“I fear I may be imposing upon you, Great King. The Great King was delighted and, having invited him in three times, requested that he enter the inner quarters for offerings.
The Master then asked Layman Zhou: “Did you see Linji in your dream? The Layman held up his fist.
The Master said, “You saw him there. The Layman said, “I saw him here. The Master said, “Where did you see Linji? The Layman had no reply.
"Yes. The Master asked Layman Zhou, "Where have you come from? He replied, "Neither coming nor going. The Master said, "That is not like an old crow flying here and there."
The Master asked the newly arrived monk, "From what direction have you come? The monk replied, "I have come from no particular direction. The Master then turned his back.
The monk followed the Master's turn with his sitting mat. The Master said, "Excellent indeed is 'coming from no particular direction'!"
The Master was strolling in a garden with a Court Gentleman when he saw a rabbit scurry past. The Gentleman asked, "The Master is a great spiritual teacher (*kalyāṇamitra*).
Why does the rabbit run away upon seeing you? The Master replied, "I am a man fond of killing."
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From the capital. The Master said, "Did you pass through Tongguan Pass?
He replied, "I did not. The Master said, "Today I have caught this smuggler of salt!"
The Master had just arrived at Linji when he began to wash his feet. Linji immediately asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master replied, "It is precisely while washing my feet. Linji then stepped forward to listen closely. The Master said, "If you understand, then understand!"

"Better not to do anything at all; why do you peck and pry? Linji shook his sleeves and left. The Master said, "Having traveled for thirty years, today I have wrongly provided a commentary for others."
While the Master was traveling on foot, he encountered two hermits at their huts. One of them was a youth with his hair tied in two points.
The Master paid his respects, but the two men paid him no attention whatsoever. The following morning, the youth brought a pot of rice and set it on the ground, dividing it into three portions.
The hermit took a mat and sat down nearby; the youth also took a mat and sat opposite him.
The Master did not call out to the boy. The Master then took his mat and sat down near him. The boy looked toward the Master.
The Hermitage Master said, "Do not say that those who rise early have no one to surpass them; there are still travelers on the night road. The Master said, "Why do you not instruct this novice?
The Hermitage Master said, "He is the son and daughter of a common family. The Master said, "In that case, I should have let him pass. The boy then stood up and departed.
He looked back. The hermitage master said, "Why such a garrulous mouth? From that time on, the boy with the cleft head was never seen entering the mountain again.
Later, while the Master was reading a sutra, the novice Wen-yuan entered. The Master turned his gaze sideways toward the sutra; the novice then went out.
The Master followed him and seized him, saying, "Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Wen-yuan replied, "Amitābha Buddha."
"Amida Butsu. The Master then returned to his quarters.
A new head monk from Silla invited the Master for a meal. When the Master reached the gate, he asked, "What monastery is this?
He was told, "The Silla Monastery. The Master said, "I am separated from you by the sea."
An old woman entered the monastery at evening. The Master asked, "What are you doing? The woman said, "I am seeking lodging.
The Master said, "What kind of place is this? The woman laughed loudly and departed.
Once, while Master Changsha Jingcen was enjoying the moon with Yangshan, Yangshan said, "Everyone possesses this very thing, yet they are unable to use it."
The Master said, "That is exactly it; I am borrowing you for use. Sanshan asked, "How will you use me? The Master gave him a kick straight in the chest.
Sanshan said, "Ouch! You are like a great tiger right here and now. From then on, people throughout the various quarters called him "Cen the Tiger."
Question: Nanquan said, "The Buddhas of the three periods do not know that there is; the wildcat and the white ox, however, do know that there is.
Why is it that the Buddhas of the three periods do not know that there is? The Master said: "Before entering the Deer Park, they were still somewhat superior. [The questioner] asked: "Why?"
"Why is it that the wildcat and the white ox, however, do know? The Master said, "How can you blame them?
He asked, "Where has Nanquan gone after his passing? The Master said, "He became a donkey for the eastern neighbor and a horse for the western neighbor."
[The student] said, "If a student does not understand this meaning, what then? The Master said, "If you wish to mount, then mount; if you wish to dismount, then dismount.
Sansheng then instructed Xiu Zuo to ask, "Where has Nanquan gone after his passing?
The Master said, "When Shitou was a novice monk, he studied under the Sixth Patriarch. Xiu said, "I am not asking about Shitou seeing the Sixth Patriarch; I am asking about Nanquan."
"Where does one go when passing away? The Master said, "I will let him ponder it.
Xiu said, "Although you, Master, possess a thousand-foot cold pine, you lack a sprouting stone shoot. The Master remained silent. Xiu said, "Thank you, Master, for your response."
The Master remained silent. Xiu returned and related this to Sansheng. Sansheng said, "If it were so, it would still surpass Linji’s seven steps.
Nevertheless, let me test him further. The next day, Sansheng went up to the hall and asked, "I have heard that yesterday you, Master, gave a response to Nanquan regarding his passing;
it may truly be called something that outshines the past and leaves nothing behind for the future, rare throughout all time."
When he heard this, the Master remained silent.
Chan Master Lizon of Zihu Yan set up a signboard at his gate that read: "At Zihu there is a dog; it takes people's heads from above and takes people's [backs] from below."
The Mind: Reaching down to seize a person’s feet—if they hesitate for even a moment, they lose their body and forfeit their life. Two monks came to visit under Linji;
as soon as they lifted the curtain, the Master shouted, "Watch out for the dog! The monks looked back, and the Master immediately returned to his quarters.
Liu Tiemo came to visit the Master. The Master said, "Are you Liu Tiemo? He replied, "I dare not. The Master said, "Turn left; turn right.
He replied, "Master, do not act so confusedly. The Master then struck him.
The Grand Master Lu Xing, the Prefectural Governor of Xuancheng, asked Nanquan: "An ancient master once raised a gander in a bottle.
As the gander grew larger, it could no longer get out of the bottle. Now, one must not break the bottle, nor may one harm the gander. What would you do, Master?"
He was born with it. Nanquan called out, "Grand Master! Yuanzheng responded, "Yes. Nanquan said, "It has emerged. From this, Yuanzheng attained understanding and immediately prostrated in gratitude.

One day, the lay practitioner Gan-zhi of Chi-zhou entered Nan-chuan’s hall to provide a vegetarian feast. Huang-po was serving as the head seat (*śrāmaṇera*). The practitioner requested that alms be distributed.
The head seat said, "The two kinds of giving—wealth and Dharma—are equal and without distinction. Gan-zhi said, "If you speak thus, how can you deserve my offering? He then took...
He went out. After a short while, he entered again and said, "I request a gift of wealth. The Master said, "The two gifts of wealth and Dharma are equal and without distinction.
Only then did he proceed to give the alms-offering.
On another day, Nanquan entered a temple to serve congee and invited [the Master] to recite the scriptures.
Nanquan then struck the gavel and said, "I request the assembly to recite the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* for the sake of the marten and the white ox. Gan then shook his sleeves and departed.
After the congee was served, Nanquan asked the head cook, "Where has the Master gone? The cook replied, "He left right then and there. Nanquan then smashed [the cooking vessel].
The Cauldron.
When Chan Master Lingxun of Furong first visited Guizong, he asked, "What is the Buddha? Guizong replied, "If I tell you, will you believe me?"
The Master said, "The Preceptor’s words are sincere; how could I dare not believe them? Zhaozhou said, "It is you yourself. The Master asked, "How does one maintain this?
Zhaozhou said, "A single film over the eye causes empty flowers to fall in confusion."
When Chan Master Zhītōng of Wǔtái was first under the assembly of Guīzōng, he suddenly cried out one night, "I have attained great enlightenment! The multitude were startled by this.

The next day, as the assembly gathered for the formal lecture, Xuedou said, "Let any monk who attained great enlightenment last night come forward. The Master stepped forward and said, "I, this humble one.
Xuedou asked, "What principle have you seen that you speak of 'great enlightenment'? Try to explain it. The Master replied, "A nun was originally made by a woman.
Xuedou marveled at this. The Master then took his leave. As Xuedou saw him off at the gate, he offered him his straw raincoat. The Master [held it up]...
Having received the hat, he placed it on his head and walked away without looking back. Later, he resided at Fahua Temple on Mount Tai.

At the time of his death, he composed a verse which said: "Raising my hand, I grasp the Southern Dipper; Turning my body, I lean against the Northern Pole Star. I thrust my head out beyond the heavens to look."
Who was this person like me?
The Venerable Puhua of Zhenzhou served as a disciple of Panshan and received his secret transmission; yet he feigned madness and spoke without restraint. This continued until Panshan passed away.

He then traveled to this land to perform his teachings. Whenever he shook a single bell, he would say: "If it comes from the bright side, strike on the bright side. If it comes from the dark side, strike on the dark side.
If it comes from the four quarters and eight directions, strike with a whirlwind. If it comes from empty space, strike with a continuous flurry.
One day, Linji had a monk seize him and asked, "What if it does not come in any of these ways? The Master pushed him away and said, "Come tomorrow!"
There was a vegetarian feast at Dabeisi (Great Compassion Monastery). When the monk returned, he related this to Linji. Linji said, "I have always suspected this fellow.
When the Magistrate of Cavalry and Infantry appeared and shouted, "Clear the way! the Master also shouted, "Clear the way! and assumed a wrestling stance.
The Magistrate ordered his men to strike the Master with five blows of the staff. The Master said, "It is like it, but it is not it."
The Master once wandered through the marketplace shaking a bell and chanting, "I seek a place to go, but it cannot be found.
At that time, Daowu encountered him, seized him by the collar, and asked, "Where do you intend to go? The Master replied, "Where have you come from?"
"I have nothing to say. The Master pulled his hand away and departed.
Chan Master Chuwai of Qianzhou was asked by a monk:

"The principles and subtleties embodied in the Three Vehicles and the Twelve Divisions of the Teachings—how do they compare with the meaning of the Patriarchs? Are they the same or different? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
The Master said, "You must discern beyond these six phrases; you must not turn with sounds or forms. The monk asked, "What are the six phrases?
The Master said, "'Speaking,' 'silence,' 'neither speaking nor silence'—all of them, none of them. What will you do about this?
The monk had no reply.
Master Caoshan of Jinzhou invited Master Mihuang for a meal. He did not arrange any seating positions. When Mihuang arrived, he spread his sitting cloth and prostrated.

Master Caoshan descended from his meditation seat, whereupon Mihuang took the master’s seat. Master Caoshan, however, sat on the floor. When the meal was finished, Mihuang departed. An attendant said:
"The Master is revered by all people; today his seat has been seized by someone.
The Master said, "If he comes after three days, I shall save him. After three days, Mi indeed came and said, "Yesterday I was robbed by bandits."

Whenever Master Gudī of Langzhou saw a monk coming, he would simply say, "Go! You have no Buddha-nature. The monks were speechless; however, if any among them did respond, [he would likewise dismiss them].
[The Master] did not accord with his intent. When Yangshan arrived for an audience, the Master said, "Go! You have no Buddha-nature.
Yangshan joined his palms, stepped forward three paces, and responded with an "Amen" (ye). The Master smiled and said, "From where did you obtain this samādhi? Yangshan replied:
"I received my name from Danyuan; I attained the ground at Guishan. The Master asked, "Are you not then a son of Guishan?
Yangshan said, "In terms of worldly truth, that is not non-existent; however, regarding the Buddha-dharma, I do not presume to say so.
Yangshan then asked, "From where did you, Master, obtain this samādhi? The Master replied, "I obtained this samādhi from Zhangjing. Yangshan—
He sighed and said, "Inconceivable! It is difficult for those who come to find a place of rest here.

When Chan Master Jieling of Shanglin in Hunan first visited Mount Gui (Weishan), the Master asked, "Virtuous One, what have you come for? The Master replied, "My armor is fully equipped. Mount Gui said, [and continued].
Yangshan said, "I have completely unburdened myself; now come and meet with the Venerable One. The Master said, "You have already unburdened yourself.

Yangshan scolded him, saying, "The thief has not yet been beaten; why are you unburdening yourself? The Master had no reply. Yangshan spoke on his behalf, saying, "Please, Master, dismiss those around you."
Guishan pointed with his finger and said, "Yo! Yo! Later, when the Master visited Yongtai, Yongtai finally explained its meaning to him.
On Mount Wutai, there was the Monk of Bimora Rock who constantly carried a wooden staff;
whenever he saw a monk coming to pay his respects, he would immediately thrust the staff across the monk's neck and say, "Which demon is that?"
"A demon has incited you to leave the household life. Which demon has incited you to travel as a mendicant? If you can speak, you shall die beneath the cross;
if you cannot speak, you shall die beneath the cross. Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Among his disciples, few were able to respond.
When Master Tong of Huoshan visited him, as soon as he saw him, he did not prostrate but instead leaped into the furnace. The Master struck Tong on the back three times. Tong—
He clapped his hands and said, "Brother Teacher, you have lured me three thousand li away! You have lured me three thousand li away!
And he immediately turned back.
This was Master Lingyou of Mount Gui.
While they were making sauce, the Master asked Yangshan, "How much salt water is used for this?
Yangshan said, "I do not understand; I do not wish to answer. The Master said, "In fact, it is I who understand. Yangshan said, "I do not know how much salt water is used.
The Master said, "Since you do not understand, I shall not answer either. That evening, the Master again questioned Yangshan regarding the events of that day.
The Master said, "How will you maintain the teaching? Yang replied, "I shall answer when asked. The Master said, "I am asking you right now.

Yang replied, "My ears are deaf and my eyes are dim; I do not understand what I see or hear. The Master said, "In all questions and answers, you must not utter such words as these. Yang bowed in thanks.
The Master said, "Ji, today you have forgotten what came before and lost track of what follows; this is no small matter."
The Master said to Yangshan, “You must personally turn the light back upon yourself and reflect inwardly. Others do not know the extent of your understanding;

try bringing forth your true realization for me to see. Yangshan said, “If you command me to look at myself, when I arrive here there is no state of perfection, nor is there a single thing or a single realization that I can offer to the Honored One.
The Master said, “In the place where there is no state of perfection, originally...”
“This is where you have formed an interpretation; you have not yet departed from the state of mind and object. Yang said, “Since there is no perfected position, where could there be any dharma?
What thing could one grasp to make it an object? The Master said, “Just now, you formed such an interpretation, did you not? Yang said, “I did.”
The Master said: "If it is so, this is the dharma of a fully present mind and object; you have not yet escaped the mind of 'mine. Originally, there was someone who offered [this] to me;
I grant that your stage of faith is manifest, but your stage of human realization remains hidden."
One day, while seeing Xiangyan and Yangshan as they were making cakes, the Master said, "At that time, our late teacher Baizhang personally realized this very principle.
Yangshan and Xiangyan looked at each other and said, "Who could answer this question?"
The Master said, "There is one person who can answer. Yang asked, "Who is it? The Master pointed to a water buffalo and said, "Speak! Speak!"
Yang took a bundle of grass and came forward; Xiangyan took a bucket of water and came forward.
Before they had set it down, as soon as the ox began to eat, the Master said, "In this way, in this way; not in this way, not in this way. Both men prostrated themselves.
The Master said, "At times it is bright; at times it is dark."
When Ziguó came to consult the Master, the Master pointed to the moon to show him. Ziguó brushed it away three times with his hand.
The Master said, "I do not say that you do not see it; it is simply that your way of seeing is too coarse."
The Master asked Dao Wu, "Where have you come from? Wu said, "I have come to visit the sick. The Master said, "How many people are sick?
Wu said, "There are those who are sick and those who are not. The Master said, "Is the one who is not sick perhaps the Venerable Zhi?
Wu said, "Whether sick or not sick, it has nothing to do with him. Hurry and speak! Hurry and speak! The Master said, "Even if you could speak it..."
He did not engage him in further discussion.
The Master asked Yangshan, "All day long you have been deliberating with this fellow; what kind of matter has been accomplished?
Yangshan drew a line in the air. The Master said, "Had it not been for me, he would surely have been deluded by you."
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "From the Western Capital. The Master said, "Have you brought a letter from the master of the Western Capital?
