The monk said, "I dare not falsely convey any news. The Master said, "A master monk; his natural state remains intact. The monk said, "Indeed."
"Who would eat leftover soup and rancid rice? The Master said, "Only you, Reverend, do not eat it.
The monk made a gesture of vomiting. The Master said, "Escort this sick monk out. The monk then went out.
When Master Zongzhi of Daowu Mountain was at Mt.
Gui, Guishan asked Yunyan, "What serves as the seat for Bodhi? Yunyan replied, "Non-action (wuwei) serves as the seat.
Yunyan then asked Guishan, and Guishan said, "The emptiness of all dharmas serves as the seat. He then asked the Master, "How about you? The Master said, "I sit."
"I allow him to sit; I allow him to lie down. "There is one person who neither sits nor lies down—speak quickly! Speak quickly!
Thereupon, Shanshan ceased speaking.
The Master pointed to a *fo-sang* flower and asked a monk, "How is this like that? The monk said, "It is enough to make the hairs on one's body stand on end.
The Master said, "In the end, how is it? The monk said, "The one under the gate of Daowu. The Master said, "The Great King of Ten Li."
Yunyan was unwell. The Master said to him, "Setting aside this shell-and-leak vessel, where shall we meet?

Yunyan said, "We shall meet in the place of neither birth nor extinction. The Master said, "Why do you not say that we do not seek to meet even in a place that is neither non-birth nor non-extinction?"
Master Yunyan Tanzheng left home to become a monk at Shimen in his youth. He studied under Chan Master Baizhang Hai for twenty years, yet the karmic conditions did not harmonize.
Later, he went to visit Yaoshan. Yaoshan asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from Baizhang. Yaoshan asked, "What did Baizhang say?"
The Master said, "I have a single phrase that possesses all hundred flavors. Sanshan said, "'Salty' is the flavor of saltiness;
'bland' is the flavor of blandness; 'neither salty nor bland' is the ordinary flavor.
What is this phrase that possesses all hundred flavors? The Master had no reply. Sanshan said, "What about birth and death right before your eyes? The Master said, "Right before my eyes..."
“There is no birth and death. Mount [Shishuang] asked, “How long have you been at Baizhang? The Master replied, “Twenty years.

Mount said, “Having spent twenty years at Baizhang, you still have not eliminated your worldly airs. On another day, while standing in attendance, Mount asked again, “What further Dharma did Baizhang teach?
The Master replied, “At times he would say: ‘Go beyond the three phrases; realize within the six phrases. Mount...
[Zhaozhou] said, "Even from three thousand li away, I am already delighted that there is no connection. Baoshan asked again, "What further Dharma do you speak?
The Master said, "Sometimes when I ascend the hall and the assembly has stood still, I drive them all away at once with my staff.
Then I call out to the assembly; when they turn their heads, I ask, 'What is this? Baoshan said, "Why did you not speak like this earlier? Today, because of you, I have attained it."
When he saw his elder brother Hai, the Master suddenly attained realization upon hearing these words and immediately prostrated himself.
While the Master was brewing tea, Daowu asked, "For whom are you brewing this? The Master replied, "There is someone who wants it.
Daowu said, "Why not let him brew it himself? The Master said, "Fortunately, there is I here."
The Master asked Shishuang, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Mount Huai. The Master said, "How long have you been there?
He replied, "I have spent the winter and summer there roughly. The Master said, "If that is so, then you must have grown quite large!
He replied, "Though I was there, I did not know it. The Master said, "His house is neither known nor perceived. Shishuang had no reply.
A monk asked, "What is it like when a single thought flickers up and one immediately falls into the realm of Māra?

The Master said, "Why do you, on the contrary, come from the realm of the Buddha? The monk had no reply. The Master said, "Do you understand? He said, "I do not. The Master said, "Do not say that you cannot realize it;
even if you were to realize it, it would still only be a matter of left and right."
Minister Pei asked a monk, "When one makes offerings to the Buddha, does the Buddha eat them? The monk said, "It is like when you, Minister, sacrifice to the household deities.
The minister related this to the Master. The Master said, "Whatever kinds of food there may be, let them all come down at once.
The Master then asked Shenshan, "After they have all come down at once, what then? Shenshan said, "Close the bowl. The Master approved of this.
One day, while the Master was making straw sandals, Dongshan approached him and said, "I, your student, beg for the Master's eyes.
May I have them? The Master asked, "To whom would you give yours? Dongshan replied, "Liang-jia has none.
The Master said, "Even if you had some, where would you put them? Dongshan was speechless. The Master asked, "Are those who beg for eyes themselves possessed of eyes? Dongshan said, "No."
"Eye. The Master then shouted her out. The nun bowed.
The Master asked, "Is your father still alive? She replied, "He is. The Master said, "How old is he? She replied, "He is eighty years old.
The Master said, "You have a father who is not eighty years old; do you know him? She replied, "Is it this coming [of the Way]? (mo shi ren mo lai).
The Master said, "One who comes in such a manner is still but a descendant.
One day, Yaoshan asked, "Apart from being at Baizhang, where else have you been? The Master replied, "I have been to Guangnan.
Yaoshan said, "I heard it was said that outside the eastern gate of the city of Guangzhou there is a large stone that has been moved by the provincial governor."
[The Master] said, "Go. [The official] asked, "Is it so? The Master replied, "Not only you, the provincial governor; even if the entire population of the state were to move, they would not budge.
Baoyan Mingzhe Chan Master arrived for an audience with Dongshan and his senior teacher, Mi. The Master asked, "Where have you two venerable monks come from? Dongshan replied, "From Hunan."
The Master asked, "What is your surname, Officer of Observation? He replied, "I have no surname. The Master asked, "What is your given name?

He replied, "I have no given name. The Master asked, "Do you still attend to official business? He replied, "There are already the officials and secretaries for that. The Master asked, "Do you still go in and out [of the court]? He replied, "I do not go in or out.
The Master said, "How can it be that you do not go in and out? Shan shook his sleeves and departed. The next morning, the Master entered [the hall].
In the Hall, the Master summoned the two senior monks (Upādhyāyas) and said, "Yesterday, when the old monk and you, Venerable Sirs, exchanged a single phrase, it did not accord.

I have been ill at ease all night. I now ask you, Venerable Sirs, to offer another turn of phrase. If it satisfies the old monk’s mind, I shall open the gruel and we shall stay together for the summer retreat.
Xiangshan said, "Please, Preceptor, ask me. The Master said, "Is it not 'entering and exiting'? Xiangshan said, "That is too dignified."
Valuing life, the Master then opened the gruel [for the assembly], and they spent the summer retreat together. One day,
while Master Cuiwei Wuxue was walking in the Dharma Hall, Touzi approached him to pay his respects and asked, "What is the secret essence of the West?"
"How do you, Master, instruct people? The Master paused for a short while. The monk said, "I beg the Master to grant us an instruction.

The Master said, "Do you want another ladle of foul water? The monk then bowed in thanks. The Master said, "Do not hide your roots. The monk said, "When the time comes, the roots and sprouts will grow of themselves."

He said, "There was once a person of rare spiritual acuity.
When the Chan Master Xingkong of Xiaoyi was being attended by the practitioner Ding, the Master struck him with a staff and said, 'I have blinded your original eye. Ding replied, 'It is not so.'"
"But today," [Ding] said, "the ancients also practiced this rite. The Master said, "Who told you that there is 'ancient' and 'modern'? Ding shook his sleeves and went out.
The Master said, "Under the clear blue sky and bright sun, there is a person lost on the way. Ding said, "Do you not wish to give directions?
The Master struck him. Ding said, "Do not blind people's eyes! The Master said, "What is there in blinding the eyes of worldly people?"

One day, when Master Xiantian was receiving monks for an audience, as soon as [a monk] spread out his sitting cloth, the Master said: "There is no need to exchange seasonal greetings; return me to the time before patterns had yet arisen."
The monk approached and said, "I have a mouth, but it is as if I were mute; that is already enough suffering. Why do you seek a fan for the month of December when I am dead?
The Master raised his staff and made a gesture to strike him. The monk seized the staff and said, "Give me back the principle [of this matter] before you even raised the staff."
The Master said, "Those who follow me shall go with me to the south or north; those who do not follow me shall die staying in the east or west.
[The student] said, "Setting aside for now the matters of following or not following, I request that the Master point out the east, west, south, and north. The Master then struck him.
When Master Piyun arrived and had just entered the abbot’s quarters, the Master asked, "Before you had seen the Elder of Dongyue, how did you act for the sake of sentient beings?
Piyun said, "I saw only clouds rising over the green peaks; who knows of the moon falling into the cold pool? The Master said:
"It is simply like this; it is difficult to find. Yun said, "Is this not the state before one has seen [the truth]? The Master then gave a shout. Yun opened his hands wide.
The Master said, "There is no limit to those who falsely accuse others. Yun covered his ears and left. The Master said, "This fellow has died for good."
Master Majie Benkong addressed the assembly from the high seat: "In these very activities and movements, do they accord with the original patriarch?

If they accord, there is no principle of wasting even a single moment throughout the twelve hours of the day. If they do not accord, then when drinking tea and conversing, one often calls upon [the name of the Buddha]..."
While holding a tea talk, a monk asked, "How can one avoid it being an improper tea talk?
The Master said, "Do you even recognize your own mouth? The monk asked, "What is the mouth? The Master said, "You do not even recognize two pieces of skin.
The monk asked, "What is the original patriarch? The Master said, "Do not rely on your father or mother in front of the assembly. The monk said, "The assembly rejoices."
"But he is leaving. The Master said, "Try to point out the nature of the assembly for me. The monk bowed. The Master said, "He often says that one nature is all natures.
As the monk was about to offer a word in response, the Master said, "You have brought shame upon your lifelong eye of travel."
Question: Setting aside these current words and phrases, I request that you, Master, point directly to the original nature.
The Master said: "How much time has it been since you lost your source? [The student] said: "I have now received the Master’s instruction. The Master said:

"If I were to instruct you, I would then be lost at my own source. [The student] asked: "What, then, is the case? The Master presented this verse: "The mind is the substance of nature; nature is the function of the mind. The mind..."

The nature is one and suchness; who is distinct and who is common? When delusion externally obscures the source, it is difficult to penetrate this very point. From antiquity to the present, ordinary beings and sages alike are like illusions and dreams.
—Master Bensheng.
The Master held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying, "If I hold it up, you immediately apply intellectual reasoning to the moment before it was raised.
If I do not hold it up, you immediately take charge of the moment when it is raised. Tell me, where does this old monk act for others?
At that time, a monk came forward and said, "I dare not arbitrarily create complications. The Master said, "I know that too."
The Acharya did not treat him as anything extraordinary. The monk said, "At low places there is more than enough to level them; at high places, one observes that they are insufficient.
The Master said, "To add knots upon knots. The monk was speechless. The Master said, "Covering the nose while stealing fragrance—this only invites culpability in vain."
Chan Master Shandao of the Stone Chamber went to study under Shitou.
One day, while accompanying him on a mountain excursion, Shitou said, "Cut down those trees in front of me so they will not obstruct my view.
The Master replied, "They will not bring an axe. Shitou then drew his sword and handed it to him upside down. The Master asked, "Why?"
[The Master] said, "However, that end comes. The head [of the staff] asked, "What do you do with that end? At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
One night, the Master was playing with Yangshan under the moon. Yangshan asked, "When this moon is crescent, where does the full form go?
When it is full, where does the crescent form go? The Master said, "When it is crescent, the full form is hidden; when it is full, the crescent..."

The Master was present at Longtan. When Chan Master Chongxin first attained enlightenment, Master Wuheshang resided at Tianwang Temple. The Master’s family lived in the lane adjacent to the temple; his family sold cakes. Every day, the Master...
He presented ten cakes to him. After the Heavenly King had finished eating, he habitually set aside one cake, saying, "I bestow this upon you so that it may provide shade for your descendants.
One day, the Master thought to himself: "The cakes were brought away by me; why has one been returned to me? Is there some other underlying meaning?"
He then went to visit him. The Heavenly King said, "This was brought by you; what fault is there on your part?

Upon hearing this, the Master somewhat understood the profound principle and consequently entered the monastic life, serving diligently at his side. One day, he asked, "Since my arrival, I have not received instruction on the essential point of the mind.
The Heavenly King replied, "From the moment of your arrival, I have never failed to point out the essential point of your mind. The Master...
The Master asked, "Where did you point out [the mind-essence]? The Heavenly King said, "When you brought me tea, I received it for you;

when you brought me food, I accepted it for you; when you bowed in greeting, I lowered my head. Where was the essential point of the mind not pointed out? The Master lowered his head and remained silent for a long while.
The Heavenly King said, "If you see, you see directly right now. Any attempt to deliberate is a deviation. At that moment, the Master attained realization.
He was enlightened. He asked again, "How does one maintain this? Tianwang said, "Wander freely according to one's nature; let go and be expansive in accordance with conditions.
Simply exhaust the ordinary mind; there is no separate realization of the sage."
A monk asked, "Who obtains the pearl within the topknot? The Master said, "One who does not prize or play with it obtains it. The monk asked, "Where is it placed?
The Master said, "If there were a place, tell me where it is."
A nun asked, "How can I go about as a monk? The Master said, "How long has it been since you came here as a nun?
She said, "Has there ever been a time when I was a monk? The Master said, "Who are you right now? She said, "I am currently in the body of a nun;
how could you not recognize me? The Master said, "Who recognizes you?"
Prefect Li Ao asked, "What is true suchness and prajñā? The Master said, "I am true suchness and prajñā.
Li said, "It is my good fortune to have met the Master. The Master said, "These are still words that go beyond the mark."
The Venerable Master Mudou Daoming said:
"I have told you clearly and plainly, yet you still do not understand; how much less could you grasp it if it were covered over?
He further said: "While I have been residing here as abbot, I have never seen a person who is truly 'without affairs' come to me. You all—why [do you act otherwise]?"
He did not approach. At that time, a monk happened to come forward. The Master said, "The Rector is not here.
You take him yourself outside the triple gate and give him twenty blows. The monk asked, "In what way have I erred? The Master said, "To add shackles upon a collar."
The Master saw a monk and said, "This is a case already resolved; I grant you thirty blows. The monk said, "I am like this, Master.
The Master asked, "Why does the Vajra at the entrance of the three gates raise his fist? The monk said, "Even the Vajra is like this. The Master then struck him.
The Abbot entered for an audience. The Master asked, "Are you not the one who lectures on the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi* (Treatise on Consciousness-Only)? He replied, "I dare not say so.

The Master said, "Leaving for India in the morning and returning to Tang China in the evening—do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Hūṃ! Hūṃ! You have failed to observe the five precepts!"
He asked the monk, "Where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "Mount Yang. The Master said, "You do not even observe the five precepts.
The monk said, "In what way am I speaking falsely? The Master said, "A śrāmaṇera does not belong here."
He asked the Sangha Rectifier, "Can you lecture on the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi*? The Rectifier replied, "I dare not say so. In my youth, I once studied the texts.
The Master picked up a sugar cake, split it into two pieces, and said, "What do you make of this? The Rectifier was speechless. The Master said:
"Is it right to call this a sugar cake? Is it not right to call it a sugar cake? The Master said, "It cannot be that one does not call it a sugar cake.

He then called the śrāmaṇera over, saying, "Come here, come here. What do you call this? The śrāmaṇera said, "A sugar cake. The Master said, "You can even lecture on the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi* (Treatise on Consciousness-Only)."
The Master asked the Elder of Wuling, "When one realizes that the tip of a single hair swallows the vast ocean, only then does one know that the great earth is but a single mote of dust.
Elder, what do you say? The Elder said, "To whom are you asking? The Master said, "I am asking you, Elder. The Elder said, "Why do you not acknowledge my words?
The Master said, "If you do not acknowledge my words, then I shall not acknowledge yours."
Question: "What is it like when a single phrase exhausts the matter? The Master said: "Your meaning has fallen. [The student] asked: "Where is it that my meaning has fallen?
The Master said: "Who is there to give thirty blows to?"
A questioner asked, "I am someone who lectures on the scriptures while also traveling as a pilgrim, yet I do not understand the meaning of the teachings.
What should I do? The Master said, "It is truly so; you must confess this as a sincere truth. The questioner said, "I beg the Master for instruction.

The Master said, "If you had not asked, I would have kept my mouth shut and remained silent. Since you have asked, I cannot remain silent. The questioner said, "Please speak, Master. The Master said, "Mind."
[He] did not disappoint others, and his face showed no sign of shame.
A questioner asked: "When one bows high to Śākyamuni but does not prostrate to Maitreya, what is that like? The Master said: "Yesterday someone asked this;
I drove them out. The questioner said: "Does the Master fear that I am not sincere? The Master said: "The staff is not here; it is the broom."
Hengliao gave him thirty blows and asked the monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa. The Master said, "Which seat is Nirvāṇa? The monk was speechless.
The Master asked again, "Where has Kāśyapa gone? The monk said, "I do not know. The Master said, "You liar who speaks empty falsehoods!
Hearing that an old master was difficult to approach, the Master went to visit him in person. As soon as he entered, the old master shouted. The Master snapped his fingers and said, "A double case.
The old master asked, "Where does the fault lie? The Master said, "This wild fox spirit! and then withdrew.

[The Master] ascends the seat and says, "Is the Head Seat here? [The attendant] replies, "He is. [The Master] asks, "Is the Abbot’s Assistant here? [The attendant] replies, "He is. [The Master] asks, "Is the Rector here? [The attendant] replies, "He is."

[The Master] ascends the seat. He says: "There are three distinct sections; we are now at the first. The subsequent text is extensive and shall be entrusted to a future day. He descends from the seat and addresses the assembly:
"When the Great Matter is not yet clarified, it is as if one has lost one’s parents. When the Great Matter has been clarified, it is as if one has lost one’s parents."
Addressing the assembly: I see that Baizhang did not know how to distinguish between good and evil. As soon as the great assembly had gathered, he struck them all at once with his staff.
He then called out to the assembly; when they turned their heads, he said, "What is this? There is no way to converse with you.
Master Huangbo was likewise so. He also called out to the assembly; when they turned their heads, he said, "The moon is like a drawn bow; there will be little rain."
It is somewhat windy; it is still a bit better than that.
A monk asked, "What is the teaching for all generations? The Master said, "Shang Daren, Qiu Yiji."
Question: "What is Chan? The Master said: "A fierce fire frying oil. A monk came for an audience.
The Master asked: "Are you a newcomer? He replied: "I am. The Master said: "Set aside your entanglements for a moment. Do you understand?"

The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Go out yourself, bearing your shackles and presenting your petition. The monk then went out. The Master called, "Come! Come! The monk returned. The Master said, "Come! Come! The monk came forward. The Master said, "I have already finished with you; go and strike the bell for the assembly. The monk went out. The Master said, "This fellow has been here for three days and still does not know how to enter the gate. He then struck him. The monk said, "I am not yet at peace. The Master said, "If you were at peace, you would not be here today. The monk said, "I am not at peace. The Master said, "Why do you not seek peace? The monk said, "I do not know where to seek it. The Master said, "I will tell you: when you see the Buddha, kill the Buddha; when you see the Patriarchs, kill the Patriarchs; when you see the Arhats, kill the Arhats; when you see all sentient beings, kill all sentient beings. When you can act thus, you will attain peace. The monk said, "What about when I do not see them? The Master said, "When you do not see them, you must not fail to see them. The monk said, "How can I avoid failing to see them? The Master said, "If you do not fail to see them, you will not be able to see them. The monk said, "I do not understand. "I am actually asking you where you have come from," the Master said. The monk replied, "Jiangxi. The Master said, "The Abbot of Letan is behind you;
he fears you will speak recklessly. Do you see him? The monk had no reply.
While he was reading the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, a monk asked, "What sūtra are you reading? The Master said, "The Great Radiance Clouds, the Blue Radiance Clouds, and the Purple Radiance Clouds.
He then pointed to the space before him and asked, "What kind of cloud is that over there?
The monk replied, "That is a black cloud to the south. The Master said, "It will surely rain today."
Question: "It is not formed by characters; it is not the eight characters. What sutra passage is this? The Master snapped his fingers once and said, "Do you understand?
He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The infinite superior causes from the lectures and praises above—frogs leap up into the sky."
A earthworm suddenly crossed over the Eastern Sea.
[Later,] he asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk said, "From north of the River. The Master said, "There is a Venerable Zhaozhou there;
have you been there? The monk said, "I have recently left there. The Master said, "What words or phrases did Zhaozhou use to instruct his disciples? The monk—
[The Master] raised the story of the tea-drinking. He then laughed loudly, "Ha-ha! and said, "How shameful! He then asked, "What was Zhaozhou’s meaning?
[The monk] replied, "It was merely a provisional expedient for the occasion. The Master said, "Alas! Zhaozhou has been splashed with a ladle of dung by you! He then struck him.
The Master then asked the novice, "How do you understand this? The novice immediately prostrated himself.
The Master also struck him. The monk went to the novice and asked, "Why did the Master strike you just now?
The novice replied, "If it had not been for me, the Master would not have struck this person."
Master Wushi Lingguan usually kept his door bolted, so few people ever saw him. One day, Xuefeng took the opportunity to knock on the door; the Master opened it.
Feng grabbed him by the chest and asked, "Are you an ordinary person or a sage? The Master spat at him and said, "You wild fox spirit!
He then pushed him out and closed the door. Feng said, "I only wanted to recognize my elder brother."
Xuefeng arrived and knocked on the door. The Master asked, "Who is it? Xuefeng said, "The phoenix chick. The Master asked, "What are you doing here? Xuefeng said, [silently].
He came to devour the old crane. The Master immediately opened the door, seized him, and said, "Speak! Speak! While Feng hesitated, the Master pushed him away and shut the door.

After Feng established his own monastery, he addressed the assembly, saying, "If I had been able to enter the gate of Old Guan at that time, where would you lot—this crew of wine-dregs eaters—have gone to search for me?"

Chan Master Daisuifa Zhen was a man of rare age who attained awakening early in life. He traveled extensively to study under various masters before arriving at the assembly of Dayue, where he remained for several years.

There, he did not eat to fullness nor seek warmth when lying down; he refined his practice through austere asceticism, for which Dayue held him in high esteem. One day, Dayue asked him: "Upādhyāya, while you were..."
"The old monk has never asked a single question here. The Master said, "Where am I to open my mouth?
Wuwei said, "Why not say, 'What is the Buddha? The Master then made a gesture with his hand to cover Wuwei's mouth.
Wuwei sighed and said, "You have truly attained the marrow."
He asked a monk, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to Mount Wutai to pay homage to Samantabhadra.
The Master raised his whisk and said, "Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are both right here. The monk drew a circle, threw it behind him, and then prostrated.
The Master called to his attendant, "Give this monk a bowl of tea."
A monk asked, "What is the singular matter of the Great Sui? The Master said, "East, west, south, and north. Beside the hermitage was a tortoise.
The monk asked, "All sentient beings have skin wrapping their bones; why does this sentient being have bones wrapping its skin?
The Master took his straw sandals and covered them over the tortoise's back. The monk was speechless.
A monk asked Master Lingshu, "What is the house style of the Master? He replied, "A thousand-year-old field has eight hundred owners.
The monk asked, "What is this 'a thousand-year-old field with eight hundred owners'? He replied, "The dilapidated house has no one to repair it."
Chan Master Lingyun Zhiqin was originally at Mount Guiyang.
There, upon seeing peach blossoms, he attained enlightenment. He composed a verse which says: "For thirty years I have sought the seeker of the sword;
Time and again the leaves fall and the branches sprout anew. Since that first glimpse of the peach blossoms, To this very day, [I have known no further change]."

Wuwei did not doubt him. When Guishan examined the verse and interrogated him regarding his realization, it accorded perfectly with his own. He instructed him, saying: "Your awakening has been attained through conditions;
it shall never again be lost. Guard and maintain it well."

Changsheng asked, "Before the primordial chaos was divided, from where did sentient beings come? The Master said, "It is like a pillar of dew conceiving a fetus. He asked, "After the division, what is it like?
The Master said, "It is like a fragment of cloud dotting the vast clarity. He asked, "I wonder, does that vast clarity itself receive the dot?
The Master did not answer. He said, "If so, then sentient beings do not come. The Master also did not answer. He said, "Directly..."
[The student asked: "What is it like when one attains a state that is purely clear and free from a single speck of defilement? The Master said: "This is still the continuous flow of true permanence.

[The student] asked: "What is the continuous flow of true permanence? The Master said: "It is like a mirror that is constantly bright. [The student] asked: "Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said: [Silence].
[The Master] said, "There is. [A monk] asked, "What is the matter that transcends this? The Master said, "Break the mirror and then I will see you.
When the Venerable Xinxing Yan-yang first visited Zhaozhou, he asked, "What is it when one brings nothing forth? Zhaozhou said, "Put it down. The Master [recounted this].
[The Master] said, "Since you have not brought a single thing here, what is there to put down? Dongzhou said, "I cannot put it down; take it away.
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. Thereafter, a snake and a tiger would constantly follow him, and he would give them food from his own hand.
A monk asked Master Duofu of Hangzhou, "What is the single grove of bamboo at Duofu? The Master said, "One stalk, two stalks, leaning.
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Three stalks, four stalks, curved."
Master Xi Mu of Yizhou ascended the hall.
A layman raised his hand and said, "The Master is nothing but a donkey. The Master replied, "I have been mounted by you, old monk.
The man was speechless. Three days later, he returned and said, "Three days ago, I was robbed by bandits."
The Master picked up his staff and drove him out. Later,
when the monk Shiti requested a bath for the Master, the Master said, "Since you do not wash away dust, nor do you wash the body, how will you do it?"
The attendant said, "The Master should go first; I will bring the soap-nuts. The Master laughed heartily.
One day, seeing the attendant carrying his bowl toward the hall, the Master called out to him. The attendant responded, "Yes? The Master asked, "Where are you going?
The attendant replied, "I am going to the hall for the midday meal. The Master said, "How could I not know that you were going to the hall for the midday meal? The attendant— [remained silent].
[The monk] said, "Aside from this, what else would you say? The Master said, "I am simply asking you about your fundamental matter.
The monk said, "If the Master asks about my fundamental matter, I am actually going to the hall for the midday meal. The Master said, "You are not mistaken to serve as my attendant."

When Master Chan Master Liao Ran of Mount Moshan was visited by Master Xiangshan Guankui, [Liao Ran] said, "If we are on equal footing, you shall stay; otherwise, I shall overturn your meditation seat."
He then entered the hall. The Master sent an attendant to ask: "Have you come to the mountain for the sake of sightseeing, or have you come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma?
Xixi replied, "I have come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma. The Master then ascended the seat. Xixi went up to pay his respects. The Master asked, "Where did you depart from today, Upādhyāya?"
[Daowu] said, "A crossroads. The Master said, "Why do you not cover it over? Xixi had no reply. He then prostrated and asked, "What is Mount Mo?
The Master said, "It does not show its crown. He asked, "Who is the master of Mount Mo? The Master said, "Neither male nor female form.
Xixi then gave a shout and said, "Why do you not transform away? The Master said, "I am neither a spirit nor a ghost; what would there be to transform? Xixi [remained silent].
Thereupon, he took the teaching to heart. He remained at Yuantou for three years.
A nun named Jiaqi came to see Master Jinghua Juzhi;
she wore a bamboo hat and held a monk’s staff. She circumambulated the master three times and said, "If you can speak the Way, I shall remove my hat."
[The Master] held up his straw rain-hat. He asked this three times, but the nun gave no reply and simply departed. The Master said, "The sun is already late; why do you not stay for a moment?

The nun replied, "If you could speak the Way, I would stay. Again, the Master had no answer. After the nun had gone, the Master sighed and said, "Though I possess the physical form of a man, I lack the spirit of a man.
It would be better for me to abandon this hermitage and travel to various regions to seek instruction."
He then went to seek out his acquaintances. That night, a mountain deity told him, "You need not leave this place; an incarnate Bodhisattva will arrive.

Later, when Dharma Master Tiantong arrived at the hermitage, the Master went out to welcome and pay his respects. Tiantong held up one finger to indicate the truth, and the Master attained great enlightenment on the spot.
From then on, whenever students came to inquire about the Way, the Master would simply raise one finger and offer nothing else by way of instruction.
There was a young attendant boy who, whenever he saw someone asking him a question, would respond by pointing his finger upward.
People said to the Master, "Master, this boy also understands the Buddha-dharma; whenever anyone asks him something, he always points his finger just as you do.

One day, the Master secretly tucked a small knife into his sleeve and asked the boy, "I have heard that you understand the Buddha-dharma—is it true? The boy replied, "Yes. The Master said, "As for..."
"What is the Buddha? A young boy raised his finger. The Master cut off the boy's finger with a blade. The boy cried out and ran away.
The Master called to the boy; the boy turned his head back. The Master asked, "What is the Buddha? The boy raised his hand, and no longer saw his finger.
He attained sudden and great enlightenment. As the Master was about to pass away, he said to the assembly, "I have obtained the 'finger-pointing Zen' of Tianlong for my entire life."
"Never exhausted.
While Chan Master Yangshan Huiji Tongzhi was seated, a monk stood on one foot and said, "The twenty-eight patriarchs of India did likewise; so too did those of the Tang land."
The Sixth Patriarch was also like this; the elder monks of the world were also like this; I too am like this.
The Master descended from his meditation seat and struck him with four blows of the rattan cane.
The Master said to the first seat: "When you do not think of good and do not think of evil—at this very moment, what is it?
The seat replied: "At this very moment, it is where I lay down my body and life. The Master said: "Why do you not ask the old monk? The seat replied:
"At this very moment, I do not see that there is a 'monk'. The Master said: "You support my teaching, yet you cannot make it rise."
Chan Master Xiangyan Zhixian went to study under Master Guishan.
Guishan asked him, "I have heard that when you were with the late Master Baizhang, you could answer ten questions with one and a hundred questions with ten.
This cleverness and sharp intelligence of yours—this intellectual understanding and conceptual consciousness—is the very root of birth and death, and of your parents."
"Before it has arisen, try to utter a single word! When the Master was thus questioned, he was left utterly bewildered.

Returning to his quarters, he searched through the texts he had studied over the years from beginning to end for a single phrase with which to respond, but in the end, he could find none. He then sighed to himself:
"Painted cakes cannot satisfy hunger. He repeatedly requested that Guishan explain this to him.
Guishan said, "If I were to explain it to you, you would later curse me away. What I have explained is mine; it ultimately has nothing to do with you.
The Master then burned all the texts he had previously studied and said, "In this life, I shall not study the Buddha-dharma. I will simply be a long-lived layman."
As a monk who received rice gruel and meals, he was spared the mental toil of labor. He then wept as he took his leave of Guishan and traveled to Nanyang.

There, beholding the remains of National Teacher Huizhong, he settled there to reside. One day, while clearing away vegetation, he happened to throw a piece of tile or rubble that struck a bamboo and produced a sound.
Suddenly, he attained awakening. He immediately returned, bathed, burned incense, and prostrated from afar toward Guishan, praising him: "The Master’s great compassion is a debt of grace."
It surpasses even one's parents. Had you explained it to me at that time, how could there have been what has happened today?

There is a verse that says: With a single blow, all that was known is forgotten; No further cultivation or practice is required. Every movement reveals the ancient path; One does not fall into the trap of silent stillness.
"Leaving no trace anywhere; his deportment transcends sound and form. Those who have attained the Way in all directions all say he possesses the highest capacity.
When Guishan heard this, he said to Yangshan, "This boy has penetrated through. Yangshan replied, "This was merely composed by means of mental ingenuity and conscious effort.
Wait until I have personally examined him myself. Later, when Yangshan saw the Master, he said, "The Master praised him."

The Master said, "Disciple, you have clarified the Great Matter. Try to explain it for me. The Master recited the previous verse. Yang said, "This was merely accomplished through the retention of past habituation.
If you have attained true enlightenment, speak further on it. The Master then recited another verse: "Last year’s poverty was not yet true poverty;
this year’s poverty is only then true poverty. Last year’s poverty still left room enough to stick in a single awl; this year’s poverty—"

Yangshan said, "There is not even a needle. Dongshan looked up and said, "I grant that you, my junior brother, have understood the Tathāgata-dhyāna, but as for the Patriarchal-dhyāna, you have not even dreamed of it.
The Master (Yangshan) then offered this verse: "I have a single function; with a blink of an eye, I look at him. If a person does not understand, call him a novice monk (śrāmaṇera).
Yangshan then reported to Guishan, "I am glad that my junior brother Xian has understood the Patriarchal-dhyāna."
Ascending the hall, he said: "If we discuss this matter, it is like a person climbing a tree, with a branch in his mouth, yet his feet do not tread on the branches and his hands do not grasp them.
Suddenly, someone below asks: 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
If he does not answer him, he violates the questioner's intent; if he does answer him, he loses his life. At such a time, what is to be done?"
"It is attained. At that time, there was the Elder Huatou who stepped forward from the assembly and said, "I do not ask about when he was on the tree;
please, Master, speak of it before he had climbed the tree. The Master then let out a great laugh.
The Zen Master Hongyin of Mount Jing invited the Elder Furi to visit him.
The Master asked, "I have heard that you, Elder, have been transforming the people of this region alone; for what reason do you now travel to the mountain peak?
Furi replied, "The bright moon hangs in the sky; the ice and frost do not grow cold of their own accord. The Master said, "Is this not the Elder's [true state]?"
“Family style? There is none. Dayue said, “A thousand peaks rise steeply; within them lies a precious moon. The Master said, “This is still merely literary expression.
What is the family style of the patriarchs? Dayue said, “Today we fortunately meet the Buddha. Dayue then asked, “Regarding ‘the hidden and secret, the complete and true’:
people know it exists, yet they cannot speak of it. This is too much of a pity for those who are innocent; people know it exists, yet they cannot speak of it.”

"You have spoken. Yet these two paths are still merely the places where people of this age ascend and descend. I do not know how the Master speaks—speaking from the personal experience, speaking for oneself, or how one speaks.
The Master said, "In my house, where there is a way to speak, there is nothing to be spoken. Dayu said, "On the path of the Tathāgata, there is no partiality or crookedness;
please, then, let us harmonize a single performance of the profound sound. The Master said, "Let the two wheels shine upon each other at will; the azure pond..."
"Beyond the clouds, there is no connection. Dayu said, "Tell those countless white-haired guests: this time, young men, do not return to your hometowns.
The Master said, "Old and young are of the same kind; there is neither partiality nor aversion. On the mysterious path of my house, let there be no divergence.
Dayu said, "A single word settles the empire; for whom are these four lines proclaimed? The Master said, "You say there are three or four; I say they are within that very midst."
"One is also non-existent. The Master therefore spoke in verse: "East and west do not look back; south and north, with whom would they remain?
You say there are three or four; I say one is also non-existent."

A monk asked, "What is it like when the breath is stilled like ash? The Master said, "It is still the effortful achievement of people of this age. The monk asked, "What is it like after that achievement?
The Master said, "The farmer tills the field but does not sow. The monk asked, "Ultimately, what is it like? The Master said, "When the grain is ripe, he does not go to the market."
The Senior Monk Quanming of Xuzhou previously asked Shishuang, "What is it like when a single hair pierces through all the holes?
Shishuang said, "You must go for ten thousand years. Quanming asked, "What is it like after ten thousand years? Shishuang said, "Passing the imperial examination is up to you to pass;
excelling above the crowd is up to you to excel. Later, he asked the Master, "What is it like when a single hair pierces through all the holes? The Master [replied].
[The Master] said: "As for 'shining boots,' let them shine; as for 'bearing fruit,' let you bear it.
A monk asked: "What is long? The Master said: "Not even a thousand sages can measure it. [The monk] asked: "What is short? The Master said:
"A gnat’s eye cannot hold it all. The monk did not accept this and departed. He then reported this to Shishuang.
Shishuang said, "It is precisely because you are too close to the actual reality. The monk then asked Shishuang, "What is long?
Shishuang said, "It is not bent or crooked. He asked, "What is short? Shishuang said, "In the game of double-six, one does not shout 'Hail!'"
Master Jingshan Shenying once questioned Master Xingxiu Sheng while traveling on pilgrimage: "It does not fall within the realm of numbers or quantity; please, Master, speak.
The Master held up his prayer beads and said, "Are these falling or not? Sheng said, "The round beads with three holes—everyone knows about them. Please [speak further]."
The Master completed the previous story and struck him. Xing brushed his sleeves and left. The Master said, "Thirty years from now, you will go away beating your breast and weeping aloud.
After Xing took up residence, he addressed the assembly, saying, "When I was at Mount Ding thirty years ago, I was thoroughly deceived by him; it was no small matter."

After the Master Mihu of Jingzhao’s Seven Masters had completed his period of study, he returned to his home temple. An elder there asked him: "When the well-rope is cut in the moonlight, people call it a snake;
I wonder, when the Seven Masters see the Buddha, what do they call him? The Master said: "If there were a seeing of a Buddha, that would be the same as..."
"Sentient beings. The elder said, "A peach pit from a thousand years ago.

When Wang Jingchu, the Attendant-in-Ordinary, was attending to his official duties, Master Mi arrived. The Attendant held up his brush and showed it to him; Master Mi said, "Can you still judge what is empty?"
"Is he still here? Gong threw down his brush and entered the residence, never to emerge again. Mi became suspicious.
The next day, he sent the Drum Mountain *gongyang* master to enter and probe his intentions; Mi also followed him there, hiding behind a screen to eavesdrop.
As soon as the *gongyang* master sat down, he asked, "Yesterday, Master Mi, I do not understand what you said that caused you to cease seeing me."
The Official said, "A lion bites a man; a hound chases a clod. Upon hearing these words, Xuefeng immediately realized his former error and hurried out.
Baizhang laughed heartily and said, "I understand! I understand! The Official said, "It is not that you do not understand;
try to say it for me. Xuefeng said, "Please, Attendant, bring it forth. The Official then held up a single chopstick. Xuefeng said, "This wild fox spirit! The Official said, "..."
This man is thoroughgoing.
From the *Imperial Selection of the Recorded Sayings of Successive Chan Masters*, Volume II:
Chan Master Linji Yixuan.
The Master questioned Huangbo about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma; he asked three times and was struck three times.

When the Master took his leave of Huangbo, Huangbo said, "There is no need for you to go elsewhere. Go directly to Dayu at Tancheng in Gaoyang; he will surely explain it for you. The Master arrived at Dayu’s place.
Dayu asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come from Huangbo. Dayu asked, "What words did Huangbo say?"
The Master said, "I asked about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma three times and was struck three times. I do not know whether I have committed an offense or not.
Yunyu said, "Huangbo’s heart of compassionate care was so earnest that he brought you to a state of utter exhaustion for your sake."

He came back here again to ask whether he had committed an offense or not. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and said, "So, it turns out Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma is nothing more than this.
Yunyu grabbed him by the collar and said, "You bed-wetting little devil!
Just now you were asking whether you had committed an offense or not, and now you say Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma is nothing more than this. What principle have you seen?"
"Quick way! Quick way! The Master struck Daoyu three times under the ribs. Daoyu pushed him away and said, "Your teacher is Huangbo;
it has nothing to do with me. The Master took his leave of Daoyu and returned to Huangbo.
One day, while Huangbo was engaged in communal labor, the Master followed behind him. Huangbo turned his head and saw that the Master was empty-handed, so he asked, "Where is the mattock?
The Master said, "Someone has taken it away. Huangbo said, "Come closer; let us deliberate on a matter together. The Master then drew near.
Huangbo held up the mattock and said, "Only this! Can anyone in the world pick it up?"
He could not pick it up. The Master reached out his hand and seized it, holding it aloft and saying, "Why is it now in my hands?
Baizhang said, "Today there is someone else who has been invited for communal labor," and he immediately returned to the monastery.
One day, as the Master was sitting before the Sangha Hall, he saw Huangbo approaching and immediately closed his eyes.
Huangbo then made a gesture of longing and returned to the Abbot’s quarters. The Master followed him to the quarters to pay his respects.
The Head Seat was standing in attendance by Huangbo’s side when Huangbo said, "Although this monk is but a junior, he knows that there is such a matter. The Head Seat said, "The old master..."
Yet his heels still do not touch the ground; he nevertheless corroborates this young man. Huangbo then slaps himself on the mouth.
The Head Seat says, "If you know, then you have attained it."
The Master was sleeping in the Sangha Hall. Huangbo entered the hall and saw him; he struck the head of the meditation board once with his staff.
The Master raised his head, and seeing it was Huangbo, he went back to sleep. Huangbo struck the head of the board again, then went up to the upper section.
Seeing the Head Seat practicing zazen, he said, "The junior monks in the lower section are actually practicing zazen; why are you here indulging in such discursive thoughts?"
Zuo said, "What is this old fellow doing? Ba struck the wooden board once more and went out.
Later, Huangbo entered the kitchen and asked the rice steward, "What are you doing? The steward replied, "I am sorting the rice for the monks' meal.
Huangbo asked, "How much will they eat at one sitting? The steward replied, "Two shi and five dou. Huangbo said, "Is that not too much? The steward replied, "It still..."
Fearing that [Huangbo] was short of words, Baizhang struck him. Baizhang then brought the case up to the Master (Dongshan). The Master said, "I shall examine this old fellow with you.

As soon as they arrived and were standing in attendance, Baizhang recounted the previous conversation. The Master said, "The head cook does not understand; please, Preceptor, provide a turn of phrase on his behalf."
Huangbo said, "Just bring it forth. The Master said, "Is this not too much? Huangbo said, "Tomorrow you shall have another serving.
The Master said, "What do you mean by 'tomorrow'? I will eat it right now," and he followed this by giving Huangbo a slap.
Huangbo said, "This madman comes here again to pull at the tiger's whiskers! The Master let out a shout and went out.
The Master went up Mount Huangbo during the half-month of the summer retreat. Seeing Huangbo reading a sutra, he said, "I thought you were a man of substance;

it turns out you are just an old monk who chants 'Oṃ' like a black bean. He stayed for several days and then took his leave. Huangbo said, "You arrived after the summer retreat began; why did you not stay until its end?
The Master replied, "I came briefly to pay my respects to the Master. Huangbo then struck him and drove him away.
The Master traveled several li and, suspecting this matter, returned and spent the summer there. Later, he took his leave of Baizhang. Baizhang asked, "Where are you going?
The Master replied, "Not south of the River; I am going back north of the River. Baizhang struck him. The Master seized him and gave him a slap.
Baizhang laughed loudly and called for an attendant to bring the meditation board and desk of the late master, Baizhang. The Master said, "Attendant," [and gestured to take them].
"Bring me some fire," [the Master] said. Baizhang replied, "Not so. You simply take it with you; later, you shall sit and cut off the tongues of everyone under heaven.
When he arrived at the place of Master Ping of Sanfeng, Ping asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "I have come from Huangbo. Ping said, "Huangbo..."
"What words did Huangbo have? The Master said: "Last night, the Golden Ox met with calamity; even until now, no trace of him is seen. Ping said:
"The golden wind blows through the jade flute; who is it that knows this sound? The Master said: "It passes straight through ten thousand layers of barriers."
"Not dwelling within the azure sky. Fengxue Ping said, "Your question is far too lofty. The Master said, "A golden phoenix born of a dragon breaks through the azure lapis lazuli.
Ping said, "Sit for a moment and drink some tea," and then asked, "Where have you recently come from? The Master said, [Heavenly Eye].
Longguang. Pingshan asked, "How have you been lately, Longguang? The Master then went out.
Upon arriving at Fenglin, Fenglin said, "May I ask you a question? The Master said, "Why do you dig into your own flesh to create a sore?"
Lin said: "The ocean moon is clear and without reflection; the wandering fish alone is deluded. The Master said: "Since the ocean moon has no reflection, how can the wandering fish be deluded?
Lin said: "Observing the wind, one knows the waves arise; gazing at the water, the wild sail drifts away. The Master said:

"The solitary hare-marked moon shines alone as mountains and rivers fall silent; with one long啸 (shout), heaven and earth turn autumnal. Lin said: "Let him unfurl his three-inch tongue to sweep across the heavens."
"Ground. [The Master said: "Try to speak on the spot. The Master said: "When meeting a swordsman on the road, you must present your sword;
if you are not a poet, do not offer a poem. Lin then ceased. The Master then offered this verse: "The Great Way is beyond sameness; It may lead west or east as one pleases."
A spark from flint cannot reach it; a flash of lightning cannot penetrate it.
Upon arriving at Dàcí, he found Cí sitting within the abbot’s quarters. The Master asked, "What is it like when you dwell serenely in the abbot’s room? Cí replied:
The cold pines are one color; a thousand years of separation. The wild old man plucks a flower; ten thousand nations bask in spring.

The Master said, "Ancient and modern, eternally transcended is the essence of perfect wisdom. The three mountains lock away ten thousand layers of barriers. Cui then gave a shout. The Master also shouted. Cui asked, "What is this?"
The Master shook out his sleeves and departed.
Upon arriving at Minghua, Minghua asked, "What is the purpose of this coming and going? The Master replied, "I am simply intent on wearing my straw sandals through."
Huayan asked, "Ultimately, how is it? The Master said, "Even this old fellow does not recognize the 'head' of the conversation.
Upon arriving at Niu-tou, the Ox saw the Master coming; he gripped his staff crosswise and sat perched across the doorway.
The Master struck the staff three times with his hand and then returned to the first seat in the hall. When the Ox came down and saw him, he asked, "Now, regarding guest and host..."
They looked at one another; each maintained his dignified demeanor. [The Master] asked, "Where have you come from, Elder? You are far too impolite. The Master said, "What did the Old Monk say?
As the Ox was about to open its mouth, the Master struck it with his sitting cloth (*zuoju*). The Ox made a gesture of falling over, and the Master struck it again with the sitting cloth.
The Ox said, "Today I am not in the right position for this," and then returned to the Abbot’s quarters.
The Master resided at Linji in Zhenzhou, where disciples gathered like clouds. One day, he said to the two senior monks Puhua and Kefu, "I wish to establish the school of Huangbo here;
you two must assist me. The two replied, "We shall respectfully depart," and went downstairs.
Three days later, Puhua came back up and asked, "What did the Master say three days ago? The Master—
He struck him immediately. Three days later, Ke-fu came up and asked, "Why did you strike Puhua three days ago?
The Master struck him as well and said, "At times a single shout is like the Vajra King’s precious sword; at times a single shout is like a crouching lion."
"Disciple, sometimes a single shout is like a probe-stick or a blade of grass in the wind; sometimes a single shout is not used as a shout.
How do you understand this? The monk hesitated, and the Master immediately shouted.
During the ascent to the hall, the two head seats of the two halls met and simultaneously let out a shout. A monk asked the Master, "Is there still guest and host?

The Master said, "Guest and host are clearly distinct. The Master called to the assembly, saying, "If you wish to understand the Linji phrase of guest and host, go ask the two head seats in the hall."
Addressing the assembly: At times I first manifest illumination and subsequently employ function; at times I first employ function and subsequently manifest illumination;

at times illumination and function occur simultaneously; and at times illumination and function do not occur simultaneously. When illumination precedes function, there is a person present. When function precedes illumination, there is a Dharma present.
When illumination and function are simultaneous, I drive the ox of the plowman and snatch the food from the hungry man; I strike the bone to extract the marrow.

They strike with the needle and the awl with great severity. Illumination and function do not occur simultaneously; there is questioning and answering, the establishment of guest and host, and the blending of water and mud.
To respond to capacities and engage beings—if one is a person of transcendent measure—one should "lift up and go" even before the question is raised;
this would still be slightly better.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Upon this lump of red flesh there is a True Person of No-Rank who constantly enters and exits through the gate of your face.
Those of you who have not yet realized this—look, look! At that time, a monk came forward and asked, "What is the True Person of No-Rank?
The Master stepped down from his meditation seat, seized the monk, and said, "Speak! Speak! As the monk hesitated, the Master pushed him away and said, "The True Person of No-Rank is right here!"
“What is this dried piece of dung? Having said this, he returned to the abbot’s quarters.
A monk asked, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master held up his whisk. The monk then shouted. The Master then struck him.
Again, a monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master also held up his whisk. The monk then gave a shout;
the Master also shouted. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him and said, "O assembly, those who seek the Dharma do not shrink from losing body or life.
At the place of my late teacher Huangbo, I asked three times about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, and three times—"
[The Master] struck him. It was like being brushed by a stalk of mugwort. "Now I am thinking of giving you another blow; who will step forward to deliver it?
At that time, a monk came forward and said, "I will deliver it. The Master handed him his staff. As the monk reached out to take it, the Master struck him immediately.
An old veteran monk came to visit and asked, "Is it right to prostrate, or is it right not to prostrate?
The Master gave a shout. The veteran bowed. The Master said, "What a fine grass-thief! The veteran said, "Thief! Thief! and went out. The Master said, "Do not say that there was nothing to it.
At that time, the Head Seat was standing in attendance. The Master asked, "Was there any fault? The Seat said, "There was. The Master said, "The guest..."
"The host's house has a fault; the guest's house has a fault. [The monk] said, "Both have faults. The Master asked, "Where does the fault lie?
The monk then went out. The Master said, "Do not say that all is well."
Dajue arrived for an audience. The Master raised his whisk. Dajue spread out his sitting mat. The Master threw down the whisk.
Dajue folded up his sitting mat and went to the hall. The assembly said, "Is this monk perhaps the Master’s relative?
He neither prostrates nor receives a blow. When the Master heard this, he ordered Dajue to be summoned. When Dajue arrived, the Master said, "The assembly says that you neither prostrate nor..."
"Receive the staff. [The monk] thought, "Perhaps this is because he is an acquaintance of the Elder," and so he respectfully took his leave and went down.
The Master asked the head of the monastery, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from selling yellow millet in the prefecture.
The Master said, "Did you sell it all? He replied, "I sold it all. The Master drew a line with his staff and said, "Can you sell this as well?"
The Abbot shouted; the Master struck him. When the Head Cook arrived, the Master brought up the previous conversation.
The Cook said, "The Abbot of the Monastery does not understand the Master’s meaning. The Master asked, "And what about you? The Cook bowed; the Master struck him as well.
Once, when Puhua was attending a donor’s vegetarian feast along with the Master, the Master asked, "A hair swallows the vast ocean; a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru.
Is this the wondrous function of spiritual powers, or is it simply the natural state of things? Puhua kicked over the dining table. The Master said, "How crude!
Puhua replied, "What kind of place is this, where you speak of the coarse and the subtle? The next day, they again attended a feast together.
The Master asked again, "How does today's offering compare to yesterday's? The Transformation once more kicked over the rice table.

The Master said, "It has been obtained, indeed, but you are far too crude. The Transformation gave a shout and said, "Blind fellow! What 'coarse' or 'fine' do you speak of regarding the Buddha-dharma? Thereupon, the Master stuck out his tongue.
The Master was sitting with the Elder of the Wooden Pagoda at Heyang inside the hearth in the monks' hall.
He remarked, "Puhua spends every day in the streets and markets acting like a madman; I do not know whether he is an ordinary man or a sage.
Before he had even finished speaking, Puhua entered. The Master immediately asked him, "Are you an ordinary man or a sage? Puhua replied, "You tell me first whether I am an ordinary man."
"This is holy. The Master then gave a shout. Puhua pointed his finger and said, "The bridegroom from Heyang;
the old woman’s Zen of the wooden pagoda; Linji’s little page—he alone possesses a single eye. The Master said, "You thief! Puhua said, "Thief! Thief!"
He then went out.
One day, while Puhua was eating raw vegetables in front of the Sangha Hall, the Master saw him and said, "You look very much like a donkey.
Puhua then brayed like a donkey. The Master said to the steward, "Prepare a fine supply of fodder. Puhua replied, "Shaoshi [Mount Shaoshi]."
People do not recognize him. He has come again to Jinling. Linji’s single eye opens for people everywhere.
The Master asked Xingshan, "What is the white ox on the open ground? Xingshan said, "Hūṃ! Hūṃ! The Master said, "Mute beast!
Xingshan said, "What about you, Elder? The Master said, "You beast!"

Magu asked, "Of the Great Compassionate One’s thousand hands and eyes, which one is the true eye? The Master seized him and said, "Of the Great Compassionate One’s thousand hands and eyes, what is the true eye?
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Magu dragged the Master down from the meditation seat and sat back down himself.

The Master asked after his well-being, saying, "I trust you have been well? Guo hesitated to respond, whereupon the Master gave a shout, pulled him down from the meditation seat, and sat back down himself.
Guo then departed.
This was Zen Master Qingzhu of Shishuang.
The Master arrived at Mt. Mui and served as the rice steward. One day, while sifting rice, Mui said, "This is the donor’s rice;
do not scatter it. The Master replied, "I shall not scatter it. Mui picked up a single grain from the ground and asked, "You say you will not scatter it, but what is this?
The Master did not answer. Mui spoke again, "Do not underestimate this single grain; hundreds of thousands of grains all come from it."
"This one grain arises. The Master said, "Hundreds and thousands of grains arise from this one grain. I wonder, from where does this one grain arise?
Muzhou laughed heartily and returned to his quarters. That evening, Muzhou ascended the hall and said to the assembly: "Great assembly," [he continued].
"There are insects in the rice; everyone, look well.

This was said because a monk had come from Dongshan. The Master asked, "What words or phrases did the Master have for instructing his disciples? [The monk] replied, "At the conclusion of the summer retreat, he ascended the hall and said:
'In early autumn and at the end of summer, brothers, whether you go east or west, you must head toward ten thousand miles where there is not a single inch [of ground to tread upon].'"
He went to a place where there was no grass. After a long while, he asked, "How would you go about it in a place where there are not even an inch of grass for ten thousand miles?
The Master said, "Has anyone offered a response? He replied, "No. The Master said, "Why do you not say, 'As soon as one goes out the door, it is already grass'?"
The Master was inside the abbot’s quarters. A monk asked from outside the window, "When we are but a few feet apart, why do I not see the Master's countenance?
The Master said, "The entire world has never hidden it. The monk went to Xuefeng and asked, "What is the meaning of 'the entire world has never hidden it'?
Xuefeng said, "Where is it not Shishuang? Upon hearing this, the Master said, "What is this old fellow dying for?"
"Urgent! Hearing this, Feng said, "This old monk has committed a transgression.
A monk asked, "From three thousand *li* away, I have heard from afar that there is one at Shishuang who 'does not look back' (*bùgù*). The Master said, "Indeed.

The monk asked, "As for the myriad phenomena being clearly manifest—does this constitute looking back or not? The Master said, "I say it does not startle the multitude. The monk asked, "'Not startling the multitude'—"
[The Master said: "It is united with the myriad phenomena. How is it that it does not look back? The Master said:
"Pervading the entire realm, it has never been hidden. Yun’gai asked: "I do not ask about the time when all ten thousand doors are closed;

what about when all ten thousand doors are open? The Master said: "What is the matter within the hall? [Yun’gai] said: "No one can receive him. The Master said: "You speak quite well, indeed. Yet even so—"
[The Master] said, "I have attained it to eight or nine parts. The monk asked, "I do not yet understand; how would you say it, Preceptor? The Master said, "No one recognizes him.
He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk said, "I have come from [where the Master] himself spoke. The Master drew a line before him and said, "You have pierced your own feet."
"Coming like this—have you yet scrutinized this? He replied, "I have not scrutinized it. The Master said, "Your patched robe is so thick; why then can you not scrutinize this?
He replied, "Although my patched robe is thick, what can I do? I simply cannot scrutinize this.
The Master said, "If that is so, then even the seven Buddhas appearing in the world could not save you. He asked, "Why say more?"
"The seven Buddhas and the thousand Buddhas appearing in the world cannot save me," said the monk. The Master said, "How utterly deluded you are!
The monk said, "What can be done about it? The Master said, "Go to the meditation hall. The monk said, "Yes. Yes."
Addressing the assembly: For those of initial capacity who have not yet encountered the Great Matter, one must first recognize the head;

then the tail will follow of its own accord. Shushan Ren came to attend and asked, "What is the head? The Master said, "You must simply know that it exists. [Ren] asked, "What is the tail? The Master said, "Exhausting the present moment.
[Ren] asked, "What is it like when there is a head but no tail? The Master said, "Even if you could spit out gold, what would you do with it?"
[The monk] asked, "What is it like when there is a tail but no head? The Master said, "There is still something upon which he relies.
[The monk] asked, "What is it like when the head and tail are perfectly matched? The Master said, "Even if he does not form such a conceptual understanding, I still do not grant him my approval."

One day, when Chan Master Jianyuan Zhongxing was seated in his quarters, Master Bao’ai came to visit him. As soon as Bao’ai arrived, the Master rolled up the curtain and remained seated within the abbot’s room.
Upon seeing this, Bao’ai lowered the curtain and returned to the guest seat. The Master then instructed an attendant to deliver a message, saying, "The Elder has come from afar."
"Not yet. "There is still a gap between the ferry crossings. Gai seized the abbot and gave him a slap. The abbot said, "There is no need to strike me;
there is the Head Monk (the Master) present. Gai said, "It is precisely because there is that old fellow, the Head Monk, that I am striking you.
The abbot returned and reported this to the Master. The Master said, "There is still a gap between the ferry crossings."

Under the guidance of Chan Master Jia Shan Shanhui, a monk from his assembly went to Shishuang. Upon entering the gate, he said, "I hope you are well. Shishuang replied, "There is no need for that, *dàlǐ* (venerable).
The monk said, "In that case, then take care. He then went to Yantou and likewise said, "I hope you are well. Yantou simply sighed twice.
The monk said, "In that case, take care. Just as he turned to leave, the Master said, "Though you are but a junior, you are indeed capable of managing this.
The monk returned and recounted the exchange to the Master. The next day, the Master ascended the hall and called out, "The master who came from Shishuang and Yantou yesterday, come forward!
He then had him recount the previous conversation exactly as it happened. When the monk had finished, the Master said, "Does the assembly still..."
"Do you understand? If no one speaks, I shall speak without sparing even my two eyebrows. He then said:
"Although Shishuang possesses the sword that kills, he lacks the sword that gives life. Yantou, however, possesses both the sword that kills and the sword that gives life."
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "For twenty years I have lived on this mountain, yet I have never once raised a single matter concerning the School of the Patriarchs.
A monk asked, "I have heard the Master say that for twenty years you have lived on this mountain and have never raised a single matter concerning the School of the Patriarchs—is this true?
The Master replied, "It is true. The monk then overturned the meditation platform, and the Master ceased speaking. On the following day, he went out for communal labor and dug a pit.
He dug a pit and ordered his attendant to invite the monk from the previous day, saying: "For twenty years, this old monk has spoken meaningless words.
Today, I request you, Venerable Sir, to beat me to death and bury me in this pit. I say it again, I request it!
If you do not beat me to death, you must beat yourself to death and bury yourself in the pit before you may leave. That monk returned to the hall and packed his belongings.
[The Master] went into seclusion. Head Seat Houtou came for an audience. The Master asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Hunan. The Master said, "Have you been to Shishuang?
He replied, "I passed through his main road; how could I not have reached him? The Master said, "I have heard that Shishuang has a 'ball' koan. Is it so?"
"No. The Master said, "Even you, Reverend, must look with urgent eyes before you succeed. The Master asked, "What is the ball? He replied, "It cannot leap out.
The Master asked, "What is the mallet? He replied, "It has no hands or feet. The Master said, "Go for now;
I have not yet met you, O *dārala* (junior). The next day, he ascended the seat. The Master asked, "Was the one who arrived yesterday here yesterday? The head monk replied, "He is here."
Xuefeng stepped forward and responded. The Master said, "There is no dharma before the eyes; the meaning lies right before the eyes. It is not a dharma of the present moment;
it is not something reached by the ears or the eyes. Xuefeng said, "Though I ask today, it is still not it. The Master said, "The crescent moon is difficult to clarify."
"It has nothing to do with heaven or earth. Tou said, "Don't be so agitated," and he made a gesture as if to overturn the meditation seat. The Master said, "Now, proceed slowly."
"Where have you offended the Elder? Tou raised his fist and said, "Can you still withstand this before your eyes?
The Master said, "An adept! An adept! Tou then made a gesture as if to overturn the meditation seat. The Master said, "Everyone, look at this warrior!
As for the deployment of the school’s gate and style, I am not his equal; but as for discourse that penetrates the ultimate principle—"
He was also one rank above this mountain monk.
When Chan Master Deshan Xuanjian was carrying the *Longquan Shuchao* out of Sichuan, he encountered an old woman selling cakes on the road to Linyang. Because of this—
He rested his shoulders and bought some cakes for refreshment. The woman pointed to the bundle and asked, "What text is this?
The Master said, "The *Commentary on the Blue Dragon* (*Qinglong shuchao*). The woman asked, "Which sutra do you lecture upon? The Master said, "The *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
The woman said, "I have a question. If you can answer it, I will give you these refreshments; if you cannot answer it, you had better go elsewhere. The *Vajracchedikā* says: 'Passing over...'"
"The past mind cannot be apprehended; the present mind cannot be apprehended; the future mind cannot be apprehended.
I do not know which mind the Venerable One is pointing to. The Master remained silent.
When the Master arrived at Longtan, he ascended the Dharma Hall and said, "I have long heard of Dragon Pond; yet now that I have come, neither the pond is seen nor does the dragon appear.
Longtan straightened his body and said, "You have truly arrived at Dragon Pond. The Master was speechless and subsequently took up residence there.
One night, while standing in attendance, Tan said, "It is deep in the night; why do you not go out? The Master replied with a respectful "I take my leave" and departed.
He then returned and said, "It is dark outside. Tan lit a paper candle and passed it to him. As the Master was about to receive it, Tan blew it out.
At this, the Master attained great enlightenment and prostrated himself. Tan asked, "What have you seen? The Master said, "From now on, henceforth..."
"I do not doubt that this is the tongue of an old monk of the world. Tan said to the assembly, "Among you there is a man whose teeth are like sword-trees and whose mouth is like a blood-basin;
he cannot be turned back by a single blow of the staff. In time, he will stand upon the summit of a solitary peak and propagate my Way.
The Master then piled the commentaries and treatises before the Dharma Hall, raised a torch, and said, "Exhausting all mysteries..."
[The Master] said, "If one were to place a single hair in the vast void, it would be like exhausting the world's pivotal mechanisms; it is as if a single drop has been cast into a great abyss.
Thereupon he burned [the documents]. The Master arrived at Mt. Mui and, carrying a double mat, ascended the Dharma Hall. He walked from west to east and from east to west, saying, "There is..."
"Is there? Is there? While [Zhaozhou] was sitting on the mountain, he did not look back at all. The Master said, "No, no," and then went out.
Upon reaching the entrance of the gate, he said, "Even so, one must not be careless. He then assumed his full ceremonial demeanor and entered again to meet him.

As soon as he stepped across the threshold, he raised his sitting cloth (kashō) and said, "Venerable Master! As the Master reached for his whisk (hakkō), Zhaozhou let out a shout and, shaking out his sleeves, departed.
At evening, Guishan asked the Head Seat, "Is the newcomer from today still here? The Seat replied, "At that moment, he turned his back on the Dharma Hall and went out wearing straw sandals.
Guishan said, "This fellow will later go to the summit of a solitary peak, build a grass hut, and there he will revile the Buddhas and scold the Patriarchs."
Small Assembly. Addressing the assembly, the Master said: "Tonight I shall not answer questions. Anyone who asks a question shall receive thirty blows of the staff.
At that time, a monk came forward and bowed. The Master struck him immediately. The monk said, "I have not even asked a question; for what reason does the Master strike me?
The Master asked, "Where are you from? The monk replied, "From Silla. The Master said, "Before you have even stepped onto the ship's railing, it is already so."
[He] gave him thirty blows. Addressing the assembly, he said: "If you can speak it, thirty blows; if you cannot speak it, thirty blows. When Linji heard of this, he said to Luopu:
"Go and ask him why, even if one can speak it, there are thirty blows. Wait for him to strike you, and then..."
[The Master] caught the staff and gave it a push. "See what he does! Pu asked according to the instructions.
The Master struck him. Pu caught the staff and gave it a push. The Master then returned to his quarters. Pu went back and related this to Linji.
Linji said, "I have always suspected this fellow. Nevertheless, do you recognize Deshan? As Pu hesitated, Linji [struck him].
Da. Longya asked, "When a student wields the Mohejian sword with the intent to take the Master's head, what then?
The Master extended his neck forward and said, "Strike! Longya said, "The head has fallen. The Master laughed loudly. Later, Longya went to Dongshan and recounted this previous incident.
Yaya said, "What did Deshan say? Dongshan said, "Deshan was speechless. Dongshan said, "Do not say he was speechless.
Bring me the head of Deshan where it has fallen, and show it to this old monk. Only then did Yaya realize his error, whereupon he prostrated himself in repentance and thanks.
A monk reported this to the Master (Linji), who said, "The old man Dongshan does not know good from bad. How long has it been since this fellow died?"
"What is the use of saving him? A monk came to visit him;
the Master stepped forward and assumed a wrestling stance. The Master said, "Such impertinence deserves a blow from this old monk's hand.
The monk brushed his sleeves and departed. The Master said, "Even granting you did so, you would still only have attained half."
The monk turned around and gave a shout. The Master said, "I must strike you before it is right.
The monk said, "There are men of clear eyes in all directions. The Master said, "Naturally possessing eyes. The monk opened his eyes wide and said, "Cat! and then departed.
The Master said, "The Yellow River clears itself only once every three thousand years."
The monks came for an audience. The Master asked the rector, "How many new arrivals are there today? He replied, "Eight. The Master said, "Call them here;
I shall press them all down at once."
Ascending the hall, he said: "When you have reached the ultimate limit of knowledge, even the Buddhas of the three periods of time find their mouths hanging on the wall.
Yet there is still one person who laughs heartily, 'Ha-ha! If you can recognize this person, your studies as a seeker are complete."
Addressing the assembly: When there are words, one rides the tiger’s head and gathers its tail; beneath the first phrase, the fundamental principle is clarified.
