When there are no words, the sharp point of the spiritual mechanism is laid bare, like a flash of lightning or a stroke of a broom.
The Master was ill. A monk asked, "Is there anyone who does not fall ill? The Master said, "There is. The monk asked, "Who is this one who does not fall ill?
The Master said, "A-ye! A-ye! The Master further addressed the assembly, saying: "To feel for echoes in empty space is but to weary your mind and spirit.
When the dream is over and you realize it was not real, what event has actually occurred?"

When Chan Master Dongshan Liangjie Wuben was first traveling on pilgrimage, he encountered an old woman carrying water on the road. The Master asked for some water to drink. The woman said, "You may drink the water as you wish;
however, I have a question that must first be answered before you do so. Tell me, how many particles does this water consist of? The Master replied, "It consists of no particles."
Dust. Baoyun said, "Go away! Do not soil my water pitcher.
Later, while making offerings before Yunyan’s portrait, a monk asked, "The former master said, 'It is just this. Is that not so? The Master said, "It is.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "At that time, I nearly misunderstood the former master's intent. The monk asked, "How so? The Master said, "..."
"I do not yet know whether my former teacher knew that this exists or not. The Master said, "If he did not know it exists, how could he have spoken thus?
If he did know it exists, how could he have been willing to speak thus?"
On the anniversary of Yunyan’s death, a vegetarian feast was prepared. A monk asked, “Master, what instruction did you receive from Yunyan?
The Master said, “Although I was with him, I did not receive any instruction. The monk said, “If you did not receive any instruction, why did you prepare this feast?
The Master said, “How would I dare go against him? The monk said, “When you first met Nanquan, why did you [act] otherwise?”
When Yunyan prepared a vegetarian feast, the Master said, "I do not value my late teacher’s moral virtue or his Buddha-dharma;
I only value that he did not explain it through for me. Yunyan asked, "The Master is preparing this feast for your late teacher;
do you still approve of him? The Master said, "Half I approve, half I do not. Yunyan asked, "Why do you not fully approve? The Master said, "If I fully approved, I would betray my late teacher."
It was Master [Zhaozhou].
Once, while Master [Zhaozhou] and the head seat Taishou were eating fruit on the winter solstice, he asked:

"There is a thing that reaches up to heaven and down to earth, black as lacquer, always present within the midst of activity, yet cannot be grasped within the midst of activity. Tell me, where does its fault lie?"
"Where is it? Tai replied, "The fault lies in the midst of active functioning.
The Master called for his attendant to remove the fruit table and asked Xuefeng, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Tiantai. The Master asked, "Did you see Zhiye?
He replied, "Yicun is liable to receive an iron staff."
Xuefeng went up to pay his respects. The Master said, "Upon entering the gate, you must have something to say;
you cannot simply claim that you have already entered. Xuefeng said, "I have no mouth. The Master said, "Let it be that you have no mouth, but give me back my eyes. Xuefeng was speechless.
While Xuefeng was carrying firewood, he dropped a bundle down in front of the Master. The Master asked, "How much does it weigh?
Xuefeng replied, "No one in the entire world can lift it. The Master said, "How did it get here? Xuefeng was speechless.
While washing his bowl, the Master saw two crows fighting over a frog. A monk asked, "Why has this come to such a state?
The Master said, "It is solely because of you, O *jñātiputra*."
Question: Among the three bodies, why is the *anāśrava* (untainted) body not included within the numerical categories? The Master said: "I have often been pressed on this point.
Chen Shangshu asked the Master: "Among the fifty-two stages of the Bodhisattvas, why is the stage of Wondrous Enlightenment (*miao-jue*) not seen?
The Master said: "Shangshu, you have personally seen Wondrous Enlightenment."
The official asked, "Is there anyone who practices cultivation? The Master said, "Wait until you become a true man, and then you shall practice.
On another occasion, the Master said, "Only when you have realized the matter that lies beyond the Buddha will you have some share in the discourse. A monk asked, "What is this discourse?
The Master said, "When the discourse is being given, you, O Ācārya, do not hear it. The monk asked, "Does the Master hear it? The Master [replied,] "Yes."
He said, "I hear it when there is no speaking. A monk asked, "What is one who is above the Buddha? The Master said, "Not a Buddha.
The Master was unwell and instructed a novice to convey his message to Yunju, entrusting him with these words: "If he asks, 'Is the Master at ease?
simply say, 'The path to Yunyan is soon to be cut off. When you deliver this message, you must stand far away, for I fear he might strike you."
"You, śrāmaṇera, take my instructions and go. Before the sound of his words had even faded, Yunju struck him with a staff.
As he was about to pass away, he said to the assembly, "I have an idle reputation in the world; who can rid me of it? No one in the assembly could respond.
At that time, the śrāmaṇera came forward and said, "Please grant me the Dharma-name for the Master. The Master said, "My idle reputation has already vanished."
The Prefect of Muzhou, Minister Chen Cao, asked a monk, "I have a matter to discuss with you, Venerable Sir; would that be possible? The monk said, "Shut your dog's mouth!

The official slapped his own mouth and said, "I am at fault. The monk said, "One who recognizes their error must surely reform. The official said, "If that is so, then I beg for your instruction, Venerable Sir."
[The Master] was eating rice. "Is it permissible?
[He asked]. During the midday meal, he picked up a sesame cake and asked a monk, "In Jiangxi and Hunan, do they have such a thing as this?
The monk said, "What did the Minister eat just now? The official said, "I struck the bell to thank the resonance."
Furthermore, while ascending the tower with his subordinates, he saw several monks walking toward them. One official remarked, "Those coming are all traveling monks.
The Master said, "They are not. The official asked, "How do you know they are not? The Master replied, "Wait until they arrive; we shall examine them.

A short while later, when the monks reached the front of the tower, the Master suddenly called out, "Venerable Elder! The monks all raised their heads. The Master said to the officials, "Not [traveling monks]."
Xindao. Wuzhuo Wenhui Chanshi went to Huayan Temple on Mount Wutai.
Upon arriving at the Vajra Cave, he paid his respects; there he encountered an old man leading an ox.
As they were traveling, the elder invited the Master into the temple. The elder called out, "Junti! and a young boy responded by coming out to welcome them.

The elder released the oxen and led the Master up into the hall; the entire structure was radiant with a golden hue. The elder sat upon his couch and pointed to an embroidered cushion, commanding the Master to sit. The elder said:
"Where have you come from recently? The Master said, "From the South. The Old Man asked, "How is the Buddha-dharma maintained in the South?

The Master said, "In this age of the Dharma’s decline, few bhikṣus observe the precepts and rules. The Old Man asked, "How many followers are there? The Master said, "Sometimes three hundred, sometimes five hundred.
The Master then asked in turn, "How is the Buddha-dharma maintained here? The Old Man said, "Dragons and snakes are mixed together; ordinary people and sages are intermingled."
They lived together. The Master asked, "How many people are in your assembly? The Old Man replied, "Three by three in front; three by three behind.
The Old Man called for his attendant to serve tea, along with some whey and curd. The Master ate it and felt his mind and spirit become clear and refreshed.
The Old Man picked up a crystal cup and asked, "Is there such a thing as this in the South? The Master said, "No. The Old Man asked, "What do you usually use to drink your tea?"
The Master had no reply and took his leave. The old man ordered a youth to see him off. The Master asked the youth, "Three times three before, and three times three after—how many is that?
The youth called out, "Virtuous One! The Master responded. The youth said, "How many is that? The Master then asked again.
"Where is this place? The youth replied, "This is the Vajra Cave Prajñā Monastery.

The Master was moved to sorrow and realized that the old man was none other than Mañjuśrī, whom he would never see again. He immediately prostrated himself before the youth and requested a parting word.
The boy spoke in verse: "An absence of anger on the face is the true offering; An absence of anger in the mouth emits a wondrous fragrance;
An absence of anger in the heart is a precious treasure— Stainless and undefiled, it is the True Constant. Having finished speaking, Junti and the temple both vanished.
He saw only Mañjuśrī riding a golden-haired lion coming and going amidst clouds of five colors. Suddenly, white clouds arose from the east and covered him, so that he could no longer see him.
Consequently, the Master took up residence at Mount Wutai. Later, he visited Yangshan, where his mind was instantly awakened through their mutual accord.
Yangshan appointed him as the head cook (*diansuo*). Once, Mañjuśrī appeared atop the rice-pot; the Master struck him with his rice-stirring paddle.
He said: "Wenshu is Wenshu; Wenxi is Wenxi. Then Wenshu spoke a verse: "The bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip;
The sweet melon is sweet from stem to end. I have practiced for three great kalpas, Yet I am still despised by this old monk."
One day, a strange monk arrived seeking alms-food. The Master set aside his own portion and gave it to him. Yangshan, having foreseen this in advance, asked:

"Just now, a person on the level of fruition arrived; did you provide him with food? The Master replied: "I set aside my own share to bestow it upon him. Yangshan said: "You have brought about great benefit."
A practitioner asked Chan Master Jingtong of Huoshan, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master then prostrated.
The practitioner said, "Why does the Master prostrate to an ordinary person? The Master replied, "Have you not heard it said: 'Reverence your disciples'?"
Chan Master Xinghua Cunjian served as the head of the administrative affairs at Dajue Temple. One day, Dajue called out to him, "Head of the administrative affairs!
I have heard you say that after traveling throughout the South on pilgrimage, you have never once struck upon a single person who understands the Buddha-dharma. On what basis do you say this?"
"What logic allows you to speak in such a manner? The Master then gave a shout. Jue struck him. The Master shouted again. Jue struck him again.
The next day, as the Master was passing by the Dharma Hall, Jue called out, "Head of the Monastery! I have a persistent doubt regarding those two shouts you gave yesterday."
The Master shouted again; Jue struck him. The Master shouted once more; Jue struck him again.
The Master said, "I learned a 'guest-host' phrase from my senior brother, the Third Sage, but I have been completely defeated by you, Senior Brother.
I pray that you will grant me a Dharma-gate of peace and ease. Jue said, "You blind fellow! You have come here to meet with defeat. Take off your patched robe!"
He gave him a severe beating. At these words, the Master realized the principle behind why his late teacher Linji had received blows from Huangbo.
Later, on the day he opened the hall for formal teaching, he held up the incense and said: "This one stick of incense is primarily for my elder brother Sansheng;
yet Sansheng was too solitary for me. It is primarily for my elder brother Da-jue; yet Da-jue was too distant for me."

When he was making offerings to his late teacher Linji, the Master said to the rector Kebin, "Before long, you will become a master who leads the assembly. Kebin replied, "I will not enter this protective community.
The Master asked, "Do you refuse to enter because you have understood, or because you have not understood? Kebin said, "It is not like either of those. Thereupon, the Master [struck him].
Deshan said, "Venerable Kebin has lost the Dharma-battle; he shall be fined five strings of cash and provided with one meal of rice and vegetables.
The next day, the Master himself struck the wooden gavel and said, "Venerable Kebin has lost the Dharma-battle and shall not eat his meal; he is to leave the monastery immediately."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "If you are a veteran warrior, then I pray you enter with a single blade directly;
do not hesitate to ask 'how' or 'what'. Chan Master Mindé came forward, prostrated, and upon rising gave a shout. The Master also shouted. Mindé shouted again, and the Master shouted once more.
Mindé prostrated and returned to the assembly. The Master said: "Had it been anyone else just now, they would have received thirty blows—every single one of them."
They cannot be compared. Why? Because for that man of profound virtue, a single shout does not function as a mere shout.
When a fellow practitioner arrived, as soon as he stepped onto the Dharma Hall, the Master shouted; the monk also shouted. The Master shouted again; the monk also shouted.
The Master stepped forward and raised his staff; the monk shouted once more. The Master said, "Look! This blind fellow still thinks he is the master."
The monk hesitated to respond. The Master struck him down directly from the Dharma Hall. A attendant asked, "What did that monk just do to offend you, Master?
The Master said, "Just now, he possessed both the provisional and the real; he possessed both illumination and function."
When I raised my hand toward his face and made two horizontal gestures, he was unable to proceed further.
For a blind man such as this, when would it be any sooner than now to strike him? The monk bowed.
Later, when the imperial carriage of Zhuangzong of the Later Tang traveled through Hebei and returned to the Uei-fu (Weifeng) temporary palace, he issued an edict summoning the Master to ask him:
"In my campaign to recover the Central Plains, I obtained a treasure for which no one has yet offered a price. The Master said, "I beg Your Majesty to show me this treasure."

The Emperor extended the legs of his *fuhoutou* (head-wrap) with both hands. The Master said, "This is the treasure of a sovereign; who would dare to offer a price for it? The Emperor was greatly pleased.
This was Chan Master Zhao of Baoshou in Zhenzhou.
The Master was sitting in the abbot’s quarters. As a monk was inquiring after him, the Master said, “The hundreds of thousands of sages have all emerged from within this very abbot’s quarters.
The monk asked, “As for what the ancients said—that the great trichiliocosm is but a bubble on the ocean—where, then, does this abbot’s quarters reside?
The Master said, “The thousand sages are present right now. The monk asked, “Who can testify to this? The Master then threw [his whisk] down.

The master lowered his whisk. The monk passed from west to east and stood before him; the master then struck him. The monk said, "Had you not studied under me for a long time, how could you have known the ultimate point?
The master replied, "Thirty years from now, these words will spread far and wide."
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the Western Mountains. The Master said, "Did you see the monkeys? The monk said, "I saw them. The Master said, "..."
"What kind of artifice can you employ? [Sanxing] said, "Upon seeing me, I cannot employ even a single artifice. The Master then struck him.
Chan Master Huiran of Sanxing Monastery went to Yangshan.
Yangshan asked, "What is your name? The Master said, "Huiji. Yangshan said, "Huiji is my own name."
[The monk] stated his name. The Master said, "My name is Huiran. [The monk] laughed loudly.
Upon arriving at Deshan, as soon as he spread out his sitting cloth (zuoju), Deshan said, "Do not spread out your cooking cloth; there is no left-over soup or rancid rice here."
The Master said, "Even if there were, there would be no place for it to land. Shanshan struck him. The Master caught the staff and pushed it onto the meditation seat.
Shanshan laughed loudly; the Master wailed to the blue heavens and then went down to attend the hall. In the hall, the Head Seat was named Tie Tian Tai (Kick-the-Sky Tai). He asked:
"A traveling monk must possess an official pass from his own school. What is this 'official pass from one's own school'? The Master said, "What are you saying? The monk asked again.
The Master struck him with his sitting mat and said, "You lacquer bucket! How many worthy and virtuous men have you offended before and after [this encounter]!
As the monk prepared to offer his greetings, the Master passed on to the second seat to receive his greetings.
The Master asked the monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk gave a shout. The Master also shouted. The monk shouted again; the Master shouted again.
The monk said, "If you strike me with the staff, I will go blind," and he shouted. The Master raised his staff. The monk then turned his body and made the gesture of receiving a blow.

The Master said, "One who does not run down the slope finds such a swift opportunity hard to encounter," and he struck him. The monk said, "You thief! and went out. The Master then threw down [the staff].
“Strike! Next, a monk asked, “Just now, how could you have tolerated that monk? The Master said, “It was because he had seen the former master.

When the Master visited Baoshou, the Abbot of Zhenzhou Wanshou, Baoshou did not rise from his seat. The Master spread out his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*). Baoshou descended from his meditation platform, whereupon the Master withdrew.
Baoshou entered the abbot’s quarters abruptly and closed the door. Seeing that the Master sat there without rising, the administrator said, “I beg the Abbot to come to the storehouse for tea.
The Master then returned to his own quarters. On the following day, Baoshou came again to pay his respects; the Master was already seated upon the meditation platform.
Baoshou spread out his sitting mat. The Master also descended from his meditation seat. Baoshou sat back down. The Master returned to his quarters and closed the door.
Baoshou entered the attendants' hall, took some ash, circled the Master's quarters with it, and then departed.
The Master then opened the door and said, "I do not act in this way; he, however, acts in this way."
Master Tanka of Youzhou was the head monk at the monastery of Prefect Mu of Zhenzhou.
Prefect Mu had an aunt who had become a nun; upon her return from traveling on pilgrimage, she wished to open the hall to teach others. The Prefect ordered Master [Tanka] to examine her.
The Master asked, "I have heard it said that you wish to open the hall to teach others; is this true? The nun replied, "It is.

The Master said, "A nun possesses a body subject to the five obstacles. How will you teach others? The nun said, "The dragon girl attained perfect enlightenment in the Immaculate World of the South at the age of eight.
What about her? The Master said, "The dragon girl has eighteen transformations. You try [to perform one]..."
"Watch it transform! The nun said, "Even if it were to transform, it would still be nothing but a wild fox spirit. The Master then struck her.
Upon hearing this being cited, Xuemou said, "Has the Master’s staff broken?"
A monk asked the Abbot of Huxi Hermitage, "How many years have you been here, Abbot? The Master said, "I have only seen the withering in winter and the growth in summer;
I do not remember the years at all. The monk said, "It is truly wonderful that you do not remember. The Master said, "Do you think I am here because I have attained something?"
"For how many years? He replied, "It has been winter for a long time. The Master said, "A tiger in the marketplace.
An old man came to visit the Hermitage Master of Tongfeng. The Master asked, "Where do you reside? The old man did not speak. The Master said, "You are truly skilled."
Regarding the occasion: The old man picked up a blade of grass on the ground and showed it to the Master. The Master then gave a shout. The old man bowed.
The Master then returned to his hermitage. The old man said, "In this way, you leave everyone in a state of doubt."
A monk arrived to visit Master Sōyō-an. The Master asked, "Who is it? The monk replied, "I am Master Sōyō-an. The Master said, "It is I. The monk then gave a shout.
The Master made a sound of sighing. The monk said, "I still want to eat a blow of the staff.
The Master then struck him. He asked another monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Jiangxi. The Master held up his itch-comb and asked, "Is there such a thing as this in Jiangxi?
The monk stretched out his knees and closed his eyes. The Master said, "The son of the eastern house is being employed by the western house."

[The Master] called out. The monk said, "Having a mouth, one need not trouble the host and guest with speech. The Master said, "Just now you were afflicted by deafness; now you are afflicted by muteness.
The monk said, "Buying iron and obtaining gold—what a display of wealth! The Master said, "Working as a hired laborer without merit, one cannot avoid fleeing."
The monk then departed. The Master said, "It may be acceptable for you to bring trouble upon yourself, but do not bring trouble upon this old monk.
When the Venerable Huo went to visit Deshan, as soon as Deshan saw him, he descended from his meditation seat and made a gesture of unfolding his sitting mat. The Master said, "This one..."
[The Master] set it aside. "Suppose you encountered someone for whom mind and objects are one as such—what would you say to them? This would spare you from being censured by those in all quarters.
Sanshan said, "That would still leave you three steps behind where you were before. You must act as a true master yourself. The Master then gave a shout. Sanshan remained silent.
The Master said, "I have blocked this old fellow’s throat! He then shook out his sleeves and departed.
Chan Master Jiugong Daogyan served as the attendant to Shishuang. When Shishuang passed away, the assembly requested the Head Seat to succeed him as abbot.

The Master addressed the assembly, saying, "One must first understand the meaning of our late teacher before one may do so. The Head Seat asked, "What meaning did our late teacher have? The Master replied, "Our late..."
The Master said: "Rest! Cease! Be cold and still! A single thought for ten thousand years! Like cold ashes and withered wood!
Like an incense burner in an ancient temple! Like a single strand of white silk! He continued, "I ask nothing else.
What is this 'a single strand of white silk'? The Head Seat said, "This merely clarifies matters on the side of a single color. The Master said, "So, it was not yet."
"Does he understand the intention of our former master? The Seat-holder said, "Do you not agree with me? Just bring some incense.

If you cannot depart when the incense smoke is cut off, then you do not understand the intention of our former master. He then burned the incense. Before the smoke had even ceased, the Seat-holder had already passed away.

The Master patted the back of the seat and said, "To 'pass away while seated' or 'die while standing' is certainly possible, but as for the intention of our former master, we have not yet seen it even in a dream."

While the Chan practitioners Qiang and De were traveling along the road, they saw Master Jingxin of Yongquan riding an ox. Not recognizing him as the master, De suddenly said, "The hooves and horns are quite distinct;
what can one do about the rider who does not realize it? The master spurred the ox and departed. Qiang and De rested beneath a tree to brew tea.
"Tea. The Master turned back, set down the ox, and asked, "Where have these two Chan guests recently come from? They replied, "From over there. The Master said, "What is the matter over there?
He forcefully lifted his tea bowl. The Master said, "This is still only the matter of 'over here.'"
"What is that matter over there? [The monk] was unable to respond. The Master said, "Do not say that the rider does not discern.
Zen Master Yungai Zhiyuan Yuanjing asked a monk, "What is the lion?
The Master said, "It roars well. The monk clapped his hands and said, "A fine hand! A fine hand!"

The Master said, "Under the blue sky and bright sun, you have been bewitched by a ghost. The monk made a gesture of overturning the meditation seat; the Master struck him. The monk said, "Before the donkey's business is finished, the horse's business has arrived.

The Master said, "Truly a master of the craft. The monk shook out his sleeves and departed. The Master said: *Note: This passage is a classic encounter dialogue (kōan) from the Zen tradition. It records a moment of spiritual testing between a master and a disciple, where the master’s actions and words are intended to cut through conceptualization and reveal the student’s true capacity.*
He took a bowl and filled it with water, intending to compare it to the great ocean.
Daowu asked, "I have long heard that you, Master, are proficient in Chan; is this true? The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven!
Daowu stepped forward and covered the Master’s mouth, saying, "Lower your voice! Lower your voice! The Master gave him a slap. Daowu said, "Heaven! Heaven! The Master grabbed [him].
Zhuzhu said, "To receive such discourtesy! I shall give you a slap. The Master said, "I, this old monk, am at fault.
He then shook out his sleeves and departed. The Master laughed heartily and said, "Had I known it would be thus earlier, I would not have seen it as such."
When Chan Master Shizhu of Fengxiang was traveling, he arrived at Dongshan. At that time, Master Qian gave him this instruction: "There are four kinds of people:
the first person has surpassed the Buddhas and patriarchs, yet cannot take a single step; the second person has walked beyond the Buddhas and patriarchs, yet cannot utter a single word."
One person says they can practice but cannot speak; another says they cannot speak and cannot practice. Which of these two is the true person? The Master stepped forward from the assembly and said:
"The one who says they have surpassed the Buddhas and Patriarchs but cannot practice—this simply means they lack a tongue and are not permitted to speak.
The one who has surpassed the Buddhas and Patriarchs in practice but cannot say a single word—this simply means they lack feet and are not permitted to speak."
"One who can speak and can practice is simply like a box and its lid fitting perfectly. One who cannot speak and cannot practice is like seeking life after one's breath has been cut off;
this is like a child born of a barren woman wearing a cangue and shackles. Sanshan asked, "What about your own portion, Master?
The Master said, "In my own portion, all is encompassed and penetrating; every step is clearly manifest. Sanshan said, "As for the Sea [Master Hai], how is it?"
"Master Shangming Gongxiu, how about you? The Master said, "When illusory people meet, they clap their hands and laugh aloud.
The scholar Zhang Zhuo was directed by Chan Master Shiyue to visit Shishuang. Shishuang asked, "Scholar, what is your surname? He replied, "My surname is Zhang and my name is—"
Zhuo said, "Frost, you say that even skillfulness cannot be found; from where does clumsiness come? Zhang had a sudden realization and presented this verse:
"Radiant, silent illumination pervades the sands of the Ganges; Ordinary beings, sages, and all living creatures share my home. When not a single thought arises, the entire body is manifest;
As soon as the six sense organs stir, they are veiled by clouds. To try to eliminate afflictions is to increase one's illness; To seek toward True Suchness..."

This too is erroneous. To accord with worldly conditions without obstruction, and to treat nirvana and birth-and-death as equal to empty transformations—this was the teaching of Chan Master Yuan’an of Luopu.

When he arrived at Cenyang, he encountered an old friend. While discussing their past experiences in Wuling, the friend asked: "In the blink of an eye, several years have passed; what [has become of you]?"
[The monk] asked, "Where do you take refuge during times of peril? The Master said, "Right in the midst of the marketplace. [The monk] said, "Why not go to a place where there are no people?
The Master said, "What difficulty is there in a place where there are no people? [The monk] said, "How can one escape and hide within the marketplace?
The Master said, "Although I am in the midst of the marketplace, for now people do not recognize me; therefore, others cannot fathom me."
Master Pang bowed and, rising, said, “In early summer it is scorching heat; in early winter it is slight cold. The Master said, “Do not speak erroneously.
Master Pang said, “I, Master Pang, am old. The Master said, “Why do you not say it is cold when it is cold, and say it is hot when it is hot?
Master Pang said, “Why act as if you were deaf? The Master said, “I grant you thirty blows. Master Pang said, “Shut my mouth and plug up your eyes!”
The Wayfarer Hachi-kei came to visit the Master. The Master asked, "Since we parted at Reikei, how many years have passed now?
Kei said, "The Master still remembers events from years past. The Master said, "I have heard it said that wayfarers forget all matters of year and month."
Xī said, "The Abbot’s administrative duties are many; please allow me time to observe carefully. The Master said, "If you strike, strike a man who understands Chan!
Xī said, "I am capable of enduring it. The Master said, "Dharma Teacher, your mountain-dwelling affairs are many."

Question: "When a single hair has swallowed up the vast ocean, what more remains to be said? The Master replied: "If one possesses the White Deer (Bai Ze) map, there will certainly be no such demons or monsters."
A monk asked, "It is said that making offerings to hundreds of thousands of Buddhas is not as good as making an offering to a single mindless man of the Way.

I do not understand what fault lies with the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, nor what virtue lies with the mindless man of the Way. The Master said, "A single sheet of white cloud spans the mouth of the valley;
how many returning birds are utterly lost in their nests?"

A monk asked Chan Master Lingchao of Shanglan, "When two dragons struggle for a pearl, who is the one that obtains it? The Master said, "The pearl covers the ground; even when seen with the eyes, it is like mud."
Chan Master Yuelun of Huangshan went to visit Jia Shan.
Jia Shan asked, "What is your name? The Master replied, "Yuelun. Jia Shan drew a circle and said, "How does this compare to that?
The Master said, "If you speak in such a manner, there will be many throughout the various quarters who will not approve. Jia Shan... [remained silent].

[Shishuang] said, "How about you, *ācārya*? The Master said, "Do you see the lunar disc? Shishuang said, "If you speak like that, *ācārya*, there are many people here who would not approve of you as they do in other quarters.
Thereupon, the Master took him as his model and began to inquire of him. One day, Shishuang asked in a loud voice, "Where are you from?
The Master replied, "I am a man from Min. Shishuang said, "Do you recognize this old monk?"
The Master said, "Does the Master still recognize this student? Mount said, "Not so. First, you must pay me the price for my straw sandals;
only then will I tell you the price of rice in Luling. The Master said, "If that is so, then you do not recognize me.
I do not yet know what the price of rice in Luling is. Mount said, "A true lion cub; you are well able to roar."
He then entered the room to receive the seal.
Chan Master Puhuan of Mount Shao came for an audience with the Master.
The Master asked, "Are you not that talkative old fellow Yin? Yin replied, "I dare not. The Master said, "There are many..."

The monk said little. The Master asked, "Is it that your entire body is it? The monk replied, "It is everywhere throughout my whole body. The Master asked, "Where do you usually defecate? The monk replied, "I defecate within the mouth of Shaozhou.
The Master said, "If there is a mouth of Shaozhou, it is fine; but if there were no mouth of Shaozhou, where would you defecate?
Because the monk was speechless, the Master struck him.
Zun Bunan went to visit the Master. They met at the foot of the mountain, and Zun asked, "Where does the road to Shao Mountain lead?
The Master pointed with his finger and said, "It goes toward the place where the green of Wuna is deep and dark.
Zun stepped forward, seized him, and said, "I have long heard of Shao Mountain; is this not it? The Master said, "It is indeed so. But what business do you have, O Kalyāṇamitra? Zun said:
"I wish to pose a question; will you, Master, answer it? The Master said, "I see that you are not made of gilded ivory;
how could you possibly draw your bow to shoot Weichi? Dun said, "A phoenix soars straight into the misty heights; who fears the wild sparrows in the woods?"
The Master said: "The painted drum hangs before the hall; strike it as you wish, but try to display your family style like that of an old monk.
Zhuan said: "A single phrase transcends beyond the thousand sages; the pine and the vine do not reach the height of the moon's orb. The Master said:

"Even if you emerge directly from beyond the limit of Avidyā (Wei-yin), you are still half a month’s journey short of Shao-shan. Zhuan said: "Where does the fault lie? The Master said: "In those boastful words."
The people of the time knew that it existed. Cundi said, "If that is so, then the true jade differs from that within the mud; it does not stir up the dust of ten thousand affairs.
The Master said, "Under the workshop of Lu Ban, one merely exerts cleverness and ingenuity. Cundi said, "The student acts thus; I do not yet know what your intention is, Master.
The Master said, "At night, a jade maiden casts her shuttle, weaving brocade in the western house. Cundi said, "Is this not simply 'the harmony'?"
"Does your family style not exist? The Master said, "A farmer fashions a jade water-clock; it is not the work of a master craftsman.
Zhaozhou said, "That is still merely literary expression. What is the Master's own family style? The Master said, "With my body laid across the universe, who is there to show their head?
Zhaozhou was speechless. The Master then returned to the mountain with him. As soon as the formal greetings were concluded, the Master called him forward and said:
The Acharya has the spirit that pierces the heavens; this old monk has the stratagem to enter the earth.
The Acharya swallows the vast ocean in one gulp; this old monk carries Mount Sumeru on his back. The Acharya comes forward brandishing a sword; this old monk awaits him with a leveled spear.
As for the single path leading upward—speak quickly! Speak quickly! Zun said, "A bright mirror stands upon its stand; I pray the Master will examine it. The Master said, "I do not examine it."
Zhuan said, "Why do you not look? The Master said, "The water is shallow and there are no fish; it is but a vain labor to cast down the hook. Zhuan had no reply.
The Master then struck him.
Chan Master Hailu of Taiyuan was once invited by someone to provide offerings for Tripitaka Master Guanding. After the seats had been arranged, the Master took his place upon that very seat.
At that time, the Dharma Master Yunshe asked, "In what year did you, Preceptor, begin your practice? The Master replied, "Dharma Master, it was recently."
Sheshen came forward. As he drew near, the Master said, "As for Kātyāyana, in what year did he practice the Way?
Sheshen was at a loss. The Master shouted, "This bed-wetting ghost!"
When Chan Master Touzi Gangwen was traveling through the mountains, he saw a cicada’s exuviae. An attendant asked, “The shell is here; where has the cicada gone?
The Master took the shell, shook it three or five times by his ear, and made the sound of a cicada. Thereupon, the attendant attained enlightenment.

A monk asked the Fourth Chan Master of Yanzhou, "In the past, there was the saying 'one does not turn one's back on an invitation. Now I invite the Master to enter a well; will you turn your back on this? The Master said:
Profoundly deep, it has no separate source; those who drink from it eliminate all afflictions.
Master Youchan Tiangai of Fengxiang possessed a monastery named Wugou Jingguang (Stainless Pure Light). He constructed a bathhouse, and someone asked: "Since this is already 'Stainless and Pure'..."
Guang asked, "Why, then, did you build a bathhouse? The monk was speechless. Later, he requested the Master to provide a reply on his behalf.
The Master said, "On a night of bright moon in the third autumn month, it is not for the sake of displaying its full orb."
Chan Master Yantou Quanhuo went to visit Yangshan.
As soon as he entered the gate, he held up his sitting cloth and said, "Venerable Teacher! Yangshan reached for his whisk, intending to raise it.
The Master said, "Truly a skilled hand. Later, he visited Deshan; holding his sitting cloth, he ascended the Dharma Hall and gazed about. Deshan—
[The monk] asked, "How so? The Master then shouted. Shanshan asked, "Where does the old monk’s fault lie?
The Master said, "A double case," and then went down to attend the hall. Shanshan remarked, "This master is somewhat like a true traveler. On the following day—
The Master went to inquire after his health. Deshan asked, "Reverend, were you the one who arrived yesterday? He replied, "I was.
Deshan said, "Where did you learn this pretense? The Master said, "Quanhuo never deceives himself. Deshan said, "In the future, do not let me down."
One day, he went to visit Deshan. Just as he was crossing the gate, he asked, "Is this ordinary or is it sacred? Deshan gave a shout. The Master bowed.
Someone reported this to Dongshan, who said, "Had it not been Master Huo, it would have been very difficult to handle.
The Master remarked, "The old man Dongshan does not know good from bad; he has wrongly applied a famous phrase. At that time, I would have used one hand to lift up and the other to press down."
Xuefeng was serving as the head cook at Deshan. One day, when the meal was late, Deshan went down from the Dharma Hall carrying his bowl.
Xuefeng, who was drying his hand-towel, saw Deshan and said, "The bell has not yet rung and the drum has not yet sounded; where are you going with your bowl?
Deshan then returned directly to the Abbot’s quarters. Xuefeng reported this incident to his teacher, who said, "Deshan, great as he may be, has not yet understood."
"The final phrase is present. When Shanshan heard this, he ordered his attendant to summon the Master and ask him, "Do you not agree with me, old monk?
The Master secretly revealed his intention, whereupon Shanshan desisted. The next day, when he ascended the hall, it was indeed different from his usual manner.

As the Master reached the front of the Sangha Hall, he clapped his hands and laughed loudly, saying, "I am glad that the old man at the head of the hall has understood the final phrase. Hereafter, heaven..."
"Subordinates cannot do anything about him. Nevertheless, he shall live for only three years. After three years, Shanguo passed away.
The Master and Luoshan were selecting a site for his stupa when Luoshan suddenly said on the way, "Master! The Master looked back and said, "Do it."
Ma. Shān pointed his finger and said, "This is a fine piece of ground here. The Master scolded him, saying, "A melon-seller at Guazhou!
After traveling several more li, they rested. Shān prostrated himself and asked, "Master, is it not true that thirty years ago you were at Dōngshān and yet did not approve of Dōngshān?
The Master said, "It is so. Shān asked again, "And is it not true that you have succeeded Dēngshān? The Master said, "It is so."
Again, he did not approve of Deshan. The Master said, "I do. Deshan asked, "I do not ask why you do not approve of Deshan; but as for Dongshan, what deficiency does he have?
The Master remained silent for a long while and then said, "Dongshan is a fine Buddha, but he simply lacks radiance. Deshan bowed.
Question: "When the three realms arise in competition, how should one deal with them? The Master said: "Sit upon them and settle them. The questioner asked:
"I do not yet understand your meaning, Master. The Master said: "If you could move Mount Lu here, then I would tell you."
A monk asked, "How does one distinguish the master amidst the dust? The Master said, "A bronze gong filled with oil.
During the suppression of Buddhism, the Master served as a ferryman on the shore of Lake E. He hung a wooden board at each end of the landing stage;
whenever someone came to cross, he would strike the board once. The Master would then ask, "Who is it? Or if someone replied, "I wish to go to the other side," the Master would dance.
He welcomed him with his oars. One day, an old woman came carrying a baby and said, "I do not ask about your presenting the rudder and dancing with the oars;
but tell me, from where did this child in the old woman’s hand come? The Master struck her. The old woman said, "I have borne seven sons;
six did not meet with one who understands them. This one alone is not even worth keeping," and she threw him into the water.
Chan Master Niutou Wei ascended the hall and said:
"The Buddhas of the three periods of time cannot employ even a single bit of artifice. The teachers throughout the land have mouths like flat carrying-poles.
What do you all think? It is not at all easy. Unless one knows that which truly is, no one else can know."
When Chan Master Xuefeng Yicun was serving as the head cook at Dongshan,
while he was rinsing rice, Dongshan asked him, "Are you rinsing the sand away from the rice, or are you rinsing the rice away from the sand?"
The Master said, "The rice and the bran are gone all at once. Dongshan asked, "What will the assembly eat? The Master then overturned the rice bucket.
Dongshan said, "According to your karmic conditions, you should have been at Deshan. One day Dongshan asked the Master, "What have you been doing? The Master said, "I have been hewing a trough.
Dongshan asked, "How many blows of the axe did it take to complete it? The Master said, "It was completed with a single blow of the axe. Dongshan said, "..."
"This is still a matter of this side. What about that side? The Master said, "It reaches the point where there is nowhere to apply the hand.
Sanshan said, "This is still a matter of this side. What about that side? The Master stopped speaking. The Master took his leave of Dongshan. Dongshan asked, "Where are you going?
The Master said, "I am going back to the mountains. Dongshan asked, "By which path did you come out at that time?"
The Master said, "I am coming from Feiyuan Ridge. Mountan said, "Where will you turn your path now? The Master said, "I am going from Feiyuan Ridge.
Mountan said, "There is a person who does not go by way of Feiyuan Ridge; do you recognize him? The Master said, "I do."
“I do not know it. Mount [Yangshan] said, “Why do you not know it? The Master said, “It has no face. Mount said, “Since you do not know it, how can you know it has no face?
The Master had no reply, so he went to visit Deshan. He asked, “Regarding the ancestral vehicle of the Buddhas, does a student have any share in it?
Deshan struck him with a staff and said, “Say something! The Master said, “I do not understand. When the next day arrived—
He requested further instruction. Mount [Shishuang] said, "In my school, there are no words or phrases; in truth, there is not a single dharma to give to anyone. The Master attained realization.
Later, while traveling with Yantou to Aoshan Town in Lishui, they were detained by snow.

Yantou spent his days doing nothing but sleeping, while the Master sat continuously in meditation. One day, he called out, "Elder brother! Elder brother! Please arise! Yantou asked, "For what purpose? The Master replied:
"In this life you have found no way to get through; you have been traveling with that fellow Wensui, and everywhere you have been brought to ruin by him.
Today, having arrived here, you do nothing but sleep. He gave a shout and said, "You glutton for sleep! You sit on your bed every day like a local deity in a village of seven hamlets.
In the future, you will go about bewitching the sons and daughters of people's households! The Master then struck himself.
Xiong said, "I am not yet settled here; I do not dare to deceive myself.
Tou said, "I took it for granted that you would one day settle a grass hut on the summit of a solitary peak and propagate the Great Teaching, yet you still speak these words.
The Master said, "Truly, I am not yet settled. Tou said, "If you are truly thus, then explain your realization point by point."
"Come! In this place I shall testify for you; in that which is not this place, I shall eradicate it for you.

The Master said, "When I first arrived at Yanguan, I saw him ascend the hall and expound upon the meaning of form and emptiness. There, I attained a point of entry. Baizhang said, "From now until thirty years hence, you must strictly avoid mentioning it.
Furthermore, he saw Dongshan’s verse on crossing the water, which says: "Strictly avoid seeking it from others; it lies far, far away from me."
The Commentary states: "He is now precisely me; I am now not he. Tou said: "If it is so, you have not even fully mastered your own salvation.
The Master further said: "Later, I asked Deshan whether a student has a share in the matters of the ancestral Dharma-lineage.
Deshan struck me with a staff and said, 'Speak! At that time, it was as if the bottom of my bucket had fallen out."
Tou shouted, "Have you not heard it said? That which enters through the gate is not the family treasure. The Master asked, "How should it be after this?
Tou said, "After this, if you wish to propagate the Great Teaching, let every word flow from your own breast;
bring it forth to cover heaven and earth for me! At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and prostrated himself in homage.
He rose and called out repeatedly, "Brother! Today at last is the day the Tortoise Mountain attains the Way.
Later, after he had settled there, a monk asked, "Master, what did you obtain upon seeing Deshan that you then departed?
The Master replied, "I went empty-handed and returned empty-handed."
Two monks arrived. The Master pushed open the gate of his hut with his hand, stepped out, and said, "What is this?
The monks also said, "What is this? The Master lowered his head and returned to the hut. As the monks were taking their leave, the Master asked, "Where are you going? They replied, "To Hunan."
The Master said, "I have a fellow practitioner living at Yantou; I am sending a letter to him for you. The letter read: "This letter is addressed to my elder brother.
Since I attained the Way at Aoshan, until this very day, I have been full and never hungry. This is from your fellow practitioner [name redacted].
When the monk arrived at Yantou, he was asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Xuefeng. I have a letter to deliver to the Abbot."

Baizhang received him and asked the monk, "What other words or phrases did he have? The monk then recounted the previous conversation. Baizhang said, "What did he say? The monk replied, "He said nothing;
he simply lowered his head and returned to his hut. Baizhang sighed and said, "Alas! In the beginning, I regretted not having spoken the 'final word' to him.
Had I spoken it to him, no one in the world could have done anything with Old Xue. At the end of that summer, the monk...
He requested further instruction on their previous conversation. The Head said, "Why did you not ask sooner? He replied, "I did not dare to do so lightly.
The Head said, "Although Xuefeng was born of the same lineage as I, he did not die of the same lineage as I. If you wish to know the final word, it is simply this."
There was a monk who had established a hermitage at the foot of a mountain. For many years he had not shaved his head and kept a long-handled ladle with which he drew water from a stream.
Once, a monk asked him, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch's coming from the West? The master replied, "The stream is deep and the handle of the ladle is long."
When the Master heard of this, he remarked, "That is truly extraordinary. One day, taking his razor with him, he went to visit the hermitage accompanied by an attendant.

As soon as they met, the Master brought up the previous conversation and asked, "Was that the words of the abbot? The abbot replied, "Yes. The Master said, "If you can say something [in response], then..."
"Then I shall not shave your head. The master then washed his head; he knelt before the master, and the master immediately shaved it off.

A monk asked: "When those of the Śrāvaka vehicle perceive their nature, it is like seeing the moon at night; when those of the Bodhisattva vehicle perceive their nature, it is like seeing the sun by day."
“I do not yet know how you, Master, have seen your nature. The Master struck him three times. Later, he asked Yantou, who struck him with three palms.
He asked a monk, “Where have you come from? The monk replied, “I have recently left the region of Zhejiang. The Master said, “Did you come by boat or by land?
The monk said, “I have traveled neither path. The Master said, “How did you manage to get here? The monk said, “What obstacle could there possibly be? The Master then struck him and drove him out.
After ten years had passed, the monk returned. The Master asked again, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Hunan. The Master said, "How far is Hunan from here?
He replied, "It is not separated [by anything]. The Master held up his whisk and said, "Is it not separated by this?
He replied, "If it were separated, I would not have arrived. The Master then struck him and drove him out. Later, whenever this monk saw someone...

He then reviled his teacher. One day, a fellow practitioner heard of this and went specifically to inquire: "Brother, what words did you encounter at Xuefeng that caused you to revile him in such a manner?
The monk then recounted the previous story. Upon hearing it, the fellow practitioner rebuked and scolded him, explaining the matter to him.
At that time, the monk wept bitterly; ever since, he would frequently burn incense in the middle of the night, bowing from afar.
The Master asked a monk, "Where are you going? He replied, "I am going to pay my respects to the Abbot of Jingshan.
The Master said, "If Jingshan asks you, 'How are the Buddha-dharma here? how will you respond? The monk said, "I will speak when he asks. The Master then struck him.
Later, the Master raised this case and asked Jingqing, "Where did this monk go wrong? Jingqing said, "His question exhausted Jingshan completely. The Master [nodded].
[The Master] said: "Jingshan is in Zhejiang; why then do you ask until you are thoroughly exhausted? Qing said: "Have you not heard it said:
'When asked about the distant, answer from the near'? The Master said: "So it is! So it is!"
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "Fuchuan. The Master said, "If you have not yet crossed the sea of birth and death, why did you capsize your boat?
The monk was speechless. The Master then returned and related this to Fuchuan. Fuchuan said, "Why do you not say that he has neither birth nor death?"
The monk returned and presented these words. The Master said, "These are not your words. The monk replied, "Fuchuan spoke thus.
The Master said, "I have twenty blows to send to Fuchuan; as for the other twenty blows, I shall eat them myself.
It is no concern of yours, *kalyāṇamitra*."
The Military Commander of Min presented a silver folding couch. A monk asked, "Venerable Sir, having received such offerings from the Great King, how will you repay him?
The Master struck the ground with his hand and said, "Strike me lightly! Strike me lightly!"
When Master Waguan was serving as attendant to Master Deshan, one day they entered the mountains together to chop wood. Deshan gave the Master a bowl of water;
the Master took it and drank it all at once. Deshan asked, "Do you understand? The Master replied, "I do not understand. Deshan then gave him another bowl.
Shishuang offered some water to the Master. The Master took it and drank it. Shishuang asked, "Do you understand? The Master said, "I do not understand.
Shishuang said, "Why do you not strip away that which does not understand? The Master said, "I do not understand; what else would there be to strip away?
Shishuang said, "You are very much like an iron stake. After [Shishuang] had settled there, Xuefeng visited him. While they were conversing over tea, Xuefeng asked, "At that time at Deshan..."
"What is the causal condition for hewing wood? The Master said, "The former master approved of me at that time. Feng said, "The Master left your teacher too early.
At that moment, there happened to be a bowl of water before them; Feng said, "Bring me some water," and the Master immediately passed it to him.
Fengjie took the opportunity to splash water over him.
Chan Master Gaoting Jian went to visit Deshan;
as soon as he saw him from across the river, he called out, "I hope you are well. Deshan then shook his fan to beckon him over. The Master suddenly—
Upon attaining enlightenment, he strode off crosswise and never looked back.
Zen Master Caoshan Benji went to visit Dongshan.
Dongshan asked, "What is your name, Reverend? The Master replied, "Benji. Dongshan asked, "Who is that one?"

The Master said, "I shall not call you 'Primordial Quiescence' (Benji). Mount Shan deeply esteemed him. From that time on, he entered the Master’s room and stayed for several years before taking his leave.
Mount Shan asked, "Where are you going? The Master replied, "I am going to the place where there is no change.
Mount Shan said, "In a place of no change, how can there be going? The Master replied, "Going itself is also without change."
A monk asked, "The student is sick throughout his entire being; I beg the Master to treat me. The Master said, "I will not treat you. The monk asked, "Why will you not treat me?
The Master said, "I shall teach you that you cannot seek life and you cannot seek death."
Jingqing asked, "When the principle of pure emptiness is ultimately without form, how is it? The Master said, "The principle is indeed thus; but as for the phenomenon, what is it?
He replied, "It is just like the principle and just like the phenomenon. The Master said, "You may succeed in deceiving Cao Shan alone, but what about the eyes of all the sages?
He replied, "If there were no eyes of the sages, how could they discern that which is not so? The Master said, "Official!"
"No room for a needle. I have privately provided you with carriages and horses.

The questioner asked, "What knowledge and understanding do you possess? You are truly skilled at posing difficult questions. The Master said, "I offer no phrases. The questioner asked, "What is it that you are questioning?"

A monk asked Xiangyan, "What is the Way? Xiangyan said, "A dragon's roar within a withered tree.
The monk asked, "What is one who walks the Way? Xiangyan said, "The eyes within a skull. The monk did not understand, so he went to ask Shishuang, "What is the dragon’s roar within a withered tree?
Shishuang said, "It still carries a trace of joy. The monk asked, "What are the eyes within a skull? Shishuang said—

The Master said, "The life-force (bloodline) is unbroken. [The monk] asked, "What are the eyes within the skull? The Master said, "They have not yet dried up.
[The monk] asked, "I wonder if there is anyone who can hear them? The Master said, "Throughout the entire world, there is not a single person who does not hear them. [The monk] said, "Not yet..."
"Examine this: what chapter or verse is 'the dragon’s roar within the withered tree'? The Master said, "I do not know what chapter or verse it is;

When joyful consciousness is exhausted, all news and traces are gone. How can a person distinguish purity within the turbid?
The Master composed a verse of four prohibitions, saying: Do not travel the path of the mind; Do not don the garment of original nature. What need is there for "just so"?

"How can one blame the old monk?
The Master then asked Cuiwei, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch's intent? Cuiwei said, "Bring me the meditation board.
The Master then passed the meditation board over to him; Cuiwei took it and struck him. The Master said, "I am willing to be struck, but there is no Patriarch's intent here anyway."
[The Master] asked Linji again, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch? Linji said, "Bring me that meditation cushion. The Master then passed the cushion over.
Linji took it and struck him. The Master said, "Strike as you will; however, there is still no meaning of the Patriarch here.
Later, a monk asked, "When the Master was traveling on pilgrimage, you questioned two venerable elders regarding the meaning of the Patriarch. I do not know—"
"Venerable sir, have you attained clarity? The Master said, "I have indeed attained clarity, yet it still lacks the meaning of the Patriarchs.
The Master then cited the words regarding Deshan’s head falling off; thereupon, he reflected upon his own errors and stayed at Dongshan to study with the assembly.
One day, he asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Dongshan replied, "Wait until the waters of the Dong River flow backward."
He then spoke to you, whereupon the Master first realized its essential meaning. He served with diligence for eight years.
When Prime Minister Pei entered Dà'ān Monastery, he asked the various virtuous elders, "By what quality was Rāhula declared foremost?"
Pei said, "I take secret practice to be foremost. Pei did not agree, so he asked, "What kind of Chan practitioners are there here?
At that time, the Master was planting vegetables in the back garden, so Pei invited him to come. He asked, "What did Rāhula consider to be foremost?
The Master replied, "I do not know. Pei then bowed and said, "A true pearl wrapped in coarse cloth."
In his eulogy for the portrait of Master Baoziyu, he said: "The sun rises over the connected mountains; the moon is full before the door. It is not that there is no body;

it is simply that one does not wish to reveal it entirely. One day, while the Master was sitting inside a tent, a monk asked: "It is not that there is no body; it is simply that one does not wish to reveal it entirely."
"Please, Master, reveal it fully. The Master pulled back the curtain and asked, "Do you see it? He replied, "I do not see it. The Master said, "It is not that you have brought no eyes."
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "Now, those who investigate the mystery must pass through the patriarchs and Buddhas before they can attain realization.

As the Venerable Xinfeng said: 'The teachings of the patriarchs and Buddhas are like encountering an enemy at birth; only then does one have the capacity for study. If you cannot pass through them, you will be deceived by the patriarchs and Buddhas.
A monk asked, "Do the patriarchs and Buddhas possess a mind that deceives others? The Master said, "Tell me, do rivers and lakes..."

The rivers and lakes have no intention to obstruct people, yet because people cannot pass through them, the rivers and lakes become an obstruction to people; one cannot say that the rivers and lakes do not obstruct people.

The patriarchs and Buddhas have no intention to deceive people, yet because people cannot penetrate them, the patriarchs and Buddhas become a deception to people; one cannot say that [they do not deceive].
The Buddhas and Patriarchs do not deceive people. If you can penetrate beyond the Buddhas and Patriarchs, then you have surpassed them.
If it is thus, only then will you realize the intent of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; only then will you be one with those of the "upward" direction.

If you have not yet penetrated this, but merely study the Buddhas and study the Patriarchs, then for ten thousand kalpas there will be no time of emergence. A monk asked: "How can one avoid being deceived by the Buddhas and Patriarchs?"
The Master said: "As for the Way, one must realize it for oneself before it can be attained.
Chan Master Tong of Beiyuan in Yizhou went to visit Dongshan.
Dongshan ascended the hall and said: "Cut off the master completely; do not fall into a secondary view. The Master stepped forward.
The assembly said, "One must know that there is one person who does not join the company. Dongshan said, "That is still the second view. The Master then overturned the meditation seat.
Dongshan said, "What about you, elder brother? The Master said, "I will tell you, Master, only when my tongue has rotted away.
Later, as he was taking his leave of Dongshan and preparing to enter the mountain passes, Dongshan said, "Be careful. The Feiyuan Pass is steep; look out for yourself."
After a long silence, Master Shishuang called out, "Attendant Dharma Master Tong! The Master responded. Shishuang said, "Why do you not go over the ridge?
Thereupon, the Master attained realization and never again crossed the ridge.

[The monk] said, "I cannot help but ask. Touhe said, "It is too far away. The Master said, "Many have mouths but do not get to drink tea."
The attendant of Deshan came to pay his respects. As soon as he had prostrated, the Master seized him and said, "Do you still agree with Qinshan’s way?
The attendant said, "I regret that I have stayed so long at Deshan; today I have no words with which to respond.
The Master then let go of him and said, "Respond as you please. The attendant thrust out his chest and said, "Now listen to me for a moment as I speak my mind."
The Master said, "That may be so under Deshan’s gate, but here it is of no use at all. The attendant said, "I have long heard that Qingshan does not deal with people according to worldly custom.
The Master said, "This will only trouble Deshan’s reputation. Go to the hall for your studies."
When Minister Chen Cao came to visit Master Zifu Ruo, the Master drew a circle. Cao said, "I have come as a disciple; even so, I am already at a disadvantage.
Yet you further draw this circle. The Master placed a single dot within it. Cao said, "I thought this was a ship from the Southern Barbarians."
The Master [Yunmen] then returned to his quarters and closed the door.

Zen Master Nanyuan Huiyong asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Xiangzhou. The Master asked, "What have you come here for? The monk said, "I have come specifically to pay my respects."
The monk bowed to the Master. The Master said, "I happen to have met the old man Baoying while he was away.
The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "I told you he was not here; why did you shout again? The monk shouted once more. The Master struck him. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "This staff was originally for you to strike me, but I have struck you instead so that these words may spread widely. You blind fellow! Go to the hall and practice."
A monk asked, "Where have all the sages of the past gone? The Master said, "They do not ascend to heaven; they enter hell. The monk asked, "And what about you, Preceptor?
The Master said, "Do you know where this old man Baoying has ended up? As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him with a whisk and said, "Do you know who it is that eats the whisk?
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said: *Note: The final line "The Master said" indicates the conclusion of the dialogue.*
"The command is actually yours to carry out. He struck once more with his whisk.
A monk came for an audience; as he was just entering the master’s quarters, the master pointed his finger and said, "Defeated! The master then picked up his staff and passed it to the monk.
As soon as the monk received it, the master struck him.
He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From Changshui. The Master said, "Does it flow east or flow west? The monk said, "It is not like that at all."
The Master asked, "How is it? The monk said, "Take care. The Master then struck him.
Another monk came to visit; the Master raised his whisk. The monk said, "Today you have failed. The Master lowered the whisk.
The monk said, "There is still this one remaining. The Master then struck him.
Attendant Shoukuo asked Master Deshan, "Where have all the sages of antiquity gone? Deshan said, "What? What?"
The Master said, "The imperial decree summons the flying dragon horse; a lame turtle pokes its head out. Shanzhao then retired.
The next day, after he had bathed and emerged, the Master served tea to him. Shanzhao tapped him once on his back and said, "What about yesterday's case?"
The Master said, "This old fellow has only today begun to have a glimpse of reality. Then Shanshan desisted.
Later, the Master went to Lukmon. One day, while he was seeing the monk Chu engaged in conversation with a monk, Lukmon came down from above and asked:
The Master said, "Monk Chu, what are you doing all day long, looking so disheveled and distracted?
Chu said, "Did you see me looking disheveled and distracted, Master? Mumen gave a shout; Chu also shouted. Both of them then ceased their activity.
The Master said, "Venerable ones, look at these two blind men! He then followed this by shouting himself. Mumen returned to his quarters and ordered an attendant:
"Please come up here, Master. He said, "Just now, when this old monk met with Chan-jun (Chu) as guest and host, where was there any failure?
The Master said, "I see your illness has grown even deeper. The Gatekeeper said, "Since I first saw Xinghua, I have understood."
The Master said, "When the Abbot arrived at Xinghua, I was his attendant; I remember the words spoken at that time.
The Gatekeeper said, "Please recite them for me. The Master then recounted: Xinghua asked the Abbot, "Where have you come from? The Abbot replied, "From Mount Wutai.
Xinghua said, "Have you seen Mañjuśrī? The Abbot then gave a shout. Xinghua said, "I asked you, 'Have you seen Mañjuśrī?'"
"Shuma! Why do you act so wickedly? The Master shouted again. Huahua remained silent. The Master prostrated himself.
Huahua said, "Tomorrow I will instruct someone to call for the Master. By the next morning, the Master had already departed. Huahua went up to the hall and said, "Look at this monk;
he is heading south carrying a broken fishing line. In the future, people will say he has seen Xinghua."
The Master said, "Today’s public case is exactly like that of such a time. Mén asked, "Why was Xinghuā speechless at that moment?
The Master said, "Because he saw that the Master did not understand the guest-host phrase, he remained silent.
When he wished to call upon the Master to engage in debate, the Master had already departed. The next day, Lùmén specially prepared tea for the evening assembly and addressed the congregation.
He said: "Those who study under the great masters must be thorough and meticulous. When entering the room for decisive discernment, one must not be casual.
To grasp a single phrase and take it as the ultimate limit, claiming 'I am sharp-witted,' is like when I first met Xinghua;
I recognized only his physical movements, and when people spoke of 'one shout' or 'two shouts,' I stopped there and took that to be the Buddha-dharma."
Today, having been seen through by one with clear eyes, it has become nothing but a source of laughter. What was the point of it?
It was simply because of my own pride and ignorance that I could not turn back to approach those of superior caliber.
Fortunately, a master of clear eyes did not spare his life or limb to provide public testimony; this kindness is difficult to repay. Why? Xinghua said: "Even if you were to shout yourself hoarse..."
The old man of Xinghua ascended to the thirty-third heaven, then tumbled back down; he had not a single breath left.
Slowly regaining his composure, he said to you, "It is not yet so. Why was this? It is because Xinghua has never scattered genuine pearls from within the purple silk curtain for you.
Why do you shout and clamor so wildly? This is truly what is called medicine and a warning.
He said, "The Way, O practitioner, is difficult to believe. Now, discern it clearly and directly; will you not then find joy for the rest of your life?
Your studies are complete.
This was Zen Master Ximing Siming of Ruzhou.
From the time the Venerable Congyi arrived at the Dharma assembly for ten days, he would constantly say to himself, "Let alone those who claim to understand the Dharma of the Buddha;
one cannot even find a person capable of raising a koan. When the Master heard this, he remained silent. On another day, as Congyi was ascending the Dharma hall, the Master called out, "Congyi!
Congyi raised his head, and the Master said, "Wrong. Congyi took two or three steps forward, and the Master said again, "Wrong. Congyi then approached him.
The Master said, "Regarding those two errors just now, was it the Senior Monk who was in error, or was it I, the old man of Ximing?
Wenji replied, "It was Wenji who was in error. The Master said, "Error! Error! He then added, "Senior Monk, stay here for the summer retreat; we shall deliberate together on these two errors.
Wenji did not agree and departed. Later, while residing at Tianping Mountain in Xiangzhou, he would frequently cite this previous conversation, saying, "I..."
While traveling on foot, I was driven by a fierce wind to Ruizhou. There, the Elder of the West Hall questioned me and made two consecutive errors.
He then asked me to stay for the summer retreat so that he might deliberate with me. I did not say that I was mistaken at that time;
rather, I knew I was mistaken as soon as I set out for the South.
On the day Master Baoshou was inaugurated at the hall, Sansheng pushed forward a monk. The Master struck him immediately.
Sansheng said, "To act as a teacher in this manner will not only blind the eyes of this monk, but will also blind the people of the entire city of Zhenzhou. The Master threw down his staff.
Taking up his staff, he returned to the abbot’s quarters.

Zen Master Chancha of Fengxi Tong’an was asked by a monk, “The student does not yet understand the timing; I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, “The uneven pines and bamboos enshrouded in mist.”
"Thin. Layered peaks and ridges; the moon rises late. The monk prepared to offer a word, but the Master said, "Before the sword and armor are deployed, the thief's body has already been exposed.
The monk asked, "Why? The Master said, "A refined bamboo before the frost need not be trimmed; ink and water merely boast of the dragon in the sea.
The monk circled the meditation seat and departed. The Master said, "Closing one's eyes to eat a snail—what a bitter and sour experience!"

The newly arrived monk, holding his staff, circumambulated the Master three times, shook the staff once, and said, "At the place where neither ordinary beings nor sages reach, I pray that the Master will speak.
The Master snapped his fingers three times. The monk said, "Today, Tong’an has been so startled that he has forgotten what came before and lost track of what followed. The Master said:
"Where are you, Upādhyāya, setting out for? The monk, having said "Venerable sir," was about to depart.

The Master said, "A patch-robed wanderer of the Five Lakes, a practitioner with a single staff—before you have reached Tong’an, you will surely be struck by doubt. The monk turned his head and said, "Hearing from afar is not as good as seeing nearby.
The Master said, "In greed for another cup of wine, he loses the fish in his full boat."
He asked the monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Jiangxi. The Master said, "How does the Dharma-way of Jiangxi compare to this place? The monk replied, [silently].
"Laiyu, you have questioned me; had you questioned anyone else, disaster would have ensued. The Master said, "I was a bit hasty just now. Laiyu said, "I am no infant;
it is useless to employ yellow leaves merely to stop a child's crying. The Master said, "I spare the turtle while harming the snapping turtle; whether to kill or to give life rests with me.
The monk asked again, "Having long cultivated the profound and subtle, how does one gain thorough understanding? The Master said, "I, the old monk..."
[The Master] turned his back. [The monk] asked clearly, "Please speak up. The Master said, "A swift hawk does not strike at sparrows by the fence.

The Master said, "If one looks into a mirror in the dark, who can distinguish beauty from ugliness? [The monk] said, "How can one thoroughly understand the higher mechanism? The Master said, "Why bother? [The monk] said, "Stop."
"Stop! The Master said, "You have just begun to understand how to ride a boat, yet you intend to leap across the Sword Water.
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "Wutai. The Master said, "Have you seen Mañjuśrī? The monk spread out both hands. The Master said, "You have spread out many hands;
Mañjuśrī is difficult to behold. The monk said, "This is killing me with breathlessness! The Master said, "You do not see him amidst the clouds."
The monk said, "A wild goose—how could it know the cold of the desert sands? The Master said, "You have come a long way to my chamber; I beg for a word from you, Master.

The Master said, "Under the gate of Sun Bin, one merely talks of divining by tortoise shells. The monk said, "One's reputation is not earned in vain. The Master said, "Go and drink tea. The monk, saying "Take care," then departed.
The Master said, "Though you have gained one field of glory, you have lost a pair of feet.
He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Taiyuan. The Master asked, "How is the Dharma-way in Taiyuan these days? The monk replied, [silently].
He saw only clouds following the rising sun and water following the ripples; he did not know what the Dharma-way of Taiyuan was like.

The Master said, "Is it not true that you have left Taiyuan? The monk said, "Suffering! Suffering! The Master said, "One does not behold the color of the ocean clouds, yet faintly perceives the sound of a drought thunder.
The monk said, "Trading gold for brass; hating the real and loving the false. The Master then returned to his quarters. The monk brushed his sleeves and departed.
[The monk] went out. The Master said, "When you can tuck in your head, then tuck it in.
When Chan Master Wuyin of Heyuan arrived at Jiufeng, Master Qian asked him, "Having come from afar, what have you seen? By what path must one emerge from birth and death?"
The Master replied, "The deep darkness has been cleared away; yet the blind remain blind. Guǐqián laughed and waved his hand at him, saying, "The Buddha-dharma is not like this.
The Master was displeased and asked, "Is there no skillful means? Guǐqián said, "Ask me. The Master repeated his previous words and questioned him again.
Guǐqián said, "A servant seeing a maidservant being diligent. Thereupon, the Master remained in attendance for over ten years.
Question: "To practice and study is called 'hearing' (learning); to sever study is called 'neighboring' (the limit). To go beyond these two is called 'truly transcending.
What is meant by truly transcending? The Master said: "Heshan knows how to beat the drum. [The questioner] asked: "What is the True Truth? The Master said:
"Heshan knows how to beat the drum. Question: "I do not ask about 'this very mind is Buddha. But what is 'neither mind nor Buddha'? The Master—
[The Master] said, "Heishan knows how to beat the drum. [The questioner] asked, "What is the matter that transcends [the mundane]? The Master said, "Heishan knows how to beat the drum.

One day, when Master Qingfeng was transmitting [the Dharma] to Chan Master Chu, Luopu asked, "Master of the Monastery, where have you come from? The Master said, "I have come from sweeping the snow. Luopu said, "The snow..."
"How deep is it? The Master said, "It is entirely upon the tree. Lü Pu said, "That may be so, but you will surely dwell in a snow cave in the future.
Later, he visited Bai Shui. Bai Shui asked, "I have heard it said that Lu Pu has a path of vital energy (*shengji*). Is this true?"
The Master said, “It is. Shui said, “You have blocked off the path of the living; come from the path of the dead. The Master said, “On the path of the living, there are countless dead people;
on the path of the dead, no living man finds a place. Shui said, “This is the way of Luopo; what about yours?
The Master said, “Not only Luopo, but even Jia Shan could do nothing about it. Shui said, “Why was it that Jia Shan—”
"How can one do anything about it? The Master said, "Have you not heard it said: 'The path of the living mechanism'?
A monk asked, "The Great Matter has already been clarified; why is it that one acts as if mourning for one's parents? The Master said, "Without the spring breeze, the flowers will not bloom;
yet once they have bloomed, the breeze blows them away."
When Zen Master Muping Shendao first visited Luopo, he asked: "Before a single bubble has arisen, how does one discern the current of the water? Luopo replied:
"Shifting the boat, he became familiar with the currents; raising the oars, he parted from the waves. The Master did not attain realization and went to consult Panlong.
He asked the same question as before. Panlong said: "Shifting the boat, one does not part from the water; raising the oars, one immediately loses the source. From this, the Master attained awakening.
Chan Master Tongquan of Yingzhou went to visit Huangshan.
Huangshan asked, "The Celestial Gate is closed; there is no path in the ten directions. If someone can speak, they shall wave their hand and exit the Zhang River.
The Master said, "The hibernation chamber does not open; the dragon has no dragon-phrase. Huangshan said, "Is this how you speak?"
The Master said, "If it is right, say directly that it is right; if it is not right, say directly that it is not right. Sanshan said, "Waving his hand, he departs across the Zhang River.
Sanshan asked again, "When it is said, 'Wherever Bian He goes, the Jingshan is beautiful; the jade seal is passed on by the Son of Heaven,' what then?"
The Master said: "The numinous crane does not rest beneath the forest trees; the rustic elder does not prize the years of great peace.
Shanshen approved of this. As for Master Yan of Ruiyan:
when he first paid his respects to Yantou, he asked, "What is the fundamental principle of constancy? Yantou said, "Movement. Yan asked, "When there is movement..."
"How is it? Tou asked. The Master said, "It is not the fundamental, constant principle. After a long silence, Tou said, "If you accept it, you have not yet escaped the sensory roots and objects;
if you do not accept it, you will sink forever into birth and death. Thereupon, the Master attained realization and prostrated himself in worship.
