Later, he went to pay his respects to Jiashan. Jiashan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "I have come from Wolong.
Jiashan asked, "When you arrived, had the dragon already risen? The Master looked back at him. Jiashan said, "This is like applying more moxibustion to a healed scar.
The Master said, "Why do you, Reverend, continue to cause such suffering? Jiashan then ceased speaking.
The Master asked Jia Shan, "In this way it is easy; not in this way it is difficult. In this way and in this way one is alert and aware;
not in this way and not in this way one dwells in the realm of emptiness. 'In this way' and 'not in this way'—I ask you, Master, to speak quickly.
Jia Shan said, "This old monk is deceiving you, Layman. The Master shouted, "Old monk! What time is it now?"
[The Master] paused and then went out.
Chan Master Lanshan Daoxian asked Shishuang:
"What is it like when arising and ceasing never cease? Shishuang replied: "One must become like cold ashes and withered wood."
"A single thought-moment spanning ten thousand years; the seal and its cover corresponding; entirely pure and free from a single speck. The Master did not attain realization.
He visited Yantou and asked the same question as before. Yantou shouted, "Who is it that arises and ceases? At this, the Master had an awakening.
While the Master was at Heishan, he saw Elder Gu off as they were leaving the gate. Holding up his staff, he suddenly thrust it forward.
Gu had no reply. The Master said, "A stone ox blocks the ancient road; a single horse gives birth to twin foals."
Baofu asked, "Regarding Yantou’s saying, 'In this way, in this way; not in this way, not in this way'—what is the meaning?
The Master called out, "Baofu! Baofu responded. The Master said, "Both are bright, yet both are dark. Baofu bowed in thanks.
Three days later, he asked again, "The other day I received the Master's compassionate instruction, but I simply could not see through it. The Master said, "I have told you everything."
[The Master] said, "I have understood. Fuku said, "The Master is carrying a torch while walking through the mountains. The Master said, "If it is so, then ask according to your point of doubt.
Fuku said, "What is meant by 'both being bright and both being dark'? The Master said, "To be born together and to die together."
Fú bowed again in thanks and withdrew. Separately, another monk asked Fú, "What is it like when one is born together and dies together?
Fú said, "Both sides should shut their dog mouths. The monk said, "Master, keep your mouth for eating your own rice.
That monk then asked the Master, "What is it like when one is born together and dies together? The Master said, "Like a cow without horns. [The monk] said, "Born together, but not dying together..."
"How is it at the time of death? He replied, "Like a tiger with its horns.

Master Xuan Sha Shibei, whose secular surname was Xie, was a native of Min County in Fuzhou. In his youth, he fished on the banks of the Nantai River; upon reaching maturity, he suddenly abandoned his boat.
He received the tonsure from Chan Master Lingxun of Fuyong Mountain. Wearing straw sandals and cloth robes, he took only enough food to sustain his breath and sat in meditation all day long;
the assembly marveled at him. Initially, he treated Xuefeng as his elder brother, but later he became his formal disciple. Xuefeng [regarded] him for his ascetic practices.
He was called Tou-tou. One day, Feng asked, "Which one is Bei Tou-tou? The Master said, "I would never dare deceive anyone.

On another day, Feng summoned him, saying, "Bei Tou-tou, why do you not go on a pilgrimage to study everywhere? The Master replied, "Bodhidharma did not come to the Eastern Land, and the Second Patriarch did not go to the Western Heaven.
Feng approved of this. Later, when they ascended Mount Xianggu, he then [bestowed the Dharma] upon him.

The Master joined forces with others to construct [the monastery], and seekers of the profound Way flocked there in great numbers. The Master entered the inner quarters to seek resolution from his teacher, never ceasing from morning until night.

Furthermore, he studied the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* and attained enlightenment regarding the mind-ground. Consequently, his responses to the needs of others were swift and nimble, and his insights were in perfect accord with the *Sūtras*.

Whenever scholars from various regions encountered points they could not resolve, they would invariably seek instruction from him. Even when engaging in rigorous inquiry with Xuefeng, he displayed the spirit of one who takes rightful precedence in the practice of benevolence.
He would not yield. Feng said, "Tou-tuo Bei is a man who has returned to his original state.
The Master took leave of Xuefeng, saying, "I inform the Abbot: every person is free and at ease; I am now going down the mountain.
Feng asked, "Who says such a thing? The Master replied, "It is you, the Abbot, who say such a thing. Feng said, "What do you think?"
"How is it? The Master said, "Not free and easy. Feng said, "I know.
Xuefeng said to the Master, "There is an Elder Nanji who has questions for which there is no answer that can be given.
One day Nanji arrived at Xuefeng’s place, and Xuefeng sent him to visit the Master. The Master said, "An ancient said, 'In this matter, only I can know it. Nanji—long... (text breaks off).
"Old man, how is it? Ji said, "One must know that which does not seek to know. The Master said, "Why does this old fellow on the mountain head undergo so much hardship?"
When the Master saw the monks approaching to pay their respects, he said, "Go ahead and bow; it is because of me that you may bow to you.
The King of Min sent lychees to the Master. Holding one up to show the assembly, the Master said, "This lychee is so red!
This lychee is so crimson! How do you all understand this? If you can speak of it as being of a single color—"
"This is still just a vague generalization. If you say it is the various colors, you again fall into the extremes of annihilationism or eternalism. How will you all handle this?
A monk stepped forward and said, "One must not fail to recognize the *lìzhī* (lychee). The Master provided his own response on the monk's behalf: "It is simply a *lìzhī*."
One day, the Master saw three newly arrived monks. He personally struck the *pǔqǐng* drum three times and invited them to his quarters.
After the newcomers had completed their formal observances (*weiyi*), they also personally struck the *pǔqǐng* drum three times and then entered the meditation hall (*sēngtáng*).
A long-resident monk came to inform the Master, saying, "The newcomers have slighted the Master. The Master said, "Ring the bell to assemble the assembly and examine them. Great!
The assembly had gathered, but the newcomer did not attend. The Master ordered an attendant to go and summon him.

As soon as the newcomer arrived at the Dharma Hall, he gave the attendant a slap on the back and said, "The Master calls for you. When the attendant reached the Master's quarters, the newcomer immediately returned to the hall.
Later, a long-resident monk asked, "Master, why did you not examine the newcomer? The Master replied, "I have already examined him for you."
Just then, Inspector Wei came to pay his respects and said, "The monk Cao Shan is truly extraordinary. The Master asked, "How many li is it from Fuzhou to Mount Cao?
Wei pointed to a monk standing nearby and asked, "Have you ever been to Mount Cao, Seat-Holder? He replied, "I have been there. Wei said:
"How many *li* is Cao Shan from Fuzhou? He replied, "One hundred and twenty *li*. Weizhong said, "If that is so, then you, Reverend, have not reached Cao Shan.
Weizhong then rose and prostrated. The Master said, "The Military Inspector ought to pay respects to this monk; this monk, moreover, possesses a sense of shame and remorse."
The Master traveled south. At Putian County, they welcomed him with a performance of a hundred theatrical acts.
On the following day, the Master asked Elder Xiaotang, "Where did all that clamor go yesterday? Tang pulled up the corner of his cassock. The Master said, "I suspect there is no connection."
Question: "I have heard the Master say that the nature of hearing pervades the entire dharma-realm. When Xuefeng beats the drum, why is it not heard here?
The Master said: "Who knows it is not heard?"
Changqing arrived. The Master asked, "Setting aside the medicinal taboos, how would you say it? Changqing said, "Why do you act so foolishly?
The Master said, "At Mount Xuefeng one gathers acorns for food; here at this place, the magpies drop their dung."
Lord Sengishu invited the Master to ascend the tower. First, he instructed the guest prefect, saying, "Wait until I have led the Great Master to the front of the tower;
then, remove the ladder. The guest prefect reported this command to the Master. The Lord said, "Please, Great Master, ascend the tower.
The Master looked at the tower, then looked back at the man, and said, "The Dharma is not a matter of such logic."
The Master was conversing with Quan Shou inside the room when a novice monk lifted the curtain to enter, then retreated and went back out.
The Master said, "That novice deserves twenty blows of the staff. Shou said, "If that is so, then the fault is mine.
The Master said, "The Buddha-dharma is not like this."
Ascending the hall, when the assembly had gathered, the Master took his staff and drove them all down at once.

He then returned to his quarters and said to an attendant, "Today I have produced a solution that nearly sent me straight into hell like a shot arrow. The attendant replied, "It is a great joy that the Master has regained a human body."
The Master gave this instruction: "The venerable elders of all quarters all say they 'receive beings and benefit life. But as for these three kinds of sick people—how do you receive them?
For one suffering from blindness, you raise the mallet or hold up the whisk, yet he does not see. For one suffering from deafness, you speak words of samādhi, yet he does not hear.
For one suffering from muteness, you try to teach him to speak, yet he cannot speak. If you cannot receive them..."
"It is so. The Buddha-dharma has no spiritual efficacy. At that time, a monk stepped forward and said, "Regarding the three types of sick people, do you permit this student to offer a discussion?
The Master said, "I permit it. How would you discuss them? The monk bowed respectfully and departed. The Master said, "That was not it."
"No. The Arhat said, "Guichen currently possesses eyes, ears, and a mouth; how will you, Master, receive him?
The Master replied, "I am ashamed," and then returned to his quarters.
Chan Master Changqing Huileng studied under Xuefeng and Xuansha for twenty years; he sat through seven worn-out meditation cushions, yet remained unenlightened regarding this matter.
One day, as he rolled up the curtain, he suddenly attained great enlightenment. He then composed a verse, which said: "How very strange! How very strange!
Rolling up the curtain, one sees the whole world. If someone asks me what school I belong to, I pick up my whisk and strike them right on the mouth!
Fengju said to Shanshan, "This boy has reached through to the bottom. Shanshan said, "Not yet. This is merely a composition of the conscious mind. One must go further."

"You must examine it thoroughly before you may attain it. When evening came, the assembly of monks came up to pay their respects. Feng asked the Master, "The Dharma Master Bei has not yet consented to you;
you must truly possess correct realization and bring it forth before the assembly. The Master again offered this verse: "Amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed.
Only when a person consents of their own accord do they become intimate with it. In the past, I mistakenly sought it along the road; today..."
"It appears to be ice within fire. Feng then looked at Sha and said, "No; this is merely a composition of the conscious mind.
The Master asked Feng, "Please grant me an instruction on the single path transmitted by all the sages of antiquity.

After a long silence, Feng smiled as the Master performed a prostration and withdrew. The Master then entered the abbot’s quarters to pay his respects. Feng asked, "What is it? The Master replied, "Today..."
"The weather is fine for drying the wheat. From this point on, his responses to inquiries never failed to accord with the profound principle (*xuanzhi*).
Once, while the Master was traveling the mountains with Baofu, Baofu asked, "The ancients said, 'At the summit of Mount Miaofeng.
Is it not simply this very thing? The Master replied, "It is indeed so, but it is a great pity."
The Master was at Xiyuan. He asked the Elder Xian, "There is Elephant Bone Mountain here; have you ever been there? Xian replied, "I have not.
The Master said, "Why have you not been there? Xian said, "Because I have my own fundamental matter to attend to.
The Master asked, "What is this fundamental matter of yours, Elder? Xian then lifted up a corner of his patched robe. The Master said, "Is it merely this?"
"This one—does something else exist besides it? He said, "Upādhyāya, what have you seen? The Master said, "How can you have a dragon's head and a snake's tail?
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "From Gushan. The Master said, "Gushan has a phrase that does not cross the stone gate."
Someone asked him, "How would you answer? He replied, "Last night I stayed at Baozi. The Master said, "A blow across the back! How would you respond to that?
He replied, "If the Master were to deliver such a blow, it would not have been in vain for me to receive the offerings of devas and humans.
The Master said, "How many times should I have let you off?"
Xuefeng asked, "I once saw Yaoshan ask Yangshan, 'Where have all the sages of the past gone?
Yangshan replied, 'Some are in the heavens; some are among humans. What do you say, Master, regarding Yangshan’s meaning?
The Master said, "If one were asked where the sages appear and disappear, saying it as he did would not be acceptable. Xuefeng said, "You flatly refuse to admit it. Suppose someone suddenly..."
The questioner asked, "How would you say it? The Master said, "Just say it is wrong. Feng said, "It is not you who are wrong. The Master said, "In what way does this differ from being wrong?"
A monk asked, "What is the Eye of the True Dharma? The Master said, "If there is a vow, do not scatter sand.
One day, Changqing said to Chan Master Congzhan of Baofu Monastery, "It would be better to say that Arhats possess the three poisons than to say that the Tathāgata [possesses them]."
"There are two kinds of speech. It is not that the Tathāgata has no speech; it is simply that he has no two kinds of speech.
The Master asked, "What is the Tathāgata’s speech? Qing said, "How could a deaf person hear it?
The Master said, "I knew you would speak from the secondary standpoint. Qing said, "And what about you? The Master said, "Go and drink tea."

[The Master] raised this as an example: Panshan said, "When light and its object have both vanished, what is it then? Dongshan said, "While light and its object have not yet vanished, what is it then?
The Master said, "According to the deliberations of these two venerable ancestors, they have still not reached a point of total eradication.
He then asked Changqing, "How would you say it now so as to achieve total eradication? Changqing remained silent for a long while. The Master said, "I knew the Master [would say this]."
He makes his living inside a ghost cave. Qingsong asked, "How so? The Master said, "Both hands griping the plow, the water rises above the knees.
He ascended the hall and said: "If someone passes behind the Buddha Hall and sees it is Zhang San or Li Si, yet if they pass before the Buddha Hall..."
[The Master] said, "It is past. Why do you not see it? Tell me, where does the efficacy of the Buddha-dharma lie?

The monk said, "Because there is a portion of coarse objects, I therefore do not see it. The Master rebuked him. He then provided a substitute answer [on the monk's behalf], saying, "If it were the Buddha Hall, you would not see it.
[The Master] asked, "If it is not the Buddha Hall, can it still be seen? The Master said, "If it is not the Buddha Hall, what is it that you see?"
When National Teacher Shenyuan Xing of Gushan was meeting with [Master] Zhaoqing, Zhaoqing said, "It is like being at home. The Master said, "You are truly insatiable. Zhaoqing said, "For now..."
[The guest] spoke modestly. The Master, however, said, "It is just a family meal. Qing said, "There is no firewood today. The Master said, "That is too stingy."
Qing said, "Take it away with ease.
The Master asked Baofu, "An ancient said, 'Not not-not, is-is. What is the meaning of this? Baofu picked up his tea bowl. The Master said, "Is that not excellent?"
The Master addressed the assembly, saying, "If one discusses this matter, it is like a single-bladed sword.
At that time, a monk asked, "I have heard the Master’s words that if one discusses this matter, it is like a single-bladed sword. The Master is a corpse; the student is a corpse.
What, then, is the sword? The Master said, "Drag out this corpse! The monk responded with an "Amen" (Ām), went beneath his robes and bowl, packed up his belongings, and departed.
When evening arrived, the Master asked the Head Seat, "Is the monk who engaged in dialogue still here? The Seat replied, "He left right then and there.
The Master said, "A fine twenty blows for you!"
The Master had a verse that said: "Directly beneath, it is still difficult to realize; Seeking through words, it becomes even more remote.
If one discusses the Buddhas and Patriarchs, They stand apart, separated by the ends of the earth. The Master raised this up and asked a monk, "How do you understand this?

The monk was speechless. He then said to an attendant, "I do not understand. Please provide a turning word on my behalf. The attendant said, "When the Master speaks in such a way, he is still separated from us by heaven."
The story reached its conclusion. When the monk related this to the Master, the Master called for his attendant and asked, "Did you provide a substitute response for this monk?
The attendant replied, "Yes. The Master then struck him and expelled him from the monastery.
The Master asked the Eastern Envoy, "As for Yangshan’s response to Muzhou—when he drew a line right before him—what was his meaning?
The Envoy said, "Was he a true master? The Master said, "Brother, you truly think so? What do you make of it? The Envoy said, [silently].
"The sun may become cold; the moon may become hot. The Master [Yunmen] grabbed the chest of Qingyuan and gave him a shove.
When Grand Marshal Wang An-guo asked the Abbot of Liaoyuan, "When the kalpa-ending fire blazes forth, where will you go to take refuge?
The Abbot replied, "I shall take refuge right here. The Grand Marshal did not approve and provided his own verse in his stead: "There is no place to take refuge. He stepped forward.
[The Master] asked, "Why do you not avoid him? The Grand Marshal said, "He does not show his head; what is there to avoid?
The Master said, "Where did you see him say he would not show his head?"
While the Master was conversing with the Grand Marshal Qingyuan Wang, he said, "All the various worldly studies are nothing but nets.
The Grand Marshal asked, "Are they still able to catch anything even now? The Master replied, "Grand Marshal! The Grand Marshal then understood.
The Grand Marshal then opened his hands and said, "Right now, what is there? The Master said, "Even this single net is not small.
The Grand Marshal cited the story of Nanyang calling for his attendant; Zhaozhou said, "It is like writing characters in the air:
although they do not take form, their traces are already manifest. The Master said, "As for speaking in such a manner, does one follow the National Teacher, or not follow the National Teacher?"
The Master said, "The Grand Marshal says that both 'following the school' and 'not following the school' are manifestations.
The Master asked, "As for Zhaozhou’s meaning, what is it? The Grand Marshal said, "Not to be ungrateful to Zhaozhou. The Master said, "That is a statement.
What is Zhaozhou’s meaning? The Grand Marshal said, "What? The Master said, "It is a manifestation. What is Zhaozhou’s meaning? The Grand Marshal—
[There was] no response.
Chan Master Shunde Daofu of Jingqing went to visit Xuefeng.
Xuefeng asked, "Where are you from? He replied, "A man from Wenzhou. Xuefeng said, "If that is so, then [I shall grant you] one..."
Xujue was a native of that region. [The Master] asked, "As for Xujue, where is he from? Feng said, "He deserves a good beating; let it pass for now.
One day, the Master asked, "Is it not the case that the ancient worthies transmitted mind by means of mind?
Feng said, "Furthermore, they did not establish written words or phrases. The Master said, "As for not establishing written words or phrases..."
[The Master] asked, "How did the Master [Nanquan] transmit it? Feng remained silent for a long while. The Master bowed in thanks.

Feng said, "Would it not be good if you asked me one more turn? The Master said, "I beg the Master for a turning phrase to ask. Feng said, "Is it just this? Or is there something else to deliberate upon?
The Master said, "If the Master acts thus, it will suffice. Feng said, "What about you? The Master said, "I would be failing [the Dharma]."
[The Master] killed a person. Xuefeng said to the assembly, "Dignified and profound. The Master stepped forward and asked, "What is this dignity and profundity?
Xuefeng stood up and said, "What are you saying? The Master stepped back and stood there.
Xuefeng delivered a formal statement, saying, "This matter is so noble and so subtle. The Master said, "Since I arrived here several years ago..."
"I have never heard the Master instruct in such a manner. Feng said, "Previously I had none, but now I have.

Does this not cause you any hindrance? [The Master] said, "I dare say it does not. This is the Master’s practice of never stopping where he is. Feng said, "It is because of you that I have come to be like this.
From this point on, the Master entered through faith. During a communal work session (*pǔqǐng*), Xuefeng raised the topic of Baizhang Huaihai saying, "To see form is to see the Buddha."
Xuefeng said, "Mind! Do you say there is a fault here or not? The Master said, "For what purpose did the ancients do this?
Feng said, "Even so, I wish to deliberate with you. The Master said, "In that case, it would be better to say, 'Tou is off plowing the field.
The Master went to visit Xuefeng again. Feng asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "From beyond the mountain ridges. Feng said, "What did you encounter there?"
He saw Dharma. The Master said, "Where else could you be? Feng said, "I do not yet believe you are.
The Master said, "Master, please do not be so sticky. Feng then desisted.
The student spat and said, "I request the Master to peck. The Master asked, "Is it still alive? He replied, "If it were not alive, one would be ridiculed by others.
The Master said, "You too are just a fellow from among the weeds."
One day, the Master personally struck the bell in the Sangha Hall and said, "Xuan Sha’s bottom line! Xuan Sha’s bottom line!
A monk asked, "What did Xuan Sha say? The Master then drew a circle. The monk said, "If one had not practiced for a long time, how could one know it was like this?
The Master said, "To lose money and suffer the consequences."
A monk asked, "A student has not yet reached the source; I beg the Master for an expedient means. The Master said, "What source? The monk said, "That source.
The Master said, "If it is that source, how could it accept an expedient means? The monk bowed and withdrew.
An attendant asked, "Master, was that not to strip him [of his delusions] just now? The Master said, "No. The attendant said, "Was it not to strip him [of his delusions]? The Master said, "No."
[The monk] said, “There is none. The monk asked, “I do not yet understand the meaning of this; what is your intention? The Master said, “A single drop of ink becomes two dragons.

Once, while they were working together to clear weeds, the bath attendant invited the Master to bathe. The Master paid no attention. When he invited him a third time, the Master raised his hoe as if to strike him, and the attendant ran away.
The Master called out, “Come! Come! The attendant turned his head back. The Master said, “In the future, when you encounter one who acts [as I do],”
Jiashan clearly recounted the incident. Later, when Tou arrived at Baofu, he had not yet finished recounting the previous words when Baofu covered his mouth with his hand.
Tou returned and related it to his teacher, who said, "Even if he acts in such a way, he has still not become a master."
The epitaph for National Teacher An-guo Hongtao by Master Shi Ju states: "When attained within the mind, even *eranda* (Ilan) becomes a sandalwood tree;
when lost in its essential meaning, even nectar becomes a garden of thorns. He asked a monk: "A single phrase must encompass both the meanings of attainment and loss."
"How would you say it? the Master asked. The monk raised his fist and said, "One cannot call this a 'fist. The Master did not approve;
he too raised his fist, showing it differently, saying, "It is precisely because one calls this thing a 'fist' [that it is so]."
When Chan Master Chuanfu of Qinghua first visited Nanta, Nanta asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Ezhou. Nanta asked, "What is the name of the Governor of Ezhou?
The Master said, "I do not dare to offend him while under his jurisdiction. Nanta said, "In this way, you do not violate the Way."
[He] was afraid. The Master said, "A man of great character—why must you test me? Nanta laughed heartily and subsequently granted him approval.
As for Chan Master Changsheng Jiaoran, he had long relied upon Xuefeng.
One day, while he was cutting down a tree with a monk, Xuefeng said, "When you reach the heartwood, stop. The Master [reached it].
[The Master] said, "Chop it off! Feng said, "The ancients transmitted mind-to-mind; why do you say 'chop it off'?
The Master threw down his axe and said, "Transmitted. Feng struck him with a staff and departed.
During a communal work session (*fusshō*), Xuefeng was carrying a bundle of rattan when he encountered a monk on the path; he immediately threw it down.
As the monk reached out to pick it up, Xuefeng kicked him over. Upon returning, he said to his teacher, "I felt quite swift today in kicking that monk.
The teacher replied, "It would have been more appropriate for you, Master, to take this monk's place in the Nirvana Hall. Xuefeng then desisted.
Xuefeng asked, "When both light and its object have vanished, what is it that remains? The Master said, "Let Jiao Ran pass.
Xuefeng said, "I let you pass; how would you explain this? The Master said, "I also let the Master pass, Jiao Ran.
Xuefeng said, "I grant you twenty blows! The Master then bowed.
Xuansha asked, “I observe that the Tathāgata does not come from the past, does not go to the future, and does not abide in the present.
What do you say to this, Elder? The Master said, “Grant me passage; I have a way to speak. Xuansha said, “I grant you passage. How will you speak? The Master remained silent.
Xuansha said, “Who will understand? The Master said, “Even the Teacher does not understand. Xuansha said, “Sentiment!”
"I know you are making your living inside a ghost cave. The Master dismissed him.
Upādhyāya Fu of Taiyuan once traveled through Zhejiang and attended a Dharma assembly at Mount Jing. One day, in front of the Great Buddha Hall, a monk asked him:
"Has the Elder ever been to Mount Wutai? The Master said, "I have. [The monk] asked, "Did you see Mañjuśrī? The Master said, "I saw him."
[The monk] asked, "Where did you see him? The Master said, "I saw him in front of the Buddha Hall at Jingshan. Later, that monk traveled to Minchuan and related this to Xuefeng.
Xuefeng said, "Why did you not tell him to come across the ridge? Upon hearing this, the Master packed his bags and entered the ridge.
When he first arrived, he stayed at Xuefeng’s monastery and rested his staff there; he then shared some tangerines with the monks. Changqing asked, "Where did you bring [these] from?"

[The monk] came forward. The Master said, "You have brought something from beyond the ridges. [The monk] said, "It was not easy to travel such a long distance; I carried it here on my shoulder. The Master said, "A tangerine?"

Tangerines. The next day he went up the mountain. When Xuefeng heard of this, he assembled the community. When the Master arrived at the Dharma Hall, he looked toward Xuefeng and then went down to oversee the administrative affairs.
The following day, he went back up to pay his respects and said, "Yesterday I offended you, Venerable Sir.
Xuefeng said, "Since you know it was such a matter, let it rest."
While Baofu was selecting melons, the Master arrived. Baofu said, "If you can speak the Way, I will give you a melon to eat. The Master said, "Hand it over to me.
Baofu passed him a slice; the Master took it and departed immediately.
Gushan asked, "Before your parents were born, where was your nose? The Master said, "You, elder brother, speak first.
Gushan said, "Now that you are born, tell me, where is it? The Master did not approve. Gushan then asked, "How about this?
The Master said, "Bring me the fan in your hand. Gushan gave him the fan and again questioned him on the previous matter. The Master shook the fan.
"No," said the Master. Shan Wangmei could not fathom this; he struck the Master with one punch.
A monk asked Zen Master Daling of Silla Country, "What is purity in all places? The Master said, "Cutting the jade branch—every inch is treasure. He then split [the branch].
Sandalwood: every single piece is fragrant.
Zen Master Jinfeng Congzhi asked a monk, "Where have you set out from? The monk replied, "Zhaozhou. The Master said, "Whose Dharma heir was Zhaozhou? The monk replied, "Nan..."
[Nanquan] said, "When did you ever leave Zhaozhou? The monk asked, "I do not know, Master; what is your honorable intention in this matter?
The Master said, "Zhaozhou truly succeeded Nanquan. That evening, the monk requested further instruction, saying, "Today I have received the Master’s compassion, yet I have not yet understood.
I pray that the Master will point the way for me. The Master said, "If you go elsewhere, do not say that these later words are gold."
At the foot of the peak, [Fengxue] asked, "Why is it so? [Zhaozhou] said, "I fear it would bring shame upon Zhaozhou.
One day, as the Master was ascending the hall and eating *hūbǐng* (sesame cakes), he took up one cake, walked around the head of the seat (*shàngzuò bǎntóu*) once, and returned.
When the assembly saw this, each of them joined their palms. The Master said, "Even if you were to raise your hands to the utmost degree, you would still only obtain..."
"Half. Later that evening, a monk requested instruction, saying: "Today the Master served fried cakes (*hūbǐng*).

When he saw the assembly of monks with palms joined, he said, 'Even if one were to raise both hands to their utmost extent, one would still only obtain half. I pray the Master will explain this in its entirety."

The Master made a gesture with his hand as if picking up a cake and asked, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Even Jinfeng would only have been able to say half of it."
As the monk was inquiring after his well-being, the Master seized him and said, "Do not dare to tell anyone that I have a kōan to present to you.
The monk made a gesture as if listening. The Master gave him a slap. The monk asked, "Why did you strike me?
The Master replied, "I want this story to circulate."

Ascending the hall, the Master said: "Twenty years ago, this old monk had the heart of a grandmother; twenty years later, he has no grandmotherly heart. A monk asked, "What is the grandmotherly heart of twenty years ago?
The Master said, "When asked about the ordinary, he answered with the ordinary; when asked about the holy, he answered with the holy.
The monk asked, "What is the absence of the grandmotherly heart of twenty years later? The Master said, "When asked about the ordinary, he does not answer with the ordinary..."
Answer: To answer an ordinary person is not to answer a sage.
When a monk arrived, Chan Master Guangli Rong of Chuzhou held up his whisk and said, "Does this old fellow from Zhenxi still possess the eye? The monk replied, "I do."
Jiā did not dare to look at another’s faults. The Master said, “This old monk is dead in your hands, O disciple.
The monk pointed to his chest and then went out. The Master said, “Disciple, you have come to see the former Master.
That evening, after inviting him for tea, the monk picked up his cup and said, “This is the matter concerning the appearance of all Buddhas in the world. What is it like before they have appeared?”
"Worldly matters," [the Master] said. He pushed away the bowl with his hand and said, "The moment you, the *jiaoli*, die, you will be in the hands of this old monk.
The monk said, "The five-li milestone stands outside the city gate. The Master said, "To trouble and confuse a teacher without cause.
The monk then rose to thank him for the tea. The Master said, "I specifically thank you, *jiaoli*, for visiting."
A monk asked Chan Master Tong’an Pí of Fengxi Mountain, “What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, “The golden rooster carries its chicks back to the Milky Way;

the jade hare conceives her fetus and enters the Purple Microcosm. The monk asked, “If a guest should suddenly arrive, with what will you entertain them? The Master said, “The golden fruit comes in the morning.”
The monkey plucks it away. The jade flower returns at evening, carried by the phoenix.
A newly arrived monk enters. The Master asks, "Where have you come from? He replies, "From Hunan.

The Master says, "Do you know that here at Tong’an, wind and clouds embody the Way, and the flowered balustrades are the pivot of the universe? He replies, "I know. The Master says, "This is not your realm. The monk then gives a shout. The Master—

He said, "A short-lived peddler of firewood, boasting in vain of his books and sword. As the monk was about to offer a reply, the Master said, "Before the sword and armor are even deployed, the thief's true self has already been exposed."
Chan Master Foji Benkong went to visit Yunju.
He prostrated and asked, "When two dragons contend for the pearl, who is the one that obtains it? Yunju said, "Cast off your karmic body and come;
then we shall meet. The Master said, "The karmic body has already been cast off. Yunju said, "Where is the pearl?"
The Master had no reply.
When Chan Master Zhang of Jishan was at Touzi serving as a fire-keeper,
Touzi was drinking tea with him and said to the Master, "The myriad phenomena of the forest and the heavens..."
[The Master] said, "It is all right here inside. The Master poured out the tea and asked, "Where are the myriad phenomena of the forest and the ten thousand images?
The monk said, "What a pity about this bowl of tea! Later, the Master went to visit Xuefeng. Xuefeng asked, "Are you not the firewood-gatherer Chang?
The Master then made the gesture of a wheel-turning staff (*cakra*), and Xuefeng approved him.
When Chan Master Zhuxi Qian was receiving visitors, National Teacher Shao arrived. During their meeting, they heard the sound of a dog biting a "spirit mouse. Shao asked, "What is that sound?
Zhuxi said, "It is the sound of a dog biting a spirit mouse. Shao said, "If it is a spirit mouse, why is it being bitten by a dog? Zhuxi said, "It has been bitten to death."
Shao said, "What a fine dog! The Master struck him. Shao said, "Do not strike; I still have my point. The Master desisted.

Zen Master Yunju Daoyuan was asked by a monk, "When one encounters a fierce tiger on the road, what should be done? The Master said, "A thousand people, ten thousand people do not encounter it. Why is that?"
The Acharya encountered [this] specifically.
He asked: "What is it like when one sleeps alone on a solitary peak? The Master said: "He would rather leave the seven bays of the monks' hall empty than sleep there.
Who taught you to sleep alone on a solitary peak?"
Question: An ancient said, "If you wish to maintain this matter, you must stand atop the highest mountain peak and walk upon the deepest ocean floor.
What is the meaning of this? Answer: High peaks and deep seas are utterly remote, solitary, and perilous; how could they be like the soft warmth within your inner chambers?
Question: "What is the Bodhisattva Red-Crested King? The Master said: "Why ask about this red-headed fellow?
Chan Master Lingquan Guiren initially asked Shushan:
"A withered tree blossoming with flowers—does this accord with him? Is it a phrase of this side, or a phrase of that side?"
[The Master] asked, "What is the phrase for that side? Sanshan said, "A stone ox breathes forth the mist of three springs;
a numinous bird does not perch in the shadowless forest."
A monk asked, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa? The Master said, "It is just like that of a butcher. The monk asked, "How does one conduct oneself?
The Master said, "Breaking the fast and violating the precepts. The monk asked, "In the end, what is it? The Master said, "Because there is no gathering of causes, there is no entry into results."
A layperson asked, "Can ordinary people also attain the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Which terrace is without the moon?
Whose tree does not bloom in spring?
—From *Fulong Fenglin Chanshi* (The Chan Master Fulong Fenglin).

A monk asked, "Does the Master still have attachment to wealth and beauty? The Master said, "I do. The monk said, "Since you are a *kalyāṇamitra*, why then do you have attachment to wealth and beauty?
The Master said, "Those who recognize kindness are few."

Master Xianyun of Shimen asked Qinglin, "How should one apply the mind to become equal to the various sages? Qinglin looked up toward the sky, remained silent for a long while, and then said, "Do you understand?
The Master replied, "I do not understand. Qinglin said, "Go; there is no place for you to apply the mind. The Master prostrated and attained awakening. Furthermore—
He did not travel elsewhere, but instead became the head gardener. One day, while he was standing in attendance after returning from work, Lin asked, "What have you been doing today?
The Master replied, "I have been planting vegetables. Lin said, "The entire world is the Buddha-body; where do you intend to plant them?
The Master said, "With a golden hoe that does not stir the soil, the spiritual sprouts grow wherever they may be. Lin was delighted. The next day, Lin entered the garden and called out, "Yun!"
"Upādhyāya," [the Master] replied, "I shall comply. Lin said, "I have planted an extra tree that casts no shadow, to leave for later generations to behold.
The Master said, "If it is a tree that casts no shadow, how could it be planted? Lin said, "Setting aside for a moment the fact that it cannot be planted, have you ever seen its branches and leaves?
The Master said, "I have never seen them. Lin said, "Since you have never seen them, how do you know it cannot be planted? The Master said, "..."
Zhi said, "I have never seen such a thing; therefore, I do not accept its planting. Lin said, "So it is, so it is.

As Qinglin was about to pass into *parinirvāṇa*, he summoned the Master. The Master responded with an "Amen" (*Ām*). Lin said, "When the sun turns behind the western mountains, you must not settle [the matter] casually.
The Master said, "Snow fills the golden sandalwood trees; the numinous branches are springtime for all eternity. Lin said, "Should someone ask—"
"You are concerned with the matter of the golden needle and thread pouch. What do you say to this? The Master said, "If it were something like feathers or down, I would never dare to act rashly."
Question: "Without falling into the trap of mechanical devices, I ask the Master to speak directly. The Master said: "The profound moon and swift mechanism are beyond compare.
How many people have you questioned thus far? He replied: "I am questioning the Master right now. The Master said: "Good brother! When the clouds part, there is no need to hide the nine-tailed fox.
Forgive your remaining years of life; return quickly to your mountain retreat."
Question: "When the moon rises at the edge of the clouds, what is it like? The Master said: "Three children embrace a flower drum;
good brother, do not come to block my path to the goal."
When Hannyaji Temple was burned down, someone asked, "Since it is Prajñā (Wisdom), why was it burned by fire?
The Master said, "A single iron bar stretching ten thousand miles. The Master often responded to situations with the words, "Good elder brother," and was thus known at the time as Brother Monk.
A monk asked, "What is it like when there is no movement from suchness? The Master said, "When will you ever reach an end?
The monk asked, "How is it so? The Master said, "The stone door has no bolt."

A monk asked Chan Master Chongyun Hui, "The main road is level and smooth; how should one tread upon it? The Master said, "If I were to point it out to you, you would go off toward the east, west, south, or north."
A monk asked Chan Master Baozi Zhangyu:
"When emotion arises, wisdom is obstructed; when appearances change, the essence becomes distinct. But what is it like when emotion has not yet arisen? The Master said:
[The monk] said, "When emotion has not yet arisen, what is there to separate? The Master said, "This lad has not yet met his match.
—Master Yunmen Wenyan.
The Master was at Xuefeng. A monk asked Xuefeng, "What is the meaning of: 'When the eyes encounter it, one does not understand the Way;

when the feet move, how can one know the road? Xuefeng said, "Heaven! Heaven! The monk did not understand and subsequently asked the Master, "What is the intent behind 'Heaven! Heaven!'? The Master said:
"Three catties of hemp; one bolt of cloth. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "I further offer you three feet of bamboo.
Upon hearing this, Feng said joyfully, "I have long harbored doubts about this patchwork robe."
The Master was in the assembly of Master Yun of Xizhong. One day, while drinking tea, he raised the question posed by Master Yun:
"Seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing are the Dharma; yet the Dharma is apart from seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing—how is this so?
A monk standing nearby said, "To see is precisely all that is currently seen, heard, sensed, and known before one's eyes; these are the Dharma, and yet even the Dharma cannot be apprehended."
The Master clapped his hands once. Yun then raised his head. The Master said, "You still lack one move.
Yun said, "At this point, I do not understand."
The Master arrived at Wolong and asked, "Does one who has realized their own nature still perceive a self? Wolong said, "Only when one does not perceive a self does one truly realize it.
He asked again, "That which is learned upon the long meditation benches—what level of capacity is that?
Wolong said, "It is the second capacity. The Master asked, "What is the first capacity? Wolong said, "Tie your straw sandals tight."
He arrived at Tiantong. Tiantong said, "Can you yet settle this with certainty? The Master said, "What does the Monk mean by this?
Tiantong said, "If you do not understand, you are wrapped up before your very eyes. The Master said, "If one understands, one is wrapped up before one's very eyes."
He arrived at Gao’an Lake. Upon hearing the Master’s ascent to the hall, he said: "Do not say that only those who have not yet attained realization are constantly in a state of anxious agitation.
Even those who have attained realization and clearly know where they are going are still in a state of anxious agitation. The Master went down from the seat and asked the Head Seat:
"What was the meaning of the Master’s statement just now? The Head Seat replied: "A state of anxious agitation. The Master said: "Head Seat, for a long time..."
"Residing here, with white hair and yellowed teeth, one speaks these words. The monk asked, "And what about you, Senior? The Master said, "If you wish to speak, you may;
if you see, then you see. If you do not see, do not speak recklessly. The monk asked, "As for saying 'floating and pressing,' what does that mean?
The Master said, "A cangue upon the head and shackles upon the feet. The monk said, "In that case..."
"In that case, there would be no Buddha-dharma. The Master said, "This is the realm of great beings such as Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra.
He asked a newly arrived monk, "You who travel on pilgrimage from all quarters say, 'I know it exists.
Bring me the three thousandfold world-system and place it upon the tip of my eyelash! The monk said, "Yes. The Master said, "Why is it that Qiantang is three thousand *li* from the capital?"
The monk said, “How could that concern him? The Master said, “This fellow is a liar who preys on the empty air.
He then asked the Head Seat, “Are heaven, earth, and the great world the same as yourself, or are they different? The monk said, “The same.
The Master said, “As for all living beings—moths, silkworms, and ants—are they the same as yourself, or are they different? The monk said, “The same. The Master said, “Why then do you interfere?”
The two masters waited for one another.
When the lecture was concluded, the Abbot invited Cuiyan for a meal. Cuiyan said, "I have a question for you, Master.
If you can answer it, I shall provide the meal. Cuiyan then picked up a sesame cake and asked, "Does this possess the Dharma-body? The Master replied, "It does."
"Regarding the Dharma-body," Yanguan said, "In that case, you are consuming the Dharma-body. The Master remained silent. Bencheng spoke on his behalf, saying, "What fault is there?
Yanguan did not approve. Dongshi said, "Yes! Yes! The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "I offer my special thanks to the Master for descending to honor this empty assembly."
Question: "What is it like when the trees wither and the leaves fall? The Master said: "The essence is revealed by the golden wind.
A monk who was a lecturer visited him. After some time had passed, he remarked: "Before I reached Yunmen, it was just like the newly risen moon;
once I arrived there, it became all crooked and bent. When the Master learned of this, he asked: "Was that something you said? He replied: "Yes. The Master said: "How so?"
"Good. I ask you: what is the newly risen moon? The monk then rubbed his forehead and made the gesture of gazing at the moon.
The Master said, "If you act like this, you will lose your eyesight in the future. After ten days had passed, the monk returned. The Master asked again, "Do you understand yet?
The monk replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Ask me. The monk then asked, "What is the newly risen moon?"
[The monk] asked about the moon. The Master said, "It is curved and winding. The monk was at a loss. Later, the monk indeed lost his eyesight. [The Master] asked:
"One lifetime accumulating evil without knowing good; one lifetime accumulating good without knowing evil—what is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "A candle."
Question: I have heard it said in the past: "When one realizes, karmic obstacles are originally empty; when one has not realized, one must repay old debts.
I do not know whether the Second Patriarch had realized this or not. The Master said: "Certainly."
The Master asked, "Where have you newly arrived from? The monk replied, "Silla. The Master said, "What did you bring across the sea? The monk replied, "The grass-thief has been utterly defeated.
The Master extended his hand and said, "Why are you here with me? The monk replied, "Exactly so. The Master said, "Feel free to leap about as you please. The monk was speechless.
A monk asked, "How can one ensure that the twelve periods of the day do not pass in vain? The Master said, "Where would you place this question?
The monk said, "I do not understand; I ask the Master to provide an illustration. The Master said, "Bring me a brush and inkstone.
The monk then brought the brush and inkstone. The Master composed a verse, saying: "To act without looking back is already a deviation; If you intend to deliberate, when will you ever awaken?"
Question: "What is it like when one swallows it all in a single gulp? He said: "I am inside your belly. The questioner asked:
"Why are you, Master, inside this student's belly? The Master said: "Give me back the head of the phrase."
The Master asked the rector Shun of Lingzhong, "When the ancients raised their whisk and then lowered their whisk, what was the meaning?
Shun replied, "Seen before the whisk; seen after the whisk. The Master said, "So it is! So it is! Later, the Master raised this same question to ask a monk.
The Master asked, "Do you say 'Yes' or 'No'? The monk had no reply. The Master said, "Is this not a breach of propriety?
He then asked the steward, "Where have you been? The steward replied, "I have been cutting thatch. The Master asked, "How many patriarchs have you cut down? The steward replied, [silence].
"Three hundred blows. The Master said, "In the morning three thousand blows, in the evening eight hundred blows. The ladle-handle of the eastern house is long;
the ladle-handle of the western house is short. What about that? Suizhi was speechless. The Master then struck him.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Xichan. The Master said, "What words or phrases did Xichan have?
The monk spread his two hands. The Master gave him a slap. The monk said, "My point remains. The Master then spread his own two hands. The monk was speechless. The Master struck him again.

He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come to pay respects at the pagoda. The Master said, "You are mocking me. The monk said, "I have truly come to pay respects at the pagoda.
The Master said, "In that case, you do not even observe the five precepts."
He asked a monk, "What sutra are you studying? The monk said, "The *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*. The Master said, "Your meaning has fallen. The monk asked, "In what way has my meaning fallen?
The Master said, "Go out yourself and take it with you."
The Master asked a monk, "What sutra are you reading? The monk pointed instead to a nearby monk and said, "Master, why do you not answer me?
The Master said, "Why does the pillar retreat three thousand li? The monk said, "How could that concern him? The Master said:
Among those who merely parrot the words, it is said: "It would have been fitting not to recognize the situation.

When the Master saw the rice steward, he asked, "Are you the rice steward? He replied, "I am. The Master said, "How many grains of rice are within each husk? How many husks are there within each grain of rice?
The steward had no reply. A later master provided this substitute response: "I gaze at the stars and look toward the moon."
The Imperial Tutor asked Beiyuan: "An ancient said, 'Universally manifesting the form-body, the samādhi of universal practice.
Why, then, does the Buddha-dharma not reach the continent of Uttarakuru? Beiyuan said, "Precisely because it is a universal practice, it does not go there. The Master said: [This is the meaning.]
When a question was posed according to the Dharma, the Master was seated.
A monk came up at an improper time, and the Master asked, "What are you doing? The monk replied, "I have come to seek instruction. The Master said:
"What doubts do you have? The monk said, "I once asked the Master: 'One night’s awakening carries firewood; firewood carries one night’s awakening.
The Master struck the chair three times and said, "How do you understand this? The monk said, "Everything depends on the occasion.
The Master rolled up his fists and said, "Shall I give you a wrestling match? The monk had no reply. Next—

One day, a monk went up to the master again. He happened upon the master while he was washing his face and rinsing his mouth. The master took a water bowl and handed it to the monk, saying, "Take this back and put it in the kitchen.
The monk took it away and then returned. When the master saw him coming, he exited through the back gate.
The monk said, "I have come to seek instruction, yet I have received nothing but a single bowl."
Because he was making offerings to an arhat, he asked the monks, "Tonight we are making offerings to an arhat; do you say that the arhat will come or not?
The monks had no reply. The Master said, "Ask me. The monk then asked, and the Master said, "Change the water and add incense. The monk said, [I understand].
"If it is so, then he has come. The Master said, "What kind of 'hunger-chaser' dumplings are there?
Come down quickly! One day, while walking, a monk followed behind him. The Master raised his fist and said, "How many such large chestnuts can you eat?
The monk said, "Master, do not be mistaken. The Master said, "It is you who are mistaken. The monk said, "Do not force the honest to be wicked."
"Base. The Master said: "In a quiet place, *svāhā*. He asked:
"What is the teaching for the one era? The Master said: "I speak to each one."
Question: "When it is neither the immediate function nor the immediate matter, how is it? The Master said: "State it upside down. The Master asked:
"The ancient Buddha intersecting with the pillar—what kind of function is that? A monk asked: "What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "A single length of rope for thirty coins.
He then provided an alternative response to the previous question, saying: "Clouds rise on the southern mountain; the northern mountain descends."
It rained. A monk asked again, "A single silk sash was bought for thirty coins; what do you say to that? The Master said, "I will hit you with it.
The Master went to the capital at the invitation of the Prince of Guang and stayed there, receiving offerings for more than two months.

Upon returning to the mountain, he addressed the assembly, saying, "I have been away from the mountain for sixty-seven days. Now I ask you: how was it during those sixty-seven days? The assembly was speechless.
[The student] was able to respond. The Master said, "Why do you not say that the Master eats a great deal of noodles in the capital?
He addressed the assembly, saying, "An ancient worthy said: 'Medicine and illness treat one another. The entire earth is medicine; which of these is your own self?"

The Master said, "When encountering the lowly, one is immediately noble. The monk asked, "I beg the Master for instruction. The Master clapped his hands once, held up his staff, and said, "Take this staff.
The monk took it and snapped it into two pieces. The Master said, "Even if you were as capable as that, you still deserve thirty blows of the staff."

Addressing the assembly: "When the ancestral masters of the past and the Buddhas of the three periods of time preached the Dharma, why did the mountains, rivers, the great earth, the grasses, and the trees not go away?
[The Master] spoke on their behalf: "A newcomer performing the rites of courtesy."
Addressing the assembly, he said: "The staff has transformed into a dragon and swallowed up heaven and earth. From where do the mountains, rivers, and the great earth come?
Whenever the Master caught sight of a monk, he would simply say, "Jian" (To perceive). If the monk attempted to respond, he would say, "Ei. He did this as a constant practice. Therefore...

The *Records of Disciples* (Mén dìzǐ lù) states: "Guàn, Jiàn, Yì. Chan Master Deshan Mi deleted the character "Guàn" and used only the two characters "Jiàn, Yì" as a verse, calling it the "Extraction of Guàn Verse" (Chōu gù sòng).
Chan Master Bazhao Jiche first visited Fengxue.
Fengxue asked, “What is the True Dharma Eye? The Master replied, “A clay pellet. Fengxue was struck by this.
Subsequently, he went to visit the former Master Bazhao. As Bazhao ascended the hall, he cited Yangshan’s saying: “Two mouths, one without a tongue; this is...”
“My fundamental teaching—Master, you have realized it. He prostrated and took his leave.
At Chengtian Monastery, he bid farewell to Chan Master Ceshuo.
A monk asked: “When the myriad sins are like frost and dew, and the sun of wisdom is able to dispel them, what then? The Master said: “The pavilions and terraces are deep.”
Night rain. When the pavilions are still, the bell tolls. A monk asked: "For what reason is it said that when causes and conditions meet, the retribution is received by oneself?
The Master said: "The pen manages the writing; a fragment of the tongue understands speech."
Chan Master Fengxue Yanzhao went to visit Nan’uan.
Upon entering the gate, he did not prostrate. Nan’uan said, “Upon entering the gate, one must discern the host. The Master said, “I ask you, Master, to distinguish this for me.
Nan’uan patted his left knee once; the Master then let out a shout. Nan’uan patted his right knee once.
The Master shouted again. The Abbot said, "Setting aside the single blow on the left, what about the single blow on the right?
The Master said, "Blind! The Abbot then raised his staff. The Master said, "Do not wield the staff blindly; do not strike the Master without cause. Say that I did not warn you."
The Head of the Monastery threw down his staff and said, "Today you have been thoroughly outwitted by this yellow-faced monk from Zhejiang.

The Master said, "The Abbot seems very much like one who has failed to obtain alms and yet falsely claims not to be hungry. The Head of the Monastery asked, "Has the *śrāmaṇera* ever been to this place before?
The Master said, "What kind of talk is that? The Head of the Monastery said, "I am merely asking you a straightforward question. The Master said, "In that case, you cannot let me go either."
[The Master] passed through [the hall], then descended to join the assembly. Upon finishing, he returned to the Hall to pay his respects. The Abbot asked, "Disciple, whom have you studied under?
The Master replied, "I spent the summer retreat with Attendant Kuò at Huayan Monastery in Xiangzhou. The Abbot said, "Then you have personally met a master of the Way.
The Abbot then asked, "How do they deliberate upon 'a single blow' in the South? The Master replied, "They deliberate upon it as something extraordinary. The Master... [continued].
He then asked, "How do you, Master, deliberate upon this one blow here? Yunyan took up his staff and said, "In the blow there is no patience with birth;
when confronting the opportunity, the teacher is not seen. At these words, the master attained a great penetration into the profound principle. He subsequently remained in attendance for six years.
One day, Nanyuan asked, "Have you heard the words Linji spoke when he was about to pass away? He replied, "I have heard them.
Nanyuan said, "Linji said, 'Who would have known that my Treasury of the True Dharma Eye would perish with this blind donkey?
Throughout his life, Linji was like a lion—seeing him was enough to kill. Now that he is about to die, why does he kneel and tuck his tail in like this? The monk replied:

As he was about to pass away, he secretly entrusted [the Dharma] to Jiangzhong. "The Master's entirety is precisely this secrecy," [Jiangzhong] said. He asked again, "How is it that the Three Sages also remained silent?
He replied, "A true son who has personally entered the inner chamber is not the same as a traveler outside the gate. Nan'uan nodded his head in approval.
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "The Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs is like the mechanism of an iron ox: when it departs, it is sealed; when it stays, it is broken.
But as for neither departing nor staying—is it sealed? Or is it not sealed? Is there anyone who can say?
At that time, the Elder Lupi came forward and asked, "This student possesses the mechanism of the iron ox; I pray the Master will not apply the seal. The Master said:

Dongshan said, "I am accustomed to fishing for whales and sea monsters in the vast depths; yet I pity those who take frog-like steps, wallowing in the mud and sand. Zhaozhou Bipo poured forth his thoughts. The Master shouted, "Elder, why do you not advance a word?
As Bipo hesitated, the Master struck him with a whisk and asked, "Do you still remember the essential phrase (huatou)?
As Bipo was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him again with the whisk. At that time, a cattle herder said, "I truly know it now."

"The Buddha-dharma is just like the king’s law. The Master asked, "What principle do you see? The official replied, "If one should cut down what ought to be cut down but does not, it will instead invite chaos.
The Master then descended from his seat.
Question: "When that which changes not according to conditions suddenly encounters one who understands, what then? The Master said: "Donning a straw raincoat, standing askew beyond a thousand peaks;
leading water to irrigate vegetables before the Five Elders."

Question: "The nine months of summer retreat have concluded; we request the Master to offer words of commendation. The Master said: "Drawing forth the whisk from the sleeve, the rain opens the dragon cave;
raising the cup, the waves surge and the flower emerges from the bowl-bag."
Question: "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said: "The horseherd’s wife at the sands of the Jinshe River.
Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "The bamboo-stem whip beneath the Zhangling Mountain."
A monk asked Zen Master Huanglong Huikai Chao-hui, "We meet in a moment of urgency;
I ask the Master to convey the message. The Master said, "The skirt-belt is fragrant from the fire."
A monk asked, "What is it like when the wind is calm and the waves are still? The Master said, "Five *liang* hang from the top of a hundred-foot pole.
A monk asked, "'A hair swallows the vast ocean; a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru. This is not yet the student's fundamental matter.
What is the student's fundamental matter? The Master said, "The sealed lid is lifted in the marketplace."

Chan Master Mingzhao Deqian asked the senior monk Qing about the story of Yangshan planting his spade, saying, "The ancients' intent lies in the place where they fold their hands; it lies in the place where the spade is planted.
The Master called out, "Qing! Qing responded, "Yes? The Master said, "Do you still see Yangshan in a dream? Qing said, "I do not need to go up [to him]."

The person under the seat said, "I simply wish to have a discussion. The Master replied, "If you wish to have a discussion, there is already the Great Teacher of fifteen hundred people presiding in the Hall."
The Master was ill. One day, National Teacher Taishen came to inquire after his health. The attendant announced him, saying, "Master Taishen has come.
The Master ordered him to be invited in. As soon as Taishen entered the abbot’s quarters, the Master said, "A-ye!
A-ye! Master Taishen, save this old monk! Taishen replied, "What is there for the Master to save? The Master raised his head and looked at him once, then said, "Ei!"
The eyes were dark and the mouth was tight; he was still that same former Senior Monk Shen. Thereupon, he turned his body and faced the wall.
The Master asked National Teacher Guotai Tiao, "An ancient said that Jushi merely recited three lines of incantation and was thus named as one who transcended all others.
How would you remove those three lines of incantation for him so that he might be named as one who transcends all others?
Guotai held up a finger. The Master said, "Were it not for this day, how could I have recognized the traveler from Guazhou?"
Once, when Master Hui was at the residence of High Official Gao Xuan’an, he saw a hanging portrait of Maitreya.
Pointing to the Buddha Maitreya, the Master called out, “Attendant! The attendant responded, “Yes? The Master said, “Has this fellow attained thorough penetration yet? The attendant was speechless.
The Master said, “Even boiling yellow bitter ginseng with its roots would not be as bitter as this. Later, Guo Tai took his place and joined his palms, saying, “Excellent! Excellent!”
The Master said, "It would be acceptable for the Abbot to live in a hermitage as a neighbor to him.
Once, while warming himself by the brazier with a monk, the monk asked: "There is no dharma before the eyes; the meaning lies within the eyes.

It is not a dharma of the present moment, nor is it something reached by the ears or eyes. Which phrase is the host? Which phrase is the guest? The Master pointed to the fire and said, "Give it to me."
"From within this, I pluck out a single eyebrow. Can you do it? The monk said, "Not only would I, but all the people in the entire world would lose their lives.
The Master said, "Why do you seize your own topknot and throw yourself into the yamen?"
The Master was serving as the First Seat at Zhiye Monastery in Wuzhou. He habitually refused to accept purified water.
The monastery officials became indignant and said, "Venerable Elder, you do not understand the distinction between the defiled and the pure; why do you refuse to accept the purified water?
The Master leaped down from his seat, picked up a water pitcher, and asked, "Is this defiled or pure? The official was speechless. The Master then smashed the vessel to pieces.

While Chan Master Guichen of Luohan Monastery was planting rice fields, he saw a monk and asked, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Nanzhou. The Master said, "How is the Buddha-dharma there?
The monk said, "It is a place of great debate and discussion. The Master said, "How can that compare to my here, where we plant fields to earn our food?"
[The student] said, "What can one do about the three realms? The Master said, "What do you call 'the three realms'?
[The student] asked, "What is the single phrase of the Arhat? The Master said, "If I were to tell you, it would become two phrases."
Question: “A single Buddha appears in the world for the sake of all sentient beings. For what purpose does the Master act today? The Master said:
“Where have you encountered a single Buddha? [The questioner] said: “If that is so, then it is my own fault. The Master said: “Retreat with care.”
While enjoying the moon, he said, "The clouds move, and the rain departs. A monk said, "It is not that the clouds move; it is the wind that moves.
The Master said, "I say that neither the clouds move nor the wind moves. The monk asked, "But just now, Master, you said the clouds move.
The Master replied, "Who is at fault?"
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Qinzhou. The Master said, "What have you brought with you?
The monk said, "I have brought nothing. The Master said, "Why do you speak falsely before the assembly? The monk was unable to answer. The Master then asked, "Does Qinzhou not produce parrots?
The monk said, "Parrots are produced in Longxi. The Master said, "That is not much of a difference either."
When the Imperial Tutor presented robes for the assembly of monks at Mount Xuefeng, the Elder Conggan was absent.
A junior monk received the robes on behalf of the elder by using the elder’s name. When Conggan returned, the junior monk said, "I have already used your name, Elder Brother.
Conggan asked, "What did you say my name was? The junior monk had no reply. The Master (Zhaozhou) interjected, "Elder Brother, you are so greedy! He added, "What [name]?"
"This is a place of greed. Furthermore, it is said that on two occasions he used the Master’s name.
When the Master, along with Changqing and Baofu, entered the prefectural seat and saw a screen painting of peonies, Baofu remarked, "What a fine peony flower!
Changqing said, "Do not let your eyes deceive you. The Master said, "What a pity for such a fine flower!"
The Master was ill. A monk asked, "How is the Master’s health? The Master propped himself up with his staff and said, "Tell me, does this hurt?
The monk replied, "Whom are you asking, Master? The Master said, "I am asking you. The monk said, "Does it hurt? The Master said, [It hurts.]
It turns out they were all engaging in intellectual reasoning with me.
One day, the Layman Wang Yanbin, the Grand Tutor, entered the Buddha Hall of Zhaoqing Monastery. Pointing to an alms bowl, he asked the hall attendant, "What kind of bowl is this?"
The Master said, "It is a *bhaiṣajya* bowl. The Official said, "I have only heard of a dragon-subduing bowl (*nāga-vinaya-pātra*). The Master said, "Wait until there is a dragon, and it will descend.
The Official said, "What if a cloud-grasping, wave-rolling dragon suddenly appears? The Master said, "He would not even look at it.
The Official said, "Your words have fallen into error."
When the Duke arrived at Zhaoqing Temple for a tea ceremony, Senior Monk Lang and Mingzhao were holding the teapot. Suddenly, the teapot overturned. The Duke asked, "What is that under the tea stove?
Lang replied, "The Spirit Who Supports the Stove. The Duke said, "If you are the Spirit Who Supports the Stove, why did you overturn the tea?
Lang replied, "After serving the official for a thousand days, one may fail in a single morning. The Duke shook his sleeves and departed. Mingzhao— [continued].
Zhao said, "Having finished eating the meal at Zhaoqing, Senior Monk Lang goes out to the wilds to hunt for acorns.
Lang asked, "What about you, Senior Monk? Zhao replied, "Non-humans will take advantage of such an opportunity."
Chan Master Daoxi of Baoen in Zhangzhou was once sending a letter with Baofu to Wang Taewei in Quanzhou. The Governor asked, "Has the Monk of Zhangnan been performing the work of a teacher lately?
The Master said, "If I say he has been performing the work of a teacher, that would be doing you an injustice. If I say he has not..."

He was acting as a host when the Grand Marshal (Taishou) came to inquire after him. The Grand Marshal said, "Recite a single phrase, waiting for the iron ox to be able to chew grass and the wooden horse to know how to inhale smoke.
The Master said, "I am sparing my mouth for eating rice. After a long silence, the Marshal asked again.
"A donkey comes; a horse comes. The Master said, "Donkeys and horses do not travel the same path. The Commandant said, "How did they manage to reach this place? The Master said:
Xie Taowei took up the conversation.
Chan Master Zhisheng of Gushan was traveling abroad when he arrived at Huanglong in Ezhou and asked, "I have long heard of Huanglong; yet now that I have arrived, I see only red."
The striped snake said, "You see only a red-striped snake; you do not see the yellow dragon. The Master asked, "What is the yellow dragon?
The dragon said, "Flowing and surging. The Master asked, "If a garuḍa were to suddenly encounter it, what then? The dragon said:
"Life and nature are difficult to preserve. The Master said, "If that is so, then you have been swallowed up by him. Long said, "I thank the Dharma brother for his offering. The Master then bowed.
The pagoda of Chan Master Baoguo Zhao was struck by lightning. Someone asked, "Why were the ancestral Buddha-pagodas and temples struck by lightning? The Master said:
[The Master] said: "This is the function of penetrating through. [The student] asked: "If it is the function of penetrating through, why did he strike the Buddha with a thunderbolt?
The Master said: "In the place of this function, where do you see a Buddha? [The student] asked: "What about the fact that it was a mess? The Master said: "What do you see?"

When Chan Master Tong’an Zhi was about to pass away at Tong’an, he ascended the hall and said: “Before the Multi-Child Stupa, the lineage sons are flourishing; before the Five Old Peaks, what is the matter?
He raised this three times, but no one responded. The Master [Tong’an] stepped forward and said: “In the night-bright curtain, they stand in formation.”
He stood up. "Myriad miles away, songs of joy celebrate the Great Peace. An said, "It must be this donkey-man who can do it.
Chan Master Guangde Yi of Xiangzhou went to visit the former Guangde.
He paid his respects and asked, "What is the Master’s secret, hidden place? Guangde replied, "Concealed."
"The body does not necessarily require mountain crags and valleys; even in the midst of a bustling marketplace, it is rarely seen by those who look.
The Master said, "In that case, I shall go to offer water and flowers. Guangde said, "Suddenly, clouds and mist gather; what will you do, *dàlǐ* (junior teacher)?
The Master said, "My drawing of water and gathering of fuel shall not be in vain. Guangde said joyfully, "Everyone, look at this second-generation Guangde!"
A monk asked Zen Master Guangde Zhou of Xiangzhou, "The scriptures state:
'Ajita, one who does not sever afflictions and does not cultivate meditative concentration is recorded by the Buddha as becoming a Buddha without doubt.
What is the principle behind this? The Master said, "The salt is exhausted, and the charcoal is gone. The monk said, "The salt is exhausted, and the charcoal..."
“How is it at times when there is nothing? The Master said: “Do not speak of your sorrows to one who is already sorrowful; to speak of them to a sorrowful person is to kill them with grief.
Zen Master Shimen Huiche asked a monk:
“When Yunguang acted as an ox, what was the meaning of that? The Master said: “One does not ride a golden horse through a humble alley; turn back.”

On the road, he was instead wearing a tattered robe with frayed edges. (Master Yun Guang did not observe the monastic precepts. Master Zhigong asked him, "What is the point of leaving the household life? Yun Guang replied, "I do not fast, yet I am fasting; I eat, yet it is not food. Later, as retribution, he was reborn as an ox pulling a cart on the road.
When Master Zhigong saw him, he called out, "Yun Guang! The ox raised its head. Zhigong said, "Why do you not say that you pull, yet you do not pull? The ox shed tears, leaped about, and died.)
A monk asked Chan Master Chengyuan of Xianglin, "Why does the exquisite flavor of *amṛta* turn into poison? The Master said, "The paper in Daojiang became expensive."
Question: "What is the essential meaning of the [Master’s] coming from the West? The Master said: "Sitting for too long leads to fatigue. A monk asked:
"What is the meaning of 'hiding one's body within the Big Dipper'? He said: "The moon is like a drawn bow; there is little rain and much wind."
Question: What is the single lamp within the room? Answer: Three people testify that a tortoise is a soft-shelled turtle.
Question: What is the matter beneath the patched robe? Answer: A fire burning the mountains in the month of midwinter. Question: What is it like when a fish swims on dry land? Answer:
Every word spoken must have its subsequent remedy. The monk said: "What is it like when it descends back into the green abyss? Answer: The head is heavy and the tail is light.
Question: "If one son leaves the household life, the nine generations of his clan all attain liberation. Why then did Maudgalyāyana’s mother fall into hell?
The Master said, "Precisely."
As he was about to pass away, he took leave of Governor Song Gongdang, saying, "I, this old monk, am going on a pilgrimage. The Vice-Governor said, "This monk is mad;
at eighty years of age, where would he go on a pilgrimage? Song replied, "A great spiritual teacher (mahāsattva) is free to come and go as he pleases."
Returning, he said to the assembly, "The old monk has finally achieved a state of unified integration after forty years. Having finished speaking, he passed away.

Chan Master Haohan of Xinkai Monastery asked a monk, "Have you come to sightsee, or have you come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma? The monk replied, "In this world of peace and tranquility, what need is there to speak of the Buddha-dharma?"
The Master said, "What a fine 'no-affairs' Chan practitioner you are. The monk said, "That would already be too much of an affair.
The Master said, "The Senior Monk spent the summer retreat here last year. The monk said, "I did not. The Master said, "If that is so, then we have never known each other before. Begone!"

Question: "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the teachings the same or different? The Master said: "When the rooster is cold, it climbs the tree; when the duck is cold, it goes down into the water.

Chan Master Dongshan Shouchu Zonghui said: "Words do not unfold the reality of things; speech does not meet the occasion. Those who rely on words perish; those who linger in phrases are deluded. Regarding this—

If you can see clearly within these four lines of verse, you will become a liberated monk. With a roof of rafters and a floor of broken tiles, and through the causal conditions of rice gruel and meals, you will be fit to serve as a spiritual friend to gods and humans. If you do not understand this, you will ultimately remain muddled and confused.
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Ruizhou. The Master said, "How far is it from here? The monk replied, "Seven hundred li. The Master said:

[The Master asked: "How many pairs of straw sandals have you worn through? [The monk] said, "Three pairs. The Master said, "Where did you get the money to buy them? [The monk] said, "I used it to buy my bamboo hat."
The Master said, "Go to the hall. The monk responded with an assent.
The Master asked the monk, "Are you not the one who has newly arrived? He replied, "I am. The Master said, "Last night you sought a place to rest;
how are things this morning? He replied, "This morning the wind is more violent; I walk along the back of the green mountains. The Master said, "That is not it. Speak further. He replied:
"Be careful," the Master said, and then struck him.
He asked: "If one does not settle the ultimate meaning within the mind, how can one reach the words of the Patriarchs? The Master replied:
"A six-legged spider climbs onto a wooden bed."
When Chan Master Fengxian Shen of Jinling was among the assembly with Master Tongming, he heard a monk ask Fayan, "What is form? Fayan held up his whisk;
some said [the meaning was] "cock's comb flowers," while others said it was "a sweatshirt that fits the flesh. The two men went specifically to seek instruction and asked:
A monk asked, "I have heard that the Master has three kinds of 'colored speech. Is this true? Fayan said, "Yes.
The master [Dongshan] said, "A hawk flies over Silla," and immediately returned to the assembly. At that time, Lord Li was seated below;

he did not accept this and said to Fayan, "I shall provide a tea ceremony tomorrow and invite both of you to ask the question anew. The next day, after the tea was finished, he prepared a chest of colored silk.
[The Master] held up a sword and said to the two masters, "If you, the Abbot, can answer my question correctly, I shall reward you with a chest of variegated silks;
if you cannot, I shall grant you only this one sword. Fayan ascended the seat. The Master stepped forward again and asked, "Today, by imperial decree, we are to engage in discourse.
Do you permit me to ask? Fayan said, "I permit it. [The Master] said, "A hawk flies over Silla," and holding up the silks, he walked away.
The assembly dispersed all at once. At that time, Faden was serving as the *karmadāna* (Vina). He struck the bell to assemble the monks before the Sangha hall to examine the Master.
