When the assembly had gathered, Faden asked: "I have heard that the two Senior Elders have long resided at Yunmen. Do you have any particularly extraordinary kōans?
Please cite one or two cases so we may discuss them. The Master said: "An ancient said: 'A white heron descends into the field; a thousand dots.'"
Snow. A yellow oriole perches upon a branch with a single flower. "How do you deliberate on this, Venerable Karmadāna?
As the attendant hesitated, the Master struck his sitting mat once and returned to the assembly.
The Master went with Master Ming to the Huai River. Seeing people pulling in a net, a fish leaped through it.
The Master said, "Brother Ming, how clever! You are just like a true monk. Ming said, "Even so, it would have been better had he not run right into the net in the first place.
The Master said, "Brother Ming, you still lack awakening. It was not until midnight that Ming finally understood.
[The Master] said: “Sheng. Chan Master Dayong Yin was asked by a monk:
“Since you are Dayong (‘Great Receptacle’), why did you drive the monk away? The Master said: “The great ocean does not admit dust. “Small [minds cannot contain it].”
Xituo Jiantuo asked, "What is the single path of the ancient Buddhas?
The Master pointed to the ground. The monk said, "I am not asking about this. The Master said, "Go!"
The Master had made an appointment with an elderly practitioner to travel elsewhere, but due to a certain circumstance, he did not go. The practitioner said, "The Buddha’s word is never double.
The Master replied, "The Dharma is never one-sided."
A monk asked Chan Master Huayan Hui: "I have heard it said of old: 'Where the deluded mind has no place, that is bodhi. At the very moment of delusion, is there still bodhi or not?
The Master said: "The sound of your coming has already been illuminated. The monk said: "I do not understand. The Master said: "Where the deluded mind has no place, that is bodhi."
Question: Master Xichan Qin asked a monk, "What is the phrase that encompasses heaven and earth? The Master said, "In the heavens, every star bows toward the North. [The monk] said: [This is it.]
"What is the phrase that cuts off all streams? The Master said, "The great earth is vast and level. He asked, "What is the phrase that follows the waves and drifts with the currents?
The Master said, "Spring brings forth life, and summer brings growth."
Chan Master Dongshan Qingbing went to visit Yunmen.
Yunmen asked, “Where did you leave from today? He replied, “Huilin. Yunmen raised his staff and said, “The Great Master Huilin is going off like that;
do you see him? The Master said, “I deeply appreciate this question. Yunmen glanced toward his left and right.
[The Master] merely smiled.
When the monk Baibunzhi asked the Zen Master, “What is the dragon’s roar within the withered tree? the Master said, “A lotus blooming in fire. [The monk] asked, “What is...”
"An eye within a skull. The Master said, "A clay ox enters the sea. Chan Master Jiji of Beichen asked a monk, "Where have you come from?
The monk replied, "From Huangzhou. The Master asked, "Where did you spend the summer retreat? The monk replied, "At Zifu. The Master said:
"What will this merit be used for? he asked. The Master said, "A double case. The monk said, "But what can be done? It is in Beichan’s hands.
The Master said, "If it is in his hands, then take it back. He struck him. The monk was not satisfied; the Master followed after him and drove him out.
When Chan Master Shoushan Shengnian and Zhen Yuantou went together to pay their respects to Fengxue, Fengxue asked Zhen, "What is the Buddha’s 'unsaid saying'?
Zhen replied, "A magpie calls from the treetop. Fengxue said, "You have accumulated quite a bit of foolish merit."
"What is it? [Xuefeng asked]. "Why do you not investigate the words and phrases? He then asked the Master, "How about you?
The Master said, "Moving the countenance to reveal the ancient path; not falling into the silent mechanism. Xuefeng said to Zhen, "Why do you not look at the sub-commentary on the *Lotus Sūtra*?"
The Master asked the monk, "You have attained that matter which cannot be recommended by others; try to speak of it. The monk then gave a shout.
The Master said, "I was asking you politely; why do you flare up in anger? The monk shouted again. The Master said, "It would not do to let you off today.
As the monk hesitated, the Master shouted at him.
Question: "When there comes a person who has exhausted everything, does the Master still receive him? The Master said: "I set aside the one who has exhausted everything;
who is this other person? He replied: "The wind is high and the moon is cold. The Master said: "How many people are sitting or lying in the Sangha Hall? The monk had no reply.
The Master said, "You have deceived this old monk.
He was asked, "What is the mark of the Brahma-voice? The Master said, "The braying of donkeys and the barking of dogs.

Then he said, "If you wish to attain intimacy, first do not bring questions to ask. Do you understand? The question is at the place of the answer; the answer is at the place of the question. If you..."
The Master asked, "Question! Question! The old monk is beneath your feet. If you hesitate, there is no connection.
At that moment, a monk came forward and bowed; the Master struck him. The monk then asked, "What of it when one hangs up one's staff in a secluded crag? The Master said, "Wrong.
The monk said, "Wrong," and the Master struck him again.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk said, "Xiangzhou. The Master said, "Did you encounter Bodhidharma on the road?
The monk stepped forward and said, "I hope you are well, Reverend. The Master said, "This is the realm of those who follow behind donkeys and horses.
The monk said, "And what about yours, Preceptor? The Master said, "It is not your province. Sit and drink tea for now. As soon as the monk sat down, the Master questioned him again.
"In what place did you spend the summer retreat? The monk said, "Shimen. The Master said, "Is the water buffalo at peace?
The monk said, "It has timely water and grass. The Master said, "Why does it damage the crops? The monk said, "Before the Honored One, I dare not act rashly.
The Master said, "Letting you off is out of the question," and he struck him.
The Monk Heishui went to visit Huanglong. He asked, "What is it like when snow covers the reeds? Huanglong said, "Fierce! The Master said, "Not fierce.
Huanglong said again, "Fierce! The Master said again, "Not fierce. Huanglong then struck him. At this, the Master attained realization.
He then paid his respects.

Master Zao-shu asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From the Kingdom of Han. The Master said, "Does the Son of Heaven in the Kingdom of Han hold the Buddha-dharma in high esteem?"
[The monk] said, "There is none. The Master said, "Alas! Fortunately you have asked me; had you asked someone else, disaster would have ensued. The monk said, "What is there to do?
The Master said, "Since you cannot even see people, what Buddha-dharma is there to value? The monk said, "How many years since you received the precepts?
The Master said, "Twenty summer retreats. The Master said, "It is wonderful that you cannot see anyone," and he struck him.
A monk asked Chan Master Qingliang Xiufu,
"What did the ancients attain that they were able to rest at once? The Master said, "What have you attained that you do not rest?"
Chan Master Longji Shaoshou addressed the assembly:
"The ordinary person possesses the dharmas of an ordinary person, yet the ordinary person does not know them. The sage possesses the dharmas of a sage, yet the sage does not understand them."
If a sage were to realize it, he would be an ordinary person; if an ordinary person were to know it, they would be a sage. These words contain one principle and two meanings.
If a person can discern them, there will be no hindrance to finding a point of entry into the Buddha-dharma.
If you cannot discern them, do not say that you have no doubts.
It is also said: "A pillar does not see the pillar; what is not a pillar does not see the pillar. Once 'is' and 'is not' have been discarded, take it up within 'is' and 'is not'.
Question: "How can one escape the three realms? The Master said: "If they are the three realms, you may escape them as you please. [The questioner] said: "What if they are not the three realms?"
"How is it with the realms? The Master said, "Where is it that they are not the three realms?
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Cuiyan. The Master said, "What words or phrases did Cuiyan use to instruct his disciples?
The monk replied, "He usually says: 'When you go out the door, you meet Maitreya; when you enter the gate, you see Śākyamuni. The Master said, "Even so, how can he say such a thing?"
The monk asked, "What about the Master, Reverend? The Master said, "When you go out the door, whom do you encounter? When you enter the gate, what do you see?
Upon these words, the monk attained realization.
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "Where sound and form do not reach, the fault lies in seeing and hearing; where words and explanations fail to arrive, the error resides in the lips and mouth.
A monk asked, "Setting aside sound and form, please, Master, speak. The Master said, "I will answer you right within sound and form."
A monk asked Chan Master Guangping Xuanzhi, "What is the realm of Guangping? The Master said, "The earth bears the splendor of famous mountains; the streams connect with the clarity of the sea."
[The student] asked: "What is it to be a person within the realm? The Master said: "You ask and I answer. [The student] asked:
"What is the essence-body of the Dharma (dharmakāya)? The Master said: "Vast and empty space, utterly free from a single speck of flaw.

[The student] asked: "What is the object within the essence? The Master said: "A single bright moon disperses over the autumn river. [The student] asked: "I do not yet know whether the essence and the object are distinct or not."

[The Master] said, "I divided them. The student asked, "What did you say just now? The student said, "In that case, they are not divided. The Master said, "The pierced-eared barbarian monk smiles and nods his head."
A monk asked Zen Master Zhien of Lingfeng, "What is the realm of Lingfeng? The Master said, "Ten thousand layers of green mountains emerge like driven stakes;
two ribbons of green water are as if painted. The monk asked, "What is the person within the realm? The Master said, "Clearly clear, dense dense; dense dense, clearly clear."

Ming. Under the guidance of Chan Master Yuan Guan of Liangshan in Dingzhou, there was a garden head who attained realization of Chan. Many among the assembly did not believe him. One day, there was...
The monk went to provoke him, seeking to elicit some sign of his realization.
He asked the gardener, "Why do you not go ask the Abbot for one or two sayings to create a karmic connection? The gardener replied, "I simply will not go ask.

If I were to go, I would have to force this old fellow off his meditation seat and make him stand on the ground. When it was time for Yangshan to ascend the hall, the gardener indeed went out and asked, "House-thief..."
"How is it when [the mind] is difficult to guard? Mount said, "If you recognize it, it does not become an enemy.
[The monk] asked, "After recognizing it, what then? Mount said, "Exile it to the realm of non-arising. [The monk] asked, "Is this not where one establishes one's dwelling and sustains one's life?
Mount said, "Dead water does not hide dragons. [The monk] asked, "What is a dragon in living water? Mount said, "It stirs up waves but does not create billows. [The monk] asked, "How is this so?"
"How is it when suddenly the torrents of rain pour down and the mountains collapse?
Liangshan, as expected, descended from his Dharma seat, seized him, and said, "Reverend, do not let it soak the corner of this old monk's *kāṣāya*."
Chan Master Zhimen Guanzuo ascended the hall and said:
"If there is even one dharma, Vairocana falls into the rank of ordinary beings;
if there are not even ten thousand dharmas, Samantabhadra loses his realm. At this very moment, where does Mañjuśrī appear? If he were to appear—"
He attained it. The golden-haired lion’s waist was broken. It is better to have one plate of rice than to wait for the ginger and pepper to be sprinkled.
Entering the hall, the mountain monk recalls that while in his mother’s womb there was a saying; today he brings it forth for the sake of the great assembly.
"You all must not engage in rational deliberation. Is there anyone who can deliberate upon this?
If you cannot deliberate upon it, do not err when citing it thirty years from now."
A monk asked Chan Master Kaifu Xian, "What is the livelihood of a patch-robed monk? The Master said, "Plowing fields in one's ears. He ascended the hall and said:
"Without using thought one knows; without using deliberation one understands. When both knowledge and understanding have vanished, what matter is there to discuss?"
The Master said: "When a single leaf falls, the whole world turns autumn.
Chan Master Muzhou of Qianming asked Dongshan, "What is it like when the mechanism is halted and the performance ends? Dongshan said, "A puppet show beneath the water. Master [Muzhou].
[Shishuang] asked, "Who is it that looks upon and appreciates? Dongshan said, "One who has stilled their mental activity and ceased their appreciation.
The Master said, "If that is so, then those who know the sound do not harmonize. Dongshan asked, "As for the matter of knowing the sound, how is it?
The Master said, "A great month has thirty days. Dongshan said, "Not yet. Speak further. The Master said, "I deserve to receive a severe blow from the Master's staff."
Dongshan said, "I will leave it at rest.
Zen Master Xifeng Yunhuo had early on sought instruction from various quarters, and later he visited Qingliang. He asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? Qingliang replied:
"Clouds obscure the trees at the Gate of the Sea. [The Master] asked, "What is it like after one has left the world? Qingliang said, "Splitting open the Iron Ring Mountains.
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment, and Qingliang certified his realization.
A monk asked Master Da-li:
"When a donor makes an offering, with what should one repay them? The Master pinched his mustache with his hand and said, "If there is a mustache, I pinch it."
"What about one who has no beard? The Master said, "That is not within your realm.
The Master asked a monk from Lianzhou Baohua, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Dayong. The Master said, "How is it at Dayong these days? The monk replied, [silence].
Recently, I managed to brew a jar of sauce. The Master called a novice and said, "Bring a bowl of water for this monk to reflect his image.
— Chan Master Yuehua Shan Yue.
An elderly monk entered the Dharma Hall and looked east and west, saying, "What a fine Dharma Hall! Yet, alas, it has no master.

When the Master heard this, he called out to him, "Sit for a moment and drink some tea. The monk asked, "If even that which is most ultimate within the profound mystery is like the hair of a tortoise or the horns of a rabbit, and one does not practice within the two truths, how can there be secret application? The Master said, "Tilt. The monk said, "In that case," [he was about to speak further].

"Snap the staff in two and cut through the straw sandals! The Master said, "Examine this closely. Chan Master Jie of Wuzhu in Qizhou and Chan Master Yue of Shangfang on Mount Yue in Huzhou came to the master’s quarters. The Master asked, "What are your names? They replied, "Qi. The Master said, "Fine, fine. He then called for tea. After the tea was served, he said, "I have heard that you two have both attained the Way; is this so? They replied, "It is so. The Master said, "If it is so, then why do you still come here? They were speechless. The Master said, "You have both attained the Way, yet you do not even know where you are. He then struck them both once with his staff and sent them away. Later, when they returned to their own monasteries, they spoke of this to their fellow practitioners. One said, "The Master of Wuzhu has attained the Way. The other said, "The Master of Shangfang has attained the Way. People all said, "How extraordinary! How extraordinary! The Master heard of this and remarked, "This is truly a case of 'the blind leading the blind. He then composed a verse: "The staff snaps, the sandals are cut; The two monks return to their own abodes. One says, 'Wuzhu has attained the Way,' The other says, 'Shangfang has attained the Way. Yue said, "How does it compare to Mount Tai? Yue was speechless. The Master immediately struck him and drove him away. The next day, Yue came to visit again. The Master asked, "What are you doing?
Yue turned his head and drew a circle with his hand, presenting it to him. The Master asked, "What is this?
Yue said, "Old and decrepit as you are, you do not even recognize a sesame cake. The Master said, "While the hearth is still hot, let us bake another one."
Yue deliberated on this. The Master dragged his staff and chased him out the door. A few days later, Yue visited again.

He held up his sitting mat and said, "When spread out, it encompasses the great chiliocosm; when not spread out, not even a hair's breadth remains. Is it in being spread out? Or is it in not being spread out?
The Master suddenly descended from his rope-corded seat, seized him by the collar, and said, "Since you are an old acquaintance, why must you act like this?"
This; Mount Yue again remained silent. The Master struck him once more.
Zen Master Shanchan of Fuchang asked a monk, "What is the Eye of the True Dharma? The Master said, "Observe the celestial bodies at night. The monk said, "I do not understand the meaning."
"What is the meaning? The Master said, "Viewing the mountains in broad daylight.
Chan Master Fayan Wenyi asked a monk, "Who can penetrate these two characters, 'sound' and 'form'? The Master, however, addressed the assembly, saying, "Venerable seniors, for now..."
The Master said, "I wonder if this monk has penetrated it yet? If you understand where this monk was coming from, it will not be difficult to penetrate sound and form.
The Master asked Master Xiu, "A hair's breadth of difference, and heaven and earth are set apart. How do you understand this? Xiu replied:
"A difference of a hair’s breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth. The Master said, "Even so, how can you understand it? Xiu asked, "How about you, Teacher?
The Master said, "A difference of a hair’s breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth. Xiu then bowed in prostration.
While monks were arriving for their turn to attend upon him, the Master pointed to the curtain. Immediately, two monks went together to roll it up.
The Master said, "One has gained; one has lost.
He then asked Elder Jue, "Did you come by boat or by land? He replied, "By boat. The Master said, "Where is the boat? He replied, "It is here."
[The monk] was at the riverbank when he realized his error and withdrew. The Master asked a nearby monk, "Do you say that this monk just now possessed the eye or did not possess the eye?

The Master then ordered the monk to take soil to fill the lotus basin. When the monk arrived with the soil, the Master said, "Take it from the east side of the bridge; take it from the west side of the bridge."
He said, "Take it from the east of the bridge. The Master said, "Is this real? Is this false?

He then asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come from paying my respects to the Great Sage at Sizhou. The Master asked, "Does the Great Sage emerge from his stupa this year?
The monk replied, "He does. The Master then turned to a monk standing nearby and asked, "Tell me, has he arrived at Sizhou or not?"
Yunmen asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Jiangxi. Yunmen said, "Have the old masters of Jiangxi been living there talking in their sleep?
The monk had no reply. Later, a monk asked the Master, "I do not know what Yunmen’s intention was.
The Master said, "Great Yunmen was exposed by this monk."
Master Sheng said, "Striking the void produces sound; striking wood produces no sound. When the Master suddenly heard the sound of the vegetarian drum, he asked his attendant, "Do you hear it?
If you heard it just now, you do not hear it now; if you hear it now, you did not hear it just now.
Do you understand?"
The Master saw some monks carrying earth and placed a clod of earth upon one of their loads, saying, "I will help you.
The monk replied, "Thank you for the Master’s compassion. The Master refused to accept it. Another monk spoke differently, asking, "What kind of mental activity is this, Master?"
The Master then ceased speaking.
He asked, "What is it like when the six sense-bases do not know their own sounds? The Master said, "Your family members are all a pack of children.
The Master spoke again, "How do you understand this? Do not say that coming to ask such a question is it; you must tell me what the six sense-bases do not know."
One who knows the sound. The locus of the eye does not know the sound; the locus of the ear does not know the sound. If there were a fundamental existence, how could one attain non-existence?
An ancient said: "To be detached from sound and form, yet cling to sound and form; to be detached from names and words, yet cling to names and words.

Thus, those in the Heaven of No-Thought (Āsaṃjñisattva-deva) cultivate their practice for eighty thousand great kalpas, only to fall back in a single morning. All things remain as they were; this is because—

One knows the fundamental reality. Thereafter, one practices through three lifetimes for sixty kalpas and four lifetimes for one hundred kalpas, proceeding in this manner until the fruit is perfected after three great asamkhyeya kalpas.
Yet the ancients still said: "It is not as good as realizing in a single thought-moment that dependent origination is unborn."
It transcends the provisional views and studies of the three vehicles. Furthermore, it is said: "In a single snap of the fingers, eighty thousand gates are perfectly accomplished;
in a single instant, three kalpas of eons are extinguished. One must investigate this deeply. If it is so, how much effort is required?
A monk asked Chan Master Shanzhao of Fenyang, "What is the phrase for receiving a beginner? The Master said, "You are a wandering monk.
He asked again, "What is the phrase for discerning a patch-robed monk? The Master said, "The sun rises in the west at dawn. He asked again, "What is the phrase for the direct..."

[The Master] said: "The phrase for making things proceed. The Master said: "Bringing it from a thousand miles away to present one's old face. He asked again: "What is the phrase for establishing heaven and earth?
The Master said: "In the continent of Uttarakuru, long-grained rice grows; those who eat it have neither anger nor joy. He further said:
"I shall use these four turning phrases to test the monks of the world. As soon as I see you come forward, I will have tested you."
[The Master] said, "Yes. A question was asked: "Regarding the Thousand Hands and Eyes of Great Compassion, what is the 'True Eye'? The Master said, "Blind.

[The questioner] said, "If that is so, then it is like two people carrying a single staff together. The Master said, "Singing a rustic song in a village of three households. [The questioner] said, "If that is so, then as for the Master..."
They were together inside. The Master said, "I thank you for your earnestness.

When Minister Zheng arrived, they engaged in a tea conversation. Minister Zheng presented a verse to the Master, saying: "Do not let yellow paper blind your eyes; The blue clouds naturally provide their own shade.
Do not bury the mind of the Patriarch With the scholastic learning of the idle. He further remarked, "I shall use this very verse to test Heaven."
The junior elder bowed. The Master said, "In that case, Fenyang is also inside. He replied, "Carrying the cangue, one passes through the legal proceedings.
The Master said, "There will be no further interrogation. Zheng said, "A double-layered case. The Master said, "If you know this, it is enough.
After Zheng had been silent for a long while, the Master let out a single sigh. Zheng said, "Wenbao! Wenbao! The Master asked, "Where is he? Zheng said, "He does not allow me [to remain]."
Jiawu let out a breath and argued, "How can you bear to be angry with me for saying that the Elder has been lingering here? The Master said, "What words are these? Zheng said, "It is true.
The Master said, "I cannot let this pass. Zheng said, "I beg the Master for a verse. The Master said, "I have no leisure for paper and ink," and then he spontaneously showed him a verse:
Seeking a secluded path through the wild weeds, The rocky pines spread their shade afar. How many seekers of the profound truth—?
The Guest has lost his original mind. Entering the hall, he said to the assembly:
"Now, one who preaches the Dharma must possess the ten wisdoms that accord with reality. What are these ten wisdoms that accord with reality?
I shall point them out for you, venerable elders: first, the same substance; second, the same great matter; third, the total sameness..."
3. Identical in Wisdom; 4. Identical in Pervasiveness; 5. Identical in Endowment; 6. Identical in Gain and Loss; 7.
Identical in Birth and Killing; 8. Identical in Roaring; 9. Identical in Entry. It is further asked: With what person is one identical in entry? With whom is one identical in roaring?
What is it that is identical in birth and killing? What thing is identical in gain and loss? Which one is it?
"Identical fulfillment. What is this identical pervasiveness? Who possesses identical true wisdom? Who is able to participate in the universal identity?
Which one is identical to the Great Matter? What entity is identical in substance? Is there anyone who can point it out? To those who can point it out, do not begrudge your compassion.
If you cannot point it out, you have yet to possess the eye for traveling to study under masters; you must discern this with urgency. You must recognize it!
"No. His face and features are still present; he cannot remain for long. Be careful.
When Chan Master Zhisong of Chengtian took his leave of Shoushan, Shoushan saw him off with a staff. As the master received it, he spoke this verse: "The Abbot’s staff..."
"Penetrating the dragons and elephants; the Linji tradition has fallen into my palm. Sanshan said, "Do not involve me in this.
The Master struck Sanshan with his sitting cloth. Sanshan said, "As expected, you have involved me. The Master said, "Today I have caught this old fellow red-handed.
Sanshan said, "It seems you have gained the advantage, yet it seems you have lost the advantage."
The Dialogue between Minister Yang and Prince Li with the Master. Question: "Amitābha spreads his transformation in the Western Land;
Bodhidharma transmits the Mind to the Eastern Realm. When the barbarian arrives, the Han appears; when the water reaches, the channel forms. The Five Peaks remain majestic and serene."
The hundred grains flow toward the central state, vast and boundless; the nature of the single spirit relies upon conditions to manifest form.
Within the three realms of existence, by what means does one establish its life-force? The Master said: "The immortal has no wife; the jade maiden has no husband. Yang said:
"A nun who has shaved her head will never again give birth to a child. The Master said: "The iron ox of Shanfu can roar; the Great Buddha of Jiazhou recites *Mahā*. Li said:
Leaping sideways, he ascends to the mountain peak. The Master says: "Riding an ox, one does not wear boots.
He asks: "Xuansha did not cross the ridge; Baoshou did not ford the river; yet Shancai visited fifty-three spiritual friends."
“Huiyuan gathered eighteen monks, both black-robed and white-robed. Xuefeng went up to Touzi three times;
Zhiyi lectured on the Lotus Sūtra for ninety days, warding off six Chinese men. Was this the howling of a jackal, or was it the roar of a lion?

Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The Master said: “When the water is swift, the fish move with difficulty; when the peak is high, the birds do not perch. Yang said: “The Great Sage of Sizhou. The Master said: [“Speak quickly! Speak quickly! (implying he was still too slow).
Yun said, "Adding another layer of mud upon the earth. Li said, "A gold coin covered by the tongue. The Master said, "At midnight, the music of song and dance stirs;
who is there to be a true connoisseur?"
The Master composed a verse on the fundamental principle. Looking left and looking right in the dim light of dusk, he extended his hand and returned;
it was already manifest. But tell me, what is this phrase that is manifest? Yang said: "Right at the moment of killing, he thrusts out his head."
The Master said: "Both feet kick at the empty air, hands crossed over the chest. Linji said: "Left whiskers, right hair—hidden within are the patterns of the Way.
The Master said: "Fame and profit have already spread throughout the world; a young girl rides a cow backward. The Master spoke again:
"When Vimalakīrti maintained his silence and Mañjuśrī praised it as excellent—if I had been there at that time, I would have given thirty blows to each of them. Now tell me, what about these two?"
“Where does this old fellow go wrong? Yang said, “His head would shatter into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree.
The Master said, “Kāśyapa did not raise his fist; Ānanda should not have pressed his palms together. Li said, “He is like a young calf before it has grown horns.
The Master said, “In haste he bends his fist to strike the gong. The Master spoke again: “The teachings have clear texts: the Buddha-body fills all of space.”
“The Dharma-realm. Today this old monk fills the Dharma-realm. Where is the Secretariat Director right now?
Yang said, “A single piece of coarse cloth skirt, with the kneecaps protruding. The Master said, “A wide-mouthed cloth trouser, three feet long, with a staff.”
Niu Yun said, "A load of river water is worth three coins. The Master said, "I see only the moisture on the tip of the nose; I do not see the dampness behind the crown.
—Guangjiao Guisheng Chan Master.
The Master went to visit Shoushan. One day, Shoushan held up a bamboo stick and asked, "To call it a 'bamboo stick' is to encounter resistance;
not to call it a 'bamboo stick' is to turn one's back on it. What would you call it? The Master seized the stick, threw it to the ground, and said, "What is this?
Shoushan said, "Blind! At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment, his mind becoming as clear as the open sky.
Question: "The chamber of Vimalakīrti does not take the sun and moon as its illumination. What serves as the illumination for the Master’s chamber?
The Master said: "My eyebrows are parted in eight characters. [The questioner] asked: "I do not yet understand the meaning of this. The Master said: "Both ears hang down to my shoulders."
Question: "What is the Master’s deepest place? The Master said: "The cat has the merit of drinking blood; the tiger has the virtue of raising the dead.
[The questioner] said: "Is it not this very thing? The Master said: "The mortar pounds toward the southeast; the millstone grinds toward the northwest."
Question: "If one suddenly encounters a person who is a great icchantika, will you still act for their sake? The Master said: "When the Dharma has long endured, it becomes corrupt.
[The questioner] asked: "Where then is compassion? The Master said: "When one is old, one becomes a demon."
Question: "If one's own matter is not yet clear, what serves as the proof? The Master said: "Striking a gong for silence in the midst of a bustling marketplace.
[The questioner] asked: "What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "Lighting a golden lamp at midday."
A monk asked, "When one hears the sound of a bell, there is only this sound; or is there something else? The Master said, "Three catties behind the head.
He asked another monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk said, "From the Eastern Capital (Kaifeng).
The Master said, "Why is your mouth broken? The monk said, "The Master must also be careful. The Master said, "Seven blows for thirteen," and they went to the storehouse to drink tea.
He departed.
When the Master arrived at Dongshan, he asked Dongshan, "When all is vast and empty with nothing to rely upon, where does the Dharma return? Dongshan said, "The threefold *karmavācanā*.
The Master said, "If that is so, then those who know the sound do not harmonize. Dongshan said, "Take the matter of those who do not harmonize with the sound and make it so."
"How so? The Master said, "A whisk made of tortoise hair is three feet long. Shan said, "Why have your eyebrows and beard fallen out? The Master then bowed.
When a monk came from Fenzhou to see Chan Master Shending Hongxin, the Master leaned on his staff and said, "Upon a single peak, a solitary tree does not form a forest—what then?
The monk said, "The river waters part the trees on the banks; the distant ravine’s emerald spring is deep. The Master asked again, "How so?"
"Birth is the mechanism of mutual interplay. The monk said, "A blind man has no eyes. He asked again, "When I was among the assembly, I did not understand a verse by Fenyang.
You, Senior Monk, have long been at this Dharma seat; you must surely understand it clearly. The monk said, "Please, Preceptor, recite it for me.
The Master said: "The Goose King flies away as the birds depart; He dwells atop Maitreya Peak (Matou Ling). The heavens are so high they cannot cover him; Great!"
The Master said, "Everyone is heading up the road; what are you doing? The monk held up his sitting mat and said, "The Ten-Thousand-Year Pine stands on Mount Zhurong.
The Master said, "I do not want you to answer my question; try to explain it for me. The monk said, "Suddenly I recall that when I was young, I once looked into a mirror;
ten parts of its radiance were reflected as red upon my cheeks. He then swept up his robes and departed. The Master said, "Seeking cleverness, he ended up being clumsy."
The Master resided at Shending, using a single dilapidated bed as his Dharma seat. His contentment with such austerity was peerless.
Both his virtue and seniority were eminent; he was revered by all quarters like the ancient Zhaozhou.

When Chan Master Guyin Yuncong Cizhao arrived at Dayang, Master Xuan asked, "Where have you recently come from? The Master said, "Xiangzhou. Dayang asked, "What is the phrase that is not separated [from reality]?
The Master said, "It is no easy matter for the Master to serve as abbot. Dayang said, "Sit for a moment and drink some tea."
The Master then went to join the assembly. An attendant asked, "Just now, it was no easy matter for the newly arrived guest to respond to the Abbot.
Why did you, Reverend, have him sit and drink tea? Yang said, "I offered him Korean aconite; he repaid me with shipboard cumin.
Go ask him yourself; there is something to be said. The attendant invited the Master to drink tea and asked, "Regarding what happened just now..."
[The monk] addressed the Abbot, saying, "It is not easy to serve as a *zhuchi* (abbot). What is the underlying meaning of this? The Master said, "True brass does not equal gold.
While the monk was standing in attendance, the Master asked, "Where do you sit? He replied, "I sit in the back hall (*houjia*). The Master said, "With whom do you discuss the teachings?
He replied, "I discuss the teachings with the Master. The Master asked, "What is the surname of the Master? He replied, "..."
"You may not have a surname. The Master asked, "What is your name? He replied, "I may not have a name. The Master said, "In that case, you do not recognize the host.
The monk then gave a shout; the Master did not respond.
Question: "What was the meaning when the ancients asked for fire? The Master said: "Let it go out. [The questioner] asked: "After it has gone out, what then? The Master said:
"The third day of the first month; the eleventh day."

Imperial Postface:

In my youth, I took pleasure in reading the Buddhist scriptures (*nèi-diǎn*). I admired only those Buddhist activities involving conditioned phenomena (*yǒuwéi fójì*) and sought to resolve all public cases (*gōng'àn*) through intellectual analysis.
Consequently, I held the Chan school in low esteem, believing that the true teaching of the Tathāgata ought not to be like this.
The Imperial Ancestor bestowed the title of State Preceptor of Universal Wisdom and Vast Compassion, Grand Master of Consecration, Changkya Hutuktu Lama.

He was truly a person of renewed incarnation and a veritable great spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*). His pure conduct was refined and authentic; his realization was perfectly integrated and unimpeded.
A refuge for Tibet, Mongolia, China, and all foreign lands; one whom the myriad monastics and laypeople alike revere and look up to.

For over a decade, I have enjoyed leisurely tea conversations at his princely residence, through which I gained insight into his skillful means and came to understand the ultimate nature of this matter.
In the first month of the spring of the Renchen year, I invited monks to observe the seven-day retreat; on the twentieth and twenty-first days, I joined them in sympathetic joy.

We sat together for two days, using five sticks of incense, at which time he suddenly attained a thorough understanding of his original nature and only then realized the principle that "this alone is the one true reality.

Nevertheless, he knew within himself that he had not yet reached the ultimate state. Yet, upon hearing the *kalaviṅka*-like voice [of the Master], he leaped with joy and offered praise, claiming he had already penetrated the subtle essence.
He spoke with such unreflective self-assurance that I questioned Changkya, who said: "The King’s insight is like a needle."

He tore down the paper window and peered at the sky through the crevice. Although he said he was seeing the sky, the nature of the sky is vast; what can be seen through the eye of a needle’s gap—can it truly be called seeing it all?

The Buddha-dharma is boundless; one must strive to advance further. When I heard these words, they deeply accorded with my own thoughts. In the second month, he again entered the retreat period at Jiyun Hall and applied himself diligently to his inquiry.

On the evening of the fourteenth, [The Emperor] said: “I have heard these words; they deeply accord with my own intent. In the second month, [the Master] again entered the formal retreat at Jiyun Hall and exerted himself in his practice and inquiry. On the evening of the fourteenth,
While walking in meditation (*caṅkrama*), he broke through [his realization] until his entire body was drenched in sweat, and the bottom of his wooden sandals fell off at that very moment.
Only then did he realize there truly was the principle of a "heavy barrier. He then returned to question Changkya [Rinpoche] regarding his realization. Changkya Gushri said:

"Although Your Majesty’s current insight represents a further step forward, it is like standing in a courtyard and gazing at the sky. Yet the celestial sphere is infinite; you have not yet fully comprehended it."
"Behold! The essence of the Dharma is immeasurable; you should apply yourself with even greater courage and diligence," and so forth.
When I presented the words shown by Zhangjia to Galingyin for his inquiry, he was utterly bewildered and failed to understand their meaning.

He merely evaded the matter, saying, "This is nothing more than a discussion on the methods for returning to the path according to the Lama’s teachings; what else could there be? Yet, I have placed my sincere faith in the instructions bestowed by Zhangjia.
I showed him that it was not so, yet he could not abandon his delusions regarding the nature of sound; I continued to urge him on with persistent reminders.

Precisely on the twenty-first day of the first month of the following year, the year of Kisi (1293), while sitting in meditation within the hall, I suddenly, without intending to, stepped through the very last barrier.
Only then did he realize the principle of the unification of the three bodies and four wisdoms, and the path of the fundamental emptiness in which things and self are one as such.

His lifelong aspirations were fulfilled with joy. He went to the residence of Lcang-skya to offer his thanks; upon seeing him, the National Preceptor (Guoshi) immediately said, "The King has attained great mastery."
The Emperor further asked, "Is there anything more? The State Preceptor then smiled, extended his hand, and said, "What else could there be?
He then moved his hand from the outside toward his body and gestured, saying, "It is nothing more than this principle; yet it is an easy matter.
This was the very matter upon which I, the Emperor, had spent my life investigating. — Recorded by the Imperial Preceptor, the Lama of the Changkya Hutuktu, Lobsang Tenpai Nyima.
He is my late master, who can bear witness for me. As for the other fellow practitioners of Zen, they merely came and went from my princely residence;
during the years of Renchen and Guisi, they sat in seven-day retreats and participated in Dharma assemblies with me.
As for Galing Xingyin’s audience with me, it was because I initially wished to join him in a seven-day retreat, but as the Abbot of Bolin was advanced in age, I inquired about him.
The Abbot of the Central Hall within the capital reported, "There is only Chan Master Qianfo Yin. Thereupon, the Emperor ordered him to be summoned.

Once he was seen, the Emperor questioned him for a very long time; however, the Master's skill was unable to provoke even a single point of doubt in the Emperor, who remained pressed, constrained, and perplexed, saying only:
When the Prince passed by Da Hui Gao on his journey, this poor monk truly had no means to deal with the situation. I smiled and said, "You all simply continue the seven-day retreat;
I shall remain here by your side to join in your joy. At that time, the causes and conditions for my awakening have already been fully recounted as follows.
If one were to say that Master Xingyin silently employed his spiritual power to enable me to clearly understand these five incense sticks—[this would be the case].

[The Emperor] said: "What is the point of spending a lifetime in such frantic pursuit? Having opened the hall at several locations, you have been unable to find even a single person worthy of the Dharma, yet you have recklessly entrusted it to a dozen or so mediocre fellows.
Later, Xingyin urged me to investigate and discern the tenets of the Five Houses. I asked: "How does one investigate and discern the tenets of the Five Houses?
Xingyin replied: "The tenets must await oral transmission. I thought to myself: "What kind of talk is this?"
Is it not so? How could oral transmission from ear to ear be the same as the meaning of the "Plucking the Flower" special transmission?

How could a dignified man of great character be willing to pick up the spittle and tears of others? From that time on, I cast aside the *yulu* (recorded sayings) and did not look at them again for twenty years;
this is something everyone in the palace and the government offices fully knows. Indeed, the fundamental tenets of the Five Houses are all one single flavor of Caoxi.
However, shifting authority and changing one's countenance to engage others—upon investigation, all such things are but meaningless words.
It is like mixing poison and nectar into a single vessel, or fusing gold and rubble into a single mass; there is no difference in how they are applied.

When brought forth, they provide a standard; each is a patriarchal master of an era and a model for a hundred generations. Yet, those of mediocre capacity fail to understand their own minds, thereby bringing defilement upon themselves.
They stir up the workings of consciousness and give rise to arbitrary attachments to phenomena, adding erroneous interpretations that invite the laughter of bystanders.
Such things are unfit to be presented before those with clear eyes. Thus, seeing that the sound of the realization of nature was repeatedly and earnestly [proclaimed]—
This is merely following the words to divide the school and aligning the phrasing to fix the meaning; it treats what has not yet been fully realized as something trivial.
If Xingyin were clearly aware of this, why would he urge me to strike and circumambulate him? What kind of mental activity is that?
Thus, the limitations of their perspective can be readily understood. For instance, the verse on the transmission of the robe in the *Dharmatrāta* tradition states:
"One flower opens into five petals; the fruiting occurs spontaneously. Later generations fabricated an interpretation of this teaching, claiming that the "five petals" refers to the Five Schools.
Now, the transmission of the robe ceased at Caoxi; thus, from Huike downward, it spanned five generations.
Because the faith of the land of China had already matured and the Dharma had pervaded the entire realm, the robe became a source of contention and was no longer used to signify faith.
The words of Bodhidharma and Huineng remain fully extant. From Huike to Huineng, were these not the "five leaves"? Thereafter, though there were ten thousand streams, they all shared the same source.
Is it not the case that the fruit is naturally accomplished? How can you equate this with the Five Houses (Wu-zong)?
Furthermore, regarding the public case of the transmission of the robe, many in the world swallow dates whole; they have not understood it at all.

When the World-Honored One went before the Many-Sons Stūpa, he commanded Mahākāśyapa to share his seat and sit beside him, then surrounded him with his *saṃghāṭī* robe, and finally declared: "I [bequeath] the Eye of the True Dharma..."
"I entrust the Secret Mantra of the Tibetan tradition to you; you must protect and uphold it. He then further addressed Kāśyapa:
"I now transmit this saṃghāṭī robe of gold thread to you. Pass it on to the one who succeeds me, until the appearance of the Buddha Maitreya, so that it shall not decay."
As for the seat divided by the World-Honored One, what kind of seat was it? And as for the *saṃghāṭī*, what exactly is that object?

As it is said, this very *saṃghāṭī* robe of golden thread, which was transmitted from Kāśyapa down to the Sixth Patriarch—how could it remain undecayed from the time of King Zhao of the Zhou dynasty until the reign of Emperor Wu of the Liang?
It truly belongs to the category of extraordinary treasures and is inconceivable. Thus it is said.
How can it be that [the Dharma] is able to remain perpetually in the world? Furthermore, what connection does it have with the Treasury of the Eye of the True Dharma (*saddharmakṣayanidhi*)?
Moreover, why did it subsequently vanish after the Sixth Patriarch? The World-Honored One clearly stated that [this teaching] shall not decay until the appearance of Maitreya Buddha;
yet before the Tang dynasty had even arrived, it was already no longer extant. Could it be that the World-Honored One spoke falsely or deceptively? Furthermore, by...

As for the statement that the *saṃghāṭī* was wrapped around Kāśyapa, what was the intention behind it? In short, since one has not yet awakened to the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye (*saddharmapuṇḍarīka*), from where could one possibly infer it?
A person must clearly grasp the *saṃghāṭī* and ensure it remains until the appearance of Maitreya;
only then can the matter of the transmission of the robe be discussed. How can one engage in fragmented and forced interpretations to arbitrarily establish a school’s tenets?
Is it further by means of the five schools that you force together and harmonize [the teachings]? Moreover, the five schools differ in their chronological order and did not exist simultaneously.

As for what the five schools clarify, it is all equally the nature of the Great Perfect Enlightenment (*mahā-vimala-avabodha*). If there were five schools, then the nature would likewise have to be fivefold.
The ancients strove solely to eradicate emotion and sever views, fearing only that one path might become too familiar, lest emotional and intellectual attachments should once again blaze forth.
Nevertheless, for this reason, I have produced a distinct approach and insight to enable people to awaken and grasp it. The minds of sentient beings are unable to take *prajñā* as their object;
instead, they now turn it into a matter of emotional views and conceptual discrimination, thereby obscuring the ancients to no small degree.
Since I have deeply understood the fundamental intent, I seek only the truth to settle my life’s work; how could I ever allow myself to be entangled by them?
Fengko (Tongke) also [said]: "One year later, I returned from Mount Qingliang. Regarding both doctrine and practice, I did not mention them at all.
Since ascending the throne, ten years have passed without seeing a single monk, nor have I ever touched upon the single word 'Chan.
Indeed, those who truly understand this matter are few; those who merely chase after fragments of the teachings labor in vain, while those who seek fame only increase their karmic burdens."
For this reason, the world’s "frogs at the bottom of the well" will inevitably give rise to groundless speculations.

Out of compassion for sentient beings who are ignorant, foolish, and vulgar, and fearing that they might thereby commit the grave sin of slandering the Prajñāpāramitā, my intention not to discuss it was by no means accidental.
Now, seeing that the time since the Sage departed grows ever more distant, the spirit of the school has been swept away, and the treasury of the true Dharma eye hangs on as thin as a thread.
Furthermore, I could not bear to witness its continued downward flow during my own reign.

Therefore, I have selected and compiled the most urgent words on the cultivation of the person spoken by the ancestral masters from antiquity to the present, publishing them for the world and future generations.

This is intended to enable them to cast off the root-dust of birth and death and to overturn the treacherous pits of saṃsāra. Students should know that this undertaking of mine is truly for the sake of the wisdom of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
This matter concerns one’s very life; it is not a question of sparing one's eyebrows that trail on the ground.

I am not here to debate the relative depth or shallowness of the realization of those who travel the path as itinerant monks for the sake of the eternal Sangha throughout the ten directions. As for this selection I have made, do not gather in crowds to chatter pointlessly about which school or lineage it belongs to;
otherwise, you will have nothing at all to do with me. Among the followers of the various schools under heaven, those who can truly act for themselves as a single great...
One must practice courageous and vigorous diligence, as if extinguishing a fire on one's own head.

Standing in the snow without feeling cold, cutting off one’s arm without feeling pain—only then will the black lacquer bucket spontaneously shatter against the void and the Jade Qilin be reined in upon the ground.

At that time, you will finally realize that these words of mine have fallen into the realm of immeasurable compassion. Should this mind not be true and sincere, nor earnest and urgent, [it will be of no avail].

One merely projects views, hearing, awareness, and cognition from words and letters, indulging in arbitrary conjecture and meticulous investigation, asking which one belongs to the Linji school and which one to the Caodong sect.
By fashioning models and delineating forms, one becomes stuck in appearances and clings to conditions;
thus seeking accord and realization through such means is like using emptiness to block emptiness, rendering one's efforts and those of the ancestors alike futile.

"The various ancient worthies employed hundreds of thousands of expedient means, yet it was as if they were trying to catch sound and put it into a box, or blowing through a net to make it fill one's ears.
Is this not, indeed, a case of frustrating people? Even when I was in the Prince’s residence, I likewise engaged with others regarding the fundamental matter."
There have been no omissions; all the recorded sayings and phrases have already been included within the *Collected Works of the Layman Yuanming*.
Furthermore, not a single instance of a karmic encounter has been circulated among the people. Moreover, I occupy the position of Emperor.

The mouth proclaims the heart-mind of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Those in the present and future generations whose obstacles of conceptualization are profound will surely harbor doubts and refuse to believe, claiming that the principle of the "special transmission outside the teachings" has not been validated by the Duke of Zhou or Confucius.

Yet, the harm caused by this is still relatively shallow. As for those who outwardly rely on the Chan school while inwardly coveting honor and profit, their deceptions will inevitably take a thousand forms.
Deceiving and deluding others with a hundred kinds of gibberish— some having once caught a glimpse of his countenance while he was in the imperial palace,
others having once heard a few words transmitted among his dharma companions— they proceed like those such as Gu Yan and Mu Chen, fabricating false accounts and privately recording them.
Taking what is non-existent to be existent, they indulge in self-aggrandizing boastfulness, carving and printing [their works] for circulation to delude those who see and hear them.
Such individuals are already unacceptable to the Buddha-dharma and ought further to be prohibited by the laws of the state.

On the day they are discovered, they shall be dealt with according to the statutes and treatises on the forgery of imperial edicts. My present action is truly because the "separate transmission outside the teachings" is on the verge of falling to the ground.

I have been compelled to do this. As for the ways of the Gate of the Patriarchs—where one can kill and bring to life, where one can grant freedom and seize—all stem from the fact that the Master’s investigation was unerring and his realization boundless.

There is a teaching: if it is meager, the mental factors will not be complete. When one explains the principle, they remain; when they do not understand, they depart. The assembly had no response.
Elder Ziyuan asked, "What is the samādhi of the present moment? The Master said, "Do you hear it? Ziyuan said, "I [hear it]."
Jiā said, "I do not suffer from deafness. The Master said, "Indeed, you do suffer from deafness.
The Master subsequently moved to Baisha on Mount Tiantai and built a hermitage there. A certain Venerable Péngyàn, who was erudite and possessed a powerful memory, came to visit the Master.
They engaged in debate regarding the Dharma-gate (zōngchéng). The Master said, "Excessive words distance one further from the Way. Now, I have a matter I wish to ask about; please listen closely."

"Among the various sages and virtuous predecessors mentioned above, were there any who did not attain enlightenment? Yan said, "If they were sages and virtuous predecessors, how could there be any who did not attain enlightenment?
The Master said, "When one person gives rise to the True and returns to the Source, the empty space of the ten directions completely vanishes.
Yet today, Mount Tiantai stands towering and prominent; how can it vanish? Yan was speechless.
Correct. When Imperial Messenger Liao entered Yunju Qingxi Chan Master’s monastery, he saw the portrait of Fayan and asked: "What is before this portrait?"
[The guest] presented some fruit. The Master said, "These are artificial fruits. Liao said, "Since they are artificial fruits, why use them to make offerings to the Real?
The Master said, "It is simply because I wish for you, Celestial Being, to recognize what is artificial."
Zen Master Zhiyi of Luohan Monastery asked a monk, "Where have you been this summer? The monk replied, "I was with Upāsaka Wuyan.
The Master said, "Did you ever inquire after him? The monk said, "I did inquire after him. The Master said, "How could one inquire after the Wordless?"
The monk said, "If one attains wordlessness, where would there be anything that could not be asked? The Master shouted, "It is just as if you were asking me, elder brother!
The Master was eating *bing-dian* (steamed cakes) with Elder Yan-duan. Yan-duan said, "A hundred kinds, a thousand varieties—their essence is not two.
The Master asked, "What is this essence of non-duality? Yan-duan picked up a *bing-dian*. The Master said, "You merely cling to the hundred kinds and the thousand [varieties]."
Ban said, "This is also the Master’s own point of view. The Master said, "You are like Old Man Luo reciting a poem on the style of combing one's hair. He ascended the hall and said:
"Throughout the entire ten directions of the world, there is not so much as a single speck of dust of a dharma to serve as an object for your seeing, hearing, sensing, or knowing."
"Do you still believe me? Even so, you must awaken before it will do; do not treat this as something trivial. Have you not heard it said:
'To clarify only one's own self, yet not awaken to what is before one's eyes—such a person possesses only a single eye. Do you understand? A monk asked:
"Not a single speck of dust can be established. Why, then, do beauty and ugliness manifest before one? The Master said: "Take this clearly to heart; ask others about it elsewhere.
—Chan Master Xuanze of Baoen.
Ascending the hall, he said: "All you venerable elders possess the ever-perfect moon; each harbors a priceless treasure within.

Thus, when the moon is amidst the clouds, though it is bright, it does not shine; when wisdom is hidden within delusion, though it is true, it does not penetrate. There is nothing to do. He stood for a long time.
A monk asked, "What is the Venerable One Who Is Immovable? The Master said, "Flying and fluttering.

When Chan Master Shaoyan of Baota was commissioned by the King of Wuyue to open a Dharma assembly, he ascended the hall and said: "Today, the Great King has prepared this Dharma feast and extended an invitation."
I, this mountain monk, seek only for you, honorable ones, to clarify your minds; beyond this, there is no other principle.

Have you clarified your minds yet? Is it not so that when you are speaking and laughing, when you are sitting in silent stillness, when you are seeking out a teacher, when you are deliberating with your companions on the Path, when you are viewing mountains and playing in waters, or when your ears and eyes are utterly cut off—is this your mind?
As explained above, all such understandings are encompassed by demonic delusions; how could they be called "clarifying the mind"?

Furthermore, there is another class of people who, apart from the delusive thoughts within the body, separately identify that which pervades the worlds of the ten directions, containing the sun and moon and enveloping the great void, as being the original true mind.
This too is merely the conceptualization of external paths; it is not clarifying the mind. Do you all wish to understand this?
The mind has nothing that is "is," nor does it have anything that is "is not. How could you possibly grasp or recognize it?
Chan Master Xiqian Yuan addressed the assembly:
"Upon leaving the Sangha Hall door and seeing Mount Wulao, the work of a lifetime of study is finished. What further use is there?"
"Come here. "Even so, you have troubled the Venerable One to come once," [the Master said]. "Take care.
Zen Master Shiming of Shishuang went to visit Zen Master Tangming Song. Song said to the Master, "The Inner Secretary Yang Dainian possesses high insight. When he entered...
"The Way is stable and real; you must not fail to see him. The Master then went to see Da-nian. Da-nian asked, "We face each other, yet we do not know one another;
from a thousand miles away, our winds are the same. The Master said, "Recently, I have received an invitation from the Mountain Gate. Da-nian said, "You are truly a master of empty talk."
The Master said, "Last month I left Tangming. Nian said, "I regret having asked you just now. The Master said, "An adept. Nian then shouted. The Master said, "Exactly so. Nian shouted again.
The Master made a sweeping gesture with his hand. Nian stuck out his tongue and said, "Truly a dragon and an elephant!
The Master said, "What words are those? Nian called for the guest master to bring some tea, saying, "It turns out he was right here in the house all along."
The Master said, "It is not necessary. After the tea was finished, he asked again, "What is the one phrase for the sake of others? The Master said, "Cuttingly.
Yang Yi said, "In that case, it is like a bride in her long skirt dragging through the mud. The Master said, "Who could equal you, Inner Secretary?
Yang Yi said, "A master! A master! The Master said, "I grant you twenty blows. Yang Yi patted his knee and said, "This..."
"What place is this? The Master clapped his hands and said, "I cannot let you off. Yuanan laughed loudly.
He asked again, "Do you remember the circumstances of Tangming’s enlightenment at that time? The Master said, "Tangming asked Shoushan, 'What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
Shoushan replied, 'On the banks of the city of King Chu, the Ru River flows east. Yuanan said, "Only..."
When he spoke these words, [Yang] Shan asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "A lantern suspended over water. Yang Shan said, "If that is so, then you have failed the ancients.
The Master said, "If you, Inner Secretary, have doubts, then seek another teacher. Yang Shan said, "A three-legged frog leaps up into the sky.
The Master said, "Feel free to leap as much as you wish. Yang Shan then laughed heartily and was lodged within the refectory.
The Master went to visit Director Li. When the official heard that he had come to pay his respects, he sent a page to inquire, saying, "If you can speak the Way, I will see you, Senior Monk.
The Master said, "I have come specifically today to pay my respects. He then sent the page again, saying, "The inscription on the monument is carved in white characters;

along the path, plant green pines. The Master said, "It is not because of today’s festival; on other days it would certainly be difficult to encounter such an occasion. The page came out once more and said:
The Commandant said, "If that is so, then let us meet with the Senior Monk. The Master said, "From head to foot.
The official then came forward, sat down, and asked, "I have heard there is a golden-haired lion in West River;
is this true? The Master said, "Where did you get such news? The official gave a shout. The Master said, "A jackal howling. The official shouted again. The Master said, "Exactly!"
The Duke laughed heartily. As the Master was taking his leave, the Duke asked, "What is that one phrase for you, Venerable One, as you depart?
The Master said, "Take good care. The Duke said, "How is this any different from other places? The Master said, "And what about you, Excellency? The Duke said, "I shall give you twenty blows!
The Master said, "Solely for the sake of its wide circulation. The Duke gave another shout. The Master said, "Blind! The Duke said, "Go well," and the Master departed.
"Very well, very well," [Nanyue] replied. From then on, he went back and forth between the gates of Yangshan and Linji, taking the Dharma as his friend.

After a long time, he took his leave to return to Hedong. Nanyue asked, "I have a phrase to entrust to Tangming; can you grasp it? The Master said, "The bright moon shines upon the traveler at night. Nanyue said, "But that does not quite match.
The Master said, "It may still be bearable when the night is deep, but after midday, it brings even more sorrow to people. Nanyue—
Yuan'an said, "The Vajra statue before Kaibao Temple has recently sweated; why is that? The Master said, "I know.
Yuan'an said, "As you are about to depart, Senior, do you have no phrase for the sake of others? The Master said, "Layer upon layer of mountain passes and roads.
Yuan'an said, "If that is so, then I shall follow you, Senior. The Master let out a single sigh. Yuan'an said, "A true lion cub; a great lion's roar!"
The Master said, "Letting go and then gathering back. Nian said, "Just now I lost my footing and fell down, but I was helped up by a servant boy.
The Master said, "What end will there ever be? Nian laughed loudly. The Master returned to Tangming.
He went to visit Chan Master Shen Dingyin. Ding was the foremost disciple of Shou Mountain;

his reputation was preeminent at the time, and among the monastics, none who were not of extraordinary refinement and talent dared to enter his gate. His disciples’ spirit overwhelmed all other quarters. The Master [Yunmen] did not cut his hair long.

Wearing tattered robes and speaking with a Chu accent, he announced his arrival and called himself a "Dharma nephew. The entire assembly burst into laughter. Yangshan Ding sent a novice to ask, "Whose successor is this elder?
The Master looked up at the roof and said, "I have come directly from Fenyang. Yangshan Ding leaned on his staff and stepped out;
seeing the Master’s tall and imposing figure, he asked, "Is it true that there is a 'Lion of West River' in Fenzhou? The Master pointed behind him and shouted loudly, "The house!"

"You have fallen into error," [the Master] said. Dongliang turned to run back; Huizhong looked back at him with a startled expression. The Master sat down on the ground, took off one sandal, and showed it to him.
Dongliang, being old and senile, forgot what he had asked and also lost track of where the Master was. The Master slowly rose, adjusted his robes, and spoke as he walked away.
"Meeting someone in person is not as good as hearing of their reputation. He then departed. Fending sent people to pursue him, but it was impossible.
He sighed and said, "Fenzhou has such a son!
He asked, "When you are traveling on foot and do not encounter anyone, what then? The Master replied, "The fishing line sinks into the water."
A monk asked, "Polishing a three-foot sword to go and transform those who are unjust—what is your intention, Master? The Master said, "Go well.
The monk said, "Understood. The Master said, "Look! The monk clapped his hands once and returned to the assembly. The Master said, "Finished."

The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk said, "Clouds pass over a thousand mountains, leaving them green. The Master said, "Why are you in such a hurry? The monk said, "Geese fly over the water, their cries mournful.
The Master gave a shout; the monk also shouted. The Master struck him; the monk also struck him. The Master said, "Look at this blind fellow!
By his due right, he should have been driven out through the triple gates. But considering that you are a newcomer, sit here and drink some tea."
The Master asked Chief Seat Xianying, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "Jinluan. The Master asked, "Where were you last summer? He replied, [silently].
Jinluan asked, "Where were you last summer? He replied, "Jinluan. Jinluan asked, "Where were you before that last summer?
He replied, "Why do you not understand my words, Master? Jinluan said, "I am unable to examine you myself. I shall have the attendant from the storehouse come to examine you;

The Master sat in formal meditation within his quarters, with a blade of wood laid across a basin of water and a straw sandal placed beside it. He would direct those who came to inquire about the Way to offer a response;

He went to visit Chan Master Gong’an Yuan. Yuan asked, “What is the monastery? The Master said, “In deep mountains, solitary tigers hide;
