how could yellow leaves conceal anything? Yuan asked, “What did you say? The Master said, “In my youth, I played with the moon at the edge of the sky.”
"The aged sun has set behind the Fusang tree. [The student] asked, "Regarding 'one phrase, two phrases, clouds parting, moon and dew revealed'—how is this?
The Master said, "It illuminates the barrier of the Patriarchs."
He went to visit the Chief Seat Zhen. Zhen asked, "Do you see? The Master said, "All things are completely absent. Zhen asked, "Or do you not see?
The Master said, "A thousand forms are all in my hand. The Master asked, "Chief Seat, how was it before you met the Sage of Dispelling [Cheng San-sheng]?
Zhen said, "Hunan and Jiangxi. He asked again, "How was it after you met him? Zhen said, "Jiangxi and Hunan. The Master said, "But..."
"Is it the same as with the Head Seat? He replied, "Beating the grass to startle the snake.
The Master said, "I shall certainly not fabricate a marvel. He then went to visit Chan Master Daguo Zhi. Zhi asked, "When the ancients saw the peach blossoms, what was their meaning?
The Master said, "A crooked thing does not conceal the straight. Zhi said, "Let that one aside for now; as for this one, what is it? The Master said, "Picking up a treasure in the marketplace."
Pilina learned of this and asked, "Does the Senior Monk know? The Master said, "When meeting a swordsman on the road, one must present a sword;
if one is not a poet, one does not offer a poem. Pilina said, "A master poet! The Master said, "A single red thread pulled by two people.

Pilina asked, "What about Yuansha’s statement, 'It is true and correct'—how would you respond to that? The Master said, "When the ocean dries up, its bottom will finally be seen; when a person dies..."
[The Master] did not know [the meaning of] "mind. [The other] said, "Exactly so. The Master said, "The pavilions tower above the clouds;
the peaks and ridges are layered with emerald green. He went to visit Chan Master Wuzu Jie. Jie asked, "What is a person who has severed all fetters?
The Master said, "Turning one's hand back to grasp the halter. [Jie] said, "Indeed, you are a master. The Master said, "A whip struck from behind does not hit [the mark]. [Jie] asked, "Why is that?"
[The monk] said, "Coming up and going down. The Master said, "Where did you see coming up and going down? Jie then struck him. The Master said, "A single word leaves no other path;
for a thousand miles one meets no person."
He went to pay his respects to Chan Master Xuedou Xian. Xuedou asked, "Does the ox eat the grass, or does the grass eat the ox?

The Master said, "To turn one's head back to seek the tail is already separated by ten thousand layers of barriers. Xuedou said, "You should know there is no front or back; it must always be manifest before you.
The Master said, "The verification is right here before your eyes. Xuedou said, "Take this for yourself and leave."
He arrived at the place of Master Jiao of Langye. Langye asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The Master said, "The Two Zhe circuits. Langye asked, "Did you come by boat or by land?
The Master said, "By boat. Langye asked, "Where is the boat now? The Master said, "At the foot of the stairs.
Langye asked, "How do you express the phrase that does not involve the journey? The Master struck his sitting cloth once and said, "Fabricated elders are as numerous as hemp."
[He] looked like a grain of millet. He shook out his sleeves and left. Xue asked an attendant, "Who was that? The attendant replied, "It was Upadhyaya Ju.
Xue said, "Could it be Master Uncle Ju? My late teacher instructed me to seek him out. Thereupon, he went down to the guest quarters and asked.
"Venerable Elder, are you not Master Shu? Please do not take offense for having offended you just now. The Master then gave a shout and asked, "Elder, when did you arrive at Fenyang?
He replied, "I arrived at such-and-such a time. The Master said, "I have heard your name in Zhejiang long ago.
It turns out your understanding is merely like this; how then can your reputation be spread throughout the world? Xue then prostrated himself and said:
Such-and-such a transgression.

To the assembly: Had Śākyamuni not appeared in the world and Bodhidharma not come from the West, the Buddha-dharma would have pervaded the world, yet no one would have opened their mouths to discuss the profound mystery.
Chan Master Bajia Guquan went to visit Ciming.
Ciming asked, "White clouds hang across the mouth of the valley; from where has the man of the Way come?
The Master looked to his left and right and said, "What fire broke out last night that burned out the ancient tomb? Ciming rebuked him, saying, "Not yet. Speak further."
The Master then let out a tiger’s roar. Ciming struck him with his sitting mat. The Master caught it and pushed Ciming onto the meditation seat.
Ciming then let out a tiger’s roar. The Master laughed loudly and said, "I have encountered more than seventy virtuous teachers (kalyāṇamitra), but today I have finally met a true master."
When Master Tiansheng Haotai arrived at Langye, Langye asked: "To bury troops and engage in combat is not yet the mark of a master. With a single horse and a lone spear, I invite you to meet me.
The Master pointed at Langye and said, "If the general does not lead with vigor, he brings misfortune upon his entire army. Langye struck the Master once with his sitting cloth (zuoju).
The Master also struck Xie once with his sitting cloth. Xie caught it and said, “That previous strike with the sitting cloth was the mountain monk’s command being carried out;
where did this present strike with the sitting cloth land? The Master said, “I humbly pray you will accept my offerings.

Xie pushed him away and said, “At the fifth watch, rising before dawn—there is yet another traveler on the night road. The Master said, “Drawing the bow after the thief has fled. Xie said, [and remained silent].
"Sit and drink tea.

When the eminent scholar Ou-yang Wen-chung heard that Chan Master Fu-shan Yuan-chien was extraordinary and unconventional, he visited his quarters; yet, finding nothing remarkable about him, he was playing chess with a guest.

The Master sat beside him. Wenzhong suddenly withdrew his board and requested that he preach the Dharma by means of the game of Go. The Master immediately ordered the drum to be beaten and ascended the seat, saying:
"If one discusses this matter, it is like two parties playing Go. Why is this so? Because they are adversaries who understand one another."
When the opportunity arises, one must not yield. If you merely string together five [points] and dally with three, you will only succeed by following a single path.
There is a certain class of people who only know how to "make a living" by closing the door; they do not understand how to "seize the horn" and "break through the pass.

When their rigid joints and tiger-mouths are displayed simultaneously, once the position is broken, their efforts are in vain. Therefore it is said: "The fat sides are easy to obtain; the lean belly is difficult to seek. If you merely contemplate and act accordingly...

Staying on the board, one loses the momentum; the mind is coarse, and from time to time the head strikes the board. Cease boasting of being a national master; it is in vain to speak of being a divine immortal.
Setting aside for a moment the question of winning the game or losing the counting pieces, tell me: when black and white have not yet been distinguished, where does that first move fall?

After a long silence, he said: "Regarding the nineteen paths that have existed from the beginning, how many people have been lost in delusion or attained enlightenment? Wen Zhong sighed with admiration and calmly remarked to his colleagues:

"Previously, I suspected that Chan discourse was merely empty and exaggerated. Today, having witnessed this old master’s karmic conditions, I realize that were it not for what has been attained and cultivated through awakening within the mind-ground, how could such wondrous principles exist?"

The Master was elderly; he retired to Huishengyan (Cave of the Sage’s Assembly). There, while reading Ban Gu’s *Discourse on the Nine Schools*, he subsequently composed the *Ninefold Band* (*Jiudai*) to expound upon the teachings and meanings of the Buddhas and patriarchs.
He extensively gathered the pivotal sayings of former worthies to provide mutual verification and corroboration. The first is called the "Band of the Buddha’s True Dharma Eye";
the second, the "Band of the Buddha-Dharma Treasury"; the third, the "Band of the Pervasion of Principle"; and the fourth, the "Band of Phenomena."

The fifth is called the "Band of the Vertical and Horizontal Interpenetration of Principle and Phenomena. The sixth is the "Curvilinear Band. The seventh is the "Band of Sublime Harmony and Integration.
The eighth is the "Golden Needle Double-Chain Band. The ninth is the "Band of Equanimity and Constant Reality. Once the students had memorized these, the Master said:
"If one were to rely upon the Dharma-gate of Perfect Ultimate Reality, there would originally be ten such numbers; yet here we have only nine."
I have already explained these various "Bands" for you. Is there yet another Band that you can perceive? If you can perceive it with intimacy and clarity, then please bring it forth and speak of it.
If you can explain it clearly, I shall grant you the aforementioned nine Bands as the perfectly enlightened Eye of Wisdom.
If your perception is not intimate and your explanation is inconsistent, then you are merely relying on my words to form your own interpretations.
"This is called slandering the Dharma. "Venerable Sir, what do you say to this? The assembly remained silent. The Master rebuked them and sent them away.

Chan Master Jinshan Tanying Daguan first visited Chan Master Taiyang Xuan, who asked him: "Dongshan specifically established the categories of partiality and correctness, ruler and subject; what meaning does he clarify?"
"What matter? Yang said, "The matter of before one's parents were born. The Master asked, "How do you realize this? Yang said, "At midnight it is perfectly bright;
at dawn, nothing is revealed. The Master was at a loss. He then went to visit Guyin and recounted the previous conversation.
Guyin said, "The Great Sun did not say it was wrong, but his mouth is too narrow; he speaks with his whole mouth yet cannot finish. I, the old monk, am not like that. The Master [was enlightened].
The Master asked, "What is it like when one's parents have not yet been born? Yinyuan said, "A brick from a dung-pile.

The Master asked, "What is it like when midnight is at its brightest, yet dawn does not reveal it? Yinyuan said, "A sleeping cat beneath a peony flower. The Master became even more perplexed and alarmed.
One day, during a communal work assignment, Yinyuan asked, "Are you carrying firewood today? The Master replied, "Yes. Yinyuan said, "Yunmen asked—"
A monk asked, "The person carries the firewood; the firewood carries the person. How do you understand this? The Master had no reply. Yinyuan said, "This matter is like a person learning to write.

One who can accurately replicate the dots and strokes is skilled; one who cannot is clumsy. This is because they have not yet been able to forget the method. When the brush forgets the hand, [one is truly skilled]."
"It is only when the hand forgets the mind that it can be so. The Master then attained silent realization. After a long while, he said, "As Shitou said:
'To grasp at phenomena is fundamentally delusion; to accord with principle is likewise not awakening. Yinyoung asked, "Do you consider these words to be medicine or a disease? The Master replied:

“This is the language of medicine,” [Zhao]chen said. Yinyue replied, “If you take the illness itself as the medicine, how can that possibly be right? The Master said, “In affairs, it is like a box finding its lid;

in principle, it is like an arrow with a straight shaft and sharp point. How could there be anything more wondrous than this? Yet you still consider it an illness; truly, I do not yet understand your meaning.

Yinyue said, “Even when wondrousness reaches such a state, it is still merely called ‘principle and phenomenon. The intent of the Patriarchs is something that intellectual consciousness cannot grasp.”
"How much less could one exhaust both phenomena and principle? Therefore, the World-Honored One said: 'The barrier of principle obstructs right view and knowledge;

the barrier of phenomena continues the cycle of birth and death. At these words, the Master was as if awakened from a dream and asked, "How do you make use of this? Yun said, "Speech does not depart from its fundamental mold."
"How can one transcend the entanglements? The Master sighed and said, "As soon as it touches the lips, it falls into the realm of conceptual thought;
all such paths are dead ends and are never the way of life. Later, while presiding over the assembly, he declared: "As soon as it touches the lips, it falls into the realm of conceptual thought;
all such paths are dead ends and are never the way of life. Even if you manage to break through, you still remain within the depths of samsara. Do not let your lifelong efforts go to waste in vain."
"To cross over this world, must you not ensure that you do not bring your life's endeavor to naught?
He took up his staff and struck once, saying, "You must not be deceived by this staff. Look, look!
This staff pierces through the skulls of all of you and leaps right into your nostrils! He struck once more.
He passed through the capital and stayed at the garden of Li Duanyuan, the Prince Consort. Li Gong asked, "Do hell and its hells ultimately exist or not?
The Master said, "The Buddhas speak of existence within non-existence; it is like seeing flowers in the sky with one's own eyes. Your Excellency seeks non-existence within existence;
it is like grasping at the moon reflected in water with your hands. It is truly laughable that you see the prison before your very eyes and yet do not avoid it."
Externally you see the heavens and desire to be born there, yet you do not realize that joy and fear reside within the mind, and that good and evil constitute the objective realm.

If you, Great Minister, simply understand your own mind, you will naturally be free from delusion. Li asked, "How does one understand the mind? The Master said, "Do not deliberate upon good or evil at all.
Li asked, "After no longer deliberating, where does the mind go? The Master said, "For now, please return home, Great Minister."
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "In my life, this mountain monk has always been fond of sumo wrestling, yet there was no one to match me.
Today, I shall wrestle with the Head Seat. [He] rolls up his *kāṣāya* and descends from the seat, summoning the Head Seat for a match. As soon as the Head Seat steps out, the Master says:"
While eating on level ground, he returned directly to the abbot’s quarters.
When Master Guangqing met Master Yu’an, the latter was ascending the hall for a discourse.
[Yu’an said: "If you wish to know the purport of Caoxi, look at the clouds flying over the mountain ahead; this is clearly and truly it—there is no need for anything else."
Chui Pan. A monk asked, "An ancient worthy said, 'Red dust arises from the bottom of the well; waves surge upon the mountain peak. I do not understand the meaning of this.
The Master said, "If you go to other places, simply ask in this manner. The monk asked, "What is your own intention, Reverend? The Master said, "What did I just tell you?"
A monk asked Chan Master Jingqing Jusu,

The layman Li Zunxu, the Prince Consort, visited Guyin and asked about the matter of leaving the household life. Guyin answered him with the kōan concerning Duke Cui Zhao’s inquiry to Mount Jing.
Under these words, the Duke attained great enlightenment. He composed a verse, saying: "To study the Way, one must be an iron man;
Upon the touch of the hand, the matter is decided. Directly advance toward supreme Bodhi; Pay no heed to any right or wrong."
One day, the Duke was seeing off the Venerable Jian. The Duke asked, "Having recently departed from Shangdang and arrived at the Central Capital, we have just engaged in this dust-free discourse.
Yet you are already returning with your tiger-striped staff to point toward the verdant peaks of Yunping and visit the clear streams of Xueling.
I wonder, what is the state of affairs here and there? The Venerable said, "A sharp sword sweeps away [all obstructions], and heaven and earth are silent."
The frosty blade is just raised, and the Ox and Cow constellations shiver with cold. The Master said, "It happens to coincide with my deafness today.
A monk said, "One arrow brings down two eagles. The Master said, "Why is the Head Seat sleeping in his straw sandals? The monk gave a flick with his sleeve.
The Master bowed his head and said, "Today you may truly be called 'subdued. The monk said, "Puhua has come out of the Sangha Hall."

When Chan Master Huayan Daolong first visited Master Shi-men Che, he asked: "The ancients said, 'If you can find peace and ease wherever you are, you will naturally accord with the tracks of the ancients.
Although these words exist, when one's doubts have not yet ceased, what then? Shi-men said: "Know."

There is [a way]. One can then find peace and ease wherever one is. It is like a person living in a prefecture or a county who, upon hearing or seeing a thousand wonders and a hundred oddities, treats them all as commonplace;

they do not know that there is something [extraordinary] and thus remain at ease. It is like a person living in a village who, upon encountering even a slight display of sensory splendor, becomes startled and spreads rumors of it being strange. Under these words, the Master attained realization.
The Layman Yang Yi, Dadian, the Duke Wen-gong, asked Guanghui:
"I have heard from the Master that all sinful karma arises because of wealth and treasures."
[The Master] said, "You urge people to distance themselves from wealth and profit. Yet, in this Jambudvīpa, sentient beings take wealth as their very life;
states and nations gather people through wealth. Within the teachings, there are two kinds of giving: that of material things and that of the Dharma.

How can you urge people to distance themselves from wealth? Hui said, "The iron cage atop the flagpole. Gong said, "A stallion from Haitan is as large as a donkey. Hui said, "A chicken from Chu [cannot crow]."
"This is a phoenix from the Cinnabar Mountains. The Master said: "Two thousand years after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, bhikṣus have little sense of shame.
Chan Master Touzi Yiqing went to visit Chan Master Yuan Tong Xiu; he asked no questions and did nothing but indulge in sleep. The attendants reported this.

Tong entered the hall dragging his staff. Seeing that the Master was fast asleep, he struck the meditation seat and scolded him, saying, "There is no spare rice here for you, Senior, to eat and then sleep.
The Master said, "What did the Abbot command me to do? Tong said, "Why do you not go off to practice Zen?
The Master said, "Fine food is not fit for a person already full to eat. Tong said, "But there are many people who—"
The Master refused to let him ascend the seat. The Master said, "Wait until he is willing; what can he possibly do then? Tong asked, "Whom has the Senior Monk ever met?
The Master replied, "Fushan. Tong said, "No wonder he is so stubborn and unruly. Then they shook hands and laughed together before returning to the abbot’s quarters.
When Chan Master Xingyang Qingpou was serving as the head gardener under Master Dayang, while he was planting melons, Dayang asked, "When will the sweet melons ripen? The Master replied:
[The Master] said, "It is already fully ripe and rotten. [The man] said, "Pick out the sweet ones and bring them here.

The Master said, "For whom would you give them to eat? [The man] said, "For those who do not enter the garden. The Master said, "I wonder, does he still eat or not? [The man] said, "Do you recognize him?
The Master said, "Even though I do not recognize him, I cannot help but give [the fruit]. He laughed aloud and departed.
A monk asked, “When Sāgara emerges from the sea, heaven and earth tremble; when meeting face-to-face, what is the matter? The Master said, “The Golden-Winged Bird King presides over the universe;
who among them is the one who puts his head out? The monk said, “What if he suddenly meets one who has put his head out?
The Master said, “It is like a hawk seizing a pigeon—do you not believe it? Only when verified before a skull will you know the truth. The monk said, “If that is so...”

"If so, then place your hands together at your chest and step back three paces. The Master said, "Turtle under the Mount Sumeru throne, do not wait until you have suffered another defeat and turned back."
When Chan Master Xianru of Mount Luofu first arrived at Taiyang, Taiyang asked, "Where are you from? He replied, "Yizhou. Taiyang said, "How many li is it from here?
He replied, "Five thousand li. Taiyang said, "Coming as you have done, have you ever trodden upon it? He replied, "I have not."
Yang said, "Do you understand how one soars through the air? He replied, "I do not understand how one soars through the air. Yang said, "If that is so, how did you get here?"

Yangshan said, "At every step you do not lose your way; throughout your entire being there is no place for discrimination. Yangshan asked, "Have you attained the samādhi that transcends all directions?
He replied, "The Sage’s mind cannot be grasped; how could samādhi manifest as a name? Yangshan said, "So it is! So it is!"

The compiler, Layman Zenghui, had been a fellow student with Mingjue since childhood. Upon reaching adulthood, their paths diverged. During the Tianxi era, while the Layman was serving as the governor of Chizhou, one day—

They met at Jingde Temple. The Master [Wang Bi] then took the *Zhongyong* and the *Daxue*, cross-referencing them with the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* and the sayings of the Chan school to verify his understanding with Mingjue.
Mingjue said, "This [text] already does not accord with the scriptural teachings; how much less so the *Zhongyong* and the *Daxue*?"
The Academician was required to investigate this matter through its essential principles. [The Master] snapped his fingers once and said, "Just realize it in this way.
The Academician attained the meaning beneath these words.
Chan Master Yunju Xiaoshun went to study under Dongshan.
One day, while begging for alms in Wuchang, he first visited Layman Liu. The Layman said, "I have a question for you, old man.
If our views accord, I invite you to open a lecture hall; if they do not accord, I ask that you return to the mountain. He then asked:
"How is it when an ancient mirror has not yet been polished? The Master said, "Black as lacquer. "How is it after it has been polished? The Master said, "It reflects heaven and reflects earth.
The layman gave a long bow and said, "I ask that you, Venerable Sir, please return to the mountain. The Master returned home feeling dejected.

Dongshan asked him the reason for this, and the Master recounted his previous conversation. Dongshan said, "Ask me instead. The Master posed the same questions as before. Dongshan said, "From here to Han..."
"The yang is not far. The Master then spoke the subsequent words. Shanshan said, "Before the Yellow Crane Tower is the Parrot Isle. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
The Master once criticized Tianyi for preaching "entangled" Chan. One day, hearing that Huai had passed away, he joined [the funeral] in the Dharma Hall.
Zhangyun said, "I am glad that the entangled vine-stump has finally been toppled. At that time, Xiu Yuan-tong was in the assembly serving as the *vinaya* master (*weina*).
Whenever he saw [Zhaozhou] scolding and reviling him incessantly, he said to his colleagues, "I must settle accounts with this old fellow.
When the night instruction began, Zhaozhou again scolded and reviled him as before. Xiu stepped out from the assembly and said in a stern voice, "Have you not seen Yuan?"
As he was awakening to the Middle Way of the sutras, the Master suddenly said, "I have stood before the assembly for a long time; I trust you all are well. He then returned to his quarters.
Xiu remarked, "This old fellow has eyes all over his body; he even managed to scold Master Huai."
Cuoyan Zhen Dianxiong frequently reviled Master [Zhaozhou] for preaching "unconcerned Chan" (*wushi chan*). Master Shishuang Yong sent someone to deliver a message, saying:
"When Shun attained enlightenment at Dongshan through the causal conditions of the 'ancient mirror,' how could that be preaching 'unconcerned Chan'? Yet you revile him."
"I have lost one of my own eyes. When the Master heard this, he composed a verse: Yunju does not understand Chan; He washes his feet and goes up to bed to sleep.
The winter melon is straight and blunt; The bottle gourd is curved and bent. Master Yong also composed a verse: Shishuang does not understand Chan;
He washes his feet and goes up to bed to sleep. The pillow falls to the ground; It breaks the monastery’s brick.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "In other quarters, there are those who dangle the heads of snakes, stroke the tails of tigers, leap across the great ocean, and hide their bodies within the edge of a sword.
Here at Yunju, it is like washing one's feet in hot water on a freezing day; at night one takes off one’s sandals and falls asleep, and at dawn one quickly ties on one’s travel-binders.
When the wind blows down the fence, one calls for laborers to split reeds and bind it back up."
The Master asked Xiu Yuan-tong, "What words did you hear from Master Huai? Xiu recited Huai’s verse on seizing the opportune moment:
The Master said, "That is not good. Is there any other statement? Xiu said, "One day an elder came to visit.
Huai held up his whisk and asked, 'Do you understand? He replied, 'I do not. Huai said, 'Two flaps of skin for ears, a set of teeth.'"
The Bone. The Master sighed and said, "A true spiritual friend.
Chan Master Qi-sōng Fórì received the Dharma from Dòngshān;
at night, this Master would carry an image of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva upon his head while reciting its [mantra].

He vowed that he would not cease his recitation until he had completed one hundred thousand [verses]. From then on, he was able to master the chapters and sentences of worldly scriptures without formal study.

He composed the *Yuanjiao lun* (Treatise on the Origin of the Teachings) in over one hundred thousand words to refute the doctrines of Li Ao and Han Yu that sought to exclude Buddhism. Those who read it were awed and submissive.

Later, while residing at the Yong'an Aranya, he authored the *Chanmen dingzu tu* (Chart of the Fixed Patriarchs of the Chan School), the *Chuanfa zhengzong ji* (Record of the Orthodox Lineage of the Transmission of the Dharma), and the *Fujiao bian* (Compendium for Assisting the Teachings).
[The work] was submitted. Emperor Renzong praised it highly and ordered it to be compiled and included in the Tripitaka, bestowing upon [Zunshi] the title Mingjiao (Illuminating Teaching).
Xu Shi, the Prefectural Governor—who had attained the Dharma from Dongshan—once sat with Letan Cheng and Shanglan Pu. Cheng asked: "I have heard..."
Langzhong Dao said: "Sitting through the night by the Yunlian Rock; planting spring pines amidst the rain.

What words did you answer when you were with Dongshan? The Official replied: "The office has been dismissed early today. Tanhui asked: "I heard you gave the answer regarding the Great Sage of Sizhou appearing in Yangzhou.
Is this true? The Official said: "Serve another cup of tea. Tanhui said: "His reputation is not in vain. The Official said: "Master, it is already late."
Returning to the mountain late in the evening, Duan said, "Today you have been seen through by Shanglan. Shanglan then gave a shout. Duan said, "It must be you who did it.
Gong said, "What can one do with the boat? The scoop has been broken."

The Duke entered the Sangha Hall of Shanglan Monastery and asked the Head Seat, "How old are you? He replied, "Sixty-eight. The Duke said, "How many years of monastic seniority (*śrāmaṇera*) do you have?
He replied, "Forty-seven summer retreats. The Duke said, "How many summers has the Holy Monk attained? He replied, "He received the precepts simultaneously with empty space.
The Duke struck the head of the wooden board and said, "In eating rice, this subordinate official is not like the Head Seat in his consumption of salt."

The Chan Master Yuquan Chenghao was visited by the layman Zhang Gong, the "Inexhaustible One" (Wujin Jushi), who was on an official mission to the region south of the capital. He paid his respects and asked, "From whom did you receive the Dharma?
The Master replied, "From Master Guang of Beita in Fuzhou. The official said, "I would like to hear about your accord with him."
The Master said, "It is simply because he refuses to explain it through for others. The official (Yang Jie) appreciated these words.
Later, when a monk entered the room, a dog was inside. The Master gave a shout, and the dog immediately went out. The Master said:
The dog can do it, but you cannot.
One day, as the assembly gathered, the Master asked, "What are you doing? He replied, "Entering the room. The Master said, "Wait for me to finish relieving myself before you go."
When he returned from using the latrine, he saw that the monks had not left. He drove them away with his staff.
When he was about to pass away, his disciples gathered around him. The Master smiled and said, "I am eighty-one years old;
for my old death, they shall carry out a corpse. All you lads, exert yourselves together! Having said, "In one year there are three hundred and sixty days," he passed away.
Chan Master Da Jue Huailian of Yuyang was extremely strict in observing the Vinaya.
Emperor Renzong once presented him with a camphor incense bowl, but the Master burned it in the presence of the imperial messenger.
He said, "My teaching is to wear robes of ruined color and to eat from an earthenware bowl; this bowl is not according to the Dharma. Emperor Renmiao sighed in even greater admiration.
When the Master requested to return to the mountains from the capital, Emperor Yingzong issued a handwritten edict stating that he might reside as he pleased in any monastery he passed through.
The Master kept it hidden and did not show it to others. Dongpo composed the "Record of the Chenshui Pavilion" for the Master, wishing—
He saw it once, but the Master never brought it out again. Only after the Master’s passing did he find it within his chest. At the time of his passing, he was eighty-two years old.
This was Chan Master Fanchang Yiyu.
The Master went to visit Beichan. Beichan asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The Master said, "Fuyan. Beichan said, "How much longer is Sida’s nostrils?
The Master said, "They are exactly as they were when you first saw them, Master. Beichan said, "Tell me, how long were they when I saw them?
The Master said, "The Master seems to have never been to Fuyan. Beichan said, "You are merely repeating the words of others."
Liu asked again, "When you came, was Master Mazu well? The Master said, "He is well. Chán asked, "What did you say to him?
The Master said, "I told the Old Monk not to be so reckless. Chán said, "Out of consideration for you being a newcomer, I could not beat you.
The Master said, "I, too, let the Old Monk off. After the tea was finished, Chán asked, "Where is your native place? The Master said, [his name].
Zhangzhou. Zen Master [Xuefeng] asked, "What is Sanping doing there? The Master said, "He speaks of Chan and speaks of the Way.
Zen Master [Xuefeng] asked, "How old is he? The Master said, "He is the same age as the pillar. Zen Master [Xuefeng] asked, "As long as there is a pillar, let us leave it at that;
but when there is no pillar, how old is he? The Master said, "Even without a pillar, one year is not lacking. Zen Master [Xuefeng] said, "At midnight, releasing a black hen."
The Master had served Beichan for the longest time. When Ciming visited Beichan, the Master stood in attendance.
Beichan said, "Fenyang’s lion is truly fierce and terrifying. Ciming replied, "I do not say that those who come are bitten to death by it.

Beichan asked, "If this is indeed so, then has the Way been cut off at Fenyang’s gate, with no one remaining? Ciming raised his whisk and said, "Why has this thing reached until today? Beichan did not respond.
When they were facing each other, the Master said from the side, "Raising a son who does not equal his father brings a generation of decline to the family line.
Zenhe said, "What kind of eyes do you possess that you dare speak thus? The Master said, "If it were a man-eating lion, it would never act in such a way.
As Ming was about to leave, he went before the statue of Longya and pointed to it, asking the Master, "Whose image is this? The Master said, "It is the image of Longya. Ming said, "..."
"Since this is an image of Longya, why is it here at Beichan? The Master said, "Two colors, one match. Ming said, "The image is here; where is Longya?
As the Master was about to respond, Ming struck him with his palm and said, "Do not say you cannot bite people.
The Master said, "A beggar sees only small profit. Ming scolded him and drove him away.
While traveling to Mount Lu, he stayed at Yuan Tong. At that time, Master Da Jue Liaan was about to depart for the imperial court.

He took leave of the assembly, saying: "This matter is clear; you must realize it. Do not let yourselves undergo the cycle of rebirth for kalpas. The Master asked: "What is this matter? He replied: "..."
[The monk] offered his realization. The Master said, “Above the head is heaven; beneath the feet is earth. What do you realize?

He replied, “If it were not for one who knows, it would be a vain labor to speak of the cold of winter. The Master said, “Is there no expedient means? He replied, “A foreigner drinking milk, yet instead blaming the skilled physician.
The Master said, “Attacking tigers by force or leaping across a river—this is merely boasting of being a skilled hand. He gave a single clap and returned to the assembly.

While the Master was at Shuangling, he received an invitation from Fachang and took his leave of the two head seats, Ying and Sheng, saying: "We have been together for three years; there is nothing we do not know. Yet, when examined, there is no lack of leakage. He drew a line with his staff and said: [The two head seats asked: "What about this? The Master said: "I am leaving. They asked: "Where will you go? He replied: "To the place where there is no going. They asked: "How can one enter that place? He replied: "By means of the path of non-attainment. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'non-attainment'? He replied: "It is like a person who has lost their way. They asked: "If one loses their way, how can they find it again? He replied: "By following the tracks of others. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'following the tracks of others'? He replied: "It is like a person who has found their way. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'finding one's way'? He replied: "It is like a person who has reached their destination. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'reaching one's destination'? He replied: "It is like a person who has arrived home. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'arriving home'? He replied: "It is like a person who has sat down and rested. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'sitting down and resting'? He replied: "It is like a person who has opened their eyes. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'opening one's eyes'? He replied: "It is like a person who has seen the light. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'seeing the light'? He replied: "It is like a person who has heard the sound. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'hearing the sound'? He replied: "It is like a person who has smelled the fragrance. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'smelling the fragrance'? He replied: "It is like a person who has tasted the flavor. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'tasting the flavor'? He replied: "It is like a person who has touched the object. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'touching the object'? He replied: "It is like a person who has known the mind. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'knowing the mind'? He replied: "It is like a person who has realized the Way. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'realizing the Way'? He replied: "It is like a person who has attained liberation. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'attaining liberation'? He replied: "It is like a person who has entered Nirvana. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'entering Nirvana'? He replied: "It is like a person who has extinguished all suffering. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'extinguishing all suffering'? He replied: "It is like a person who has attained the ultimate peace. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'attaining ultimate peace'? He replied: "It is like a person who has returned to the source. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'returning to the source'? He replied: "It is like a person who has merged with the Great Void. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'merging with the Great Void'? He replied: "It is like a person who has become one with the Dharma-realm. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'becoming one with the Dharma-realm'? He replied: "It is like a person who has transcended all phenomena. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'transcending all phenomena'? He replied: "It is like a person who has realized the unborn nature. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'realizing the unborn nature'? He replied: "It is like a person who has attained the state of non-duality. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'attaining the state of non-duality'? He replied: "It is like a person who has entered the gate of the Great Vehicle. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'entering the gate of the Great Vehicle'? He replied: "It is like a person who has ascended the mountain of wisdom. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'ascending the mountain of wisdom'? He replied: "It is like a person who has gazed upon the ocean of reality. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'gazing upon the ocean of reality'? He replied: "It is like a person who has fathomed the depths of the Dharma-nature. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'fathoming the depths of the Dharma-nature'? He replied: "It is like a person who has attained the unconditioned. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'attaining the unconditioned'? He replied: "It is like a person who has realized the ultimate truth. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'realizing the ultimate truth'? He replied: "It is like a person who has attained the Great Enlightenment. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'attaining the Great Enlightenment'? He replied: "It is like a person who has become a Buddha. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'becoming a Buddha'? He replied: "It is like a person who has fulfilled all vows. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'fulfilling all vows'? He replied: "It is like a person who has benefited all sentient beings. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'benefiting all sentient beings'? He replied: "It is like a person who has brought peace to the world. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'bringing peace to the world'? He replied: "It is like a person who has established the True Dharma. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'establishing the True Dharma'? He replied: "It is like a person who has manifested the great compassion. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'manifesting the great compassion'? He replied: "It is like a person who has embraced all beings as oneself. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'embracing all beings as oneself'? He replied: "It is like a person who has realized the equality of self and other. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'realizing the equality of self and other'? He replied: "It is like a person who has transcended all dualistic views. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'transcending all dualistic views'? He replied: "It is like a person who has entered the realm of the Tathāgata. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'entering the realm of the Tathāgata'? He replied: "It is like a person who has attained the ultimate liberation. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'attaining the ultimate liberation'? He replied: "It is like a person who has realized the Great Nirvana. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'realizing the Great Nirvana'? He replied: "It is like a person who has returned to the source of all things. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'returning to the source of all things'? He replied: "It is like a person who has merged with the Great Void. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'merging with the Great Void'? He replied: "It is like a person who has become one with the Dharma-realm. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'becoming one with the Dharma-realm'? He replied: "It is like a person who has transcended all phenomena. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'transcending all phenomena'? He replied: "It is like a person who has realized the unborn nature. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'realizing the unborn nature'? He replied: "It is like a person who has attained the state of non-duality. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'attaining the state of non-duality'? He replied: "It is like a person who has entered the gate of the Great Vehicle. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'entering the gate of the Great Vehicle'? He replied: "It is like a person who has ascended the mountain of wisdom. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'ascending the mountain of wisdom'? He replied: "It is like a person who has gazed upon the ocean of reality. They asked: "What is the meaning of 'gazing upon the ocean
"Let us set this aside for now. As for the matter of the Gate of the Patriarchal School (Zongmen), what is it? Ying said, "Mount Sumeru is placed in the nostrils.
The Master said, "In that case, looking down from a cliff at the eyes on the shore—suddenly, a great deal of sorrow. Ying said, "Deep-Sandara (the Dragon King) rolls his eyes."
The Master said, "Alas, how can it be otherwise? There is no difference between the holy and the ordinary, yet there are many gates to the skillful means.

Ying said, "An iron snake cannot penetrate it. The Master said, "What common ground is there for conversation with a fellow such as this? Ying said, "It is simply because my own faculties are shallow; do not resent the springtime of the Great Sun.
He then drew a line and said, "Let us set aside the matters of the Zen school for a moment. As for this matter here—how is it? The Master [remained silent].
[The Master] struck him with his palm. Yingshan said, "This man from Zhangzhou—do you have no sense of propriety?
The Master said, "With a realization such as yours, when would I wait to strike you? [He] struck again. Yingshan said, "That too was brought about by this old monk."
After [the Master] had settled there, Fenyang Shanzhao went to the mountain to visit him. Fenyang said, "Master, you usually love to inspect the various quarters;
why do you come today to ply your trade in an old temple? The Master said, "I was merely beating the grass to startle the snake."
Ying said, "Do not try to plaster over people. The Master said, "And what are you doing thrusting your head into a vat of glue?
Ying said, "An ancient said, 'I see two clay oxen fighting their way into the sea,' and that is why I dwell on this mountain.
I wonder, what have you, Reverend, seen? The Master said, "In the future, when you have a thatched roof over your head, someone may—"
The Master asked, "How would you respond? Ying said, "The mountain peak is not as good as the foot of the ridge.
The Master said, "Tell me, are you fit to take charge of the affairs of this mountain? Ying said, "A pickaxe is no match for a plow.
The Master said, "Have you ever dreamed of the ancients? Ying said, "What about you, Master? The Master spread out both hands. Ying said, "A shrimp jumping."
"It does not come out of the measure. The Master said, "Cease trying to compare a three-inch candle to the brilliance of the sun. Ying said, "But how can you deny that the public case is right here?
The Master said, "Disciples of Zen who throw the lineage into chaos are as numerous as hemp and millet."
When Zen Master Foyin Yunju Liaoyuan was entering his room for instruction, Su Shi (Zi-zhan) happened to arrive. The Master said, "There is no place to sit here.
Su replied, "I shall temporarily borrow the four elements of Foyin as my seat. The Master said, "I have a question for you, Scholar; if you can answer it, you may take your seat."
"If you cannot explain it, you shall forfeit your jade belt. Su Xian joyfully requested instruction. The Master said, "The four great elements are fundamentally empty;
the five aggregates do not exist. Where, then, does the Layman sit? Su then presented the belt, and the Master gave him a single robe.

The Western Commandery Commander, Duke Wang Shao, considering his own karmic burden from taking life to be heavy, sought purification and requested that the Master preach the Dharma at Shanglan Monastery.
The Master lit incense and said, "This incense is for the General Who Kills Without Flinching and the Great Layman Who Attains Buddhahood on the Spot.
The assembly praised this as excellent, and Shao’s mind was likewise spontaneously relieved.
Chan Master Zhihai Yizheng was asked by a monk:
"What is it like when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished? The Master said: "The green grass by the riverbank. [The monk] asked: "What is it like after it has been polished?
The Master said: "The lush willows in the garden. [The monk] asked: "Are polishing and not polishing the same or different? The Master said: "The same."
"Set that aside for now; give me back my mirror. The monk hesitated, and the Master gave a shout. The Daoist asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "The dragon roars in the golden cauldron; the tiger sighs in the elixir field. He asked, "What is one who dwells within the Way?
The Master said, "Exhaling the old and inhaling the new. He asked, "How far apart are the Way and those who dwell within it?"
The Master said: "A crane caught in a snare atop a precipice;
soaring toward heaven, the common folk remain oblivious.
One day, while Master Zhi-feng of Huayan was sitting in meditative absorption within the Samantabhadra Hall, a divine being suddenly knelt before him. The Master—
He asked, "Who are you? He replied, "I am a deity who protects the precepts. The Master said, "I have a long-standing transgression that I have not yet eradicated;

do you know of it? He replied, "What sin does the Master have? It is merely a minor oversight. The Master asked, "What is it? He replied, "All water from a broken bowl is also the property of a donor.
Yet the Master habitually pours it out and discards it; this is not appropriate. Having finished speaking, he vanished. The Master [reflected upon this].
He drank all the water used for washing his alms bowl. After doing so for a long time, it caused him to contract a spleen ailment, which only healed after ten years.
At Shangfang on Mount Rui, he met Master An of the Tian Tai school and served him as his teacher.
There, while reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he reached the passage: "When one establishes cognition upon cognition, that is the root of ignorance. Regarding cognition...
"There is no seeing; this is itself nirvana. The Master then read it by breaking the phrasing: "When knowledge and seeing are established, that knowledge is the root of ignorance.
When knowledge and seeing are absent, seeing is itself nirvana. At this, he attained a realization. Someone said to the Master, "You have broken the phrasing.
The Master replied, "This is my place of awakening; I shall not change it for the rest of my life. At that time, he was called An Lengyan (An of the Śūraṅgama).
A monk asked Chan Master Yuanqi of Yantang, "When the night moon spreads its light, why is there no reflection in the azure pool? The Master said, "An adept playing with reflections."
The monk passed from east to west and stood there. The Master said, "Not only are you playing with shadows; you are also terrified of your own head.
Chan Master Yunju Daoqi and Damei Xu came to visit him. The Master asked, "Where have you come from? If you have come from the Sangha Hall, then you are deceiving me."
[Zhaozhou] said, "You have not come from the Sangha Hall; you are merely deceiving yourself. From where have you come? At these words, Mei attained sudden enlightenment.
This was Zen Master Zhidi Bianlong.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The majestic and sublime reality (dharmatā) fills the void; its adamantine essence is indestructible. Does the great assembly see it or not?

If you say you see it, yet the essence of reality fundamentally possesses no blue, yellow, red, or white, nor length, shortness, squareness, or roundness, and is not a phenomenon of seeing, hearing, sensing, or knowing—then how do you go about describing this act of seeing?"
[The Master said: "As for principle, if you say you do not see it, yet the Way is so lofty and its true reality fills all of empty space—why then do you not see it?
A monk asked, "What is the path that leads upward? The Master said, "That which is beneath your feet. The monk said, "In that case, I am constantly treading upon it.
The Master said, "Do not mistake it."
A monk asked Zen Master Chengzhi of Qixian on Mount Lu:
"The seer Vimalakṣa took Sudhana by the hand and saw as many Buddhas as atoms of dust.
But when he had not yet taken his hand, what did he see? The Master said: "What do you see now?"

The Master’s character was lofty and simple; he disciplined himself with rigorous strictness, never acting in violation of the laws of propriety. In his later years, he read the Tripitaka three times through.
Believing that reading while seated was not a mark of sufficient reverence, he would instead recite it while standing or walk while perusing the texts.

When Chan Master Nanyuan of Huanglong first traveled to seek instruction, he was still young, yet he followed the Master for many years; thus, much of what he did throughout his life was modeled after the Master’s example. He once said, "Qixian..."
The Master has surely come from among the humans and devas; he is a beacon for the monastic community.

When Chan Master Huanglong Huinan returned from his tour as a fundraising leader, he ascended the hall and said: "In this world there are five things that are not easy: first, the one who transforms others is not easy; second, the donor..."
Not easy. Third, it is not easy to transform the raw into the cooked. Fourth, it is not easy to eat while sitting upright.
What kind of person is there who is yet another kind of "not easy"? After a long silence, he said: "Aha! Then he descended from his seat.
The Master asked Cuiyan, "I have heard that you, the Head Seat, frequently use the story of the woman emerging from samādhi to teach people.
Is this true? Cuiyan said, "No. The Master said, "To be extravagant yet not frugal, or frugal yet not extravagant—why do you say 'no'?

Cuiyan said, "If one were a monk of genuine capacity, even salt and medicine could not suffice for him. The Master then turned his head and called to his attendant, "Inform the administrative official."
[The Master] sat. "Tomorrow, we shall simply cook white congee.
The Master’s demeanor was solemn and profound; throughout the monastic community, there were those who never saw him break into a smile during his entire life.
While residing at Jicui, one night while sitting in meditation, a light illuminated the room. He instructed his attendant not to speak of it. — Recorded by Fourth Patriarch Yan Chang.
The Old Master’s Letter to His Dharma Heirs. Entering the Hall: This mountain monk is of slight talent and meager virtue; how could he be worthy to serve as a teacher to others?
Yet, I am not ignorant of my own fundamental mind, nor do I deceive the sages. That which was unavoidable regarding birth and death, I have now avoided;

that which had not yet escaped saṃsāra, I have now escaped; that which was not yet attained as liberation, I have now attained; that which was not yet attained as mastery, I have now attained. Therefore—

The Great Awakened World-Honored One had not a single dharma to be attained at the place of Dīpaṃkara Buddha. What, then, was transmitted to the Sixth Patriarch at Huangmei in the middle of the night?
He spoke a verse, saying: "Attained or not attained, Transmitted or not transmitted— When one returns to the root and attains the essential meaning, what more is there to say?
I recall how Shoushan once let it slip: 'The daughter-in-law rides the donkey, while the mother-in-law leads.'"

When Chan Master Foyan Qingyuan (Yangqi Fanghui) was attending Chan Master Ciming’s formal lecture, the Master stepped forward and asked: "When a solitary bird warbles its song, leaving the clouds to enter the tangled peaks—what then?"
Foming said, "I am walking through the wild weeds; you, moreover, have entered a deep village. The Master said, "An official does not permit even a needle;
let me ask one more question. Foming then shouted. The Master said, "A fine shout! Foming shouted again, and the Master also shouted. Foming then shouted twice in succession.
The Master prostrated himself. Ming said, "This matter can only be shouldered by one who is a true person. The Master shook his sleeves and departed.
One day, Ciming asked the Master, "When Mazu saw Shurangama, he attained awakening immediately. Tell me, where did his delusion lie?
The Master replied, "To awaken is easy; to remain deluded is difficult."
He ascended the seat. At that time, a monk stepped forward. The Master said, "Before the old fisherman has cast his line, leaping scales surge forth upon the waves.
The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "I do not believe you. The monk clapped his hands and returned to the assembly. The Master said, "How much wind from the Dragon King can he endure?"
Question: "Whose tune does the Master sing? Whom does his lineage of the Dharma follow? The Master said: "If there is a horse, ride it; if there is no horse, walk. [The questioner] said:
"An elder with such youthful vigor possesses truly clever stratagems. The Master said: "Out of consideration for your advanced age, I grant you thirty blows of the staff.
Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "A three-legged donkey prances about on its hooves. [The questioner] said: "Is this not it? The Master said: "Do not mistake this for it."
"Is that so? The Master said, "Elder of Hunan. As the Master descended from his seat, the Venerable Jiufeng Qin seized him and said, "Today I am delighted to find a fellow practitioner.
The Master asked, "What is this matter of being a fellow practitioner? He replied, "Jiufeng plows the furrow; Yangqi drags the harrow.
The Master said, "At such a time as this, who is in front—Yangqi or Jiufeng? Qin... [remained silent].
[The assembly] was about to deliberate when the Master spread his hands apart and said, "I thought we were fellow practitioners; it turns out we are not.

At the memorial service for Ciming’s忌辰 (anniversary of death), as soon as the assembly had gathered, the Master placed both fists over his head before the portrait, drew a line with his sitting cloth (*zagu*), struck a circular mark, and then burned incense. Stepping back three paces, he assumed the posture of a woman.
The person bowed. The Head Seat said, "Stop making such a fuss. The Master said, "Head Seat, what do you say? The Head Seat said, "Master, stop making such a fuss.
The Master said, "A rabbit eating cow's milk. The Second Seat stepped forward, drew a circle, and then burned incense.

He also withdrew three paces and performed a woman’s bow. The Master stepped forward, assuming a posture of listening. As the Second Seat hesitated, the Master— *Note: The text provided ends abruptly with "師" (the Master), leaving the sentence incomplete.*
He gave the monk a slap and said, "This lacquer bucket is acting recklessly.
He then asked the monk, "The clouds are deep and the path is remote; from where have you come on such a grand carriage? The monk replied, "The heavens have no four walls.
The Master said, "How many straw sandals have you worn through? The monk then shouted. The Master said, "After one shout and two shouts, what then? The monk said, "Watch!"
The old monk was in a hurry. The Master said, "The staff is not here; sit for a while and drink some tea.
He then asked the visiting monk, "Amidst the clouds piled with fallen leaves, where did you depart this morning? The monk replied, "From Guanyin.
The Master said, "What do you say regarding the phrase beneath Guanyin’s heels? The monk replied, "I have already met him just now. The Master said, "As for that which has been met..."
"What is the matter? The monk had no reply. The Master said, "Let the second seat act as proxy for the head of the assembly and speak.
He also had no reply. The Master said, "Both have failed each other."
In the hall, the Master asked the monks, "How will you swallow the chestnut thorn? How will you penetrate the diamond circle? One day, seven newly arrived monks came;
the Master asked them, "The battle formation is complete; why do you veteran generals not come out from the ranks to meet Yangqi?
A monk struck him with his sitting cloth. The Master said, "A true adept. The monk struck again. The Master said, "..."
"One sitting mat. Two sitting mats. Again, the Master asked, "How about this? The monk hesitated. The Master turned his back and stood there. The monk struck him again.
The Master said, "Tell me, where does Yangqi’s *huatou* fall? The monk pointed to the space before him and said, "It is right here."
The Master said, "Thirty years from now, when you meet a person of clear eyes, do not fail to present this correctly. For now, sit and drink tea.
Chan Master Cuiyan Zhenji asked Chan Master Ciming, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master replied, "Cloudless, yet clouds arise upon the ridge; the moon exists, yet it sets."
Baixin looked at him with glaring eyes and shouted, "With hair white and teeth missing, you still hold such a view!
How will you ever escape birth and death? The Master was struck with awe and sought instruction. Baixin said, "Ask me. The Master repeated his previous words and questioned him.
Mingzhen shouted, "Cloudless, yet it rises above the peaks; the moon exists, yet it falls into the heart of the waves. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
He said to National Teacher Nan, "In the future, I shall become a master of gruel and rice at a crossroads. There was...
"The monk has come from Huangbo; I must certainly examine him. Master Nan said, "Why wait for another day?
I shall act as Huangbo’s monk; you may test him now. The Master then asked, "Where have you recently departed from? He replied, "Huangbo.

The Master said, "I have heard it said that the old man at the head of the hall does not touch the ground with his heels—is this true? He replied, "From where did you, Venerable One, receive such news?"
The Master said, "Someone has transmitted it here. Nanpu laughed and said, "It is actually you whose feet do not touch the ground.
The Master also laughed heartily and departed.

When Chan Master Lingyin Dezhang first resided at the West Sutra Repository Hall of the Great Xiangguo Monastery, Emperor Renzong summoned him to the Yanchun Pavilion for a meal and bestowed upon him the title of Grand Master Puzhao.
The Emperor asked, "What is the single phrase that strikes the vital point? The Master replied, "A single word transcends all."
"Beyond the blue heavens, walking on the precipice before the ten-thousand-fathom peak. [The Master] asked, "What is it like to walk on the precipice?
The Master then gave a shout. [The Master] said, "In the presence of the Emperor, how can you act like this?"
Later, he was again summoned to enter the Hua-cheng Hall for a vegetarian feast (*zhāi*). Xuanshou Xian asked, "The vegetarian banquet is now grandly opened;
how shall one repay the Sagely Ruler? The Master said, "Seeking bird tracks in the sky. He asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Seeking fish traces in the water."
A monk asked Chan Master Da’ning Daokuan, “If Kāśyapa possessed right view, why did he smile when the flower was presented? The Master said, “He could not restrain his impatience.”
Question: Since it is the one true Dharma-realm, why are there a thousand differences and ten thousand distinctions? The Master said: "The roots are deep and the leaves are lush. Question:
I do not know whether one can still transcend this or not. The Master said: "Seeking cleverness leads to clumsiness."
Cen Master Wuzhen Daowu addressed the assembly, citing Dongshan:
"On Mount Wutai, clouds steam rice; before the steps of the Buddha Hall, it is 'dog-urine-day'."
A fried cicada atop the tip of a banner-pole; three monkeys winnowing coins at night. I, the old monk, am not like this:
A three-faced wildcat treading on the moon; two white oxen grasping smoke in their hands; a crowned green hare standing upon the courtyard cypress.
"The shelled turtle has escaped and flown into the sky. Old monk, your complications have all been seen through by you all.
The old man Dongshan was truly extraordinary. Nevertheless, he could only manage three or four steps;
he did not go beyond seven jumps and eight leaps. Tell me, where does the crux lie? Today, this old monk will not begrudge [his life].
[The Master] raised his eyebrows. For a long while he remained silent, then said: "Excessive courtesy diminishes one's virtue; silence truly possesses merit.
Let the vast ocean change as it may, I shall never speak for you."
The Master was bedridden with illness. The head of the monastery asked him, “How is your health these days, Reverend? The Master said, “I have no strength for my morning gruel and evening rice.
After a long silence, he asked, “Do you understand? He replied, “I do not understand. The Master said, “A rat carries a grinding pestle on its tail.”
Several people arrived for the first time and performed prostrations. The Master said, "Are you all masters from Zhejiang?

The monk replied, "Monkeys warming themselves by the fire. The Master said, "Why are you jumping about? The monk said, "Today I have had the honor of meeting the Master. The Master said, "I pray that you may enjoy the offerings.
The monk was speechless, and the Master struck him.
The Master was in Ciming’s assembly. One day, he carried a basket of snails around the monastery, saying, "Selling snails," and challenged the assembly to offer a word.
None of them were in accord. An elderly veteran monk saw him as he lifted the curtain; he looked at the Master with his eyes and then threw himself down and lay there.
The Master immediately set down his basket and walked away.

A monk asked Chan Master Fang of Jiangshan in Yuezhou, "The rushing torrent passes the blade; the swift flame outruns the wind. I wonder, under the gate of Jiangshan, is it permitted to borrow [the Way] or not?
The Master said, "The sky is cold, the days are short, and the nights are even longer. The monk said, "An embroidered phoenix in a brocade curtain—passersby find it difficult to [penetrate]."

[The monk] said, “I have seen it. The Master said, “From within the skull, the vital breath gushes toward heaven. The monk called out, “Preceptor! The Master said, “The head of a rooster and the tail of a phoenix.
The monk said, “Everywhere else they wash in the mud; Jiangshan has brought forth a painting. The Master said, “Today Jiangshan is acting as a guest.”
"Furthermore, I hope that you, O Acharya, will transmit this well. Even so, one must not let it pass. Thereupon, he struck the meditation seat once.
Chan Master Tan of Xingjiao Monastery resided at Xingjiao;
the attendant from Xuedou, Shengzong, stepped forward and asked: "Before all Buddhas appeared in the world, every person..."
His nostrils reach to the heavens. After he has left the world, why is there no news at all? The Master said: "Before Chicken Foot Peak, the wind is still.
Zong said: "Not yet. Speak further. The Master said: "Great snow fills Chang'an. Zong said: "Who knows this meaning? It makes me remember Nanquan.
He shook his sleeves, returned to the assembly, and did not prostrate himself. The Master said: "Xin Xing."
The Master said, "Today I have lost the advantage. He then returned to his quarters and sent someone to invite Zong to come.
The Master said, "Just now I gave a wrong response to a single phrase. Why did you not prostrate yourself before the assembly of devas and humans?
You should have covered it over. Zong said, "A great man has gold beneath his knees; how could he deign to prostrate himself before an eyeless old monk? The Master said, "I have another saying."
Xuedou said, "This is the principle before words; it has not yet reached the ultimate. Try saying another word. Xuefeng said, "I have thirty blows to spare;
I entrust them to you to strike Xuedou. Xuedou bowed in prostration.

When Chan Master Jingduan of Xi Yu first met Master Nong, he realized the essential point of the mind. He later went to see Master Longhua and received his seal of approval, whereupon he returned to his hometown.
He stitched various colored fabrics together to create a lion skin, which he wore at that time; consequently, he was known as Duan Shizi (Lion Duan).

Chancellor Zhang Dun admired his Way and personally requested him to open the Dharma assembly. The transformative influence of his teachings spread extensively throughout Wushan. On the day he opened the hall:
Sengxuan read the preface. Before he had finished reciting the Lotus Sutra in its seven fascicles, the sound of a fisherman’s song was heard first.
The Master stopped him and then ascended the seat. After offering incense and making prayers for the Emperor, he raised his voice and chanted: "Originally, I am but a lone fisherman of Xiangxiang."

From the west and from the east, from the south and the north, the great assembly clamorously praised him. The Master looked at them and said with a smile, "Observe closely the Dharma of the Dharma King;
such is the Dharma of the Dharma King. He then descended from his seat.
One day, Chancellor Zhang invited the Master for a meal. The Master became angry and spoke this verse: "Zhang Dun, Zhang Dun!
You asked me to visit your grave, yet while I eat vegetarian food, you eat meat. Zhang Dun laughed heartily.
Furthermore, because Dun invited him for a meal, he was served wontons. The Master spoke in verse: "Fragrant wontons, plain wontons, Served in full bowls, swallowed whole.
Garbage passes right over the sandbar; The dragon palace and the ocean treasury are naturally clear."

When Shen Dun was summoned to court, he took his leave of the Master. The Master said, "For now, you must protect and cherish the Buddha-Dharma. Shen Dun replied, "Neither promoting nor abolishing—it is this that protects and cherishes the Buddha-Dharma.
The Master ordered an attendant to fetch some sugar to give to the Excellency for his journey. As Shen Dun was eating the sugar, the Master asked:
"Is it sweet? Dun replied, "Sweet. The Master said, "If it is sweet, then stay. Dun smiled and rose.
The Master arrived at Huating, where the assembly requested him to ascend the hall. "The lion of Vulture Peak roars in the clouds;
there is nothing to deliberate upon regarding the Buddha-dharma—better to perform a somersault," he said, and then descended from his seat.
Question: "What is it like when the pronghorn has not yet grown its antlers? The Master said: "I am afraid. The questioner said:
"Since you are a *kalyāṇamitra* (a spiritual friend), why are you afraid? The Master said: "I have never seen such a strange beast."
When the Master arrived south of Chang, he met Master Chao of Shangfang. A nun came to visit him, and the Master said, "Come back at the third watch of the fifth watch tomorrow morning.
Early the next morning, the Master sat with his face smeared with red powder. When the nun entered and saw him, she was struck with amazement and immediately attained enlightenment.
Chan Master Tianning Daokai went to Haihui to visit Master Touzi.
He asked, "The teachings of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are like the everyday tea and rice; apart from these, is there any other way to benefit people?
Touzi said, "You say that within the realm, the Emperor issues his decrees; do they still require [the authority of] the Dragon Throne?"

"Even Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang did not have it. As the Master was about to offer a word in response, the Master [Linji] struck the Master’s mouth with his whisk and said, "From the very moment you conceived this thought, you already deserved thirty blows. The Master immediately attained awakening; he prostrated twice and then departed.
The Master said, "Come here, Ācārya! The Master [Linji] did not look back. The Master said, "Have you reached the ground of non-doubt? The Master [Linji] covered his ears with his hands.

Later, he served as the kitchen steward (*dianzuo*). His attendant said, "The duties of the kitchen are not easy to manage. The Master said, "I am not afraid. The attendant asked, "Are you cooking porridge? Or steaming rice?
The Master said, "The laborers wash the rice and set the fires; the practitioners cook the porridge and steam the rice. The attendant said, "..."

"What are you doing? The Master said, "Out of compassion, Preceptor, let him go about in leisure. One day, while attending Touzi as they walked through the vegetable garden, Touzi passed his staff to the Master.
As soon as the Master received it, he continued walking along with him. Touzi said, "It is only right that it should be so."
The Master said, "Carrying the Master's sandals and holding his staff for him is not considered an extra burden. Zhaozhou said, "There is someone else traveling with us.
The Master said, "Which one does not accept the teaching? Zhaozhou withdrew. In the evening, Zhaozhou asked the Master, "The conversation from this morning was not yet finished.
The Master said, "Please, Master, bring it up. Zhaozhou said, "Born in the hour of the Rabbit; born in the month of the Dog. The Master immediately ordered a lamp to be lit.
The Master said, "Your coming up and going down has not been in vain. The Teacher said, "Being by the Master's side, it was only natural that I should act thus.
The Master said, "Who does not have servants and attendants in their own household? The Teacher said, "The Master is advanced in years;
we cannot do without him. The Master said, "To be so earnest! The Teacher said, "I shall have my share in repaying your kindness."
Addressing the assembly, he said briefly: "Now, those who have left the household life do so out of weariness with the toil of worldly dust and a desire to seek liberation from birth and death.
They rest the mind and cease discursive thought, severing all attachments to external conditions. Encountering sounds or forms, they are like flowers growing upon a stone;
encountering profit or fame, it is like grit in the eye. Since beginningless time, you have not failed to experience such things; why must you continue to cling to them with such bitter longing?"
If you do not rest now, when will you ever? If you can exhaust this very moment, what further matter remains?

If you attain a state where the mind is without affairs, even Buddhas and Patriarchs are but enemies; all worldly matters will naturally grow cool and detached, and only then will you correspond with that "other side.
Have you not seen how Yinyangshan refused to see anyone until his death, and how Zhaozhou refused to speak of it until his death?
Ren was a man who gathered acorns and chestnuts from a flat carrying pole for food; Damei used lotus leaves as clothing; the "Paper-Robed" Wayfarer wore nothing but paper;
and the Venerable Xuantai wore nothing but coarse cloth. Shishuang established a Hall of Withered Trees for people to sit and lie upon, intending only to kill your mind.
Touzi had his attendants prepare rice so that they might cook and eat together, intending to have you realize it through economy.
This is the matter. Furthermore, the various sages of the past have provided such precedents; if you possess no superior quality, how can you bear to remain as you are?
O worthy ones, if you investigate this thoroughly, you will certainly not fail others. If you are unwilling to take it up, I fear you will find it increasingly difficult in the future.
Today, I tell you all that our lineage has already lost its footing; how could it be otherwise?

You may go further to ascend the hall and enter the room; you may wield the mallet and brandish the whisk, knit your brows and glare with bated breath, or deliver blows to the east and shouts to the west—acting like one possessed by an epileptic seizure.
Yet have you not seen how Bodhidharma came from the West and sat facing a wall for nine years at Mount Shaoshi?
Or how the Second Patriarch went so far as to stand in the snow and sever his own arm? One could say they endured every hardship imaginable. Nevertheless, Bodhidharma never uttered a single word.
First, regarding his departure: the Second Patriarch never asked a single question. Could one call Bodhidharma "one who does not act for others"?
Could one call the Second Patriarch "one who does not seek a teacher"? Could either be said? Not at all.
When Chan Master Xuanben of Lingyin saw a monk reading a sutra, he asked, "What sutra are you reading? The monk was speechless. The Master then presented this verse:
Reading the sutras yet not knowing the sutra, In vain you labor and damage your eyes. If you wish not to damage your eyes, Clearly discern the sutra.
Chan Master Yuanzhao, the founder of the Huelin lineage, was held in the highest esteem by Emperor Shen宗.
Once, the Emperor summoned him for an audience; the Master remained composed and natural, showing neither agitation nor change. On the day he departed from the capital, [the Emperor]...
As princes, dukes, and nobles escorted him, their carriages and cavalry followed one after another. The Master instructed them, saying, "The months and years cannot be toyed with;

old age and sickness do not wait for man's appointment. Strive only in diligent cultivation without indolence; this is what truly constitutes being a 'true companion' (zhenxiang). Those who heard this were moved without exception.
Chan Master Changlu Yingfu ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying:
"The rivers and mountains wind around the balustrade, as if they were a screen of ink and water; the halls and pavilions soar into the void, as magnificent as the grotto-heavens of the immortals.
The myriad phenomena of the forested universe interpenetrate with the ocean-seal [samādhi], and a single path of divine radiance remains entirely unobstructed."
[Obstruction. "Do you all understand? After a long silence, he said: "In the vast expanse of heaven and earth, standing alone, what limit does one gaze toward?
[End of session. Chan Master Furi Zhicai ascended the hall and said:
"The city is bustling and chaotic; the empty mountains are silent and still. Even so, movement and stillness are as one, as are life and death."
Non-dual. The four seasons revolve; the nature of things remains serene. Summer does not depart, yet autumn comes of its own accord;
the wind is not cool, yet people naturally feel refreshed. Now as then, there has been no change by even a hair’s breadth. Who is less, who is more? The body has no dual function.
Virtuous practitioners of dhyāna, since the body has no dual functions, why did the Dragon Girl manifest the eighteen transformations?
Have you not seen that to play in the tide, one must be a master of the tide? Take care!
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The wind and rain howl and rustle, blocking your faculty of hearing. Falling leaves swirl together, blocking your faculty of sight.
Fragrances and stenches mingle in confusion, blocking your faculty of smell. Cold, heat, bitterness, and sweetness, block your faculty of taste.

The warmth and cold of cotton garments block your faculty of touch. Upside-down delusive thoughts block your faculty of mind. O practitioners of Zen, even if you were able to turn these all upside down—"
This is a pile of bones on level ground. *Paṃ*.
Entering the hall, he raised the story of the "Pine Tree. The Master said: "Zhaozhou’s courtyard pine was told to the Chan guests;
it is a black-lacquered screen, with the pine needles providing a bright partition."
Master Kaisheng Qi opened the hall for his inaugural sermon. He delivered this statement: "The field for selecting Buddhas is now open; gods and humans are gathered here in universal assembly.

Is there anyone who has long traversed the field of awakening—a guest who has finished their study of Chan—who will come forward to meet me? At that time, a monk stepped forth. The Master said, "A master! A master! The monk replied, "Do not..."
[The monk] was in a great hurry. The Master said, "So, you are not a master after all. The monk held up his sitting cloth and said, "Look, look!
In the kingdom of Magadha, this edict was personally issued. The Master said, "How is it now? The monk bowed. The Master said, "A dragon’s head and a snake’s tail."

Chan Master Fashou of Fayun Temple studied the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*, the *Awakening of Faith*, and the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*. He had attained a subtle mastery of their profound meanings, yet he harbored considerable doubts regarding the Chan school.

Upon hearing of the flourishing reputation of Master Huai’s Dharma assembly, he went directly to pay his respects. Master Huai asked, "What sūtras does the Preceptor lecture upon? The Master replied, "The *Avataṃsaka*. [Master Huai] said, "The *Avataṃsaka*..."
Yan asked, "What is the primary tenet? The Master said, "The Dharma-realm is the primary tenet. He asked, "What is the primary tenet of the Dharma-realm? The Master said, "Mind is the primary tenet.
He asked, "What is the primary tenet of mind? The Master had no reply. Huai said, "A difference of a hair's breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth.
You must examine this for yourself; you will surely achieve enlightenment. Later, he heard a monk recount the story of Baimiao’s visit to Baoci.
"When feeling has not yet arisen, what is it like? Miaozi replied, "Separated. Thereupon, the Master attained great enlightenment.
He resided at Changlu in Zhenzhou with a community of over a thousand people. When the Elder of Quanpao arrived and ascended the seat, the assembly looked on and laughed at him.
No one came forward to ask a question. The Master stepped forward, bowed, and hurriedly asked, "What is the self of Fa-xiu?

Jiao laughed and said, "Fa-xiu, with his iron face, does not even recognize his own self? The Master replied, "Those who occupy the position are deluded. The entire assembly marveled at his resolve to uphold the Dharma.
The Elder Fú of Chánglú’s eye of the Way was not clear. He constantly took the offerings he received and transported them by boat upriver to provide meals for monks.
