When the Master heard of this, he went to examine whether it was true or false. Upon his arrival, he saw Fú ascending the hall and saying: "Entering a desolate field without discrimination—how utterly reckless!
Picking up whatever grass comes to hand—there is still a bit more to it. Having said this, he descended from the seat. The Master was greatly [impressed].
Fengxue was startled and said, "To speak of Chan in this way—who would say you do not understand it? You are merely referring to the arising and ceasing found everywhere.

He then went in person to the abbot’s quarters to pay his respects and recounted the previous events in detail, further requesting instruction on the words of the formal teaching. Fuyuan explained the meaning according to the text.
The Master said, "If that were so, then people everywhere would not have idly said that you do not understand Chan. Fuyuan did not accept this. The Master said:
"Please strike the bell to assemble the community. There is the Elder Fashou here who will attend to matters with the Upādhyāya.

Fuhui then departed. Li Boshi was skilled at painting horses. The Master rebuked him, saying, "You are a scholar-official who has gained fame through painting; moreover, you paint horses hoping for people to praise your excellence.
To have such mastery as to enter the belly of a horse—this is truly enough to be feared! Thereupon, Boshi ceased his brushwork. The Master thus exhorted him.
He painted an image of Avalokiteśvara to atone for his transgressions. Huang鲁直 (Huang Tingjian) was skilled in writing erotic lyrics (*yanci*);

the Master likewise rebuked and scolded him for this. Huang laughed and said, "Will you now place me in the belly of a horse? The Master replied, "You stir up the lustful hearts of people throughout the world with your erotic words;
it will not end with the belly of a horse—I fear you will actually be born in the *niraya* hells. Huang stood in awe and apologized, thereafter exerting himself with diligence to seek the Way.

The Minister of Rites, Yang Jie, the Layman of Non-Action (Wuwei Jushi), traveled extensively to study under various renowned masters. In his later years, he followed Tianyi, who frequently cited the kōans and sayings of the elder Pang, urging him to investigate them deeply and reach profound realization.
Later, while serving as a shrine official at Mount Tai, one day at the first crowing of the cock, he beheld the sun rising like a great platter; suddenly, [a great awakening occurred].
Wu then composed a verse in parting for Old Pang, saying: "When a man grows old, he must marry; when a woman grows old, she must wed.
What leisure do you have to further discourse on the talk of non-arising? He sent this with a robe, and Pang praised it as excellent.
He met Chan Master Furong Kai. The Official asked, "How many years has it been since we parted? Furong said, "Seven years. The Official asked, "Have you been practicing the Way?

Have you been studying Zen? Furong said, "I have not been playing these drums and pipes. The Official said, "In that case, you have been wandering idly through mountains and waters, capable of nothing at all.
Furong said, "It has not been long since we parted, yet you are well able to discern with such high insight. The Official laughed heartily.

The Master had a verse for departing this world which said: "There is nothing to be attached to; there is nothing to be abandoned. In the vast void of space, 'zhi-hu-ye-zhe' (the particles of discourse).
Taking what was mistaken as correct, I go to the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss."
Chan Master Ciyun Hui ascended the hall and said:
"A sliver of moon reflects in the cold pool; a faint cloud fills the azure sky. For one who has attained the Way, this is a truly excellent message.
Is there anyone here who has attained the Way? A faint cloud pierces through your skull; a sliver of moon strikes you."
The nostrils. Be careful.

Master Huitang Zuixin of Huanglong, a Chan master, said that the layman Wu Dunfu claimed to have seen many spiritual friends and that his mind-ground was clear and pure. One day, while casually reading about Deng Yinpeng...
The Record relates: [Dongshan] saw [his robe] stand upright and transform away, yet the garment remained aligned with his body without slipping off.
Suddenly, he wondered: "That transformation was extraordinary and thus unfathomable; but why did the robe also conform to it? He asked the Master about this.

The Master said, "Now that your robe hangs down to the ground in conformity, do you still have doubts? Dongshan replied, "I have no doubts. The Master laughed and said, "Since there are no doubts here—"
"In that case, even a transformed garment worn upside down would fit the body; what room for doubt is there? Under these words, Dunfu attained awakening.
The Master then went to see Chan Master Yu at Fachang. Yu asked, "I have heard that you, Master, have completed the construction of a grass hall;
is the work finished? The Master said, "It is finished. Yu asked, "How many laborers were used? The Master said, "Only a few hundred laborers. Yu said angrily, "Great..."
"Fine, Cao Tang. The Master clapped his hands and laughed, saying, "This is merely intended to cause all people in the world to harbor doubt.
On the day Master Nan passed away, he composed a verse: "The person who departed in the past departs this very day; The person of today does not come as before.
Since the present one does not come and the past one has not gone, White clouds and flowing waters wander in vain. Who?
The scale and the ruler are said to be level; yet within the straight, there is still the curved. Who says that the principles of things are uniform? Planting hemp, one still harvests millet.
Piteous are those who rush about throughout the world; six times six is originally thirty-six.
Chan Master Jingning Kewen Baofeng sat out the summer retreat at Daguai.
When he heard the story of a monk asking Yunmen, "Is it true that the Buddha-dharma is like the moon in the water?

Yunmen replied, "In the clear waves, there is no path through. At this, the Master attained realization. He then went to see Huanglong, but they did not reach accord; instead, Huanglong said, "I have..."
"It is a good thing that this old fellow does not recognize me. He then went to Xiangcheng to see Master Shun.
Shun asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "From Huanglong. Shun asked, "What sayings or phrases has Huanglong been teaching lately?

The Master said, "Recently, the local government commissioned the Elder of Huangbo to take over Huanglong. Huanglong gave a turning word, saying: 'Reciting hymns on the bell tower; the legs of the bed...'"

Xiazhong Cai was testing someone for a phrase that would accord with the truth. When that person spoke a phrase that hit the mark, he went to the abbot, Sheng Shangzuo, and said, "A fierce tiger sits in the middle of the road.
Longshu then ordered him to go and reside at Huangbo. Shun Buque remarked, "Sheng Shangzuo only managed to utter a single turning word, yet he immediately secured Huangbo’s residence;
he has not even dreamed of the Buddha-dharma. Upon hearing these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. Only then—

Realizing that this was Huanglong’s pedagogical maneuver, the Master turned back and saw Huanglong. Huanglong asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "I have come specifically to pay my respects to the Master.
Huanglong said, "It happens that I am not here at present. The Master asked, "Where have you gone? Huanglong replied, "To Tiantai for a communal work assignment; to Nanyue."
While traveling in the mountains, the Master said, "In that case, this student has attained mastery. Yunlong said, "Where did you get those shoes on your feet?
The Master replied, "I bought them for seven hundred and fifty cash at Mount Lu. Yunlong said, "When have you ever attained mastery?
Pointing to his shoes, the Master said, "When have they not been masterful? Yunlong marveled at this.
One day, Long said, "Just now I ordered an attendant to roll up the curtain and asked him, 'When the curtain is rolled up, what is it like?

He replied, 'It illuminates the whole world. I asked, 'When the curtain is let down, what is it like? He replied, 'Not a drop of water can leak through. I asked, 'What is it like when it is neither rolled up nor let down?
The attendant was speechless. What would you have done? The Master said, "The Abbot should take the attendant down to the Nirvana Hall."
[Longtan] finally attained it. Longtan exclaimed, "The people of Guansi truly have no brains! He then looked toward a monk standing nearby.
The Master pointed at him and said, "Even this monk has not yet seen a dream. Longtan laughed heartily.
The Master asked the lecturer, "When the calamity of fire arises and the mountains, rivers, and great earth are all consumed by flames, do the world and empty space also perish?
The lecturer replied, "The scriptures contain clear explanations; how could there be any reason for this not to be so? The Master said, "Where would you place all these ashes?
The lecturer laughed and said, "I do not know. The Master also laughed and said, "What you have been lecturing on is merely ink upon paper."
It is merely a matter of speech.
Liu Yi’ung once studied under Foyin and was quite conceited. One day, upon seeing the Master, he asked, "For how many years have you been performing plays, Elder?
The Master said, "I am waiting specifically for the musicians to arrive. Liu said, "I do not enter this association. The Master said, "..."
"But alas, you are right here in this very assembly! Liu hesitated. The Master clapped his hands and said, "A frog’s Zen can only leap once.
Again, while sitting, Liu pointed to his Zen robe and asked, "What do you call this? The Master replied, "Zen robe."
[The monk] asked, "What is Chan? The Master then shook his robes and said, "I cannot shake them off. Liu was speechless.
The Master gave him a blow and said, "Your skill is such as this; how dare you test an old monk like me?"
Langzhong Qian Yi visited the Master. After they had conversed for a long time, Qian went to the toilet. The Master instructed an attendant to lead him out from the west side.
Qian suddenly asked, "Since this is the 'eastern office' (toilet), why go toward the west? The Master said, "How many people seek it toward the east?
When the Master went to report his visit, Qian’s mastiff escaped. The Master avoided it, and Qian teased him, saying, "This is the instruction of a Chan practitioner!"
"Are dragons and tigers afraid of dogs? The Master replied at once: "Tigers in secluded ravines are easy to subdue; dragons guarding the residence are difficult to bring down.
Qian praised this.
The various mountains of Nankang were gathered together when Foyin arrived late. The Master asked, "Why have you come so late from Yunju?
He replied, "I was wearing straw sandals and passing through the belly of Guizong; that is why I am late. The Master said, "In that case, you have been swallowed by Guizong."
[The monk] said, "Alas, I cannot bring myself to spit it out. The Master said, "If you cannot spit it out, then defecate it!
A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Master Baogong said: 'If you wish to seek the Buddha-way with the mind, ask the void;
only then will you emerge from the dust. Now that you seek the Buddha-way, what does the void say to you? At this, the monk...
He attained great enlightenment upon hearing these words.

A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master laughed loudly. The monk said, "Why do you laugh? The Master replied, "I laugh at you for following after words and giving rise to intellectual interpretations.
The monk said, "I have simply met with an unexpected setback. The Master shouted, "Do not prostrate yourself! The monk then returned to the assembly.
The Master laughed again and said, "To produce understanding based on words.
A monk asked, "Suppose there is one person wishing to leave Chang’an and another person wishing to enter Chang’an; which of them comes first?
The Master said, "How many people have been puzzled by this? The monk said, "Night travel is not permitted. The Master said, "A mosquito piercing iron."
“Ox,” he said. [The Master continued: “An old monkey cries in the ancient trees atop the mountain; new geese descend onto the level sands at the riverhead.
The Master said, “The people of Chang’an have already entered [the city]. What do you intend to do? He replied, “On a spring day, Mount Hua is green.
The Master said, “Although this monk is young, he is indeed one with whom it is worth deliberating.”
A monk asked, "The Great Master Yunmen wished to strike old Śākyamuni to death with a single staff;
you, Master, now wish to bury Yunmen alive in a heap of refuse. I wonder, Master, do you permit this student to examine your transgressions?
The Master said, "Do not be so hasty. The monk said, "Master, you sit and block off Mount Lu; why then do you not recognize me?"
Jiā said this. The Master said, "Thirty blows. Jiā said, "Guān. The Master said, "Diǎn. Jiā said, "Zhá. The Master said, "I shall spare you because you work as a street vendor."
In the master’s room, he asked a monk, "Have you finished yet? The monk said, "Not yet. The master said, "Have you finished eating your congee yet?
The monk said, "Yes, I have. The master said, "Then why do you say not yet? He asked again, "What sound is that outside the door?
The monk said, "The sound of rain. The master said, "Then why do you say not yet? He asked again, "What is that in front of you? The monk said, "A screen. The master said, "..."

Furthermore, the Way is not yet fully realized. He asked again, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. He then said, "Listen to this verse: 'In accordance with conditions, every matter is complete;
In daily life, what is lacking? All things are simply ordinary; Naturally, there is no inversion.'"
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The trousers have no crotch; the breeches have no opening. Three or five pecks of green ash upon the head—Old Zhaozhou has little left to show off.
Yet, 'In the state of Guoqing, the talented are noble; when a family is wealthy, the children are arrogant. Alas!
While the grain does not flourish in the sunlight, they compete to plant peach and plum trees in spring. This causes those who toil at the plow to become, for the most part, flower-sellers."
Chan Master Qingxian of Longqingsi served under Huanglong, who held him in high esteem. At that time, he was at Huangbo together with Cuiyan Shun.
Shun frequently interrogated the Master, and the Master responded with such spontaneous and unyielding wit that Shun said to Huanglong, "Xian is arrogant and reckless; moreover, his speech..."
He had not yet distinguished between contact and purity. Long said, "The Dharma should be thus; it is by seeking it through the emotions that right and wrong are created.
Once the Dragon had crossed the Double Peaks, the Master went to visit him. The Dragon asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "Baiyang. The Dragon asked, "When did you leave there?"
The Master said, "The thirteenth day of the first month. Long said, "My heels ache terribly; give me thirty blows! The Master said, "Not merely thirty blows.
Long shouted, "After traveling on foot for so long, you have not a breath of spirit left! The Master said, "Even the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas are just like this.
Long said, "You come here in such a manner; when have you ever reached the realm of the Buddhas by even a hair’s breadth?"
Jie asked, "The Buddhas have not necessarily reached the realm of Qingshan. Longshu followed up by asking, "What is your place of birth?
The Master said, "In the morning I ate white congee; now I feel hungry again. [Longshu] asked, "How is my hand like a Buddha’s hand?
The Master said, "Playing the lute under the moon. He asked, "How are my feet like a donkey’s feet? The Master said, "A heron standing [in the snow]."
The snow was not of the same color. The Dragon gazed at him with a sigh and asked, "Having shaved off your hair and beard, for what purpose do you do this?
The Master said, "I simply desire to be without affairs. The Dragon said, "If you have no affairs, why is it necessary to shave your hair? The Master said, "If I did not shave my hair..."
"How can one know there is nothing? [The monk] said, "In that case, 'A few clear strokes of the chime are beyond right and wrong;
a single idle man dwells within heaven and earth. The Master said, "What words are these? [The monk] said, "A sharp and clever patch-robed monk. The Master said, "That too will not do."
Long gave a shout. The Master clapped his hands once. Long shouted again. The Master then departed. Later, while serving him, Long said, "There is a Venerable Bian here;
you must be on your guard. The Master asked, "What excellence does he have? Long said, "If he were to pat your back once, what would you do?
The Master asked, "What would happen then? Long said, "He would extend both hands. The Master said, "How extraordinary!"
"Where have you been studying this empty pretense? Long laughed. The Master then spread out both hands. Long gave a shout. The Master then departed.
After the midday meal, he again stood in attendance. Long asked, "Loose and relaxed, the two of us sharing one bowl—how do you understand this?
The Master said, "A hundred fragments. Long said, "The entire earth is a single Mount Sumeru. If you were to pick it up in the palm of your hand, what would you do?"
"How do you understand this? The Master said, "A double case. [The guest] said, "Here, I may speak as I please in barbarian tongues or Chinese;
but when I reach Tong’an, how will I pass through? The Master said, "He too must reach such a state before he can succeed.
[The guest] said, "Suppose he suddenly points to the brazier and says, 'This is a black-lacquered brazier; that is a black-lacquered incense table.'"
"Where is the place that cannot be reached? The Master said, "Right here before me. Let us speak in this manner for now;
were it anyone else, they would laugh at the Abbot. Long struck once, and the Master then gave a shout. The next day, they went together to inspect the monks' hall. The Master said:
"Fine Sangha Hall," [someone] said. The Master said, "Excellent workmanship. [The person] asked, "In what way is it excellent? The Master said, "One beam supports one pillar.
[The person] said, "This is not the point of excellence. The Master asked, "And how about you, Preceptor? Long (the Master) pointed with his finger and said:
"This pillar is so round; that beam is so flat. The Master said, "A great spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) of humans and devas must be you, Reverend.
He then departed. As he was leaving the hall, Long said, "Just now, when you spoke like that, did you accept me or reject me?
The Master said, "If it were like that, how could I ever have attained a place of peace and happiness? The Master then went to the abbot’s quarters to pay his respects.
Long said, "According to your understanding and views, you have only attained the beginning, but not the end. The Master said, "I can attain both the beginning and the end.
Long asked, "What is the beginning? The Master said, "When the wind passes, the tree-tops sway. Long asked, "And what is the end? The Master said, "When the wind passes, the tree-tops sway."
"What is the 'end'? The Master said, "A blow from a blade or a strike from an axe. Long said, "I am not like that, old monk. The Master asked, "What is the 'beginning'?
He replied, "The hair is disheveled; the ears stick out. [The Master] asked, "What is the 'end'? He replied, "Tightening the straw sandals.
The Master said, "Thank you for answering my question. Long then gave a shout. The next day, while standing in attendance, Long asked, "Have you attained the seat? (or: "Have you gained the seat?")

[The Master] put on his robe. [The student] asked, "What provision is there for what comes after? The Master said, "When encountering a square, it is square; when encountering a circle, it is circular.
[The student] said, "Speaking like that, you still have lips and teeth. The Master said, "Qingxian, it is so. But how about you, Master?
[The student] said, "Come closer, and I will tell you. The Master clapped his hands and said, "That which you have used for thirty years—today I have caught it!"
Bai laughed loudly and said, "They are all equally spirits. The Master then shook out his sleeves and departed. From this point on, students vied with one another to seek him out.
This was Zen Master Hetan Hongying.
A monk rose from his prostrations and, letting down a corner of his *kāṣāya*, asked: "What is it like when one strips off the robes and discards the armor?
The Master said: "Fortunately, the smoke of war has subsided; the bow-tips hang suspended on the wall. The monk then pulled up his *kāṣāya* and asked:
"What is it like when one readjusts the robes and armor? The Master said: "Had you not reached the banks of the Wu River, I would have known you were unwilling to cease. The monk then gave a shout.
The Master said, "I am terrified! The monk gave a clap. The Master said, "This too is finding life within death. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "I thought you were one with the talent to capture Yan and break Zhao; it turns out you are just a smuggler of salt."
Chan Master Shun of Shuangling asked, "The Master in the hermitage likes to ask scholars to 'shut their throats, lips, and mouths' and speak a single phrase.
Has the Head Seat ever spoken such a phrase? The Master gave a dry laugh. Later, he composed a verse: "The mother-in-law tastes the vinegar; three-foot-long beak.
The daughter-in-law washes her face and touches her nose. Daowu’s response gained him his waist-cloth. Xuán.
Sha Kai opened the letter; it was blank white paper. Master Shun submitted in defeat.
Huangbo Jicui asked the Abbot of Yong’an, “Master, I have not seen you for a long time; what have you been doing? Qi replied, “I saw that there was something with Librarian Wei.”
"At the Anle (Peaceful Bliss) Hermitage," [Qiji] said. The Master said, "Report this to me. Qiji recounted what he had attained. The Master said, "You are right; Wei is not yet right.
Qiji was unable to fathom this and told it to Wei. Wei said, "You are wrong; it is forever not wrong. Qiji went to Jicui to verify this with Master Nan.

Nan also laughed loudly. When the Master heard this, he composed a verse, saying: "Light and darkness intermingled—the mechanism of killing and enlivening. This is the realm of the Great Man, known by Samantabhadra.
Born from the same root, yet dying on different branches; the old master in the hermitage is made to laugh to his heart's content."
Chan Master Baoyun Shouduan went to study under Yangqi.
One day, Yangqi suddenly asked him, "Who is your preceptor? The Master replied, "Venerable Yuru of Chaling.
Yangqi said, "I have heard that he had an awakening while falling over a bridge and composed a remarkably wondrous verse about it. Can you recite it? The Master [recited it].
He recited: "I have a bright pearl; for a long time it has been locked away by the dust of worldly toil.

Today the dust is cleared and its light shines forth, piercing through the myriad peaks of mountains and rivers. Qixi rose and hurried away with a smile, leaving the Master staring in astonishment. He did not sleep all night, and at dawn—
He consulted him about this. It happened to be the end of the year. Xiangqi said, "Did you see those who were performing the *dagu nuo* exorcism yesterday?
The Master replied, "I saw them. Xiangqi said, "In one stroke, you are not their equal. The Master was again startled and asked, "What do you mean? Xiangqi said, "They love being laughed at."

"You fear being ridiculed by others. The Master attained great enlightenment and addressed the assembly: "Clearly and vividly we know it is only this very thing. Why, then, do we fail to penetrate it?
It is simply because when we see someone open their mouth, we call it 'words and phrases'; and when we see someone close their mouth, we call it 'a long silence.'"

Furthermore, it is said that movement and activity constitute the manifestation of practice; opening one’s mouth and exhaling breath, there is nothing within the entirety of the ten directions that is not oneself.
Thus, one falls into the midst of the mundane path, still harboring a lingering resentment as if toward something recent. Have you not seen Yunmen say:
"Awakening to the Way by hearing sounds; clarifying the mind by seeing forms. He then raised his hand and said, "Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, bring money to buy some sesame cakes.
Lowering his hand, he said, "It turns out it was actually steamed buns. Furthermore, have you not seen when I was at Fahua, where I once addressed the assembly, saying:
"Master Wuye said that so long as even a hair’s breadth of thoughts regarding holiness or ordinariness has not been exhausted..."

"You cannot avoid entering the womb of a donkey or a horse. Great assembly, even if you were to suddenly exhaust all saintly and mundane thoughts upon a single hair-tip, you still could not avoid entering the womb of a donkey or a horse. You blind fellows! Just look in this way. *Chan* (Investigate)."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "This matter is like being atop a ten-thousand-fathom cliff;

everyone knows that if one lets go of the hand, one will plunge to the bottom, yet none can bear to give up their life. Today, Fahua, without moving a single hair’s breadth, shall cause you all to reach the bottom.
He threw down his staff and descended from the seat.

Chan Master Renyong of Baoning was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "That which is near the fire is scorched first. The monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "There are thorns in the mud.
The monk asked, "What is one who walks the Way? The Master said, "Be careful not to tread upon them."
Ascending the hall, he said: "It has hands and feet, yet it has no front or back; those with clear eyes cannot see it. Heaven revolves to the left, and earth turns to the right.
He struck his knee and said: "A gust of west wind comes, and two or three leaves fall."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The Old Śākyamuni preached the Dharma for forty-nine years, yet never uttered a single word.
Upagupta’s room was filled with counting sticks, yet he never ordained a single person. Bodhidharma did not dwell at Shaoshi; the Sixth Patriarch did not reside at Caoxi.
Since they themselves have no sores, do not wound them. He patted his knee and looked at the assembly, saying: "How joyful!"
"The world will attain great peace.
The Master said, "One is one, two is two, three is three, four is four; the numbers are very distinct.
Above and below follow the order of seniority. Following the order of seniority—what business is there? [He drew a line with his staff and said: 'The assembly, one!'"
At that time, sixty sexagenary cycles have already passed.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The three realms are but mind; the myriad dharmas are but consciousness. Clouds arise beyond the railing; raindrops fall before the eaves.
The mountain stream is as clear as indigo; the mountain flowers bloom like brocade. If you do not investigate the source at this moment, you must wait for the future."
He asked Maitreya, "The layman Sun of the Bi family came to visit me recently from Yangqi.
He happened to arrive while I was presiding over a legal case. The man said, 'I am bound by the affairs of the king; how can I escape them?'"
Nan asked, "Can you fully comprehend this? Pointing with his finger, he said, "Have you grasped it thoroughly? The scholar said, "I hope the Master will point it out for me.
Nan said, "This is the profound and vast vow of Bi-bu (the Minister of Justice) to benefit all living beings. The scholar said, "I do not yet understand how this is so. Nan showed him with a verse:

"Manifesting in the body of a civil official, He widely propagates his compassionate vows, deep and vast. Where he points with gravity for the sake of others, Under the blow of the staff, blood flows profusely. The scholar... [remained silent].
At this point, there was an awakening.

This consists of five sets of Dharma talks by Chan Master Weizhao of Baofeng, titled "Instructions for Librarian Cong," the first of which states: "Caoshan established four prohibitions that exhaust the very life-vein of the patch-robed monks."
If you have penetrated through this, you must strictly avoid relying on it. Those who intend to settle the matter in the future must necessarily possess a separate path of vital energy. Second:
"A patch-robed monk walks among the heterodox; the ancients said that falling into the heterodox is the sickness of one who has settled the matter."
Ming’an said: “One must recognize the master before one can succeed. The third [case] says: Chantideva (Chandé) habitually told people, “You may not practice Chan;

you may not study the Buddha. You simply must be like a great dead man. He feared that upon hearing these words, people would take them as meaning there is nothing to do, or that there is no dharma to accord with the mind.
This is precisely what it means to be unable to die. If one were truly able to die, one certainly would not [understand it in such a way].
If you are willing to hold such a view, you must be extremely careful when acting on behalf of others in the future. Fourth: Our school establishes the five ranks as its fundamental principle.

Yet, people often clarify them through phenomena and principle, comprehend them through stillness and illumination, perceive them through subject and object, or understand them through essence and function;
thus they fall entirely into the realm of the present moment. How can this be called the wondrousness of the "special transmission outside the teachings"? It is merely a path toward birth and death.
"What is that place of attainment? When nothing at all is like this, how can one attempt to fathom it? It will not suffice. The fifth [case] says:
"Because there is sentient being, there is the leakage of sentiment; because there is seeing, there is the leakage of vision; because there is speech, there is the leakage of words.
Even if you were to attain the absence of seeing, the absence of sentiment, and the absence of speech—if someone were to grab you by the collar and ask, 'Who are you?'—[how would you respond?]"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddhas of the past have already entered nirvana; you people should not dwell upon them with longing remembrance.
The Buddhas of the future have not yet appeared in the world; you people must not engage in idle conceptualization. It is precisely this very day."
"Who are you? [The Master] ascends the hall and says: "Fundamentally unborn, now likewise without extinction—this is the pattern of that which cannot die.
Arising right where it is, extinguished wherever it goes—this is the model for living life. A great man must, directly, abide within arising."
The stream of death flows on; one lies amidst a forest of thorns, bending, stretching, and moving according to circumstances as they arise.
If one can act thus, the great gate of liberation—the Samādhi Adorned with Immeasurable Expedient Means—will open wide and unimpeded.
Should this not yet be so, immeasurable afflictions and all manner of worldly toil will stand like mountains before one’s face, blocking the ancient path.
Snow was falling. A monk asked, "I do not ask about the Patriarch’s coming from the West; what is the matter of the seasonal conditions?
The Master said, "One flake, two flakes, three or four flakes—falling into the eye, yet one still does not realize it."
Chan Master Shimen Yuanji ascended the hall and said:
"The ten directions gather together; each and every one studies non-action (*wuwei*). This is the field for selecting the Buddha;
with an empty mind, they return as the valedictorian. "Great assembly, as for hearing, seeing, sensing, and knowing—which have never been interrupted—how can you speak of 'mind'?"
Is the principle of emptiness seeing without seeing, hearing without hearing—this that you call the emptiness of mind? Wrong.

Is it forgetting the workings of the intellect and ceasing all deliberation, casting aside all phenomena, dissolving the subject-object duality to enter the primal source, and extinguishing both nature and characteristics to return to the Dharma-realm—this that you call the emptiness of mind? Wrong. It is not so, yet it is also not otherwise.
"It is attained. Neither 'thus' nor 'not thus'—neither of these is attained. "I do not yet understand; ultimately, how is it? "Do you understand yet?
After a long silence, he said: "If truly there is nothing to be done, yet nothing is left undone, then heaven and hell follow one another constantly.
With a three-foot staff, he stirs the Yellow River; the eight-armed Nārāyaṇa peers with cold eyes. Infinite fish and dragons all flee in haste; having caught them... (He trailed off.)
The three-legged turtle of the river sheds its shell; with an iron awl, the omens of good and ill are clearly distinguished.
I ask the white-haired old man of the eastern village: when good and ill have not yet manifested, what is there to do? Rest, rest, rest! From antiquity to the present, spring follows autumn.
Let the bright days pass as they may, according to one’s lot; why begrudge anything that lacks elegance? *Du!* (A sharp exclamation of realization).

Master Nan of Zisheng ascended the hall on the occasion of the Emperor’s birthday and, looking around at those present, said: "Do you all understand? The Lord outside the curtains of night-brightness undergoes no change amidst the myriad transformations;
the Honored One atop the crystal palace is not obscured by the four ministers. He governs with effortless composure, issuing no commands."

He thus proceeded. His lifespan exceeded that of ten billion Mount Sumerus, and his transformative influence permeated the sands of the great trichiliocosm. But tell me, at such a time as this, how does he conduct himself?
"The rustic elder knows not the nobility of the imperial carriage; in the six streets, he is too weary to listen to the sound of the quiet-whip."
A monk asked Chan Master Dàtōng Shànběn of Fǎyún:
"The precious stupa is originally without seams; how can one point this out to people? The Master said: "Mist and clouds arise from its front and back; stars and moon circle its eaves and rafters.
The monk asked: "Who is the person within the stupa? The Master said: "Throughout the day, he does not interfere with the affairs of the mundane world."
For many years he occupied the region of white clouds. [A monk] asked, "Is there anything further above this? The Master said, "You are truly insatiable.
Wherever the Master went, upon seeing images of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in either standing or walking postures, he did not dare to sit. Regarding the *i-phu-se* (upāsaka) meal, he would use fish.
Regarding the name "Minced Meat": one does not eat it. Its true sincerity responds to circumstances; guarding the mind and remaining free from transgression is of this same nature.
A monk asked Chan Master Yan of Zishou Monastery in Shouzhou:
"Is there anything extraordinary within the Great Canon? The Master said: "I only fear that you will not believe it."
The student asked, "How is it that these are so? The Master said, "The black is ink; the yellow is paper. The student said, "Thank you for answering my question, Master."
The Master said: "Grasp the meaning at the tip of the hook; do not fixate on the zero point of the scale.

He ascended the hall and said: "Heaven and earth are serene and still; the seas are calm and the rivers clear. The wind does not whistle through the branches; the rain does not break the clods of earth.
Spring brings forth and summer nurtures; autumn harvests and winter stores. This is the Dharma of the world. What, then, is the Buddha-Dharma? After a long silence, he remained still.
He said: "If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the Tathāgata’s True Wheel of Dharma.
Chan Master Xiuyong of Touzi studied under Master Huilin;
upon having a realization while falling, he composed a verse, saying: "This one fall, this one fall—ten thousand catties..."
Even gold should be consumed: a hat upon the head, a satchel at the waist, and the clear wind and bright moon carried on the tip of the staff.
Lord Fu Zhenggong was alerted by Zhao Qingxian Gong and, without ceasing day or night, exerted himself to advance in this Way. He went to visit Master [Furong Daokai] at Touzi.
At that time, the Master was ascending the seat for the assembly; seeing the Master looking around to his left and right, Lord Fu suddenly attained realization.
Adopting the etiquette of a disciple, he hurried to the master’s quarters. The Master commanded an attendant to invite him to enter the inner room.
Upon seeing him, the Master immediately said, "The Excellency has already entered; Fu Bi is still outside. When Fu Bi heard this, sweat poured down his back, and he attained great enlightenment.

Lord Zhao Bian, styled Yue Dao, was over forty years old when he cast aside sensory pleasures and focused his mind on the teachings of the religious schools. At that time, Fohui resided at Nan Chan Monastery in Quzhou;
the Lord visited him daily, yet Fohui never permitted him to utter a single word. Later, while the Lord governed Qingzhou, in matters of administration—

He spent much of his time in silent meditation. Suddenly, a great thunderclap struck with such force that he attained immediate enlightenment. He composed a verse, saying: "Sitting in silence within the hall, leaning back against the empty rest;
The source of the mind is unmoving, as still as water. A single stroke of thunder opens the gate at the crown of my head; It awakens that which has been my own from the very beginning.
When Huìwén heard this, he laughed and said, "Zhào Yuèdào has simply hit the jackpot. The Master once inscribed a verse for himself in his study:
He said: "The golden belt at my waist has already been retired and hidden away; the message within this is quite ordinary.

If people of the world wish to know the old man of Gaozhai, he is simply Zhao Sili of Ke Village. He spoke again, saying: "Be careful not to mistake him. At the time of his death, he wrote a letter to Fohui, in which he said:
"Had it not been for the constant admonitions and instructions of my teacher throughout my life, I certainly would not have gained such strength at this moment."
When Zen Master Huanlong Sisi Wuxin first visited Xiexian Xiu Tiewen, Xiu asked, "Where are you from, Senior Monk? The Master replied, "From Shaoguo in Guangnan.
Xiu asked again, "Have you ever been to Yunmen? The Master replied, "I have. Xiu asked again, "Have you ever been to Lingshu? The Master... [replied].
[The Master] said, "I have been there. Xiu asked, "What are the branches of the Ling tree? The Master said, "The long ones are naturally long; the short ones are naturally short.
Xiu said, "You barbarian from Guangnan, do not confuse the order! The Master said, "As for the donkeys heading north, they are just like that," and he shook his sleeves and left.
Xiu recognized his potential, but the Master had no intention of staying. He went to Huanglong to visit Haitang, who raised his fist and asked:
The Master said, "If you call it a 'fist,' it is an offense (*chu*). If you do not call it a 'fist,' it is a contradiction (*bei*).

What would you call it? The Master was at a loss. After two years, he finally attained realization; yet his eloquence remained such that there was nothing with which he could be refuted. Guishan was troubled by this.

Once, while conversing with him, as the Master reached the height of his sharpness, Guishan suddenly said, "Stop! Stop! Talking about food—how can it satisfy one's hunger? The Master was cornered and said:
"I have arrived here with my bow broken and my arrows exhausted. I pray that the Master will show me compassion and point out a place of peace and happiness.

The Hall Master said, "A single mote of dust flies up and obscures the heavens; a single mustard seed falls and covers the earth. As for a place of peace and happiness, I strictly forbid you, Venerable One, from possessing such a multitude of worldly trappings.
You must truly die the consciousness-mind that has existed since immeasurable kalpas, and only then will it be possible. The Master hurried out. One day...
Hearing that the administrative official was beating the practitioners, a sudden clap of thunder struck, and he attained great enlightenment immediately.
He rushed to see Huìtáng, forgetting to put on his shoes, and proclaimed, "Everyone under heaven merely practices Chan; I am one who has realized it.

Huìtáng laughed and said, "To have passed the examination for the Buddha with first honors—how could you be contained by such a title? Thereupon, he was given the sobriquet "Old Man Sīxīn" (Dead Heart).
He went to visit Chan Master Fuchang Yu. Yu asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The Master replied, "I have come here directly from Huanglong.
Yu asked, "Have you seen Chan Master Xin? The Master said, "I have. Yu asked, "Where did you see him?
The Master said, "I saw him where one eats porridge and eats rice. Yu thrust a fire-tongs into the brazier and said, "What about this? The Master—
He searched for and removed the fire tongs, then struck him.
Wang Zhengyan asked, "I have heard that birth occurs through the conjunction of three conditions. I have also heard that one dies and is immediately reborn.

Why is there such a thing as being 'snatched from the womb' to be born? The Master said, "It is like when you, Zhengyan, served as the Commissioner of Transport (Zaoshi): wherever you resided, you remained right there."
"Regarding that state, do you still have doubts? The King replied, "I have no doubts. The Master asked, "Then what is it that you doubt? At these words, the King attained realization.
When the Master resided at Cuíyán, there was a shrine to a local deity on the mountain where villagers offered sacrifices of wine and meat every day without fail.

The Master instructed the administrative officers to demolish it, but they declined, saying they did not dare to invite calamity upon themselves. The Master said, "If it were capable of causing calamity..."
"I shall take this upon myself," he said, and proceeded to dismantle it with his own hands. Suddenly, a giant python coiled within, extending its head as if to devour him.
The Master rebuked it, and the serpent fled; he slept peacefully thereafter without further incident.
He took charge of Yunyan and constructed a sutra repository. The Grand Historian Huang Tingjian composed a commemorative inscription for it.
Someone had engraved the epitaph for their relative on the reverse side of the stele. The Master scolded them, saying, "To commit such an act of insult and arrogance without avoiding calamity!

Before he had finished speaking, a flash of lightning overturned the roof, and a bolt of thunder struck through the doorway, splitting the reverse side of the stele in two. Upon inspection, the epitaph had already been reduced to ashes.
The records he had stored remained intact and undamaged.
Later, falling ill, he retired to Huìtáng. During the night assembly, he held up his whisk and said: "Look! Look! When the whisk is sick, the mind of Sīxin is sick;
when the whisk is at peace, the mind of Sīxin is at peace. The whisk pierces through the mind of Sīxin; the mind of Sīxin pierces through the whisk."
At such a time as this, if you call it a whisk, it is again the "Dead Heart" (Sīcitta); if you call it the "Dead Heart," it is again the whisk.
Ultimately, what would you call it? After a long silence, he said: "Do not bring right and wrong to judge me;
the frivolous interpretations of this floating life have no concern with me. To those who requested his final word, the Master showed them a verse: "The final word— It is directly..."
One must sever the path of the mind; once the gates of the six sense organs are empty, the ten thousand dharmas are without arising or ceasing.
If one penetrates the source here, there is no need to seek liberation. Throughout my life I have loved reviling others, only because it brings me long-lasting joy.
Chan Master Letan Caotang Qing ascended the hall and said:
"Form and mind are not different; self and other are without distinction. Raising his whisk, he said: "If you call this a whisk—"

Entering hell is like an arrow shot; it cannot be called a whisk. Having eyes yet being as if blind—even if one manages to break through both ends, it is still a black ox lying dead in stagnant water.
The Layman Huang Tingjian of Tai-shan Valley first visited Master Xiu Yuan-tong;
the details of their conversation are contained in the "Chapter on Yuan-tong. From that time forward, he composed a text of vows and strictly refrained from alcohol and sexual indulgence.
Eating only morning congee and the midday meal, he applied himself with keen resolve to seeking the Way. Having relied upon Master Hei-tang, he requested instruction on the direct and expedient path.
The Master said, "As for Confucius’s words, 'Do you disciples think that I am hiding anything from you?

I hide nothing from you,' how would you, Taishi, explain this in ordinary discourse? The Master was about to respond when the Master said, "Not so! Not so! The Master remained bewildered and distressed.
One day, while walking together with the Master in the mountains, the rock-orchids were in full bloom. The Master said, "I have heard of the wood..."
"Is the scent of the osmanthus flowers fragrant? The Official said, "I smell it. Tang said, "I have hidden nothing from you.
The Official was relieved and immediately bowed, saying, "Does the Master truly possess such a compassionate and earnest heart? Tang smiled and said, "It is simply that I wish for you to reach home.
After some time, he went to visit Chan Master Sixin Xin. Following the assembly into the inner quarters, Xin saw him and, opening his eyes wide, asked, "Elder Xin!"
"Death. The Master has died. He was cremated and reduced to two heaps of ash. Where can we meet? The Official had no words.

Xinyue said, "What you have attained through your studies under Huitang has not yet been put into practice. Later, while serving as an official in Qian Nan, his power of the Way grew even more eminent.
Amidst a state of non-conceptualization, he suddenly realized the meaning of what Death-Mind (Sixin) had asked. He sent a letter in reply, saying: "In years past, I once received your grace..."
One must constantly and painfully rouse oneself; otherwise, one remains as if in a long dream or intoxicated stupor, lingering indistinctly within the shadows and glimmers of appearances.

This is because doubt has not been fully exhausted and the life-root (*jīvamūla*) has not been severed; thus, one merely looks toward the precipice and retreats. While on the road in Qian-nan during my exile, I was awakened from a nap at midday.
Suddenly, upon reflection, I realized how much I have been deceived by the old monks of the world. Only the Venerable Sishin refused to grant me his seal of approval;
this was truly his foremost act of compassion for me.
The lay practitioner Wu Xun De-fu, a member of the Secretariat, visited Huìtáng for consultation.
Huìtáng said to him, "I shall not ask about the many studies, understandings, memories, and extensive learnings you have accumulated throughout your life.
Tell me, before your parents were even born, bring forth a single phrase. As the official hesitated, Huìtáng struck him with his whisk. Immediately—

Having grasped the profound meaning, he presented three verses in succession. The last one said: "Tsk! This worldly fellow of much knowledge has gnawed through all the public cases of the past and present.
Suddenly, from amidst a heap of refuse, he picks up a dung ball of a dung beetle—obviously not worth a single coin."
Ten thousand taels of gold cannot buy it. He casually picks it up and shows it to others, simply because it is difficult to watch when the tray is spinning.
Chan Master Congyue of Doushuai was formerly the head of the assembly at Daowu; he led several monks to visit Master Zhi of Yungai. Before Zhi had even finished speaking with him—
After he had recited several lines and fully understood what was contained within them, Zhi laughed and said, "I observe that the Senior Seat’s temperament is extraordinary;
why is it that his speech and breath are like those of a drunkard? The Master’s face flushed and sweat broke out as he said, "I pray that the Master will not withhold his compassion.

Zhi spoke with him again, probing him with sharp questions, until the Master was utterly bewildered. He then requested to enter the room for private instruction. Zhi said, "Have you ever seen Fachang Yu?"
"Is it not so, Master? The Master said, "I have already read his recorded sayings; I am content with that myself and have no wish to see him.
Zhì asked, "Have you ever seen Master Wén of Dòngshān? The Master said, "That fellow from Guānxī is a source of endless vexation.
He drags around a hempen skirt that smells of urine; what excellence does he possess? Zhì said, "You should simply take up your investigation within that very smell of urine."

The Master followed these instructions and went to visit Dongshan, where he profoundly grasped the profound essence of the teachings. He then visited Zhi, who asked, "Since you have seen the man from Guansi, how is the Great Matter?
The Master replied, "Had it not been for the Venerable Master’s guidance, I would have missed my entire life."
He then performed a ritual of prostration and thanks. The Master subsequently visited Zhenjing. Later, he took up residence at Luyuan.

There was a man named Qing Su who had long studied under Ciming; he lived in a single room and never once associated with others. Once, while the Master was eating lychees preserved in honey, Su happened to pass by his door.
The Master called out to him, saying, "This is a fruit from your native region, elder; you may share it with me. Su replied, "Since my late teacher passed away..."
"Later, it has been a long time since I have obtained this food. The Master asked, "Who was your former teacher? Su replied, "It was Ciming.
I have had the honor of serving him for thirteen years. The Master then said with astonishment, "To have endured the duties of service for thirteen years!"
"How could it be anything other than having attained the Way? He then offered him some leftover fruit and gradually grew close to him.
Su asked, "Whom did your teacher see? The Master replied, "Dongshan Wencui. Su asked, "Whom did Wencui see? The Master said, "Huanglong Nanquan. Su said, "..."
Nan-p’ien-t’ou had seen his former master for but a short time, yet the Dharma path was already flourishing so greatly.
The Master (Yun-men) became increasingly astonished; he then placed incense in his sleeve and went to pay homage to Su. As Su rose to avoid him, he said, “I am of meager merit;

my former master gave me a prediction that I was not permitted to act as a teacher. The Master was even more reverent. Su then said, “Out of pity for your sincerity, I shall transgress my former master’s prediction. Throughout your life...”
The Master presented his realization and requested verification. Baizhang Su fully understood what he had seen.
Su said, "What you have seen can lead one into the Buddha-way, but it cannot lead one into the realm of Māra. The Master asked, "Why is that? Su replied, "Have you not heard the ancients say:
'The final phrase is where one first reaches the secure barrier'? After several days of this, Su finally gave him his seal of approval, yet he cautioned him, saying, "Do not reveal this to others."
"My disciples all possess correct knowledge and correct view; however, you left your teacher too early and were unable to exhaust its subtlety.
I shall now point it out for you so that you may enjoy it and attain great mastery. On another day, by no means should you succeed me.
Later, the Master succeeded Zhenjing, exactly as he had been cautioned.
In his quarters, the Master established three questions to test his students. The first was: "One brushes away the weeds and gazes at the wind, seeking only to see one's nature.
Where, then, does the nature of a person now reside? The second was: "Only by recognizing one's own nature can one escape birth and death.
When the light of the eyes falls to the ground, how does one escape? The third was: "Once one has escaped birth and death, one knows the place of departure. What are the four great elements?"
"Separated! To what place has he gone?
When Chan Master Ledtan Zantang Wenzhun first arrived, Yunyan’s seat was vacant.
The Prefect ordered Sishi Xin Chan Master to recommend someone he knew. Xin said, "The Abbot Zhun."
“Zhudé, I have never known him. However, I have seen a verse he wrote on washing a bowl that is quite excellent. Mù requested him to recite it. Xīn recited: “The, the, the, and the;
the nostrils of the patch-robed monk point their great head downward. If you do not understand this, go ask Old Lady Wáng of the eastern village.
Mù marveled at this and consequently invited him to preside over Yún’ān.

One day, a newly arrived monk came for an audience. As he spread out his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*), the Master said, "Before you have performed the greetings of courtesy, where have you recently come from, Upādhyāya?
The monk replied, "From Guizong on Mount Lu. The Master asked, "Where has Guizong returned to? The monk said, "Aha! The Master said, "You are making your living inside a toad's den.
The monk said, "Why do you not acknowledge my words, Preceptor? The Master said, "Do you not yourself come from Guizong?"
The Master said, "Yes. He added, "A donkey in front and a horse behind—what a Chinese! He asked the second senior monk, "Where have you recently come from?
He replied, "Yuanzhou. The Master said, "Where did you spend the summer retreat? He replied, "Mount Yang. The Master said, "Did you see Little Śākyamuni? He replied, "I saw him."
The Master said, "How long are your nostrils? The monk hesitated. The Master said, "The talk has fallen away, Master. He asked another monk, "What have you come for?
The monk replied, "I have come specifically to pay my respects to the Master. The Master said, "The clouds at the mountain peak are never idle;
the water flowing down the ravine is far too busy. The monk said, "Master, do not deceive people. The Master said, "The horse is large."
The Master asked, "Why did you pass right under the feet of the *acarya*? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "In fact, it is you who are deceiving this old monk.
One day, on the Dharma Hall, he encountered the Head Seat and immediately asked, "Where are you going? The Seat replied, "I am about to go with the Master..."

"I would like to discuss one matter," he said. The Master replied, "Please do so. He asked, "The handle of the ladle at the eastern house is long; the handle of the ladle at the western house is short.
The Master said, "Why is it that you pick up a tea jar from Gong County, yet serve with a porcelain bowl from Raoyou?
He replied, "Looking down at the water from the edge of a cliff—one needlessly brings about a scene of sorrow. The Master cried out in protest, and the visitor stuck out his tongue and withdrew.
A monk asked, "The scriptures state: 'If there is one person who awakens to the truth and returns to the source, the empty space of the ten directions will all vanish.
I do not yet understand how this principle works. The Master then opened his palm and pointed his fingers, saying: "Zi, Chou, Yin, Mao; Chen, Si, Wu, Wei.
One is Luo, two is Tu, three is Shui, four is Jin, five is Taiyang, six is Taiyin, and seven is Jidu. Now...
The sun and the planet Ketu enter the house of Cancer. Baofeng does not beat this drum or blow this flute;
he then descends from his seat and addresses the assembly, saying: "To drill a pearl and polish a jade tablet is easy; to look into a hollow and drive in a wedge is difficult.
I shall not ask about the moonlight white with clouds and the pine sounds cold with dew; but tell me, all of you, what about Mahāmaudgalyāyana?"
"What matter were you and Subhūti discussing?
Master Qingliang Hongfan Hui addressed the assembly, saying:
"Master Linyuan said to me: 'The practitioner’s method of preservation is like a person who must take medicine when ill.'"

Medicine. The efficacy of medicine is easily seen; one must strictly observe dietary prohibitions for it to take effect. Otherwise, what benefit is there in taking the medicine? Birth and death are a great illness;
the teachings of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are the excellent medicine; a defiled mind is the impure food.
If one cannot abstain from this, the disease of birth and death will never diminish. I cherish these words and recall the *Complete Enlightenment Sūtra*, which says:
For all sentient beings in the final age, if their minds do not give rise to delusion, the Buddha says that such people are Bodhisattvas in the present life.
The *Dharmapada* states: "If one gives rise to a mind of diligent effort, this is delusion and not true diligence; only when the mind is free from delusion is diligence boundless.
When the Great Meditation Master Si of Mount Nanyue attained entry into the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-samādhi*, he immediately recited: "This is..."

True diligence is what is called the true Dharma-offering. Throughout his life, the Great Master Guoshi of Fenyang answered the questions of seekers with nothing but the words, "Do not engage in false conceptualization.
These were words that accorded with the nature of reality (*dharmatā*) and revealed the gateway to the path of seeing.
Yet, Chan practitioners have altered these words, seeking instead some primordial subtlety; this is truly laughable.

The Venerable Youpeng, a lecturer, had previously composed commentaries on such sutras as the *Śūraṅgama-samādhi* and the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa*. Scholars revered him, yet he often harbored doubts regarding the path of direct pointing taught by the Patriarchs;
consequently, he frequently associated with Chan practitioners. One day, he went to visit Kaiyuan. Before his foot had even crossed the threshold, he suddenly attained realization.
Kaiyuan came out and asked, "What have you come here for, Master? The Master said, "I do not dare to hold my ears high while disparaging my eyes.
Kaiyuan said, "You are so old and venerable; why must you be like this? The Master said, "He who considers himself self-sufficient does not grow. Kaiyuan said, "..."
[Daowu] said, "Setting aside for a moment my morning study of the *Avataṃsaka* and my night reading of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, tell me:
what is the single phrase for the present moment? The Master said, "The sun is exactly at midday. Kaiyuan said, "That was idle talk. Speak further.
The Master said, "Throughout my life I have relied on loyalty and trust; today I shall face the wind and waves. Even so, as for the Master speaking thus, what connection is there?"
Sheshuo said, "A newly ordained monk must wear straw sandals. Kaiyuan said, "I will let you pass for now.
But what would you say if you encountered Bodhidharma? The Master gave a shout. Kaiyuan said, "This lecturer has his temper rising toward the ox and the dipper today!
The Master said, "No second offense shall be tolerated. Kaiyuan clapped his hands and laughed loudly.
The Chan Master Wuzu Fayan went to Baiyun and brought up the story of a monk asking Nanquan about the mani jewel for inquiry. Baiyun rebuked him, and the Master attained realization.
He offered this verse of karmic resonance: "A plot of vacant land before the mountain; With palms joined, I earnestly questioned the patriarch."

"Several times I sold it back only to buy it again, out of affection for the pines and bamboos that draw in the pure breeze. Yun granted him formal approval (*inka*) and ordered him to take charge of the mill.
One day, a monk saw the mill turning and suddenly pointed at it, asking, "Is this supernatural power (*abhijñā*), or is it the natural order of things (*dharmatā*)?
The Master lifted his robe and spun the mill once; the monk was left speechless. Not long after, Yun arrived and said to the Master, "There is..."
Several Zen practitioners came from Mount Lu; each had attained a point of awakening. When asked to explain it, they could indeed speak with a clear rationale.
When presented with a kōan (in-yuan) to investigate, they understood it clearly. When asked to offer a verbal response, they were able to provide one. Yet, it was simply not yet there.
The Master was greatly perplexed by this. He thought to himself, "I have already attained realization; I can explain it and I can clarify it. Why then am I still not 'there'?
He investigated this for several days until he suddenly attained awakening. All that he had previously cherished was cast aside at once.
He went to see Baiyun, who danced with joy, while the Master simply smiled. Afterward, the Master...
He said, "Because of this, I have broken into a cold sweat, and I have thereby clearly realized a thousand loads of pure wind. One day Yunmen addressed the assembly, saying, "An ancient said:

'It is like casting an image in a mirror. Once the image is formed, where is the mirror? The assembly offered various responses, but none were in accord with the truth. He brought the case up to ask the Master.
The Master stepped forward to pay his respects and said, "It is not even slightly less [than the image]. Yunmen smiled and said, "You must..."

that alone shall be your point of view. The student was bewildered and withdrew. He spent three years in intensive study and practice. One day, he entered the room.
The Master finished speaking. Baizhang said to him, "The words you have uttered already possess ninety percent of the truth.

Try once more to explain them to me. The Master then analyzed and presented his understanding. Baizhang said, "Your explanation is indeed ninety percent correct, but try to deliver a definitive judgment for me.
The Master then passed judgment according to each question. Baizhang said, "It is well, it is well; yet you have not yet attained the level of my own discourse. After the midday meal...
"You may come to the Patriarch’s Stupa; only after I have verified each point with you one by one shall it be so.

When he arrived there, the Patriarch cross-examined him using such sayings as "The mind is itself Buddha," "Neither mind nor Buddha," "Muzhou is a fellow carrying a wooden board," "Nanquan slaughtered the cat," and "Zhaozhou’s 'The dog has no Buddha-nature' and 'The dog has Buddha-nature. To all these, his responses were entirely without hesitation.
[The Master] was at a loss. When he reached the story of "Zihu’s Dog," the Patriarch suddenly turned his face away and said, "It is not so. The Master asked, "If it is not so, then how?

The Patriarch said, "If this is not so, then everything preceding it is also not so. The Master said, "I beg the Venerable One for your compassionate instruction. The Patriarch said, "Look at what he says:
'Zihu has a dog that takes people's heads when they come from above, takes people's waists when they come from the middle, and [takes people's feet] when they come from below.'"
"Seize the person’s feet! Those who enter the gate must look well. As soon as you see a monk enter the gate, say, 'Look at the dog!
If you can deliver a turning word at the very point where Xiangzi Hu says 'Look at the dog,' you will leave Xiangzi Hu tongue-tied and cause this old monk to clench his mouth.

This is precisely where you must reach a definitive realization. The next day, when [Xiangzi] entered the room, the Master secretly revealed this teaching to him. The Patriarch laughed and said, "I do not say that you are not [capable]."
"This is a man who has reached a definitive conclusion; these words are exactly like those spoken by my late teacher.
The Master said, "What kind of person am I that I could be like Master Duan? The Patriarch said, "Not so. Although I have inherited his lineage, I consider his words to be clumsy."
This was likely because he used the methods of Master Yuanlu to receive people.

As for this old monk, when I am with Master Yuanlu, we walk hand-in-hand with those such as Baizhang, Huangbo, Nanquan, and Zhaozhou. If one merely encounters clumsy speech, they will find it unbearable;

yet you, Master, consider this not to be so, and thus you have dragged your staff across the river. Now that the great waters are overflowing, you have consequently remained at the Fourth Patriarch’s monastery.
His peers pulled him back home. After another two years, his grandfather finally gave his consent. Once, while discussing the past and present, [the grandfather] took the Master by the hand and said:
"To understand your discourse, you must have my raising of the case; to understand my raising of the case, you must have my discourse. From this day forward..."
The secret essentials of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, the pivotal keys of all quarters—none escape your grasp.
Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "Since the time of the Patriarchs, people have misunderstood; they take mere words and phrases to be the Way of Chan.
They do not realize that the Way has no substance, yet it is given a name based on that substance; the Way has no name, yet it is given a title based on that name. Only...
Just as the Elder has just now come out in such a manner and immediately returned to the assembly:
does he possess the eye or not? If he possesses the eye, where is that eye when he comes out in such a manner?
If you say he does not possess the eye, how could he go out in such a manner? O worthy ones, if you can see this clearly and decisively, then you will know.
The Second Patriarch prostrated and stood in his place; he had truly attained the marrow.

This very thing is the life-root of all Buddhas of the three periods, the life-vein of the six generations of patriarchs, and the place where the old monks of the world establish their bodies and lives.
Nevertheless, one must arrive at it personally before it can be realized.
An elderly master gave this turning word: "Suppose a thatched hut were erected at the crossroads, but people were not permitted to defecate there.
A monk raised this to question the Master. The Master said, "You have already defecated; what more do you want anyone else to do?"
Having heard of this previously, he burned incense and gazed afar at Dawsui, prostrating in gratitude to Chan Master Wuweizongtai.

This master had studied under the Fifth Patriarch, who had assigned him the koan of Zhaozhou washing the alms bowl for his practice. When [the student] entered the room for instruction, the master brought up this very koan.
The Master asked, "Tell me, what did Zhaozhou say to him that the monk attained enlightenment? The Master said, "'Go wash the bowl.
The Patriarch said, "You know only the matters of the road; you do not know the flavor of the road.
The Master said, "Since you know the matters of the road, what flavor could there be on the road? The Patriarch said, "Do you not know? He then asked, "Have you ever..."
"Have you traveled through Zhejiang? The Master said, "Not yet. The Patriarch said, "You have not yet attained realization. From that time on, for five years, the Master was unable to respond.
One day, the Patriarch ascended the hall, looked at the assembly, and said, "An eighty-year-old old man rolls a brocade ball," and then he descended from his seat.
The Master joyfully stepped forth from the assembly and said, "Preceptor, try rolling it once and see.

The Patriarch made a gesture with his hand as if beating a *daizhanggu* drum and sang a folk song of Mianzhou in the Shu dialect: "On Mount Douzi, they beat the earthen drums; On Mount Yangping, they scatter white rain.
As the white rain falls, they fetch the Dragon Maidens; They weave silk, twenty-five *zhang* long, Half of which belongs to Luojiang, and half..."
Half [of the mountain] belonged to Yuwu. Upon hearing this, the Master attained great enlightenment. He covered the Patriarch’s mouth and said, “It is enough to sing only up to this point.
The Patriarch laughed heartily and returned.
This was recorded by Chan Master Baizhang Huaihai.

The Master had stayed with the Fifth Patriarch for the longest time, yet he had not yet attained realization. At that time, Yuanwu was the Head Seat (Zuoyuan); the Master went to him to seek instruction.

Yuanwu said, "Brother, try telling me where you have doubts. The Master then cited the story of Deshan’s informal sermon: "I do not answer questions; those who ask questions receive thirty blows of the staff.
Yuanwu said, "Prostrate yourself! I can act as your teacher, yet you still do not understand this very case. The Master then prostrated himself.
When the ritual was concluded, Wuzhuo ordered him to repeat his previous words. The Master said, "Deshan’s informal lecture stated that he would not answer questions.
Wuzhuo covered his mouth and said, "Just look at it like this! The Master left and cried out loudly, "A grievance! A grievance!
How can there be a public case (gong'an) that merely instructs people to look at a single phrase? A monk said to the Master, "Brother, you must not speak in such a manner. The Head Seat must..."
There was a skillful means. After ten days of sitting in meditation and investigating the matter, he suddenly resolved his doubts and went to pay his respects to Wuzu.
Wuzu said, "Brother, you have finally realized that I did not deceive you. He then went to the abbot's quarters, where the Patriarch (Nanquan) greeted him with a smile.
The Master posted a notice at the gate for the attendants that said: "Dongshan has three statements. If anyone can speak them, they shall be admitted to the monastery.
The monastics were all disheartened. One day, a monk carrying his sitting mat went straight to the master’s quarters and said to him, "I cannot speak them, but I simply wish to be admitted.
The Master was greatly pleased and called the rector to arrange a place for him beneath a bright window.

When Chan Master Qing Su Jiuding heard the Fifth Patriarch cite the dialogue concerning the meaning of the First Patriarch’s coming from the West, he attained sudden enlightenment. He composed a verse, saying:
"Upside down, upside down! The new bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it. To act in such a manner is utterly groundless. Turning one's head back—"
He put on his robe and went out. When the Patriarch saw him, he asked, "What about Baizhang’s story of the wild fox?
The Master replied, "Those who come to discuss right and wrong are themselves the people of right and wrong. The Patriarch was greatly pleased.
When Governor Lü Gong came to visit the Great Image, he asked, "Since this is the Great Image, why does it have two pillars slung over its shoulders?
The Master replied, "There are no idle hands on a boat. When they reached the pavilion and beheld the Avalokiteśvara image, the Governor asked again, "This is the realm of Maitreya’s transformation."
"Where does Guanyin come from? The Master said, "When a family is wealthy, their young children are spoiled; when they are restrained, they then show reverence.

Dharma-shan, the Senior Monk, had long relied upon the Fifth Patriarch but had not yet attained realization. One day he went to the Patriarch’s quarters, where the Patriarch asked him, "Do you not act as a hindrance to the myriad dharmas?"
"Who is this person called 'Fashian'? He said, 'Fashian is not so. The Patriarch pointed his finger and said, 'Stop!
Stop! Fashian is not so—how can that be? At these words, the Master attained awakening."
The Master arrived at Donglin and entered the hall of Chan Master Xianmi. There he saw that [Xianmi] had attained the essence of the "plain and real" (pingshi).
One day, [Xianmi] took up a flower, circled Chan Master Xianmi’s seat once, and with his back turned, thrust it into the incense burner.

He said, "Master, tell me: what is the meaning? Xianmi offered several responses, but none were in accord. After more than two months had passed, [Xianmi] then commanded the Master to try explaining it. The Master...
He said, "I have merely taken these flowers and inserted them into the incense burner; why does the Master suspect me? What business could there be?
Yu Daopo of Jinling made her living by selling oil and food.
She would regularly follow the assembly to inquire about the Dharma with Langye Huijue. Langye took up the "Unlocated True Person" of Linji...
He explained this to her. One day, she heard a beggar chanting a "Lotus Flower" song that went: "Were it not for Liu Yi transmitting the letter, by what means could one reach Lake Dongting?
She suddenly attained great enlightenment and threw an oil-cake to the ground. Her husband said, "Have you gone mad?"
Baozhang said, "This is not within your realm. He went to see Langye. As Langye gazed at him, he recognized his level of attainment and asked, "Who is that person of no rank?

Baozhang replied immediately: "There is a person of no rank with six arms and three heads, Straining and angry, he splits Mount Hua in two with a single blow. The waters of Wan’an flow on, unaware of spring."

When Yuanwu was inaugurating his hall at Jiangshan, just as he reached the front of the Dharma seat, a woman leaped out from among the assembly and pressed against him with her body once, then returned to the crowd.
Yuanwu said, "If one does not find strange what is strange, the strangeness will naturally vanish. On the following day, Yuanwu went to her home.
The old woman did not come out. She said in a stern voice, "A mere child with a yellow mouth like this also claims to come out to open the hall and preach the Dharma.
Wuzu said, "Old woman, stop showing off; I know you well enough. The old woman then laughed loudly and came out to meet him.
Whenever a monk arrived, she would say, "Child! Child! If the monk hesitated, she would immediately shut the door.
When Chan Master Fodeng Xun went to test her, the old woman saw him and questioned him as before. Xun asked, "Where is my father? The old woman turned around and bowed toward a pillar.
Xun immediately kicked it over and said, "I thought there was something truly extraordinary here," and then he left. The old woman scrambled up and called out, "Child! Child! Come back!"
"I pity you indeed," [Baizhang said]. Xu simply paid no heed.
He offered this verse on the occasion of Mazu’s illness: "The face of the sun, the face of the moon, like lightning flashing in the void.
Though it cuts off the tongues of all people under heaven, It clearly says only half the truth."
When Master Shimen Cong was at Baoci, he heard the cry of a dove and asked a monk, "What sound is that? The monk said, "It is the sound of a 'jū-jū' [dove].
The Master said, "If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the Tathāgata’s True Dharma Wheel."
Chan Master Huīhuī of Jingci visited Hongzhi.
Hongzhi questioned him, saying: "When there is brightness within, do not meet it with darkness; when there is darkness within, do not look at it with brightness.
Huīhuī’s words did not accord with the Master's intent. Returning from his evening meditation, he went before the Sacred Monk and burned incense.

Xiang was there, and Hongzhi arrived just then. Upon seeing him, the Master suddenly understood the previous conversation. The following day, when [Xiang] entered the room for private instruction, Hongzhi brought up the lines:
"Alas, on the day he departed, his countenance was like jade; yet now, sighing as he returns, his hair is like frost. When Xiang questioned him about this, the Master said: "His entry and departure."
His emergence was subtle; from that point on, his responses to questions were unhindered, and Zhi (Zhaozhou) acknowledged him as a true son within the room.
When a monk asked Chan Master Xuedou Chanzong, "What is the True Dharma Eye? the Master said, "A black bean."
Question: "What is the Sovereign? The Master said: "Grinding the three-foot sword, waiting to slay those who are unjust.
Question: "What is the Minister? The Master said: "White clouds never rest; flowing water is ever busy. Question: "What is the harmony between Sovereign and Minister?
The Master said: "Clouds move and rain falls; the moon is bright and the stars shine."
Question: What is "the partial within the central"? The Master said: "Before the rhombus-flower has been illumined.

Question: What is "the central within the partial"? The Master said: "A perfect sphere, without a single bit lacking. Question: What is "coming from the central"? The Master said: "Throughout the entire realm, not a speck of dust remains.
Question: What is "arriving at the simultaneous"? The Master said: "The playful exercise prior to the act of biting the arrowhead. Question: What is...?
"Simultaneously reaching the center. The Master said: "The ten directions are not obstructed. Question:
"What is 'transferring merit to the position'? The Master said: "Letting go of all supports, the entire body is manifest;
a lone boat and its fisherman sleep amidst the reeds. Question: "What is 'transferring the position to merit'? The Master said: "Wind and moon atop the ridge at midnight."

[The Master said: "Silence. A lone cry from an old monkey in a high tree. [The student] asked: "What is the simultaneous manifestation of function and rank? The Master said: "Leaving the gate, one does not tread the path by which one came;
before one's eyes, flying dust is utterly free of a single speck of grime. [The student] asked: "What is the simultaneous concealment of function and rank?"
The Master said: "The clay ox drinks up the moonlight of the clear pool; the stone horse, spurred on, does not turn its head.

From the time Chan Master Yuanshi Jixiang first arrived at Tianyi, he applied himself with diligent effort day and night, never letting his side touch the mat. One day, he happened to laugh out loud and disturb the assembly.
Tianyi banished him. During the middle watch of the night, while staying in a village field, he beheld the stars and moon shining brilliantly and attained a realization.
At dawn, he returned and hurried to the abbot’s quarters. When Tianyi saw him, he asked, "How do you explain the Five Ranks of Lord and臣 (Minister) of Dongshan?
The Master replied, "In my place, there is not even a single rank. Tianyi ordered him to attend the hall and said to his attendant monk, "This fellow indeed possesses a certain insight."
"How can one remain in this state while failing to recognize the fundamental principle? Next, during the "Entering the Room" ceremony, Tianyi had five attendants stand in a line in advance.
When the Master arrived, they all called out, "Venerable Shishang! Thereupon, the Master secretly realized the profound essence and composed a verse:
"The single rank is just revealed, and the five ranks are distinguished; Lord and minister harmonize, and purple clouds gather. The night-bright curtain is rolled up, shining without partiality."
The multi-storied golden halls manifest supreme dignity; celestial robes proclaim excellence.
